I poked my head back into the air and sucked in a deep breath and brushed my wet locks that was plastered across my face away. I soaked until the water cooled before I emerged, wet and wrinkly and towelled myself off thoroughly. It was getting late, or rather early since the raid had commenced at midnight and I went straight to bed.

## Chapter 2

I woke late the next day and glancing at my chronometer on the wall I saw that I still had a few hours before my next engagement so I retrieved my weapons and sat naked on the floor in front of them. I emptied the cylinders of both revolvers and inspected the spent casings. One of them had been dented and scratched and I sent it floating in front of me at chest height. I started channelling power into the casing, feeling the rough edges with my mind and smoothing them out. It took a lot of magical power to create even a small amount of the dark crystal that comprised everything in the Skylands, even the rug I was sitting on. The Mages had swiftly figured out how to create matter from magic and the crystal they created could take many forms. Some were long, crystalline filaments that could me made into cloth. Some were hard and dense and was used to construct buildings. Some were softer but stronger and like the legendary metals of old. Creating matter from magic was not common knowledge and it was knowledge that was guarded by the Mages closely. My friend, Kendall, were a genius and was a Mage in training and had taught me what little I knew. I knew enough to repair some of my war gear but most advanced magic I had not bothered to learn. The machines created by true Magineers where far more accessible and easy to use than doing the magic by yourself. I spent much of my personal energies repairing the shell casing, and then I spent even more reloading the shots. I fitted the empty casings into a quick loader of opaque purple crystal and fitted the loader into a thick squat rod of the same type of crystal. I channelled power into the charger since the Powerstone inside was still depleted. I swore and squinted at my dispenser up in the corner. No magic streamed from it even though I had paid my magic bill for the month. This was happening with frustratingly increasing frequency. The magic providers had started failing all over the neighbourhood and people were starting to grumble. Despite the outages the rates kept getting higher. People were getting desperate and I had heard rumours of a new gang starting up in the Undercity. They were selling charged powerstones at somewhat reasonable prices. People thought that they were tapping one of the mainlines that led from the arcane collectors at the base of the Skylands to the various distribution centres throughout the cities but they were protected by powerful wards. Only the Mages had the knowledge and access to enough power to breach them, a rag tag band of criminals certainly did not. I had heard reports from some of my sources that bodies drained of their personal energies had been found and I had a creeping suspicion that the gang, that called themselves the Robin Hoods in homage to an ancient fable, was killing people for their magical power. So far only people that would not be missed had been killed and the Justiciary ignored them. The Robin Hoods most likely paid them off. I resolved to file a complaint about the magic outage later and I had to rely on my own power store for the maintenance of my war gear. I briefly considered using the power in the Powerstone on my choker but I would need that magic to manifest my armour. I sighed and poured more power into the charger and bluish streamers of light coiled into the apparatus in my hand. The dark crystal started glowing with a pretty purple light as the magical circuitry woke up. The casing started to fill up with a fine blue powder and a circle of blue crystal formed around the opening of the casings as the shots themselves started to form. The Powerstone in the charger filled up long before the shots were fully formed and I set the charger aside to finish the work on its own as I picked up the casings from my other revolver. These were of a much higher calibre than the others and the casings were much sturdier and had survived the battle intact. I only had the one charger so I started to recharge these individually. I split the stream of power in two and sent another of the shells afloat before me. I squinted in concentration. Channelling two streams were more than twice as taxing than just one. I frowned harder and split the stream in two again and two more casings joined the others in a lazy orbit. The runes inscribed on the outside of the crystal shells started glowing a bright blue as the recharge spells ignited. There were two more casings on the floor and I split off two more streams. My head started hurting almost instantly and my hands started trembling but the remaining two rose to join the slow dance of the others as they too started to recharge. Before long I had a splitting headache and I felt ready to throw up but I persevered. This was like physical training, the more I pushed myself the stronger I would become. I'd seen Kendall do this with two dozen shells at the same time without too much effort but I did not have that kind of focus. Not yet anyway. The charger, being more efficient than I was, finished quicker but I could not stop now, I had to see it through or the result would be unstable. At best the half-finished propellant and bullets would merely dissipate back into the magic they were formed of but at worst the result could be much more volatile. The edges of my vision was darkening when the runes on the casings winked out and the shells fell clattering to the floor as I relaxed my mind. I fell back and lay down on the cold rug and closed my eyes. The perspiration that covered my body soon had me shivering but the cold felt heavenly. The headache quickly abated but the sense of fatigue would linger. I reached up and lifted my left breast to scratch at a drop of sweat chafing in the fold between my breast and my ribs. Shit, I was not even thirty yet and they had already started to sag slightly. I guess that was the curse of having larger than average breasts. Gravity sure was a bitch. I may have dozed for a bit but eventually my growling belly forced me to my feet and over to the kitchen. Though calling it a kitchen was a bit of a stretch, it was more of an alcove in the main room that was also my bedroom. My apartment was one single room and a bathroom. I opened my fridge and scanned the meagre contents. I had some bread on the counter and a bit of leftover fungus. I sighed. Both the bread and fungus was equally tasteless and neither appealed to me right now but I forced down the sandwich I made. I would need the sustenance before the day was out. As I ate I pretended that it was an oat and ham sandwich like the ones I had heard of in the stories about the Old World. I could hardly believe that meat had been in abundance back in the day, that mankind had actually cultivated animals for the express purpose of killing them for their flesh. The legends said that a creature called a cow had been brought up to the Skylands when it was first formed but that there was nothing here that they could eat and they soon had gone extinct. The fungus was the only remnant of the old world and no one really knew how or why it managed to survive down in the tunnels of the Undercity. I washed the sandwich down with fresh water from the tap. At least the water was cool today. Sometimes only tepid water came from the tap when the cooling systems had a magic outage. Again I entertained the idea of moving to a better part of the Skylands. It would cost me all of the money I had saved up but real estate was in short supply, like most other things up here. I wished that I had been born a hundred years ago when the Skylands was smaller and the industry did not soak up almost all of the available magic from the Great Geyser. Back then everyone had had enough magic. I put on my choker and activated the spells embedded and my clothes started to form around my body, layer by layer. First came the thong and the bra, then the corset and the trousers and finally the coat. I slung my weapons belt around my hips and holstered my revolvers as the coat formed on my torso like a thin sleeve. I glanced into the polished crystal wall by the door and noted that my clothes were thick enough to preserve my modesty and I left my apartment. A faint whiff of magic blew over me as I left the wards built into the walls in my apartment. I had absorbed all of the magic inside to the degree that even the meagre magic field outside seemed like a thick cloud of power. I reached out as far as I could reach and pulled the magic inside and I perked up a little. It was almost nothing, but almost nothing was more than what I currently held. Glanced at my gauntlet and swore. I had to hurry if I was to make it in time for my mission and I rushed to the Skyway. I just barely caught the tram and it hurtled down below to the Undercity. I got a few curious glances by some of the other travellers, probably due to the half-formed state of my clothing. My coat had just started to grow its tail and looked rather lopsided. It had not formed its buttons yet and my corset was only at the stage of a waist cincher so my bra was proudly on display. I did not really care, I did not know any of these people and their opinions meant little to me. I reached up behind my head and started to braid my hair. I really needed to cut it, the purple curls were brushing the ends of my shoulder blades and I preferred it a bit shorter. My clothes finally manifested fully as I stepped off the Skyway and exited the station and entered the Undercity proper. The interior was lit dimly by sparsely placed glow globes with dark sections between. This was not a residential area, most of the caves down the sides of this thoroughfare led to one of the many fungus farms and most of the people around me were farmers but I could easily identify a few thugs. I stepped around a man lying in a growing pool of blood. Judging by the rate the pool was growing the man was dead, or soon would be. A boy ran toward me and leaped the corpse with practised ease without giving it a second glance and I patted my pockets out of habit to make sure he had not tried to steal anything from me, even though the pockets were empty. I ignored a beggar as I stepped through an open door and my ears were assaulted by loud conversation that echoed harshly against the bare crystal walls. I sat down by the bar as I had been instructed and ordered a beer with side of strong whiskey. The barman barely glanced at me as he plopped down a small crystal tumbler and sloshed clear liquid into it. He did not seem to care that he spilled all over the bar and he filled up a pint of the bluish liquid. The bitter tang of the beer mingled with the sharp odour of the strong spirit in my nostrils and I picked up my glasses. I had no intention of drinking any of this, not before a job. I sat down at the edge of the bar and put the glass of beer to my lips and pretended to drink as I glanced to my sides. I did not like sitting with my back to the room and I extended my mind to sense anyone approaching from behind. My depleted store of personal energies drained steadily as I scried my surroundings but it would be worth it if I did not get stabbed in the back. A man sat down next to me and leaned closer.

"Hello, Kyra."

I grinned without looking. "Hey, Greg. How you doing?"

"Can't complain. I guess I am here for the same reason that you are?" I finally turned my head to look at him. This day he had braided his thick blond hair into several stylish braids whose ends brushed the sleeveless vest he wore. Crystal encased his forearms and overlapping plates covered his chest. His blue eyes twinkled as he glanced at me and ordered the same kind of drinks I had.

"And what would that be?"

"Fucking escort duty. Do you reckon we will see any action?" I shrugged and I suppressed a grin as his eyes obediently dipped to watch the ripple in my cleavage the motion produced. Greg was a nice guy, as far as mercs go. More importantly, he was a skilled fighter. He could shoot worth a damn but it was the wickedly curved short sword that had earned him his reputation. The man was a whirlwind of death with it and combined with the shield projector on his gauntlet he could get close enough to use it.

"Possibly. If it was not likely they would not have hired two of us," I said with a weary tone.

He arched an eyebrow at me and thanked the barkeep. For a mercenary he had impeccable manners. He slammed down his shot and chased it down with a long draught of his beer. He wiped the foam from his lip with his forearm.

"Who are they?"

I shrugged again, putting some unnecessary jiggle into my boobs. I enjoyed tormenting him, knowing that he was too nice to try anything shady. I'd seen him run screaming into a group of hostiles and viciously carve them apart without flinching but faced with an attractive woman he became hilariously timid.

"Dunno. Stardust dealers most likely." I know what you think. Yesterday I had killed a bunch of Stardust dealers and helped destroy a major manufacturing plant and today I was protecting some of their ilk. Hypocrite much? Money was money though and I'd kill or protect about anyone for a large enough paycheck. There were those that claimed vehemently that all life was sacred but I was not one of them. Life was life and sometimes it ended. More often than not it ended at the hands of someone else who wanted what you had. That was just how life on the Skylands was. There were also those that claimed that life was much better Outside but those were fools. No one had ever been Outside, the Barrier would not allow it. I remember a few years back when a group of rich youths had constructed some sort of flying machine and set out on an expedition, believing that they could breach the Barrier from the inside. Half the Skylands had followed their progress, right up until they crashed into the Barrier and fell to a fiery death in the Great Geyser. Fucking idiots I say.

"You must be Kyra and Greg?" I turned around on my stool and was face to face with a nervous looking man. His eyes flickered, never staying in one place and he shifted his balance back and forth. His clothing was far too expensive for a place like this and I'd give him an hour or two before someone robbed him or worse.

"Yeah, what of it?" His eyes finally fixed on Greg and he drew himself up and squared his shoulder. Despite being shorter than Greg he managed to look down his nose at him.

"I hired you."

"Very well, and your name is?"

"It is not important. You may call me Ghost." I snorted. I bet he thought that was ominous. He glared at my sound of amusement as if I should recognise the moniker.

"Alright, 'Ghost'. What's the deal?" I put as much mockery into his name as I could. It deserved mockery, if anyone deserved such a nickname any less than him I could not think of anyone.

"Security. I have a business transaction scheduled and I need you to keep the peace." I rolled my eyes and shared a look with Greg. Ghost could dress it up as much as he wanted but no respectable business transaction would require two mercs nor would it take place in the Undercity. I nodded, I already knew that we would not get any useful intel from this guy and we would have to wing it. I stood up and looked at Greg. He held up his finger and lifted his mug to his mouth and drained it before he stood up.

"Alright, let's get going." He must have come to the same conclusion as I since he did not ask any further questions. He waved his hands in a "Lead the way" gesture and Ghost spun on his heel and set off for the exit. I dropped a few coins on the counter and Greg reached for his own wallet. I held up a hand.

"This round is on me."

"Thanks. You know that you are my favourite, right?" We hurried to catch up to Ghost.

"You say that to all the girls, I'm sure." At least he had the decency to look abashed.

"Well, yes. But I don't mean it unless I am talking to you." I knew he was lying through his teeth but even so the compliment warmed my heart. It was not often I was complimented and I cherished the moments when it happened.

"Thanks. That means a lot coming from such an upstanding citizen such as yourself."

Without breaking his stride he threw me an elaborate bow. We followed Ghost in silence for a few minutes before he led us into a side passage off the main thoroughfare. I tensed and saw Greg do the same beside me. These tunnels were always dangerous but I think that no would-be robbers would try anything with two mercs. There were far easier prey around. Ghost did not seem to take notice and I decided that he must be from a better part of the Skylands. I touched my gauntlet and set my armour to manifest fully, I had a feeling that I was going to need it. Ghost led us to a crossing of the caves and stopped in the middle.

"They will be here soon." Neither Greg or I deigned to answer, instead we searched the area. This was not a well trafficked crossing and we were alone. I sent out a quick mind-pulse but got no returns from either of the corridors. We were alone. I looked at Greg.

"You take up position down that corridor, you can flank them if they try anything."

"Sure thing." Ghost intervened.

"What? I want both of you here. Try to look intimidating." I sighed deeply.

"I'd rather have him on the flanks if this deal goes tits up."

"And I would rather have him close by than having him just slink away into the shadows if something does go wrong." Greg bristled at the insult and his hand closed around the hilt of his sword. I held up a hand to forestall him.

"Do as he says. I can't be arsed with this." I leaned against the wall and waited. Ghost seemed more and more agitated for each minute that stretched out and he jumped as the faint echo of footsteps reached us. They were coming from the right and I motioned for Greg to take up position on the other side of the crossing. We waited for several more minutes until a man emerged into the light of the glow globes. He looked each of us up and down before he shouted over his shoulder.

"It's clear. Two mercs and some poof." Ghost grimaced but did not offer any objections. Four more men emerged from the shadows. I waved at one of the mercs.

"Hey, Darius. Long time no see." Darius returned my wave.

"Kyra. Always a pleasure, though I much preferred your outfit the last time we met."

"You mean that time when I was naked and dancing on the tables?" He leered at my armoured form. Even though it covered me it was still shaped to my feminine form.

"Precisely. I was worried that you may have forgotten."

I laughed. "Stop with the false modesty, it does not suit you."

"Enough!" Ghost stepped forward to the man in the midst of the mercs, the one obviously in charge. "Do you have the merchandise?"

The man smiled. It was not a pleasant smile.

"Do you have the money?"

"Of course. I am a man of my word."

"Implying that I am not."

"Of course, you are Undercity scum but you have what I require."

"Insulting your trade partners may not be such a wise move."

"Are you threatening me?"

"Of course. You uppercity assholes are all untrustworthy." 

Ghost bristled and I sent him a glance in warning. He was not paying attention to me and I pushed off from the wall to be ready. If he kept provoking the drug runners this could get ugly. My heart started beating in anticipation of the fight. The other mercs carried firearms and various close quarters weapons but none was armoured. There were four of them though and only three of us and I was certain that Ghost would be useless in a fight. Unless he was a Mage, but then why would he even have hired us? Just for show?

"Do you have the stuff or not?"

"Show me the money."

"Show me the merchandise." The other man laughed, a deep sound from the belly.

"Looks like we have a standoff boys. And lady." He nodded in my direction. Was Ghost insane or just stupid? Just show them the money and get this deal done before it got ugly. Apparently Ghost had realised his mistake.

"Fine." He pulled out his wallet and pulled out a wad of bills that he held up for them to see. I groaned and the man seemed to share my reaction.

"What am I supposed to do with that?" 

Ghost frowned. "What? This is the sum we agreed on."

The man rubbed his face wearily.

"Those are high denomination, how are we supposed to use that down here?" Ghost frowned at him, not understanding. "Fuck it, we will make it work but if this relationship will continue you need to get in the game 'Ghost'. Low denomination bills is the name of the game down here. Do you need to take notes?"

"I'll manage." Ghost bit the words out through clenched teeth. The man waved and a fifth man entered from the darkness carrying a bag. He stepped up to Ghost and held up the bag and his hand to accept the money. I had to give it to Ghost, he did not step back. He placed the money in the proffered hand and accepted the bag. He set it on the crystal floor and opened the bag as the man handed the cash to his leader who started counting. Both men seemed satisfied.

"Well, Ghost, everything seems to be in order. See you next week, remember what I told you. I will make sure you are given directions in advance." He and his men melted into the shadows and Darius winked at me before he followed his boss. Ghost drew a relieved breath.

"Well, we are done here. Let's go. Carry this." Greg rolled his eyes but did not complain as he slung the bag over his shoulder. We left the way we came.

"Be wary, we are not home yet." 

"But the deal is done." Ghost protested. How had he even managed to set up this meeting while being this clueless?

"Yes, but they will try to take their money back."

"But we have a deal! Besides, they could have tried just back there. They had us outnumbered, something I will remedy the next time."

I could not believe I had to explain this to him.

"Yes, but then you would not have returned for more. Someone will try to rob us, and eventually the money would come back to them. The next time you meet they can claim plausible deniability. They did not renege on the deal, it is not their fault if you are stupid enough to get robbed afterwards." That shut him up and I kept my eyes and ears on alert. I tried to extend my senses but my store of personal energies were too depleted from my earlier exertions. We entered another crossing and something barrelled into me and I was sent stumbling into the opposite wall. I heard a grunt from my side as Greg was similarly assailed. I twisted in the grip of my attacker and felt a blow land on my helmet. My attacker cursed in pain as his hand bruised against the dense crystal. I managed to turn us around and ran him into the wall. The wind escaped him with a loud whoosh next to my ear and his grip weakened. I ripped my arm free and drew the large knife strapped across my lower back and stabbed it into his soft belly. His entire body stiffened as I bisected his kidney and I shifted my stance for more leverage. I pivoted my body and sawed his belly open. For good measure I stuck my free hand into the wound and pulled out the long pulsating ropes of his guts as I stepped back to let the fall wetly to the dark floor. He slid down the wall as he tried to gather up his entrails and I dismissed him and spun around to assess the situation. Greg had ditched the pack and was fencing with two men. Ghost rolled on the floor with another. I took a step to aid him, knowing that Greg could handle himself. A small figure dashed through the light of the glow globe and snatched up the bag and vanished down the side corridor.

"Motherfucker!" I launched into a sprint after the figure but could only just hear the retreating footsteps over the fight behind me. I dropped my knife and pulled my revolver, the large one. The figure I was chasing flashed through the light of a glow globe ahead and I shifted my feet to slide to a halt. Sparks flew around my heels as they dug into the crystal floor. I thumbed the selector on the side of the revolver and the cylinder chambered my selected shot. Each of the shots in the large revolver was individually enspelled and in the core of each bullet was nestled a small Powerstone. It was not a true Powerstone since it was not truly rechargeable but it did not need to be. It just needed to work the once. I raised the revolver in the general direction of the footsteps and fired. The spell in the bullet ignited immediately and the flare of the tracer almost blinded me. The shot went wide but I had not truly intended to hit the running figure. The flare illuminated the corridor and I got a better view. I lowered the revolver and fanned the hammer, slamming my palm against it and fired quickly. The various spells in the five shots whistled down the corridor. One burst in a blossom of flame that sent shrapnel ricocheting off the walls. One vanished harmlessly down the corridor, failing to trigger as it did not find flesh. One more joined that one but two found its target. I jogged to the fallen form as it slid into the view of a glow globe. I kicked the body over and winced. A small girl, thirteen years if but a day cried out in pain. Her lower hip had ruptured as the explosive shot struck her pelvis and her leg was attached with just a few tattered bits of skin and sinew. Eyes were wide with shock and pain and the blood pooling beneath her matched the colour of her curly hair. I swore. These bastards were using children for their dirty work! Her shirt had slid up on her torso to expose the pale skin of her belly and already the veins beneath the skin were darkening, spreading rapidly. The spell in the second shot that had struck her were already poisoning her blood, within moments her body would start liquefying from within. It was not a good way to die. I steeled my heart and raised my boot. I hesitated for a moment. I gritted my teeth and brought my boot down on her pretty little face with all my might. Her skull cracked with a sickening crunch and she went limp and most importantly; silent. I pulled my boot out with a wet sucking sound and avoided looking at her caved in face. I turned my back on her and snatched up the bag as I ran back to finish the fight. I holstered my revolver and drew the other one. I needn't have bothered, Greg had cut his two assailants apart and the number of wounds on their bodies astounded me. Ghost stood cradling a nasty cut to his face but his opponent lay stretched out with a knife through his temple. Ghost was not such a pussy after all. The man I had gutted still moaned and whimpered and I put a bullet through his brain. Any man sending children into a war zone did not deserve to live, even wounded as he was. I tossed the bag at Ghost who caught it and he stumbled under the unexpected weight.

"Carry your own damn bag." Greg looked at me curiously. I bit out the answer to his unspoken question.

"Little girl." His face hardened and fury flared in eyes. Greg loved children. The only thing he loved more than cutting people apart was his little daughter, especially after her mother had died. I stalked down the dark caves, not really caring if Ghost followed. I was sure that the Stardust dealers would not send more guys after us, not after this shit show. Ghost and Greg soon caught up with me and both of them were smart enough not to talk to me. This was not the first time I'd seen a dead child, but it was the first time I had killed one directly even though I had not known it was a child when I shot her. Had I known I would have let her go. At least I had been able to end her pain. Small mercies in a merciless world. I received my payment outside the tavern we had met Ghost and I counted it thoroughly. I had been prepared for him to try to undercut me but there were actually more than what we had agreed upon. I looked at him and he guessed my question.

"Consider it a tip, for a job well done. I hope that you will work with me again next week?" I really did not want to, but money was money and if the dealers saw me along next time then maybe they would not pull this shit again. Or maybe they would just send more men to ensure success. As long as they did not kill Ghost then they would not care if some mercs were caught in the crossfire.

"Yeah, sure. Same place?" He nodded and I left without a word. Greg soon caught up with me.

"You ok?"

"No."

"Wanna talk about it?"

"No."

"Alright. Come find me, if you do."

"Thanks, but don't count on it."

"Marissa would like to see you. It has been too long."

I almost smiled at the thought of his daughter but I was not in the mood. "Maybe later."

"She admires you, you know. You are the main reason she wants to become a merc."

That surprised me.

"Not you? She does not want to be like her father?" 

He chuckled. "No. I am just her silly dad. You are Kyra Zorantis, the proud warrior!"

"I don't feel so proud right now."

He grabbed my arm and spun me around to face him. "Don't blame yourself, you didn't know!"

"That does not make me feel any better. A little girl is dead, and I pulled the trigger. She'd been alive right now if it weren't for me!"

"Yes, she would've. For today. Tomorrow someone else might've killed her, or worse. You of all people know what it's like down here."

"Yes, she might have died tomorrow. Or been raped. Or she may have grown up, found a man and had children. She could have had a life but now she lies dead in the dark. Alone. Her mother will worry sick about her tonight before she realises that her little girl won't be coming home!" Tears were streaming down my face and I turned from Greg in shame once I noticed. I started walking again. Greg was wise enough not to say anything until I regained my composure. We entered the Skyway in silence and my tram rolled in. Greg squeezed my hand in sympathy as I stepped aboard. He would take the tram in the other direction. He lived with his daughter in the Undercity, right below the surface. It was a fairly safe area and he hoped that he could one day afford a place on the surface were she would be even safer.

"Take care, Kyra. Don't let this bring you down. Remember, you didn't know."

I ignored his words and sat down heavily on the floor of the tram. I barely held it together until I got home and collapsed on the floor in the hallway.

## Chapter 2

I had eventually managed to drag myself to my bed and passed out after disengaging my clothes and I woke up a cold shivering naked ball atop the covers. The image of my boot heel crushing that poor girls face assailed me but I was completely cried out. I had no more tears to shed for her. I sat up and rubbed my aching eyes and noted that my apartment was thick with magic. At least the magic provider had come back online. I could not really manage to care and I left for the bathroom. I splashed tepid water on my face. Of course, if the magic dispenser worked then the waterworks would be offline. I heard a sharp knock on my door before it opened an instant later. I groaned. Only two people had access to my apartment; mom and Kendall and mom would not have knocked. I was not in the mood for either of them.

"Kyra! I need your help. Kyra? You home?"

"Yeah, in the bathroom." I dried my face and he poked his head through the open door as I emerged from the damp cloth.

"You look like shit."

"Thanks."

"You OK?"

"No." I pushed him aside and sat down heavily on my bed. He struck a dapper figure, like always. Kendall was tall, blond and handsome and he always dressed to impress, no matter the occasion. Today he wore a tailored three-piece suit in varying shades of blue that complimented his bright azure eyes that was currently peering at me over his indigo tinted spectacles. He put the crystal head of his cane under my chin and tilted my face up to look at him. Not once did his eyes stray to roam over my naked body. Of course, it was not something he hadn't seen before. It was with his face between my legs that we both had discovered that he preferred men back when we were both teenagers. It had been a rather humiliating experience for me, especially when he sheepishly offered to finish me off with his mouth but I had declined. It did not feel right to force him to do something that his heart was not in.

"What happened?" His face was a picture of concern and I knew I could trust him. He knew most of the things that I had done and he still loved me. Tears welled up in my eyes as my vision blurred. I guess I had some tears left after all.

"I had a job. Standard escort for a drug deal."

"Stardust?" His face set in a disapproving expression. His brother had died of an overdose a couple of years back and ever since then he had been a staunch supporter of the war against drugs.

"Yeah. We were ambushed on the way back and someone snatched the bag. I did not see them but managed to shoot them in the darkness."

"And?"

"It was a little girl."

"Fuck. I hope you killed the ones who put her up to it."

"The men who attacked us yes, but their boss is still out there."

It pained me to kill an innocent, possibly another victim of Markus' but I had no choice. I jumped onto the bed and landed astride the still screaming Markus.

"Are you Markus?" He just kept screaming and I pistol whipped him and put the edge of my blade on his Adam's apple.

"Are you Markus?" He just stared at me with terrified eyes. I flipped the covers down and saw the scar on his shoulder. My knife turned his frightened screams into a wet gurgle as I sawed it down almost to the bone. He reached up to clutch at the blood but I batted his arms away until he let out a final breath and lay still. Someone would have heard the gunshots and called the Guard so I scrambled off the bed and holstered my weapons. I held out my hand and sent a tongue flame to ignite the bed. Another tongue of flame set fire to the kitchen and I closed the patio door behind me. The flames were spreading rapidly as I climbed the wall and jumped down on the other side. Luckily no one was on the streets and I was not forced to murder any witnesses as I hastened from the burning building. I heard the clatter of armour as the Guard approached and I ducked between to houses to let them pass. Two of the guardsmen wore the new powered armour and I drew a sigh of relief as they passed. Even in my own armour and with my weapons I was unsure if I could take out even one of the armoured men. Back when I was in the Guard we never had toys that awesome. My stint in law enforcement had been short, the corruption in the leadership and the poor pay had driven me to the mercenary life. A block from the Skyway I ripped off my bonnet and shimmied out of my dress and ditched them in an alley. Beneath I wore a tight tube bra and a very short skirt, just barely long enough to cover my weapons. I shook out my hair and tossed it about and smudged out my makeup and suddenly I had become a whore returning home from a visit with a wealthy client instead of a middle class lady wandering the streets at night. The Guard at the Skyway ogled my body with a complete lack of suspicion and I made a token proposition to reinforce my cover. He was one of the good ones and refused me with the excuse that he was on duty. At least he had the decency to look genuinely regretful. The Skyway deposited me near my home and I noted that I was not alone when I stepped through my door. Kendall sat in the dark on my bed, waiting. I kicked off my shoes in silence.

"Well?" His voice was hoarse.

"It is done." I could hear his relieved exhale in the darkness.

"And his client?"

"Was a Mage."

Kendall noted the past tense.

"Was?" "He put up a fight. I did not have a choice."

"Dear Gods, forgive me." It was a sign of his distress that he mentioned the Gods. For as long as I've known him Kendall had despised all of the religions. If the Gods existed, and that was a big 'if' then they had abandoned the Skylands centuries ago. I heard a strangled sob from the bed and I sat down next to him and let him fall into my embrace. We fell back onto the bed and Kendall buried his face in my bosom as his sobs reached heart wrenching levels. Before long my own tears welled over and dripped silently down my cheeks but it was not the dead Mage that filled my thoughts. It was a tiny red haired girl with a crushed face that stared at me accusingly with her one intact eye. It was hours before either of us slept.

## Chapter 4

The weeks dragged on but I was unable to chase the little girl from my thoughts, no matter how much I drank or how many men I dragged home to fuck me into oblivion. I joined Ghost for another Stardust deal but this time Darius was on our side. A token attempt to rob us on the way back was thwarted when Darius contemptuously cut down the lead man and the rest scattered. After that I helped Detective Ford with another raid. This one was much smaller than the first and there was hardly a fight. I did not even get to fire my pistols. Easiest money ever. It was on the way home from such a raid when the shit truly hit the fan. I was walking to the Skyway from the site, admiring the brilliant display of magic in the sky as heavy rain splashed and vaporised all over the Great Barrier. The blueish light cast from the myriad little detonations brightened the streets as if it was broad daylight, but in an ethereal flickering light. Such a heavy rainfall was rare and the streets were lined with people watching the display in awe. Then suddenly the barrier flashed brightly, blinding everyone who watched it. I blinked to clear my vision. What the hell had caused such an impact? I had just regained enough of my eyesight to see the crowd around me blinking stupidly when the Barrier flashed again and I was deafened by thunderous boom. Cold wetness splashed my face and I recoiled in surprise. My vision cleared into complete darkness. Had I gone blind? Terrified screams rang out on all sides and I was buffeted by panicked people. I braced my feet wide to remain standing but someone careened into me from behind and we tumbled to the ground. I kicked the person off of me and rolled to all fours. Someone stumbled over me and I fell on my side. Light flickered and I let out a relieved breath I had not realised I was holding. I was not blind after all. The air split by a deafening roar that stretched on and on. That had not been thunder, nor a human bellow. It sent a shiver of uncertainty down my spine. I had never heard such a sound before. The glow globes along the street slowly came back online, but dimly. I was soaked through by the heavy rain as I stood up and dodged a screaming woman who sprinted full tilt away from the direction the roar had come from. Then realisation struck me and I almost fainted from shock. It was raining. Not a single drop of rain had fallen on the surface of the Skylands in centuries. Certainly not in my lifetime. I retreated to the side of the street to avoid the throng of people and looked up to the skies. There was no sign of the Great Barrier that had dominated the sky all my life. There was nothing protecting us from the Outside! The roar returned, followed by muffled gunfire. A wave of people rounded the corner further up the road and collided with the crowd on the street and it quickly became a clusterfuck of tangled bodies. I saw several vanish below the sea of heads and I winced. Being trampled by a panicked mob was not a pretty way to die. At least it was somewhat swift. The gunfire intensified and I started pushing through the crowd. I kept to the outskirts or I would have been carried away by the torrent of panicked flesh but even in the fringes I was jostled by careless shoulders and elbows. I could see several other mercs and guardsmen shoving through the crowd in the direction of the gunfire. I activated my armour and was glad that it had not dissolved entirely yet from my recent fight. I was suddenly glad that I had not had the chance to use my guns in the raid for I had a creeping feeling that I would need all the ammunition I had before the night was done. It took forever, probably a quarter of an hour, to get to the corner where the wave of people had come from and I rounded it. I was almost bowled over as the crowd surged forward. Fuck this. I dove through the windows of the house to my side and rolled to my feet in a shower of crushed crystal. I found the stairs and dashed up them two steps at a time. This part of town, near the edge of the Skylands, did not have the dozens of stories tall buildings closer to the centre and sported one or two story houses. I opened a window on the second floor and poked my head outside. Excellent, the lip of the roof was in reach and I clambered up onto the roof. The roofs were flat to allow future expansions and I even saw some protrusions where the owner had started growing a third floor. The houses were packed tightly and I could easily make the leap onto the next house. I ran down the block and peeked over the edge down onto the street and for the first time beheld what the people were running from. I froze at the sight. Creatures, for I didn't know how to otherwise describe them, were crowding the street in double ranks, slashing at the people with claws and blades. Behind them the street were littered with corpses. I sensed the magic before I saw it and an explosion tore a dozen of the tightly packed people apart. The end of the crowd collapsed as the creatures flowed gracefully into the gaps created by the blast and started cutting people down. A flash of lightning from above illuminated the attackers clearly for the first time and that was a vision I will never forget. They were humanoid in the sense that they had one head, two arms and two legs but there all similarities ended. Their hides were a grayish green and covered in thick scales. Their faces were elongated, lipless snouts with flickering cloven tongues. They walked hunched over, keeping their balance with a thick tail and along their backs looked like what was neatly folded wings. They moved with a feral grace and animal cunning but their teamwork was intelligent. I sensed the magic again and instead of watching the carnage I found the source. It was a figure in long dark robes that was not as brutish as the others. As it lifted it's hands I saw that they were pink and fleshy like my own and lacked the claws of its companions. The amount of power he put out into the spell was astonishing. I would have passed out of exhaustion if I had cast a spell like that directly from my personal energies but he did not even stumble. Three guardsmen and five mercs pushed out of the crowd and quickly established a front line. The creatures may look terrifying, and was probably stronger than a human due to sheer mass but they did not seem to be much faster. The mercs and the guard fought them to a standstill. One of the mercs went down but two more and a third guard joined them from the crowd. I sensed the buildup of magic again and realised that the enemy Mage would blast them apart. I rose and stepped off the edge of the house. I spent some of my personal energies to halt my fall and landed lightly on my feet and pulled my pistol. I launched into a sprint toward the Mage and thumbed the selector on my revolver and felt more than I heard the cylinder spin to chamber the round I had selected. It was the same kind of bullet that I had used on Markus' lover. The Mage saw me and redirected his spell in the last possible second and death soared toward me. I dove headlong to the side and I could feel the crackling static arc across my armour. I rolled on my shoulder into a combat crouch and brought my pistol up. I fired once and smiled darkly as the shot rippled across his shield and tore it apart. It was an expensive shot, and the only one I had currently loaded in my pistol. My second shot struck him squarely in the chest and he slowly sank to a knee. He was already dead, though his body did not yet know it. It was the same poisoned bullet I had used on the little red haired girl. I rushed to the kneeling Mage to make sure that he would not do any final shenanigans. His cowl had fallen back and I was surprised at his youth. He could not have been older than me and he was very handsome. The scar that bisected his right eye and continued beneath was almost identical to my own but his eye was, unlike mine, milky white. He snarled something at me but it came out as a wet gurgle as he dribbled a foul black goo down the front of his robes. I pulled my other revolver, the one loaded with cheaper kinetic rounds, with my left hand and shot him through the head. I holstered my large pistol and drew my sword as I turned to the battle and charged the creatures from behind. It was a risky move, if they turned I would be outnumbered but if they didn't I would be able to strike them from behind. They had apparently not heard my gunshots, or not understood what they meant for they did not carry firearms of their own, and I stabbed the first one between its wings. My angle was good and the sharp point pierced the light armour it wore and cut through its scales. It hissed in pain and fell forward. I shot the one on the left in the back point blank and as it stumbled the merc fighting it chopped it down with his axe. I killed two more with my sword before one of them noticed me and drew back from the fight to attack me. It swiped at me with its blade and I revised my earlier opinion. They were faster than humans, but not particularly skilled with its weapon. It telegraphed its intention all the way from its shoulders and I deflected it easily. A textbook riposte that would have had any experienced merc bat it aside with a laugh caught it in its snarling maw and it dropped as I severed its spinal cord. I pulled my blade free and searched for a new opponent. I found none and realised that my unexpected arrival had turned the tide and the few creatures that remained bounded away on all fours. It was a strange sight to behold. I sensed magic from above and threw myself to the side but was flung violently against the side of the building by the shock wave of an intense explosion. My armour saved me from any wounds but I was dazed and felt my entire back slowly starting to turn into a large bruise. I rolled onto my back and saw a dark shape glide away over the rooftops. The others had not been so lucky. Two forms lay burning on the street and one of the guards sat cradling his severed leg. Two of the mercs pushed to their feet and staggered. I sensed magic all around in the distance and the roar of explosions was a constant reminder that a battle raged throughout the city. Another of the titanic roars echoed down the streets. The creature making that roar must be large beyond comprehension. One of the other mercs offered his hand and I accepted his help to my feet. I found my pistol and sword on the ground nearby and I returned them to my hands on streamers of magic. He pointed at the fallen Mage.

"What happened to that guy?"

"Killed him."

He eyed me appreciatively. "Impressive. He was quite powerful."

I nodded in agreement. At the end of the day Mages were human and I had gotten the drop on him. I may not have been so lucky had he seen me coming. I decided to change the subject, pleasant as his flattery was. I squatted by one of the dead creatures and lifted a sprawled wing.

"What are these things?"

The man shrugged. "Beats me. But they die if you poke holes in them. Wanna find some more?"

The sounds of fighting reached us as if to punctuate his words and we set off in a jog. It was difficult to make a way through the mess of mangled corpses and I stumbled and almost fell more than once. Another loud roar thundered across the town and the increasing frequency of the roars worried me. We rounded a corner and I came to a skidding halt. Several of the creatures were fighting a single man and I recognised Greg with a lurch in my stomach. He was pushed into a corner with no means of escape. The fighting shifted and I saw two children and a woman huddled behind the ferocious mercenary. The woman had an expression of pure panic on her face but even so she clutched a small knife in case one of the creatures got past Greg. The blond mans' wicked blade was a blur but he was too hard pressed to attack and was forced into a purely defencive pattern. With a howl I unloaded my revolver and two of the creatures went down hard with blood gouting from holes in their backs. One of my shots went wide and grazed Greg's arm and he recoiled in pain. One of the creatures spun to face me and Greg stabbed it in the back. The kill left him overextended and one of the other creatures raked his side with its claws. I dove into it and stabbed it between the wings as one of my companions killed the last one from behind. Greg winced as he examined his wounds and clamped a hand on his grazed shoulder. Even over the distant gunfire I heard the sizzle of cooking flesh as he used his limited magic to cauterise the wound. He did the same with the claw wounds on his side before he addressed me.

"Thanks, Kyra. You really saved us here."

"Don't mention it. Who are the civvies?"

He shrugged. "Dunno, found 'em a while ago being chased by these assholes." He indicated the dead creatures. I looked over his shoulder at the frightened woman.

"Go back that way, the way is clear for now and if you hurry you can get to safety. Greg, you should go with them and make sure they are safe." I wanted him out harms way what with him being wounded and all.

"Fuck that. I ain't backing out of a fight. Not when we are invaded from Outside."

I chill crept down my back at his words. I had not reflected over the implications of the sudden appearance of these creatures. There were people, and other creatures, Outside! What we had been taught our entire lives had been wrong. We had been taught that the world had been destroyed centuries ago by Wild Magic but that had obviously not been the whole truth. I forced the unsettling thought aside. We had more pressing matters to attend to.

"Can you keep up?" I indicated his wounds.

"Bah, these scratches? I'll be fighting far after you drop of exhaustion, girl."

I scoffed, he was not that much older than me. Without offering a retort I led the way down the street to in the direction of the sounds of battle. A group of musketeers joined us and together we formed ranks across the street. A faint whispering made me tilt my head to try to figure out what the source could be. A snapping sound startled me and I threw a glance behind me. A large group of creatures had landed behind us and folded their wings to make room for their fellows still falling from the sky.

"Behind us! Form ranks!" The musketeers were good and calmly turned. The first rank knelt and as one they shouldered their muskets. The creatures formed a loose mob and charged us. They were well within optimal range but no one shouted the order to fire. I glanced to either side and realised that their sergeant must have fallen and no one had stepped up to assume command.

"First rank, fire!" I was surprised to hear my own voice call the order but my thoughts was drowned by the gunfire. Purple smoke belched from the muzzles of the muskets and partly obscured the creatures. I could see their entire front rank cut down and I waited a moment to let their bodies fall.

"Second rank, fire!" Again the leaders of the mob were mowed down. The creatures showed no hesitation and they nimbly leaped the bodies of their fallen.

"Fire at will!" The final rank fired and I cursed as I realised that the musketeers had not mounted their bayonets. There was no time and I shouted with all the strength and confidence I could muster.

"Charge!" I put my words into action and launched into a sprint toward the rapidly approaching monsters and I hoped that the musketeers would join me. If they didn't I would most like die. I was only a few steps from the leading three monsters and they snarled and hissed at me as they drooled through their snouts. I raised my pistol and shot the two to the sides and the leader glanced at them. If these creatures were capable of having expressions I would have guessed that it was startled at the sudden loss of his flankers and I easily skewered him with my sword. Our momentum brought its dying body careening into me and we went down hard. So this is how it ends. I was pinned beneath the heavy body and it snarled and snapped its jaws at me before the light went out of its eyes. Another of its kin towered above me and raised its blade to stab it into the eye slits of my helmet. Greg shot past above me in a daring leap and blood gouted from the creatures opened throat as his blade bit deep. The creature stumbled back and fell and suddenly there were men all around me. They reversed their muskets and used them as clubs, bashing heads and cracking ribs. I used the respite to calm my mind and I heaved the body pinning me aside with my magic. I pushed to my feet to assess the situation. The men had it under control, outnumbering the remaining creatures two or three to one. One musketeer would distract a monster while the other two clubbed them to death. Then the third rank joined the fray and I noted approvingly that they had fixed their bayonets. I saw one man shoot a monster through the head point blank and I realised that they had reloaded. They were certainly well trained to have manged to do that in such a short time. Before I could rejoin the fight it was over and a cheer erupted from the throats of the men. I did a double take, I had not led this many men into the charge. More must have joined us during the short fight. I raised my sword in the air and the men quieted.

"Reload and form up. There are more of these bastards to kill!"

Again they cheered and set to reload at an astonishing rate. These guys were good and for the first time I noted their uniforms. These were the elite musketeers, men who were on their way to the special forces. They were lightly armoured over their coats and carried sabres in addition to their muskets. In a few short moments they had formed into a column six man broad and fifteen deep. Greg joined me at the head of the column as we set off at an easy jog. We ran onto a large square near the edge of the Skylands and staggered to a stop. We had found the source of the roar and my mind recoiled from the sight. It was large, my guess had been correct. It was a creature straight out of legend. The dragon was large and on its back stood a dozen robed figures flinging death and destruction from their blazing hands. A large group of creatures were pushing a line of the special forces back but their massed semi-automatic fire kept them at bay. The magic was an entirely different story and groups of men died with each blast the Mages on the dragon threw. I picked out several Mages on the ground but they seemed occupied with more defencive spellwork. Even as I watched the hail of shots from the special forces were stopped in the air in front of the winged monsters. They were erecting a barrier to let their winged allies to close with the riflemen. My group had not yet been detected but it could only be a matter of time. I looked around and saw a lot of worried faces. Some were slowly backing away. The dragon roared again and I clutched my head. How did the Mages on its back stand the sound? The roar slowly faded away and I saw a handful of my men run away the way we had come.

"Form ranks! Ready your weapons!" Training kicked in and the musketeers formed three ranks of fire.

"Advance!" We marched in a line toward the backs of the creatures advancing on the special guard. I squinted at the dragon and the air blazed up around it as I found my magesense. Cold realisation struck me at what I saw. Blazing tendrils of power flowed from the dragon to the Mages, and the beast itself shone like the sun. It was so full of magic that it was beyond comprehension. It must have been enough power to destroy most of the Skylands in a single blow. Why hadn't it? I pushed the question aside as we entered range of the muskets.

"Shoulder arms!" I barely waited for the men to comply before I gave the order to fire and we scythed down the rear ranks of the monsters. I watched with grim satisfaction as several of the Mages went down. They had focused their shields forward and had not expected an attack in the flank. The barrier failed in a spectacular shower of magical sparks and the special forces renewed their attack. I saw the start of their charge when the world exploded. I was thrown rolling across the cobbles but my armour kept my bones intact. My clothes beneath caught fire and I screamed in pain as my skin burned. I rolled to a stop and tried to focus through the ringing in my ears and the pain where my armour left me exposed. I pulled my shield close to my body and made it airtight. The flames winked out when they consumed the air on the inside of my skin before they could burn me too badly and I returned my shield to its normal state and drew a relieved breath. I opened my eyes and saw only a vast, scaled belly above me. The dragon had joined the fray. It stood over me as it swiped and bit at my musketeers. Something struck me as odd, straps and buckles criss crossed the belly of the beast. A harness? Then my jostled brain made the connection. Of course, the Mages needed something to hold onto when the dragon moved or they would have been thrown off it. A wild cackle escaped my lips as I pushed up to a crouch beneath the monster. It was not large enough for me to stand upright under it but I fit if I squatted. I ignited one of the enchantments on my sword and cut through several of the straps. I scored the scales underneath but did not draw blood. That was not my intention. I squat-ran down the length of the dragon and cut through the straps easily thanks to my enchantment. Then I did something incredibly stupid, but in the midst of the bloodlust and shell-shock I thought it was a grand idea. I sheathed my sword and grabbed the harness by the dragons hind leg. I pulled myself onto its side and was almost thrown off when it leaped toward the special forces. They fired and I prepared to feel the bite of bullets when a stray shot found me but nothing happened. I glanced over my shoulder and saw a shimmering barrier a few yards away. The Mages was shielding their mount. I clambered up onto its back and luck was with me that day. None of the Mages faced the rear of the dragon. It was difficult keeping my footing on the bucking beast but I managed with just a few stumbles. I drew my large revolver, I had dropped the small one in the blast, and cocked the hammer. I thumbed a shield breaker into the chamber and aimed at the Mage standing right below the neck of the dragon, the Mage I guessed was the leader due to his position on the beast. I supposed that the Mages would not shield themselves personally since the larger shield around the dragon would protect them as well but I did not want to take any chances. I fired and the shot punched in between his shoulder blades. He pitched over the dragons shoulder. Any sound he made was drowned by the dragons agonised roar. The beast reared onto its hind legs and the Mages snatched at the harness. I barely managed to do the same and kept my footing. The Mage closest to me looked over her shoulder and her eyes widened as she spotted me. She let go of the harness with one hand, summoning a burning ball of blue fire. I had fallen on my shoulder and my revolver was partly pinned beneath my ribs but I managed to wrench it into line and open up. The shot took her in the head and as her skull emptied the spell in her hand misfired and devoured half of her body. She rolled limply down the great beasts ribs and it roared again in pain. Did it feel pain when one of its Mages died? The barrier failed as the Mages were jostled around and I felt the loose harness start to slide. The beast stabilised as it snatched a soldier into its great jaws and mangled his body. I pushed to my feet and saw out of the corner of my eyes a familiar face charge to cut at the foreleg of the beast.

"Greg, no!" The words had barely left my lips before one of the remaining Mages flung a bolt of flame at him. Greg threw up his arms in a cross in front of himself and shield sprang up before him. The flame pushed him back and I saw an expression of strain on his face a second before his shield failed and he vanished into the fire. A cry of denial was torn from my lips. Rage boiled through me and I shot a dazed Mage clinging desperately to the harness. Two steps across the slick scales brought me within range of the Mage that had slain Greg and I thrust my blade through her back. I watched in grim satisfaction at the tip of my blade that protruded from between her breasts. I put my shoulder on her back and pushed her off the dragon. A fireball struck my shoulder and I fell off the dragon, burning again for the second time in mere minutes. As I fell I drew a bead on the Mage and I shot twice. By pure chance my first shot was my sole remaining shield breaker and it shattered the shield he had erected around himself. The second round was explosive and his chest burst apart in a shower of gore. The dragon bucked and roared and the harness slipped off its body, dumping the remaining Mages onto the square. Thunder struck as the remaining soldiers fired and I could hear the myriad impacts of the shots on the dragon with wet plops. It sidestepped away from the soldiers, unfortunately in my direction. Its paw almost trampled me, instead a long claw pierced my thigh. My scream was drowned out by another volley and the beast retreated further. Without its creatures or its Mages it was taking a pounding. Why didn't it use its magic? It stepped over me and I was showered in a rain of thick blood. The side that had faced the soldiers was covered in tiny wounds from the shots but the sheer mass of holes was astonishing. It coiled and spread it wings and I saw a multitude of holes appear in the fleshy membranes as a volley thundered out. With bunching muscles the dragon launched into the air and was swiftly swallowed by the darkness. I fought my darkening vision, using the last of my magic to cauterise the deep wound in my thigh. Then I surrendered to the darkness.

## Chapter 5

I awoke slowly and found myself comfortably nestled in soft sheets. My thigh ached dully and patches of my skin itched horribly. Without opening my eyes I reached over to scratch at the itching skin and I heard a sharp intake of breath as I moved.

"Kyra?" I recognised the voice instantly.

"Kendall?" My voice was a weak murmur and I forced my eyes to open. He leaned closer and dug my hand out from beneath the sheet and clasped it to his mouth.

"I was worried that you would never wake up." His blue eyes brimmed with tears and they spilled over to vanish into his stubble. Stubble? He had been clean shaven last I saw him the day before last, no way did his beard grow this quickly. How long had I been out?

"I'm not hurt that bad. I've had worse." It was true, a stab in the leg and a few burns were far from the worst injuries I have lived through. He stared at me with open mouth.

"You have been unconscious for four days, we thought you would die of magical exhaustion!"

I frowned, sure I had spent much, if not most, of my personal energies during the fight but it should not have been enough to kill me. You needed to do something extraordinarily powerful in a single go to rip the life out of your body or else you would simply pass out way before the spell actually killed you. Unless you bound yourself to the spell and it sucked you dry as you lay helpless. I had done no such thing. The last thing I had done was a simple cauterisation.

"Kyra, listen. The Dragonkin, they drink magic. You should have seen the square where the dragon was, it had absorbed the ground itself. It dissolved the crystal and ate the magic! You stood on its back and let it drain you!"

"What? No! I saw the dragon channel power into its Mages, it did not drain them."

"Yes. No. You don't understand. It drank the power from the space around it and gave it to the Mages. The Dragonkin themselves seemed to be unable to use the magic but they could gift it to the Mages."

"That would explain their endurance."

He nodded slowly.

"Our current guess is that they came to feed on the Great Geyser and found us absorbing all of its power. I shudder at the thought at what would have happened if it had simply hovered in the Geyser."

My eyes widened at the implication. "Could it have starved us of magic?"

The realisation was staggering. If something blocked the vast beam of magic erupting from the earth far below then the whole Skylands would wall into the sea. Our monolithic city balanced on the top of the ray. The magic sustained us and formed all of the matter around us, but for the first time in my life I realised that we were terminally dependent on it. If it wavered we would all fall to watery graves. Of course, that had been fine as long as we thought that we were alone in the world and the Outside was a chaotic wasteland filled with dangerous Wild Magic but that seemed to no longer be true. Perhaps it had never been. I flexed my leg and winced at the sharp stab of pain. Kendall immediately started fussing over me.

"Are you in pain? Shall I get a nurse?"

I shook my head.

"Nah, just testing the wound. It should hurt much more than this after only a few days. Your doing?" I arched an eyebrow at him. He smiled smugly.

"Yes. I made sure they gave you the same care they would have for me." His face fell. "They left many to die on the streets."

I nodded slowly. I had expected to be left as well. Resources went to the powerful and the Guard, us mercs were expendable.

"I am amazed that you managed to pull that off. I am counted amongst the lowest of the low, despite how useful mercenaries have proved to be."

His lips curled into a tiny smile.

"They did not really have a choice."

"What?"

"You are famous now! You are all over the news."

"What?!" I cringed at the surprised whine in my voice. I had never strived for fame, I preferred to live in the shadows.

"Kyra, you climbed a dragon and fought the Mages on top of it, not only that you killed most of them and disabled the rest. You practically saved the city."

"But there were hundreds of Guards there!"

"And they were getting slaughtered. You turned the tide with your foolish antics. They call you Dragonbane now." His eyes held a mix of amusement and awe and the latter gave me a sinking feeling in my stomach. I never wanted my friends to look at me like that. I was just Kyra, a piece of shit murderer. Not a bloody hero! I killed a fucking child not too long ago!

"Don't, " his voice was soft but firm, "I know that look. Just don't."

I squeezed the hand he still had wrapped around mine but I still could not believe it.

"Hang on." He hurried from the room and returned a few moments later clutching a large green crystal in his fist. He frowned at it a moment and it blazed into light as he channelled power into it. A hololithic view projected into the air above it. It was a clever illusion and I noticed immediately it had been enhanced by whoever had created it. It had been much darker the day of the battle. I watched the dragon leap through the air and glide on its huge wings to slam into the ranks of musketeers I had led onto the square and I barely saw myself roll to a stop beneath it. As I started climbing the dragon a voice chimed from the crystal.

"The invasion by the creatures known as the Dragonkin were thwarted here by the hero Dragonbane who climbed the back of the dragon and killed the Mages wreaking havoc on our proud Guard and special forces." I saw Greg get killed again and my vision blurred as tears came unbidden to my eyes. The reporter did not even mention his heroic sacrifice as she carried on. "The hero was later identified as the mercenary Kyra Zorantis and her wounds are treated at an undisclosed location. I am sure we will hear more from her when she has recovered. We do know that her wounds are not life threatening, but she was severely drained by the dragon's aura." I was faced with a perfect image of myself, first a closeup of my face and then a full body image where I struck a silly pose, aiming with my revolver at someone behind the imager and brandishing my sword behind my head in a move that would have gotten me killed in an actual fight. These images had been taken at my registration as an official mercenary, for identification purposes. The footage of me on the back of the dragon replayed and I refused to look away as Greg died again in my minds eye. I closed my eyes as Kendall cut off the power to the crystal. A sudden realisation struck me and my eyes snapped back open.

"Marissa! Have anyone checked on her?"

Kendall was confused.

"Marissa? Who's that?" I groaned.

"Greg's daughter!"

"Who's Greg?" 

My eyes welled up again.

"The mercenary that was killed in the vid, the one that charged the dragon. He was my friend."

Kendall reached out to stroked my hair and I leaned my head into his palm.

"I'm sorry, Kyra. I didn't know."

"You couldn't have. His wife died years ago and his daughter is all alone. I need to check on her."

"You are in no state to leave right now."

"Fuck that!" I snapped at him. "I've fought in worse condition. Now that I am not drained of all magic I'll be fine." I sat up and realised that I was naked as the sheet fell down to my waist.

"Where are my clothes?"

"No. Listen to me, Kyra. You stay here, tell me where Greg lived and I will go look for Marissa."

"No. I need to do this myself. I owe that much to Greg. He died because of me."

"Don't do this to yourself, Kyra. He died in defence of the Skylands, it was heroic and noble and not at all your fault."

"No. You are wrong. He came to aid me. If I had not been foolish enough to climb that dragon he would have stayed back. He would not risk his life like that, Marissa needs him too much. No, he died because of me."

"For fuck sake, Kyra, if you had not climbed that dragon we don't know what would happen. You did the right thing. Foolish, but right."

"And now Greg is dead!" I had not meant to shout but I could not control my voice. Tears were streaming freely down my face now. Kendall watched me in silence for a long while before he reluctantly drew my choker from his pocket and handed it to me. I snapped it on and felt it constrict my throat comfortingly. I activated it and stood up and staggered as my wounded leg took my weight. Kendall was immediately by my side to support me but I shrugged him off. I carefully put my weight back on my leg and I felt something tear inside. I hoped the stitches or staples would hold but I could not see them underneath the dark bandage wrapped tightly around my thigh. I gave myself a cursory inspection. Most of my body had been protected by my armour but I was still severely bruised and the inside of my right arm and the back of my legs were burned. It didn't look too bad and I would be fine. At least I assumed so since the burns were not dressed. I touched the Powerstone on the front of my choker and commanded it to dress me as swiftly as possible.

"Where are my weapons?"

"I left them at your place, they would not take them inside the hospital. Policy."

I had expected that. I did not like the thought of going out there unarmed but I would have to make do. At least I had my personal magic to rely on. While I waited for my clothes to manifest I raised my hand and tried to form a small ball of fire but instead my vision darkened and I staggered. Kendall caught me and I hissed through my teeth as the cloth of his shirt rubbed against the raw skin of my burns.

"Don't. You won't be able to use magic for some time. You need rest to recover."

"I've been sleeping for days."

He gave me a glare in admonishment but kept his mouth shut. He knew me well enough to not waste his breath when I was being stubborn. Before long my choker had clothed me enough to walk outside. It had dressed me in a thin, skintight garment that clung to every curve. I may as well have been naked but it would suffice for now until the rest of my clothing had formed. I started for the door.

"Do you want me to come with?"

"No, I need to do this on my own. But thank you. For everything."

I left him there and I felt like an ungrateful ass but I would have to make it up to him later. Marissa was more important right now, she had been alone for several days and I was unsure if she was able to feed herself without Greg. Surely she could make a sandwich or something but I had no idea how much food Greg kept at his house. Certainly enough for Marissa to eat if for a day or two if he was held up but it had been more than that by now. I dodged several nurses on the way out, I did not have the time to argue with them. Undoubtedly they would try to keep me here longer. It would not do to let the great hero out too early and have her collapse on the street. I did not really care about them, Marissa was foremost on my mind. Fortunately the street outside the hospital was sparsely trafficked and I made my way to the Skyway. My knees felt weak and I sat down in one of the seats. Several people on the tram looked at me strangely but I was almost at my stop before someone recognised me.

"Hey, it's the Dragonbane!" Before I knew it I was mobbed by people, thanking me and trying to touch me. I lost count of the number of hands that thumped me on on the back or shook my hand or squeezed my shoulder. One daring hand even squeezed my boob and I lost my temper. I pushed through the crowd and dove out of the open tram doors onto the platform. The door closed before the mob realised and I hurried from the station. Even though the crowd had been friendly being surrounded by people while being unarmed stressed me out. Luckily I reached Greg's home without further incident and the lift brought me up to his floor. I steeled myself for a long minute before I put my hand on the crystal embedded beside the door. A chime sounded from inside and I waited tensely for a long while. Eventually a small voice reached me through the door.

"Who is it?"

Good girl, don't open the door before making sure.

"It's Kyra." I heard rustling as she disengaged the locks and pulled the door open a crack. A blue eye stared out through the crack and she pulled the door open wide when she saw that I was alone. She stared up at me with wide eyes. She had the looks of her mother, or at least I assumed so since she did not look at all like Greg. She had pale skin and a mane of black hair. The only feature she had inherited from Greg was his piercing blue eyes. They were slowly filling with tears and her lower lip was quivering. I knelt down and held out my arms and she flung herself into my embrace. We clung to each other for a long while before she finally spoke.

"Dad's not coming home, is he?"

Her tiny voice finally unmade me and I sobbed into her hair.

"No."

The small body in my arms started to shake with silent sobs. I could tell that she was trying her hardest to not cry, to be strong like daddy had taught her. It broke my heart all over again. An eleven year old should not have to be strong when she had just lost her only remaining parent. Eventually our sobs subsided and I pushed her to arms length.

"Are you hungry?" She shook her head as tears continued to drip down her face. I could tell that she was lying.

"When did you last eat?" She shrugged one shoulder.

"You need to eat. Your father would not want you to starve yourself. Come on, pack your things."

"Are we leaving?"

"Yes. You can't stay here on your own."

"Where?"

Her question left me stumped. I supposed that she could live with me, but my apartment would be cramped. It couldn't be helped.

"My place, then we will see."

She nodded and dashed into the apartment. What a trooper. As I waited for her to get ready I went to the fridge and opened it. As I had expected it was almost empty except for some beer. Luckily Marissa had not drunk it, it would fill her up for a while but it was way too strong for someone of her moderate size. I claimed it for myself and popped the cap by putting it against the edge of the counter and slamming my palm on top of it. I drained half of the beer in one go and suddenly realised how thirsty I was. I had not drunk nor eaten in days. I returned to the main room and saw Marissa stuffing the last of her things into a case. Greg had not been wealthy and they did not own much between them. She had more things than Greg had, despite being poor he had not been able to say no to his girl. He had loved her more than anything. I welled up again and forced myself to swallow the tears. Marissa needed me to be strong for her. I drained the beer and left the bottle on the table and picked up her case. It was not heavy, containing mostly clothes. I found an extra one-shot pistol and quickly loaded it before I tucked it into my newly formed belt. A large knife from the kitchen joined it and I instantly felt better with some weapons on my person. I held out my hand and Marissa put her tiny paw in it and we left her old life behind forever.

## Chapter 6

I rang the bell and pushed the door open. I had been recognised on my way here several times but either my dark glare or Marissa's tear streaked face warded off any harassment and we had arrived here without incident. We stepped into the hall.

"Mom?" I heard a surprised yelp and then my mother ran into the hall. She pulled me into her arms.

"Oh, my baby! When did you wake up?"

"Earlier today."

She refused to let me go for a long while until she noticed Marissa. She knelt on the floor.

"Who's this?" She dabbed at her eyes with her sleeve as she tried to smile at the young girl.

"This is Marissa. Her father was a friend of mine." Mom looked at me sharply as she noted the past tense but she did not offer any comment. She had noted Marissa's large eyes watering up.

"You two must be hungry, come and let me feed you."

In short order she had us seated by the kitchen table and she was frying up fungus for us. She absolutely refused to let me help, instead I sat clutching Marissa's hand. It seemed that she had run out of tears but her silence worried me. She had had always been a talkative child, always pestering me and Greg about stories of our fights. I hoped that time would return her to her normal self but I knew how losing a parent changed you. I sure as hell had changed when dad was killed. Mom cooked in silence, visibly trying to not express her relief of my recovery for Marissa's sake. She plopped plates of steaming fungus in front of each of us before she sat down and clutched my hand.

"Mom?"

"Yes, dear?"

"I kinda need that hand to eat." She released my hand immediately.

"Oh, I'm sorry." I forced a smile at her and then a sudden pang of hunger in my belly forced me to focus on the food. The fungus that had comprised every meal of my life was bland and tasteless but mom had always managed to make it palatable and this particular dish was one of my childhood favourites. Even so the sight of Marissa eating it mechanically made it tasteless in my mouth. Even so I ate it, if not only to make the hole in my belly disappear. Despite the excellent cooking the food sat like a weight in my belly. My mother surprised me with her words.

"I'm sorry."
