"What for?" She turned her gaze down onto her hands.

"I was not there when you woke up. Kendall sent me home to get some rest." I reached out and grabbed her bony hand. She was looking very frail these days.

"It's OK. I did not stay long after I woke up. I had to take care of business." I glanced meaningfully at Marissa who was gulping down water with both her hands cradling the large glass. Mom nodded, I knew she would approve of my priorities.

"What are you going to do now?"

"I don't know. I guess she will live with me."

"Nonsense! Your old room is still here you know, she can stay there."

"You don't have to do this."

"It would be nice to have someone around, the place have felt awfully large for just an old woman."

"You are not that old, mom."

"I know, but I feel old." A sudden yawn made my jaws crack and my mother stared at me.

"You need your rest, young lady. You will stay here tonight, now off you go. Go lie down." 

I wanted to protest but instead I blurted out "Yes, mother," and walked off to my old room. I didn't bother dissolving my clothes, I would wear them tomorrow after all and I dropped them on the floor in a heap. It didn't feel right sleeping naked in my old bed like I did nowadays so I rummaged through my closet and found one of my old nightgowns. What had once been a loose garment on me was now almost painfully tight and I had to squish my tits severely to get them in place. The hem barely reached mid thigh but it would have to do. I climbed beneath the sheets but the soft pitter patter of small feet made me open my eyes again. Marissa nestled in beside me and I held her as she silently cried herself to sleep. I had no more tears to shed with her and soon after her breath calmed into the deep breaths of sleep did I follow.

## Chapter 7

A little over a month later found me sitting alone in a bar. Technically I was not alone, the bar was quite crowded, but I had no one accompanying me specifically. One of the few perks with my new hero status was that I rarely paid for my own drinks anymore and I had been abusing that privilege tonight. I was on my way to pass-out drunk and I was determined to reach that point. Perhaps then I would be able to sleep without dreaming. My dreams kept returning to that night when the Dragonkin invaded, to the blood soaked streets and the mangled corpses. It was a sight I had seen countless times before after other battles but something with this particular one had stuck with me. I did not know if it was because foreign monsters had invaded what I had grown up thinking was an inviolably safe place. Safe at least from outside invaders. There were more than enough people on the inside that was far from safe. It may also have been that for the first time I had found myself in command, and my troops had been slaughtered as a direct consequence of my orders. I did not truly believe that last one, I was far too cold of heart to let that bother me. Men died in battle, and that was just how life was. Perhaps it was that Greg had died because of me? I wasn't sure but in my dreams all of the corpses were small and framed with a wild mane of red hair. I shook my head to clear the images and held up my fingers to order another shot. I slammed it back and I did not even wince anymore at the sharp bite of the drink. I picked up the gem from my coat pocket and clutched it tightly. It lit up and shone between my fingers as text started scrolling down my eyes. The others would not be able to see it, the text was just for me. It was a formal invitation to the First Expedition, and was a very long winded way to say "Come join us." The Expedition was the only thing people seemed to be able to talk about lately, and with good reason. No one had left the Skylands since the Great Barrier first went up, a couple of fools had tried a number of years ago but they had crashed and burned. Now when the Barrier generators were repaired after their overload at the paws of the dragon the engineers had managed to install a gate and for the first time ever the Barrier could be opened at will. A great pier had been grown out of the crystal rock to spear through the barrier and a shipyard had been constructed outside. Magic had been withdrawn from large swathes of the Skylands deemed 'non-essential' and I'd heard rumours that even the crystal of the ground there had started evaporating. Even one of the satellite Skylands orbiting the main one had been decommissioned and consumed in the construction of the shipyards. The Guard and special forces had been recruiting heavily, mainly from the mercenaries and there were talk of creating a marine corps to man the new flying machines. The first of these flying machines was the First Expedition. Or rather, the people sent on it were the Expedition, the vessel itself had been dubbed The Pioneer and was due to leave in a week. I would have to make a decision soon. My reverie was broken by a man who leaned casually against the bar to my side and he smiled at me. I sighed, yet another man who wanted to bang the famous hero. I looked at him again and changed my mind. He was well built and rather handsome, and the brutal scar down his cheek lent his otherwise soft face a certain ferocity. I sighed and pushed a thought into the crystal and I could just barely make out the message as it surged toward the partnered gem. It would seem that I was going Outside. I pushed the thought aside and turned to the man.

"Alright, let's go." His face fell into a rather amusing expression of confused surprise.

"What?"

"I assume you were going to chat me up and then try to bring me back to your place."

He opened and closed his mouth as if at a loss for words.

"Thought as much," even to my own ears my words were slurred, "everyone wants to bang the great hero Dragonbane, " I hiccoughed. "So what are you waiting for, hurry up or I won't let you stick it in my ass."

That got him moving, as I thought it would. I had never truly understood mens fascination with that particular act, not because I didn't enjoy it but there were so many more interesting things to do with the other two holes. Hell, I even had a guy once who preferred to stick it in the fold of my knee for some reason. I started leading him down the street to my place, Marissa was at mom's tonight so I had my place to myself. I realised that Marissa must stay with Mother while I was gone. I pulled the man, whose name I no longer remembered if I had even gotten it, into my apartment and he pushed me aggressively up against the wall to kiss me. I let him grope at me for a moment before I tired of his game and ripped his shirt open. Buttons popped off and bounced from the walls. He was indeed very well muscled and his hands were clean, clean enough that I knew he was not working with them on a day to day basis.

"Are you a merc?"

"Yeah." He did not pause his kisses for more than a single syllable. I was not truly in the mood for talking and I pushed his hands to the lacing of my corset as I shrugged out of my coat. Tonight I had had my choker form a simple waist cincher and he managed to disengage the row of hooks with a deft squeeze of my ribs. It was obviously not the first time he had pulled that particular move off. I raised an eyebrow at him. "Smooth."

"Thanks. I've always been proud of that one." He ripped open the blouse I wore underneath and again buttons clattered to the floor. I did not care, the blouse could reform in minutes, unlike his shirt. His face held no mournful expression of his destroyed garment as he stared hungrily at my breasts. I leaned forward and made my elbows almost touch to give him a better view.

"Are you just gonna stare at them? Get in there, big boy!" He did not need prompting twice and he dove in with his lips and hands. He reached behind me to unhook my bra and my it joined my corset on the floor and I threw my head back with a sigh as his lips found my nipple. My eyes rolled back in my head as he sucked hard and I pushed him back to fall onto the bed. I leaped on top of him and straddled him before I smothered him again with my breast. He did not complain at all as I cut off his air. His fingers slipped beneath the hem of my trousers and probed my wetness. I was more than ready and I let him breathe for a bit as he laughed. I had already undone his belt and started tugging on his trousers and he lifted his hips off the bed to help me. I licked my way down his torso and threw myself into the act. At least with my mouth full of cock I was too preoccupied to take note of the little girl with the crushed face watching me mournfully from the recesses of my mind.

I woke up with a splitting headache and my throat was parched. A weight was on my chest and I opened my eyes and struggled to raise my head to see what was lying on me. I large hand cradled my breast and a heavy snore made me look to the side. A man was sleeping heavily beside me and the events of last night returned in bits and pieces. A hollow feeling filled me and I could suddenly not stand his touch and I threw his hand off of me. He woke with a snort and his eyes focused on me. A slow smile spread across his face and he reached for me.

"Hey..." he started but I cut him off.

"Get out."

"What?"

"Get out. We are done here."

"But I thought..."

"Listen. Last night was fun, " it had been, but right now I felt dirty and I just wanted to take a bath and wait for the headache to pass, "but it is morning and I have shit to do."

I tried to throw his trousers at him with magic and too late I remembered that I still could not use my magic properly and I almost heaved whatever remained in my stomach onto the floor. I swallowed the bile back and forced myself to my feet and threw the garment at him physically. Even that movement almost made me retch and I staggered.

"But I thought tha..."

"No. You had your fun," the bitterness in my voice surprised even me, "and you nailed the Dragonbane. Now. Get. Lost." He clapped his lips tight, visibly angry. He said nothing as he angrily thrust his legs into his leggings. He put on his ruined shirt and slung his jacket over his shoulder. He had obviously given up trying to stay, I heard him mutter 'Bitch!' under his breath as he slammed the door behind him. I sat back down on the bed and put my face in my hands. A sudden taste in my mouth had me run into the bathroom and I hurled bitter bile into the toilet. Cold sweat erupted all over my body and I sat panting with my head in the bowl for a long time before the pain in my head receded enough for me to flush the disgusting mess down the drain. I reached over and opened the faucet on the tub and laboriously climbed into the tub without rising fully. The scalding water slowly filled up and I angled my head to keep my lips above the surface but eventually I had to push into a sitting position to avoid drowning. I had half a mind to not bother but eventually self preservation won out over the pain each movement induced. I found myself slowly shaking my head to keep the pain coming. As long as my body was drowned in either pleasure or pain I was too focused on it to think, and I really did not want to do that. Water was spilling over the edge of the tub and I reached up to shut the stream off. Water was still expensive, even more so when the magic shortage had become even greater now that the shipyard soaked much of the output from the Collectors. I'm not sure how long I sat in the tub but the water was cold when I finally pulled the plug with my feet and I sat in the tub until it was completely empty. Sweat poured from me, but it was the clean sweat of overheating and not the foul ooze from earlier. I felt marginally better and pushed to my feet. I gulped down several glasses of water and considered returning to my bed but the thought of climbing between the soiled sheets repulsed me. Instead I pulled on a clean thong and sat down in my only chair and pulled a spare blanket around me. I woke up some time later to an infernal ringing in my ears and I realised it was the doorbell. The door opened a moment later and Kendall entered. He carried a long wrapped bundle in his arms but I did not manage to muster any curiosity. My head was not pounding as badly any more and I offered him a weak smile. He kicked off his shoes and entered. His nose wrinkled and he waved a hand in front of his face.

"Shit, Kyra it reeks in here. What did you do?"

"If you can't tell by the smell then you are not getting laid enough." He did not offer a response to my witty remark, instead he opened the small window behind me and the cool fresh air brought some clarity to my muddled thoughts. Finally some curiosity reached me.

"What's in the cloth?" He grinned proudly as he sat down on the edge of the bad, making sure that the piece of cloth he sat on was unstained from my nightly activities.

"You asked, and I have delivered." With a dramatic flair he pulled the cloth from the parcel and my eyes widened. It was a rifle, like the ones the special forces used. No, it was not quite like theirs. This one had a small protrusion beneath the barrel, right in front of the trigger guard.

"I snatched this from the battlefield and have made some improvements. I think you may need them before long." My eyes narrowed in suspicion. 

"What have you heard?" I did not think that it had been made official already that I had chosen to join the First Expedition but I could not be certain.

"Nothing, should I have?"

"Never mind, then why do you think I will be needing it?" He gave me a disparaging look.

"Please, Kyra, I know you better than anyone. Of course you are going on the First Expedition. You hate this place more than most and I know you'd jump at the opportunity to go Outside."

His voice was sad, but accepting. He did not like that I would go, but he knew that I had to. He had most likely known even before I did.

"Yeah. But don't tell anyone, it's not official yet and I'd like to tell mom and Marissa myself before that."

"Of course. How is she doing?"

"Mom? Or Marissa?"

"Both."

"Mom is glad to have someone to care for again. She has been suffering from empty nest syndrome ever since I moved out after dad was executed. Marissa on the other hand... I don't know. As long as someone is with her she seems fine but when she does not realise that she is not alone she just kinda stares." Kendall nodded in understanding.

"She just lost her father. Give her time." Sudden worry made my stomach clench.

"Will you check in on her and mom when I'm gone?"

"You know you don't have to ask."

We stared at each other in silence for long minutes, speaking volumes without using words. Suddenly his eyes brimmed with tears.

"I am going to miss you."

"I will be back, it is just a scouting mission." 

He laughed bitterly. "You say that now but there is an entire world out there. Anything could happen. There are fucking dragons out there." He chuckled, despite the tears that threatened to spill over. "That is a sentence I never thought I would say."

"I will return, Kendall. If I find a place out there that is better than here I will not leave you, mom, and Marissa here." He seemed to accept that.

"Here, let me show you how this works."

"I know how a rifle works you idiot." He smiled slyly at me.

"Not this one. As I said, I've made some improvements."

"Well show me, o great and most illustrious craftsman." He stuck his tongue at me and I finally noticed a detail on his face.

"You kept your beard! Or at least, part of it."

He reached up to stroke the neatly trimmed goatee. Why was it even called a 'goatee'? Was 'goat' even a word?

"Yeah, it kinda makes me look distinguished, don't you think?"

"Yeah, sure, whatever. Can we not talk about your vanity and get on with the gun show?"

He muttered something under his breath that sounded suspiciously like "You brought it up first, bitch" but I could not be sure. 

He deftly brought the weapon up and handled it with easy familiarity. He pressed a button on the side and the boxy protrusion I had noted dropped into his waiting hand.

"This is called a magazine. I found the term in an ancient script from before the Apocalypse. Apparently most weapons had them and they could fire tens of bullets per second."

I felt my eyes widen at his ludicrous claim.

"What a load of shit!"

He shook his head. "No, it really said that though I have no idea how they managed it, if it is true." He showed me the open top of the magazine and I saw a bullet in there.

"It holds seven rounds, and you slip it in," he slammed it back into place with a clink of crystal on crystal, "and then you rack the bolt, like so."

He did the motion with practised ease and I could hear the round clink into the chamber.

"After you fire, you eject the case with the same action." I arched my eyebrow at him, so far he had told me nothing new.

"Yeah, so far you have told me nothing I did not know, apart from the magazine bit." He smiled darkly at my interruption and racked the bolt again. The unspent case was flung from the breech and I heard the next round clink into place.

"And now it is ready to fire again, " he added with a smirk.

I let out a slow whistle, impressed. That was even quicker than the special forces who had to place a round into the breech by hand.

"Nifty."

"Ain't it? When the magazine is empty you can just reload swiftly, or revert to breech loading if you so desire."

The rate of fire would be nothing short of astonishing and I almost drooled at the thought. He tapped the magazine with a graceful finger.

"These are simple kinetic rounds. I have not figured out how to make the magazine reload itself like your revolvers so you will have to use a special charger I have in my bag to build them from scratch. The casings will start to dissolve immediately after firing, so if you can retrieve them you can reuse the power they were formed of, otherwise reforming them won't be a big issue."

"These, though" he pulled another magazine from his pocket, "is similar to the rounds for your big revolver, with one major difference." He paused for effect and I decided to oblige. I was in a sudden charitable mood, new toys tended to have that effect on me.

"And that is?" I let some of my enthusiasm fill my voice and he perked up at the attention.

"As you already know, the shots for your revolver already have predefined spells embedded, these does not. Instead they are empty templates, holding power already. You simply need to embed them with a spell just prior to firing."

Again I whistled with appreciation.

"How do I do that?"

"One of two ways, see this gem here?" He tapped a small azure gem mounted on the left side of the breech, opposite the bolt action. I nodded in affirmation.

"Whatever spell held in here will be duplicated into the shot. The spell can be changed at will by casting a new into it, or by flicking this little switch here." He indicated a tiny lever near where the thumb would rest when in firing position.

"What does it do?"

"There are several template stones embedded in the stock, the switch toggles between them. You can replace each of them whenever you wish depending on what you expect to face. Currently it holds a shield breaker, the blood poison and a simple explosive spell."

"You are a very dangerous man, Kendall." I had never truly grasped his brilliance, but the fact that he had managed to whip this together in just a month astounded me. He shook his head.

"Nah, you are the dangerous one, Kyra. I am more of a force multiplier. Anything I can do to make sure you return to me, I will do." The sincerity in his eyes really brought his concern home. He truly was worried that he would never see me again. Overcome with affection for my friend I stood up and let the blanket slip from my shoulders. I sat down in his lap and hugged him close. The rifle nestled between my breasts and the cold crystal felt reassuring against my skin.

"If I live, I will return. I promise you that." I forced as much conviction as I could into my voice and he hugged me back without responding. His next statement surprised me.

"I have to go."

"But you just got here." He pushed me away and I had to leap to my feat to avoid landing on my ass on the floor.

"If you truly mean to return then I have some more toys to build that may aid you and if you are leaving in a week I better get started."

I was touched.

"Thank you."

"Whatever it takes to get you back, my friend. Besides, I still owe you." His face hardened at his words and I knew that he thought of my murder of Markus and his part in it. He left without further words, leaving his bag and the rifle behind. I picked up the weapon and caressed the smooth surface. I ejected the magazine and caught it before I racked the bolt and caught the shot remaining in the breech as it sailed out. I pushed it back into the magazine and the round on the floor soon joined it. With renewed energy I changed the sheets on the bed and got dressed. Despite my throbbing head I decided to pay mom and Marissa a visit. Might as well tell them the news now that there was no going back.

## Chapter 8

The following week passed surprisingly uneventfully. Apart from the tearful conversation with mom and Marissa nothing else worth mentioning happened. I think that mom was secretly happy that I was leaving. She knew I hated this place and I think she hoped that I would find a better place for myself Outside. I highly doubted it, but I swore to myself that if I did I would make sure that she would see it one day. Several times as I was out and about I saw the Pioneer overhead on one of its test runs. It was not an overly large vessel, most of its bulk was made up of the large oval envelope above the gondola and I knew that most of that must contain the engines. It would be compact living once aboard. It had been decided that we would travel west for two weeks and turn back home if we did not find land by then. The next expedition would go east if that was the case. Centuries ago we had known where the Skylands were but the maps had been lost since then. Even if we had had maps we had no way of knowing if the world even looked the same after the Apocalypse. I worried at how we were supposed to find the Skylands again, but I assumed that the crew had figured out some way to navigate. It was made official that I was to be joining the Expedition and people kept wishing me good luck, but lamented that the Skylands' protector would be leaving them. As if it had not been dumb luck that I had 'earned' my current title. Before I knew it I was standing on the pier with the rest of the expedition. All of them mercenaries, and thus expendable like me, except for the colonel chosen to be our leader who was a senior Guardsman. I noted with disdain that Raynard was one of the chosen and I did my best to ignore him and to cherish the last minutes I had with my little family. Mom and Marissa stood to either side of me, clinging to one of my hands each. There was no sign of Kendall and that worried me. He would not miss this for the world and his absence was telling. The colonel strode onto a platform and held up his hands for the crowd to quiet down. Gradually the din subsided.

"People of the Skylands! Today is a glorious day." His voice boomed effortlessly across the plaza, incidentally the same square where the dragon had killed so many people. It was obvious that he had once been a drill sergeant with a voice like that.

"Today we send people Outside for the first time in centuries. What we believed to be a deserted wasteland is obviously not so, as evident by the recent invasion of the monsters now known as Dragonkin." He let the silence drag out as if in mourning before he continued.

"Several brave volunteers have agreed to head out there and see for themselves what lies Outside and assess the threats to our nation and how best to counter them. Among these volunteers are the Dragonbane herself! Come up here, Miss Zorantis." I was surprised to be called up to the podium and I gave my mom a quick hug. I silently wondered if it was the last time I touched my mother. I knelt and gathered Marissa into my arms and held her tight. I had always liked the girl but these last few weeks she had managed to climb into my heart and take up residence. I tried to pull away but she refused to let go so I simply picked her up and brought her with me. Mom cried silently as I left with her newly adopted granddaughter and I swallowed down the sadness myself. I awkwardly climbed the podium, obstructed by the girl in my arms but the crowd loved it. They cheered loud and long at me and Marissa hid her face in my hair in fright of the loud sound and large crowd. I stroked her back as I positioned her to rest on my hip. The Colonel launched into his speech again but I was no longer listening. I cooed softly to Marissa until she relaxed in my arms but she still clutched me tightly. A disturbance in the crowd drew my attention and I saw with relief that Kendall was elbowing his way to the front of the crowd. He looked tired with large bags under his eyes and he signalled until I nodded to convey that I had seen him. He edged as close to the podium as he could and I saw he clutched a small bag in his hand. Realisation struck me. He had kept working around the clock and had rushed here as soon as he finished. Love for my friend constricted my throat and I was thankful that the Colonel had not addressed me directly. Before I knew it his speech was over and the mercenaries started filing aboard the ship behind us. I jumped down to Kendall and I exchanged Marissa with a final kiss on her cheek with the bag he held. Then he pulled me into a fierce embrace.

"Come back to us," he hissed in my ear and then he kissed me. It was not a lovers kiss, but the kiss of a brother who did not truly believe that he would ever see his sister again. I pried Marissa's fingers from my collar and I forced myself to turn away.

"I promise," I said over my shoulder and I walked away without looking back.

"Kyra!" The heartbroken scream of a small girl broke my heart but I did not look back at her. If I had I would not have been able to keep walking. I boarded the ship and stubbornly refused to look out the view ports at the crowd. Raynard opened his mouth to say something but my glare shut him up for once. I found a relatively secluded spot between bulkheads and I sat down and tried not to cry as the engines revved and we started to leave the place where I had spent all of my life.

## Chapter  9

The voyage had quickly become incredibly boring and I already missed my little family. That surprised me quite a lot since I had spent months by myself without missing them before. Perhaps knowing they they were at least in the same city as I had comforted me and now that I had no way to reach them the isolation struck that much harder. I had thoroughly explored the Pioneer, from top to bottom, aft to stern and I had learned what I could. I had even sneaked into the engine room at night when it was manned by a skeleton crew and inspected the machines. Kendall had explained the basics of steam engines to me once and the concept was fairly easy to grasp. The boiler was powered by a large Powerstone that fuelled a simple heating spell that boiled the water into steam. The pressurised steam was then let out into the cylinders that turned the gearbox that in turn spun the propellers on the outside. The low pressure steam was then funnelled into the envelope overhead to provide lift. The water cooled and condensed back to the injector to be returned to the boiler. The engine room took up the bulk of the gondola and even stretched partly into the envelope and I wondered if it was possible to go up there. I assumed that there would be some maintenance shafts and pathways up there just in case one of the steam containers ruptured. I was getting bored of the endless card games and was even tempted to provoke Raynard into a fight or a fuck. Or maybe both. I steeled my resolve to avoid him. I wanted nothing to do with him, at all. We had almost gotten into a fight on the fourth day when I caught him cheating at cards but the other mercs had managed to calm us down. The next day had not been so fortuitous and a fight had broken out. One of the mercenaries whose name I had already forgotten had had his throat slit during the scuffle. No one had seen it happen and whoever had done it remained silent. We considered eating him since none of us had tasted meat before but he had had several boils on his torso that made us think twice. None of us could afford to get ill and we would hopefully taste untainted flesh once we made landfall. If we made landfall. In only three days we would turn back if we did not find land. Since we were not going to eat the poor merc we simply looted his corpse of valuables and dumped him overboard to fall to a watery grave far below us. We mercenaries were nothing if not pragmatic. I found myself tucked into my secluded bulkheads, yet again going through the bag Kendall had gifted me just prior to our departure. It contained a small book with a stylus tucked into the back. It was a small grimoire, and it was strictly forbidden to give them to someone who had not sworn the Mage oath. He could be executed if someone learned that he had given me one. With it I could construct complex spells, or components of spells and then recombine them on the fly. The book would compile them, test them according to my instructions and impart the spell template into a crystal. I knew only the basics of spell construction but I now had at my disposal the means to implement that knowledge. He had also included two small tomes of knowledge, one on the basics of spellwork and one with more complex concepts. I had scanned the pages of that one but the runes made my head swim and I had reverted to the simpler one. That one made more sense to me but so far I had only created one spell that might be useful. The crystal containing the spell nestled comfortably in my pocket and I was quite proud of it, despite its simplicity. When activated it would float to hover above my head and emit a light to see by in the darkness. I could achieve the same with a pure act of will but the crystal let me do it effortlessly and more importantly the magic powering the spell had already been spent in advance and would not rely on my personal energies. My reverie was broken by a muffled shout that I could not make out clearly but the urgency in the tone was infectious. I put the things back in the bag and crawled out of my little haven. I rushed to the bow of the airship and joined the cluster of mercs and crew huddled around the viewport.

"What's going on?"

Raynard turned to me without his usual sneer, instead he wore an expression of pure awe.

"Land." He pointed out the viewport and I squinted along his finger. A thin hazy line of the horizon may have been something other than the endless ocean that spread in all directions.

"You sure?"

He shrugged his massive shoulders.

"Lookout seems to think so. Can you imagine, Kyra? Land?"

I merely shook my head silently. I couldn't truly imagine it. Only having seen the dark crystal hues of the Skylands, the thought of land, actual soil, that was the stuff of our myths and stories was beyond my comprehension. The crew returned to their duties with renewed vigour in their movements as we mercs stared at the thin haze on the horizon. Within an hour it was quite obvious even to me that what we had observed was indeed land. The haze slowly deepened into tans and greens and before nightfall we made out a large expanse of strange structures. They were like pillars, brown interspersed with white, with long thin protrusions all over the top.

"What are those structures?" It took me a moment to realise that it was my voice that had uttered the question.

"I don't know. Could they be…" Whoever had spoken let his voice trail off and one of the other mercs, a small twitchy man named Alder, asked gruffly. "Could they be what?"

"Trees?"

Alder scoffed. "Don't be silly. Trees are a myth."

The first man glared at him. "Just a few months ago anything Outside was a myth."

Alder had no response to that but he still shook his head in defiance. None of us slept that night, instead we remained by the viewport, staring at the landscape rolling past beneath us. The pillars were undoubtedly trees, and what must be grass covered every open space between them. I realised that we were flying over a forest and a hysteric giggle escaped me. My laughter was infectious and soon we all stood chuckling like idiots as we beheld the wonder beneath us. Dawn broke and revealed the edge of the forest on the horizon. Endless plains of grass spanned beyond. Colonel Grayson joined us and ordered us to gather around him.

"We approach our first dropoff. I need two volunteers to go down and explore this area before the rest of us head east and explore there."

All of our hands shot into the air, all of us were eager to set foot on actual ground. The Colonel grinned at our enthusiasm and pointed at me.

"I want the Dragonbane to be one of the two. Who wants to join her?"

Again all hands but mine shot up. Excitement bubbled through me at my good fortune. I was unsure if I could have tolerated another few days aboard the Pioneer with the knowledge that others where down there exploring. Grayson randomly pointed at one of the other mercs and I heard a feminine squeal of delight. I let out a pent up breath that Raynard had not been chosen to join me. Alissa strutted up to stand next to me and I smiled at the shorter woman with the deep green hair that she wore in tight braids. She almost vibrated with excitement. I realised that I did the same and I ignored the sour faces of the others. They could gripe all they wanted, I was going to the ground today! Grayson droned on about how the Pioneer would return for us in a month and wait for three days before giving up and returning home to the Skylands. I did not truly listen, my mind focused on what I may find down there. He repeated the warnings he had spoken several times before about being wary of what we ate. The records surviving from before the Skylands isolated themselves behind the Great Barrier spoke of poisonous plants and berries, whatever berries where, but that meat was rarely dangerous unless mishandled. My mouth watered at the thought of meat. I had no longing to eat plants, having grown up entirely on fungus, but the thought of meat thoroughly enticed me. I wondered how it tasted. I dashed into the barracks and gathered up my personal belongings and weapons and left the rows of hammocks behind. I would so not miss sleeping in a hammock among the snores and wheezes of the mercenaries. After a few hours that felt like an eternity I found myself at the same door where we had pitched the corpse overboard last week. The Pioneer had descended and positioned itself into the wind to hover above an opening in the forest below. This was the manoeuvre the crew had practised the most before we left. The Pioneer had to be almost stationary for us to disembark safely and the opening in the trees were too small for the ship to land properly. We could of course have landed on the plains beyond the forest but then we would be exposed to whatever could be lurking out there. At least the trees offered some protection. Grayson gave the order and the door opened. I swung out the arm and the wire attached uncoiled and fell to the ground fifty feet below. Alissa moved to grab it but I was having none of that. I wanted to be the first Skylander on the ground so I leaped out of the ship and grabbed the wire and swiftly rappelled to the ground. The last thing I saw of my countrymen were Alissa's astonished face as I sailed past her and then I was falling. The air howled in my ears as I gained speed and I clenched the handle I clutched. With a wrenching sensation in my arms my free fall was arrested to a more manageable pace and then my boots hit the soil. I sank an inch into the soft ground and stumbled to the side. I had not expected the ground to be this soft. Alissa landed beside me with a loud whoop of jubilation and the crew of the Pioneer wasted no time in withdrawing the wire and gunning the engine. I ignored the ship as it started to ascend and instead I knelt on the forest floor and drew my hands through the grass. I can't explain the feel of the rigid growths against my palm nor the scents that assaulted my nose. The wind rustled softly through the trees and I racked my memory for the term of the green protrusions. Leaves? Was that the word? And the protrusions were called branches. Yes, that was it. Branches and leaves. The enormity of the unknown world surrounding us struck me and I sat down heavily on my ass. Apparently Alissa came to the same realisation and she retched on the ground beside me. I scooted back to avoid the foul liquid. She glanced at me bashfully as she blushed prettily.

"Sorry."

"It's alright. Quite overwhelming, isn't it?" She nodded, looking around with wide eyes as she wiped her mouth with her sleeve. I offered her my canteen and she gratefully rinsed her mouth with the fresh water. She stoppered it and returned it to me. The gem on the side started to glow faintly as the enchantment activated. Our canteens was one of the many inventions created for our journey. As long as it was not full the canteen would pull moisture from the air to refill itself. It was a slow process but would hopefully keep us from dying of thirst if we could not find a reliable source of water. She carried her own of course but I wanted to be on good terms with her. She appeared to be a nice woman, for a merc, and since we were stuck with each other for a month I'd rather make her a friend. I pushed up to my feet and my companion joined me. I glanced at her.

"Wanna check out the forest?" She nodded gleefully and burst into a sprint and I rushed to joined her. We ran like children through the wood, stumbling on unfamiliar roots and other underbrush as we went, marvelling at everything we saw and smelled. I almost careened into Alissa as she stopped dead, staring intently at something on a bush. I drew up next to her, instantly on alert.

"What is it?" My hands fell to rest on my weapons

"Pretty." She pointed a tiny creature sitting on a flower. It was very small but had large wings of many intricate colours.

"Yes, it is very pretty. What is it?"

"I don't know." The tiny creature flapped it wings and flew away in an odd pattern, as if its wings were too big for it. Alissa looked at me with a beaming smile and I realised that my own cheeks were aching from the strain of my wide grin. This was awesome.

"Try to keep up!" I burst into a sprint again and could hear her right behind me. I laughed and dove over a fallen log covered with moss and rolled back to my feet without losing much momentum. Words and names for things bubbled up from the dark recesses of my memory. Everything I had heard in the old lore and legends came back slowly and I put names to some of the things I saw. Most of the things I had no names for. I leaped a boulder and came face to face with a startled little creature with a fluffy tail that swiftly scurried up the bark of a tree. My foot splashed into something cold and wet and I stopped instantly. Alissa careened into me and we fell into a tangle with a grunt. She landed on top of me and I could not help myself but pulled her into an embrace and laughed. She stared into my eyes scant inches away and smiled and I impulsively reached up and planted a swift kiss on her lips. I laughed at her startled expression and pushed her off me. I approached the small stream I had stepped in and knelt next to it. I marvelled at the clear water as it streamed gently across round pebbles. I dipped my hand in it and ignored the bite of the cold water and I picked up one of the stones and rolled it around my palm. Alissa cupped her hands and brought water to her lips.

"Careful, we don't know if it is drinkable."

She froze for a moment, her lips almost touching the water. Then she dipped her lips and drank. She wiped her mouth on her sleeve and grinned at me.

"Only one way to find out!" I returned the grin and followed suit. It was the best water I had tasted so far, with an odd taste I was not used to but far from unpleasant. We walked more sedately after that. Side by side we made our way through the forest in the direction of the plains and soon I felt fingers intertwine with mine. I squeezed her hand and felt her return the gesture. The forest seemed so peaceful, no hint of Wild Magic at all. Come to think of it, I felt a magic field surrounding us that was much more powerful than the one in the Skylands. All of the magic back home got soaked up by the industry or the Barrier and there was precious little left over despite that fact that we lived on a massive geyser of magic. Out here there seemed that the atmosphere was more saturated since none of the creatures around us seemed to use much or any at all. The afternoon passed swiftly and night fell quickly as the sun vanished behind the mountains in the distance. Before long we could barely make any headway without stumbling and I considered bringing out the light spell I had constructed but weariness crashed into me. The sleepless night before made itself known and I heard Alissa yawn beside me.

"We'd better make camp for the night. I can barely see where I put my feet." She sighed wistfully before she responded.

"You are probably right, but I'd much rather keep exploring."

We quickly found another stream beside two large boulders and made out camp between them. We would be relatively sheltered there. I walked around the boulders, inscribing a few simple wards from the magic book Kendall had given me to give us warning of any kind of attack and we cut some low hanging branches from a tree that did not have leaves but some kind of short, sharp protrusions that smelled really nice. Despite their sharpness the branches were surprisingly soft once piled onto the ground and we lay down on our makeshift beds inside the circle of wards. The night was surprisingly chilly after the warmth of the day and we huddled close for warmth. Despite my elation of finally being on the ground I fell asleep quickly. It had been much to take in in a short time and I was exhausted.

The first light of dawn on my face woke me up and I poked the woman in my arms. She grumbled but her eyes opened wide as she remembered where we were. Without speaking we set off again. My belly grumbled and I reluctantly produced one of the rations we had packed. We had so far not found anything here to eat and I put the dried fungus in my mouth and washed it down with water from my canteen. Alissa sighed and followed suit.

"If I never eat this fungus again it would be too soon. I hope we find something to eat today. I am dying to try something else."

"I saw a tiny creature yesterday. It did not appear to have much meat on it but a few of them would be a fine supper."

"Really, what did it look like?" 

I spent a few minutes describing the little adorable furry creature and Alissa clapped her hands in delight.

"Oh how I wish that I could have seen it."

We walked in a pleasant silence, craning our necks to take in the surroundings. I did not think that I would ever tire of not being surrounded by the oppressive crystal of home. The mere thought of returning filled me with dread even though I already looked forward to seeing my family again. How they would enjoy coming here. I resolved to bring them here, if it were in my power. I pointed out another of the small furry creature to Alissa as it chattered angrily at us from the safety of the branch high above. She squealed in delight when she saw it.

"Aw, it's adorable!"

It was hard for me to reconcile the seemingly innocent woman beside me with the ferocious mercenary she must be to be extended an invitation to the First Expedition. The sun had started to set on our second day Outside when I stretched out my arm to my side to halt Alissa. She followed my stare and froze as well. Between two trees not thirty yards from us stood a large creature. It was watching us warily with large brown eyes. It was sleek with long legs and a slim body but its head was adorned with horns that had many sharp points. It seemed ready to spring into action at our slightest moment, to attack or flee I had no idea. I was confident that the armour I still wore would protect me from being gored by the horns but Alissa wore much lighter armour. Ever so slowly I slid the rifle from my back and lined up the sights. I hesitated. The creature was beautiful, but the thought of meat made my mouth water and my belly growl. The sharp report of the rifle disturbed the tranquillity of the forest and the creature bolted. A flock of small flying animals erupted from the crown of a nearby tree but I paid them no mind. I rushed toward the place I had last seen the horned creature and I scanned the ground. It was gone and I swore vehemently. Alissa drew up next to me and pointed.

"Dragonbane, look. Blood."

I looked at where she indicated and I smiled. There were indeed blood on the ground.

"Nice catch. Let's go!"

Now that I knew that I had hit it and that it bled, the trail it left was easy to follow. Splashes of blood and broken twigs marked its passage and before long we found it lying on the ground next to a large tree. It lifted its head weakly and glared at us with panic in its eyes. It was bleeding heavily from its side and I could hear its laboured breathing even from where we stood. I saw blood bubble out of the wound and I realised I had hit it in the lung. I had seem similar wounds on my victims enough times to know that it was dying unless it was treated. I had no intention of helping it survive though and I drew my knife from behind my back. It kicked with its legs in an effort to put distance between us but it succeeded only in stirring up the dead leaves on the ground. It lashed out with its horns as I drew close but I caught them with my hand and forced its head to the ground. I slit its throat with the sharp edge of my crystal blade and its agony swiftly vanished as it died. I felt uncharacteristically saddened at its death. I thought that I had killed enough people to not feel anything anymore. The memory of a small, still form with a crushed face flashed before my eyes but I forced the image aside. I was too excited to finally try meat. I looked up at Alissa.

"Which parts do you think we should eat first?" She shook her head, unable to take her eyes off the dead creature. 

"I guess the legs would a good a place as any to start."

Alissa glanced at me.

"There are much more than we can eat tonight."

"Yes, there is."

"Won't it spoil?"

"I don't know." I shrugged. "Cooked fungus lasts longer than fresh. Perhaps the same is true for meat?"

Alissa nodded in agreement.

"Maybe. We should keep some fresh though and see if the theory holds true."

"Good thinking. Do you think we have enough magic to cook most of it?"

My companion shrugged as she drew her knife and opened the belly of the creature.

"I'm not sure. I hardly ever use magic actively, I'm not sure how much I can hold. I am sure you can though, you are the Dragonbane." I did not like the amount of awe in her voice as she said my title.

"I'm just a merc, like you. Climbing that dragon was stupid, but at least it got me out here."

"I guess we cook as much as we are able and save the rest."

We helped each other butcher the beast. None of us knew what we were doing but before it got too dark we had managed to empty it of its innards and skin it and started separating the flesh from the bones. It was gruesome work but I had seen enough death and mangled bodies to not let it bother me. I had even done much of the mangling myself, come to think of it. Once we had some suitable cuts ready we sat down and held the raw flesh in our hands. Blood dripped between my fingers as I channelled power into the flesh and it started to cook from the inside. I let it hover an inch above my palms when it got too hot to hold. I swore and jerked my hands away as sizzling fat dripped onto my hands and I lost my concentration. My meat fell onto the ground but I did not care that it got a little dirty. The smell emanating from the cooking meat smelled way to good to let the small mishap dampen my spirit. I picked up the meat and juggled it between my hands to let it cool off a bit and I saw Alissa doing the same. I could hardly wait to sink my teeth into the tender flesh and I saw in my companions eyes that she felt as I did. When I could finally hold the piece of meat in my hands I looked at my new friend.

"Are you ready for you first taste?"

She nodded with twinkling eyes and I raised the hunk of flesh to my face. It was so different from what I had expected, but oh so incredible. The fungus I was used to barely required me to chew it, it was so spongy but this was tough. I had to really gnaw pieces of it off but it was juicy. So very juicy. Fat dripped down my chin as my teeth cut through the fibres and the rich flavour filled my mouth. I moaned in delight and my eyes rolled back in my head as I chewed. I'm not sure quite what I had expected but it was not this. This was so much better. Before I knew it the piece was gone and I immediately cut a new slice off the carcass to cook it. Alissa and I gorged ourselves on the dead beast, too busy stuffing our faces to speak, until we could barely move. I was full almost all the way up to my throat but I still wanted more. I felt suddenly sleepy and almost stretched out on the ground then and there but we had to take care of the rest of the meat. Alissa burped and slapped a hand over her mouth in embarrassment. I chuckled and forced out a long belch and we both fell into fits of giddy giggling. It was as if we were drunk, but on meat and it was one of the best feelings ever.

"We better cook the rest of the meat."

"Yeah. I'm not sure how much magic I have left though." I looked at her in surprise, we had not spent that much cooking the meat so far. Was she really that magically weak? I could not really hold that against her though. Most people of the Skylands had no reason to hone their magic potential. The machines did the work for them. When Alissa ran out of magic to cook with she made it her task to finish butcher the creature and I cooked the pieces she handed me. We saved a large piece of meat to see if it would spoil faster than the cooked meat and we laid it out on the hide of the beast. We were both incredibly sleepy from our heavy meal by then and I barely had enough energy to ward our campsite before we fell into a satisfied sleep.

## Chapter 10

I woke up from one of the best nights of sleep I'd ever had and for breakfast we gorged ourselves once more on flesh. It was not as good as it had been when freshly cooked but still beat any meal from back home. There were a lot of meat left over when we were both full and Alissa asked the pertinent question as she tapped her lower lip thoughtfully.

"How do we carry this?"

I considered her question for a moment before I came up with an answer.

"My shirt. We make a bundle. I don't really need it under all this armour. Come, help me get it off."

We spent a couple of minutes taking off my pauldrons and armoured corset and I stripped out of my dark blouse. She helped me back into my armour afterwards. It would chafe more without the soft blouse but I could live with that if it enabled us to bring the meat with us. We made a bundle of the shirt and meat and tied it with the sleeves to the strap of my rifle. It was not very heavy but hung on one side of my body, messing up my balance but I could live with it. We set off on our trek again but to be honest, I no longer had any clue if we were still walking in the same direction. The forest looked largely the same, even though I had not yet tired of looking at it, and I had no idea how to navigate in the wilderness. Not for the first time the sheer amount of knowledge lost to us during our isolation struck me. For all of our magic and technology we had absolutely no clue how the world worked out here. I guess that was our true mission here, to gather knowledge to use in further expeditions. Suddenly curious about the woman I had spent every waking moment with for the last few days I started questioning her.

"Do you have anyone left back home?"

It was a short while before she answered as she helped me clamber over a fallen log.

"Just a few friends. No one close. You?"

"Just my mom and best friend. And my daughter." I was surprised at that last part. When had I started to consider Marissa to be my daughter?

"Really? I have not heard that the great Dragonbane had a daughter."

"She is not really my own. I kind of adopted her when her father was killed during the Dragonkin invasion."

"Was he your friend?"

"Yes."

"I am sorry for your loss, and hers."

"Thank you, Alissa."

We walked in silence for a few minutes.

"What did your mother say when you told her you were going?"

"She cried. A lot. But she was not particularly surprised. Ever since dad was killed she knew I would leave if I had the chance. I can't stand that place."

"I know that feeling. Who killed him?"

"The government." Alissa winced at that and something in her expression gave me a clue.

"They killed you parents too." I did not frame it like a question, more like a statement but she nodded anyway.

"Dad lost his leg in a freak accident at work and they killed him when he could no longer work. Mom was very upset and joined a protest. The Guard shot her."

"I'm sorry."

"Thanks." She dabbed at her eye discretely but I caught the gesture from the corner of my eye.

"Hey, come here."

I grabbed her by her arm and pulled her into an embrace and I felt her take a shaky breath.

"Was it long ago?"

"Long enough." I could tell by her voice that it still pained her and I held her silently until she relaxed. She pulled out of my embrace.

"C'mon. Let's keep going for a while before we break for lunch."

When we pulled meat out of the bundle for lunch I stared at it suspiciously. It looked distinctly greyer and greasier than yesterday but it smelled fine so we ate it anyway. Despite its greasy exterior it was dry and chewy on the inside. Nevertheless it was better than anything I'd had back home and our supply of meat dwindled rapidly. The creature had not been overly large and we had truly gorged ourselves. We had enough for dinner and possibly for our meals tomorrow. The raw piece of meat smelled funky but we decided to keep it to study it's decay.

We did not speak of home as we walked, instead we walked mostly in silence and occasionally pointed out particularly interesting things we found like a plant or small animal that did not flee before us. The days were warm and I was sweating heavily under my armour and it was chafing and itching abominably especially since I no longer wore the blouse underneath to divert the moisture. I reduced the amount of armour I wore and my gorget shrank to its usual choker and my armoured corset grew thinner and the neckline plunged down severely. I sighed in relief as my neck and upper chest was exposed to the air and started cooling me down. I considered ditching my coat but I had too much stuff in my pockets to bother putting them somewhere else. Alissa eyed my corset with envy as it shrank. I pulled my shoulders back and crossed my arms beneath my breasts.

"Are you jealous?" Her eyes darted up to meet my gaze before she forced her gaze forward.

"Well, yeah."

I suppressed a giggle.

"Yours ain't so bad, though not as big."

She gave me an odd sideways glance.

"But just the fact that you can vary the size like that. It must be incredibly handy."

"What?" I was thoroughly lost.

"Wait, what?" Apparently Alissa was as confused as me. "What are you talking about?"

We both realised the misunderstanding at the same time and she burst into a fit of laughter as my neck and face heated up.

"Where you talking about your tits?" She fell back into giggles and I wanted to hide behind some trees. She made a show of inspecting my breasts and I bore the scrutiny stoically. I deserved her mockery.

"While very nice, I was actually talking about your armour. Pervert." I forced my arms down along my sides.

"Well, I get that now. Shut up."

"Aw, c'mon don't be like that. Make them dance for me, I promise I will be a good girl and watch."

"Shut up." Sometimes my eloquence surprised even me. I walked in sullen silence for several minutes as Alissa kept chuckling every now and then.

"You are so adorable when you sulk."

"I'm not sulking!"

"Yes, you are! That pout is so cute!"

"I'm not pouting!" I pouted.

She pulled her brows down in a displeased expression and turned the corners of her mouth sharply down and extended her lower lip in an exaggerated pout. She spoke in a gruff voice that was obviously a poor imitation of my own.

"I'm Kyra and I am sad that Alissa was not looking at my boobs and I refuse to make them dance for her."

I threw up my hands in exasperation.

"Fine!"

I shimmied my shoulders and Alissa clapped her hands in delight. I could not help chuckling at her expression. How had this carefree woman ever survive the harsh life of a mercenary back home? Or did these tranquil surroundings transform her into the girl she had once been?

That night we made camp by a brook and I had the sudden idea to boil some of the meat in the fresh water to make a soup. It turned out to be a failure as the grease from the meat gathered on the surface and the flavours was all watered out.

"Well, at least we learned that boiled meat is not as good as freshly cooked meat."

I had noted that Alissa always saw things from a positive perspective. She was the temperamental opposite of me. Where I was cynical she was oddly naive. Where I prepared for the worst she envisioned a happy path. Where she laughed in amazement at an animal I suspiciously assessed the threat level and my hands rarely strayed far from my weapons. When we woke up at dawn the meat smelled decidedly bad.

"I'm not sure we should eat this. It smells kinda bad." Alissa nodded slowly in agreement.

"Perhaps one of us should eat it, too see what happens. As long as we both don't get ill at once we can handle it. We need to learn when the meat becomes inedible." Her voice was filled with hope and I swallowed an amused snort.

"Sure, go ahead. I think I will stick to rations this time."

I almost gave in when I saw the obvious relish on her face as she devoured the flesh but her reasoning was sound. We could not afford both of us to sicken at the same time. I sighed wistfully as I washed down my dried fungus with water. At least we had not been forced to rely on our magic canteens much. Fresh water seemed to be plentiful out here. I really hoped that we would come across another creature to kill for meat before I had to eat any more of these abominable rations. I wondered if there were some technique to find one actively instead of just hoping to stumble on another like we had the first. Alissa just shrugged when I voiced the question, too busy stuffing her face with food. I let the idea to hunt roll in the back in my mind and tried to figure out what kind of tracks such a creature would leave. It's feet had appeared disproportionately small and would not leave much of an imprint on the ground. Perhaps it would leave snapped twigs in its wake? Probably not. I assumed that there were other animals that would eat creatures like the one we had slain as a primary food source and it would simply not do to leave obvious trails behind. Such behaviour would swiftly be culled by simple attrition. Before noon Alissa was looking pale and she had started sweating.

"Kyra, I don't feel so good."

"Bellyache?"

She nodded. "I think I'm gonna throw up soon."

"I guess this proves that the meat was inedible at this point." She glared daggers at me.

"Are you gloating over this because of my ribbing earlier?"

I nodded with a wide smile on my face.

"You earned this, Alissa." I smiled to take the edge out of my words. "Try drinking some water, maybe it can flush it through your system faster."

"I don't feel like swallowing right now."

"Do it! You'll feel better, I promise."

Alissa grumbled but put her canteen to her lips and took a tiny sip and glared at me.

"Happy?"

"Nope. Drink more."

She forced down several swallows and breathed heavily for a few moments before she spoke.

"You know what? It actually does feel a little..." Her words were interrupted by her gagging and doubling over. I just barely managed to sidestep the watery fluid mixed with slimy bits of meat that spewed from her mouth. Alissa fell to her knees and kept retching and I knelt next to her and held her green braids from her face until she finished. She was grey in the face and sweating heavily when she straightened back up.

"Better?"

"A little. I regret not taking your advice this morning." She retched again but her belly was empty and she only spat some bile on the ground to join the rest of the smelling mess slowly soaking into the soil.

"Worth it though. That meat was superb." I nodded.

"Well, now that we know how long cooked meat will keep there is no point lugging this around any more." I shook the improvised bundle containing the offending meat.

"Yeah, I suppose. But it still feels wrong to just toss it."

I arched my eyebrow.

"You'd rather eat the rest of it?"

She shook her head violently and the motion set her straight back to heaving. I stroked her back until she finished and she fell on her side, panting. I let her rest for a bit as I untied the bundle and discarded the spoilt meat onto the forest floor. I tucked my greasy blouse into my pocket and set it do dissolve. I'd have it reform tomorrow so I could wear it. Alissa recovered and sat up and rinsed her mouth with water that she spat back out.

"Ready to keep going?"

She nodded affirmative, too winded to speak properly.

"Still hurts though and I feel weak. Do you think it is lethal?"

That thought had not crossed my mind and I was surprised at the calmness she spoke of her own possible death.

"I don't know. You did not eat that much of it and it was still relatively fresh. I hope you survive. I'd hate to be forced to carry your stuff if you croaked."

She glared at me, not appreciating my humour and I punched her lightly on the shoulder. Despite herself she smiled weakly and I helped her up on her feet. She swayed on her feet until she gathered herself and she set off at a reduced pace. I caught up easily and remained close to catch her should she stumble. Surprisingly she managed to remain upright but despite her stability she tired early and we decided to make camp long before the sun set. We camped by a large pool in a stream and I went down to the shore to fill our canteens. A silvery flash a bit out in the pool caught my eye and I stared intently at the spot. Was something lurking beneath the surface? The water was clear enough for me too see to the bottom and it was not deep enough for a large beast to hide but the sun reflected off the surface in a blinding way and I could not be sure. I returned my attention to our flasks and then in a few minutes and then I caught the flash again from the corner of my eye. I was wondering if I had imagined it but this flash was accompanied by s splash and spreading rings on the surface. There was clearly something in the water.

"Alissa! There is something in the water."

I just barely heard her roll over from her resting position.

"Danger?"

"I don't think so, " I said uncertainly, "it was a small flash just beneath the surface. I'll investigate. Stay watchful."

I could feel her eyes on my back as I stood and made my way out into the shallows. I set my armour to manifest fully. You could never be too careful. I ignored the water rushing into my boots as I waded out to knee depth. I could dismiss the boots later and reform them during the night in a dry state easily enough. I stared intently into the water and from my new angle the sun did not blind me in an area around me. I could see nothing strange in the water. I started to turn back when a thought struck me. I had not observed the flashes until I had remained motionless for a few minutes as I fiddled with the flasks so I froze and stood motionless to see if something would happen. A dark shape drifted into view and I started in surprise. The shape darted away into a spot where I was blinded by the sun with a similar flash. I froze again. I waited for a few tense minutes.

"Find anything?"

I waved for her to be silent and kept still. The dark shape drifted into view, this time joined by another. I fought my urge to move and waited for them to come closer. The way it moved betrayed intent and I decided that it was clearly some sort of animal. They were dark and blended in with the gravel on the bottom of the pool and I could only see them when they moved. They were not large, about as long as my forearm and about as wide. One glided within reach and I lunged to grab it. Since they were so small I was certain that they could not hurt me too much even if I grappled them but they were surprisingly quick and darted away. Again I stood still until they came near me again. They did not seem to remember that I had startled them and soon were nudging my boots curiously. I slowly reached down until my hand hovered above the surface before I lunged again. Despite my nearness I had no chance to grab it and it felt slimy as my fingers brushed it as it darted away. I cursed and froze again. These creatures intrigued me. How could they survive under water? Did they not breathe? Again the creatures glided close and I knew I would not be able to catch them with my bare hands. I focused my mind and slowly sank tendrils of magic into the water. I carefully formed a net of magic and slipped it beneath one of the shapes. I carefully and slowly wrapped the net around the creature without letting it touch the magic before I ripped it from the water. It started wriggling helplessly as it rose into the air.

"I got one!"

"What is it?"

"I have no idea, I'll bring it to you!"

Remembering its slick hide I kept it in the net and carefully made my way back to Alissa. It was difficult to maintain the net around the struggling animal and walk at the same time and I almost lost my focus when my foot snagged on a large stone but I managed to return to my friend. Alissa sat up as I approached and I dumped the creature in her lap. She flinched and yelped as the slimy thing landed on her trousers and she scooted aside as the thing flopped pathetically on the ground. We stared at it in fascination. It was dark on the top but pale on the belly and shimmering on the sides. I leaned close to it and saw that it was scaled like the Dragonkin, but slimy. Instead of arms and legs it had some sort of flat appendages, apparently made to enable it to move through the water. I am sure I had heard the term for moving through water but at the moment I could not remember it. I'd never seen this much water in one place before, apart from the ocean but that had always been well outside my reach, and it unnerved me. I had heard of people drowning in their tubs so I knew water was dangerous. As long as I could sit in it with my head above the surface I did not fear it that much but I would not want to fall into a deep pool. Alissa poked it with her finger but it did not seem to notice. It kept flopping around helplessly.

"Do you think we can eat it?"

I shrugged in response.

"Are you feeling better? Are you ready to eat?"

"Yeah. I feel weak, and cold, but I could eat some."

I drew my knife and tried to grab the thing. After a short struggle I managed to force it to stay still. It wriggled in my hand but remained somewhat stationary. I put the edge of my knife against its neck. It did not seem to have a throat I could cut to kill it so I was planning to sever its spine to put it down. I applied pressure with my knife but the tiny scales proved surprisingly tough and I resorted to sawing. Eventually I forced through the scales and the thing went limp as it died. Unlike everything else I had killed, human and beast alike, its eyes did not change. You could always see life fade from the eyes of your victims but this creature had dead eyes even when it was alive. I flipped it over and struggled to open its belly to remove its innards. The scales on its belly proved almost as touch as the ones on it back and the soft belly did not offer the same kind of leverage but I was stubborn. Eventually I had it opened and I scooped out the innards. I lifted the heart to show Alissa.

"Look. It is still beating."

"Really? But it is quite obviously dead?" 

I nodded silently. On a whim I popped the still beating heart into my mouth and swallowed it whole. I could feel it wriggling on its way down and I giggled at the sensation. Alissa watched me with large eyes.

"How did it taste?"

"Like blood, basically." She nodded knowingly as I spread the creature open. Its sides were lined with pale flesh entirely different in colour and texture to the beast we had eaten. I tried cutting some loose with my knife but it proved oddly resistant. Only tiny fragments came loose and the morsels hardly seemed worth the effort.

"Cook it whole, the other animal became softer when we cooked it remember? Maybe it will be easier to handle then."

"Good idea."

I held it in both hands and channelled power into it until it sizzled and steamed. A completely unfamiliar smell rose from it as it cooked. Not at all like the larger horned beast but far from unpleasant. The pale, slightly translucent flesh turned into an opaque white and it started to darken at the edges when I supposed it was finished. I scraped my knife at it and it parted easily.

"I think you were right Alissa." I cut out a large piece for her and handed it over with the blade of my knife and she reached eagerly for it.

"Careful, it's hot."

She did not heed my warning and snatched up the meat and juggled it from hand to hand until it cooled enough to eat. She bit into the flesh.

"Well, how does it taste?"

Alissa chewed and swallowed.

"I can't describe it. It is completely different in every way from the other meat. You better try some for yourself."

I did and it tasted glorious. She was correct of course, it was an entirely different experience of flavours and between us we swiftly finished the animal. We licked out fingers clean in contentment. The small animal was surprisingly filling.

"Make camp," I told Alissa, "and I will go catch some more."

In an hour I caught three more of the creatures and Alissa prepared and cooked them. We ate one of them and decided to keep the rest for tomorrow. As with the other meat we kept a small piece uncooked to see how quickly it would spoil. We made beds from the same kind of branches we had each night and I set all my clothes to dissolve. Sadly I could not selectively dissolve just parts of them. I could reduce the amount of clothing my choker manifested but if I wanted to dissolve my blouse and boots then the rest had to go too. I turned down the armour to just my underwear, the minimum I could keep and still have the boots dissolve. As we watched the sunset I gradually became more and more naked. Thankfully it was a warm evening but there was a certain chill in the air that promised a cold night. That proved true as soon as the last rays of the sun dipped beneath the horizon and I shuddered as cold shivers spread across my skin. Alissa shrugged out of her own coat.

"Come, sleep next to me for warmth."

"Thanks."

I climbed beneath the makeshift blanket and Alissa snuggled up against my back. It was nice with some physical contact, even though she was still fully clothed. A faint scent of sweat reached my nose at our proximity and I realised that neither of us had bathed since we left the Skylands. The water in the pool was too cold to wash in comfortably but perhaps we could heat it up magically. With the thicker magical field out here we may even afford to do it. I fell asleep in the arms of a pretty woman and a mind full of the thoughts of warm baths. It was a good night. 

We woke up at dawn and hungrily devoured one of the creatures we had caught the previous night as my clothes reformed around me. The uncooked meat already smelled foul and judging by how Alissa had reacted to eating the smelly meat yesterday we chose to discard the piece. The cooked meat still smelled fine so we ate it without fear. After breakfast we set out through the forest once more. Since we had not faced any threats at all since we made landfall I did not wear my helmet to enjoy the fresh air better, and that proved to be a poor decision later in the day. We were speaking of stopping for lunch and eat the last creature when Alissa spotted something in the foliage. She grabbed my arm and brought us both to a halt. I looked in the direction she pointed.

"I heard something."

My hands fell to my weapons as I strained my ears. I heard a rustling of leaves and was instantly on alert. Alissa walked slowly and carefully toward the sound. It did not sound like a large animal but even so I readied my rifle. If it was a creature then we may be able to eat it. Alissa saw it first and she gasped.

"Oh, it is so cute!" Her voice was a girlish squeal and I stepped to the side to see around her. I could not do anything but agree. It was small, smaller than the horned creature I'd slain and much larger than the water beasts we had eaten but it bore no similarities to either of the creatures. It was squat, walked on all fours and was covered in thick brown fur. It stared at us with frightened brown eyes and backed further into the bush beneath which it hid. I slowly raised my rifle but Alissa reached out and pushed my rifle down.

"We can't kill it. It is just a baby!"

I glanced at her.

"How do you know?"

She shook her head. "I just know. Look how frightened it is. It is not even trying to flee. Let's just go, leave it be."

I wanted to shoot it. I wanted to taste its flesh but it was annoyingly adorable. Reluctantly I nodded and we took a careful step backward. A twig cracked beneath my boot and a loud roar split the air. I had heard a roar like that before and it sent my mind back to that rainy night when I had fought a dragon. My whole body tensed and I whirled around. The roar had come from behind us but I knew that we were chanceless against a dragon. My eyes found the source of the roar and I relaxed when I saw it was not one of the huge scaled beasts. This creature was a larger version of the small one now behind us. Much bigger. It was on all fours but was still almost as tall as me and easily five times heavier. It was covered in the same brown fur but it was obvious it packed some serious muscle beneath it. Both of us froze in surprise. The large paws of the creatures was larger than either of our heads and it looked powerful enough take them off with a single blow. I was barely armoured today but I was not sure if even my full armour would protect me from a single swipe of those long claws. The creature roared again and charged us. It was surprisingly swift for its size and I raised my rifle and shot without aiming. At this range it mattered little, especially with such a large target. The bullet sank into its shoulder and the spell within ignited and blew a large chunk of flesh from the creature. It roared in pain but kept coming. I started to shift my weight to roll to the side but it was already upon me. I suddenly found myself soaring through the air with a searing pain blossoming in my side. My back struck a tree and I was wrenched violently around and rolled across the ground. My head struck something hard with a sickening crunch and darkness claimed me.

I woke up slowly to a world of pain. My head was pounding and my side was on fire. Memories returned in a flash and I froze, tensing in pain as my wounded side locked up. I refused to move from the surge of pain, instead straining my ears. If the creature was still nearby it might find me by the slightest sound I made. Only the tranquil silence of the forest greeted my ears and the now familiar chirping of the small flying animals sang for me. I even recognised the chatter of one of the small furry animals that hid in branches above. I inched my eyes open and looked around without moving my head. The dim light blinded my sensitive eyes but I risked pain by looking around properly. I winced in pain as my head threatened to split open but I saw no sign of the creature, nor of Alissa. Worry settled in my belly and I foolishly tried to stand up. The world pivoted and I fell back down. I probably had a concussion. My grimace made the crusted blood on my cheek crack with a soft whisper and I noticed with some concern that my side was wet and sticky beneath my corset and I turned my attention downward. Unfortunately my cleavage blocked sight of my side and the stiff corset did not let me push my boob to the side in order to see. Instead I trailed my fingers down my side lightly and they came away bloody. I found several rents in my corset from the claws that had ripped straight through it and into the soft flesh beneath. I gritted my teeth in preparation for further pain and tried to cauterise the uppermost wound with my magic. Pain exploded in my head and I fell on my back. I was completely unable to use magic in my concussed state but if I could not stem the flow of blood I would weaken from blood loss and possibly die. I pushed myself up to a sitting position. I decided to make a makeshift bandage of my blouse and I reached to my hurt side to unhook my corset. It was tight, by design, and I had to compress it to get it off. As soon as I pushed pain blossomed in my abused ribs and I relented with a whimper of pain. Fuck, I could not even get my blouse off to make a bandage. Instead I slowly struggled out of my coat and cut off the sleeves. I tied them around my ribs to cover the wounds. I just hoped that I had managed to tie it tightly enough to stem the bleeding. I pushed carefully to my feet and swayed for a bit until I regained my balance. I had been knocked through the air and rolled down a small slope where I had come to a brutal stop against a boulder. I climbed the slope and found myself panting from exertion. I found my rifle on the ground where the strap had been ripped apart by the beast when it struck me and I bent to retrieve it. I stumbled and almost fell as I bent down but somehow managed to remain on my feet. To my relief I did not see Alissa's mangled corpse anywhere but it was quite obvious where the beast had gone. A large shrubbery was overturned with its roots stretched through the air and a large trail of blood led off between the trees. The wound my explosive shot had inflicted had been massive but it was only a flesh wound. It would bleed profusely but it had hit no vital organs. Assuming that these creatures where built like us humans who had all of our vital organs hidden within our ribcages. The beasts Alissa and I had slain so far seemed to support that theory. Worried about my new friend I followed the trail of blood. I racked the bolt of my rifle and caught the spent shell and gasped from the pain of my sudden action. I put the empty shell in my now sleeveless coat pocket. I would need all of the magic I could get my hands on when my headache subsided and I could treat my wounds properly.
