Gripping my rifle with both hands hurt, but I forced myself to do it in case I encountered another of the giant monsters. I am not sure how long I followed the trail, time blended into a long pain filled torture but I suddenly found it. It lay slumped on the ground in an ungainly heap and it was quite clearly dead. It must have chased Alissa and bled to death. I ignored the corpse and walked a circle around it, looking for the body of my friend. To my great relief I did not find her and could only assume that she had managed to avoid the beast. Hopefully she had not been fatally wounded before she managed to get away. To my dismay I found spatters of blood that was obviously not from the large monster. I followed the spatters for a dozen step where they suddenly stopped. Alissa must have cauterised the wound before she carried on. I found no obvious trail of where she had went and I returned to the corpse. I would need to eat to replenish the blood I had lost and the beast contained an abundance of meat. Maybe Alissa would return once she realised that she was no longer chased, if she still lived. A whimpering from the corpse made me stop suddenly and raise my rifle. The beast was not breathing but the low growl was unmistakably originating from the large mound of flesh and fur. A movement near its belly drew the line of my rifle and I cautiously crept closer. It was the smaller version of the beast that had first drawn our attention. The small creature pushed its head against its dead parent as it whimpered again. When I drew closer it turned its head at me and showed its small teeth as it growled at me. Despite its smaller stature I had no doubt that it was perfectly capable of savaging me if it got close enough but as long as I had my weapon trained on it I would be able to put it down long before it reached me. As I drew closer its growling turning into fearful mewling and it started backpedaling. It was obviously unwilling to leave its dead parent behind and it held its ground when I tried to edge it from its mother. I wondered if it was able to hunt on its own or if it was dependent on its mother. I needed the flesh of the dead beast to survive but I dared not ignore the little animal. It may attack me as soon as I turned my back. I considered my options. I could leave and let it be, but then I would forego the large meal ahead of me so that was not really an option. I could ignore it and risk attack as I butchered the carcass but my cautious nature warned me against that course of action. I could kill the baby and then be safe but I did not like that idea. The look in its eyes reminded me of the look of that poor little girl I had murdered despite being completely different. The girl had had fierce green eyes and this little thing had soft brown set in a face that could never be mistaken for anything remotely human. I hardened my heart and allowed the throbbing pain in my head and the burning agony of my side push my emotions aside. Feeling numb I held my rifle in my left hand and pulled my small revolver with my right. I cocked the hammer with my thumb and aimed at the baby's head.

"I'm sorry," and to my surprise a tear rolled down my cheek. It must have been from the pain. The sharp report of the shot echoed between the trees. Hopefully it would bring Alissa running. Feeling disgusted I holstered my pistol and drew my knife as I knelt and put my rifle on the ground. Using my left arm sent shivers of pain from my bruised ribs and left with only my right arm butchering the beast proved arduous and I soon found myself sweating profusely. I took a break and drained half my canteen in a single draught before I started cutting into the dense flesh. Blood was dripping down my elbow before I had managed to free a sizable piece of muscle. It was still warm and I realised that the beast had not been dead for long. I prepared to cook the meat with my magic but stopped myself when I remembered that I had almost passed out when I tried to cauterise my wounds. I resorted to eating the meat raw and I cut it into smaller pieces that I popped into my mouth. Despite my pain and regret at killing the baby it tasted marvellous. It was better than either of the two kinds of animal I had already tasted, despite it being raw. Blood dripped down my chin from the corners of my mouth but I did not care, it was too good. I finished the entire piece of meat I had cut loose and my belly strained against the confines of my corset and I regretted not being able to unmake it. I considered dissolving it but then my coat would go with it along with my makeshift bandages so I had to accept the tightness for now. Leaning back against the soft fur and the lingering warmth within the dead behemoth I struggled to remain awake. Sleeping while concussed was dangerous and I forced myself to free more meat. I made a bundle out of my coat to carry it and slung it over my healthy shoulder with the strap from my rifle. I shouldered the weapon and set off in the direction Alissa must have fled. Walking would keep me awake and if she had not come yet then she had not heard my gunshot, or she was not conscious enough to reach me. My mind went blank for I don't know how long, everything blended into a senseless state of pain and the focus to set one foot before the other. My head gradually cleared until I noted the sun was setting. I felt queasy and I was not sure if it was my injuries or the raw meat in my belly. I had seen no sign of Alissa and realised that I had not called out for her. I may have passed within yards of her without knowing. I decided that it was just as well. Now that I knew that there were very dangerous beasts in this forest it would be unwise to call attention to myself, even if it meant I would not find my friend. Silently I wished her the best, if she was even still alive. I found a stream and decided to make camp for the night. For the first time since I made landfall the dark of night seemed menacing. It felt as if I was surrounded by huge beasts just waiting for the best moment to strike. I desperately wanted some light to dispel my worries and realised that I could solve that easily enough. I dug into my pouch and withdrew the light crystal. If only I could activate it without passing out. I would just need a tiny bit of magic. I frowned at the crystal in my hand and focused. I swallowed down the bile that rose in my throat. I nearly shouted in triumph as the crystal blazed into life and rose slowly to hover above my head. The light revealed no menacing beasts around me and I drew a relieved sigh. A hysterical giggle escaped my lips and quickly turned into a pained groan as my abused ribs protested. I shook my canteen to gauge its contents. Half full. It was time wash my wounds and I untied my blood soaked sleeves. One of them had dried stuck in the wound and I gritted my teeth and ripped it loose. Fresh blood poured out of the hole in my skin. Fire danced in my wounds as I poured the water into them to wash away the grime. I wished I had some alcohol to clean them but I had to make do with water. I stuffed the soiled sleeves into my coat pocket and resorted to cut the legs off my pants off. I would have to walk through the forest in what was basically booty shorts but it could not be helped. I tied my new makeshift bandages around my ribs and forced myself to eat more of the meat despite my nausea. I was covered in cold sweats when I was finished and I might have already contracted a fever. I was too tired to make myself a bed of branches and instead just lay down where I sat. Without most of my trousers and the sleeves of my coat it would be a cold night but it couldn't be helped. I just hoped that my concussion had abated enough that I would wake up come morning.

## Chapter 11

Turns out that it had since I woke up at the first light of dawn, feeling as if I had barely slept at all. The pain in my head was lesser, at least as long as I did not move my head too quickly. A breakfast of raw flesh brightened my mood somewhat and I untied my bandages again. I crept down to the small stream and refilled my canteen to wash the wounds again. They did not bleed much and I decided not to try to cauterise them again. I dipped my finger into one of the holes in my corset in an attempt to gauge how deep they were and to my relief most of the force of the blow had been absorbed by my corset and my ribs had stopped the claws from going to deep. The rents were about the length of a finger but not deep. I would have some impressive scarring if I survived the coming weeks. I topped off my canteen and retied my ribs with my trouser legs. They were not that soiled and I chose to reuse them. I did not have anything left to make fresh bandages of anyway. Well, there was the sleeves of my blouse but I'd rather save them for the next round since my trousers would serve a couple of more hours. In the haze of the previous day I had lost all sense of direction and I glanced up at the sun. I made a guesstimate and started walking. The sun felt warm on my back and the air was fresh in my lungs. Despite my worries about Alissa and her wellbeing I was in a surprisingly good mood. My belly was full of meat no one in the Skylands had ever tasted before and I was Outside. I kept a wary eye for anything dangerous. The tranquil forest had lulled Alissa and me into a false sense of security. Just like back home there were dangers that could assault you without warning, out here it was just not people that were dangerous but beasts. I was not assaulted by anything sinister and a low sound reached my ears around midday. I had been considering a lunch break but I was unsure if the meat had spoiled by now. I had been about to smell it when the sound reached my ears and I was instantly on alert. It was not a sound I had heard Outside so far. I turned in the direction of the sound. It was low and melodious. Was it one of the flying animals that kept chirping? If so it must be much larger than the others I had so far seen since the pitch was much lower. The volume increased as I drew nearer and my curiosity spiked. It was a lovely sound and I am sure that the creature capable of making such a sound would not be dangerous. A hunter did not announce its presence in such a manner. I stepped around a tree and entered a small opening in the trees and froze. Just a dozen yards from me was a woman and she noticed me instantly. Her soft wordless singing cut off abruptly at my appearance. She was kneeling in the grass, picking something from the ground. Her hand was still in a basket on the ground beside her. She was wearing a grey dress made from some material that was quite clearly not made of materialised magic. She seemed as surprised at my sudden appearance as I was at encountering a woman in the woods. I smiled at her at the same time as I firmed my grip on my rifle. Her hand was hidden in the basket and she may very well have a weapon in there. I drew breath to speak when she moved with unexpected alacrity. She rose in a smooth movement and hiked up her skirts, flashing lovely tanned legs, and she darted away as fast as her legs could carry her. I stood in dumbfounded surprise for a moment before I launched into a sprint. Pain blossomed in my side and head at the sudden movement but I forced it aside. I had no time to hurt right now.

"Hey! Wait! I won't hurt you!"

If she heard me she showed no sign of it as she sprinted away from me, long dark hair streaming in the wind of her passage. I hobbled along as best I could but soon I only caught flashes of her between the trees. I could not spare breath to call out to her again and instead focused on even breathing. I darted around a tree and came to a stumbling halt at the sight before me. The woman was crouched before me, brandishing a knife but it was not she who had startled me into inaction. It was the girl in a combat stance before her. It was the girl I had killed back home. My eyes felt as if they would bug out of my head and my breathing came in ragged gasps that had nothing to do with my recent exertions. The world was spinning with her face in the centre. How was she here? How was she alive? What? I did not even register the glinting point of the spear aimed squarely at my chest. My hands twitched upward to block with my rifle as a ferocious snarl marred her pretty face when she twirled her spear and the butt of the shaft struck my temple and for the second time in as many days darkness claimed me to with a crushing sound.

Consciousness returned slowly along with yet more of the abominable pain. Waking up like this was getting old. The back of my head was resting against something soft yet firm and a damp cloth dabbed across my face. It is what had woken me up but I was not ready to open my eyes yet. Even the light coming through my eyelids were enough to blind me. I lay there and did not move as I let the cloth caress my face. The coolness of it was balm to my pain and by the gentleness of its touch I perceived no threat. After a while I cracked my eyes open a slit. Above me where the girl I had killed. She frowned slightly with concentration as she dabbed at my face, cleaning off the blood presumably. I studied her features and reassessed her. It was not the girl I had killed, but they were similar. Eyes a sparkling green with a speckling of copper and a mane of fiery red hair. This woman, though, was no longer a girl and looked like the dead child might have had had she had a chance to grow up instead of having my bullet shatter her femur. Gracefully arched eyebrows in the same colour as her hair perched atop her large eyes. Despite her red hair her face was only lightly speckled with freckles near her nose. Her full lips was pressed together, the tip of her tongue poking out the corner of her mouth as she worked. She looked quite adorable and I opened my eyes fully. Her eyes widened a fraction of a second and my head was jostled as she moved. Before I could react she had a knife pressed to my throat and her face was inches from my own. That was a rookie mistake. I could head butt her from that distance and get my arm up before she could do more than nick the skin of my neck. Cutting a throat is not something you do in one quick motion with a knife. It was messy work that involved some sawing and ripping. I kept my face calm and stared into her pretty eyes.

"Don't move." Her voice was a low hiss but it was quite audible due to our proximity. I had the sudden urge to raise my head and peck her on the lips just for her reaction but I kept still.

"Who are you?"

I saw no reason to lie. "Kyra."

"Very well, 'Kyra'. Where did you come from? How was it that you were in the Elwyer forest?"

I glanced down at the knife. "Do you mind? Do you have some water? I'm parched."

I said the words as an excuse to put some distance between us, or rather between my skin and the edge of the knife. She glared suspiciously at me.

"Don't try anything."

"I won't." I flashed her my most my most disarming smile but she did not seem to truly buy it. She scooted back from me and I winced as my head bounced against the ground. At least it was soft and did not crack my skull for a third time. She flowed smoothly into a combat stance, holding the knife point toward me and slightly upward in front of her belly. I reassessed my opinion of her fighting prowess, she apparently had some training. A memory flashed before me and again I saw her twirl her spear expertly to knock me out. Yes, she was definitely trained. I winced at the memory though and I silently berated myself for not manifesting my full armour after being wounded. I could only blame my concussion and worry over Alissa. I pushed the green haired woman from my thoughts in order to focus on the redhead next to me. I sat up and grimaced at a spike of pain through my head. I was getting sick of pain. As I raised my hand I noted that I had acquired some new bling. A thick bracelet of some sort of shiny material encircled my wrist and I was surprised to see runes inscribed on its surface. They glowed blue from the magic stored within. I glanced at my other wrist and saw a matching manacle. I realised that I was naked from the waist up, wearing only my impromptu booty shorts and a tight bandage around my ribs. They had even taken my shoes. Of course they had taken my weapons and I noted my corset and torn blouse in a small heap in a corner of the tent we were in. It was made of some sort of strange material, light tan in colour and opaque but the sunlight from outside still shone through and illuminated the interior adequately. I glanced wistfully at my blouse, they had shredded it getting it off me, most likely cutting it off my body before they knew the extent of my wounds. I reached up to my choker to dissolve it but instead my fingers brushed something cold. I was wearing a collar, presumably of the same material as my manacles. I studied the runes on my wrist until the woman handed me a flask of water made of the same kind of material as the tent. I grabbed it and it proved soft and slipped from my hand. I stared at it in surprise. A soft canteen? What the hell? I was too thirsty to think about it for long and I snatched it up, ripped out the stopper and poured the water down my throat. It was tepid, but I found it delicious. When I felt the water slosh around in my belly I replaced the stopper and put the skin beside me, away from the woman. I did not want her to take it from me.

"Thanks. You did not tell me your name."

She remained stubbornly silent.

"Very well. I'll call you 'Red'. Is it alright if I call you 'Red'?"

She scowled, but did not offer her opinion. She looked slightly confused at my demeanour. I suppose she had expected me to be frightened or angry but my careless attitude seemed entirely unexpected. I crossed my legs and faced her.

"So. What now, Red?"

Red seemed to regain her composure.

"I ask the questions!"

I nodded in agreement and waited patiently for her to continue. When she did not offer any questions I arched my eyebrow.

"Well?"

"Why were you in the Elwyer forest?"

"I was walking."

She scoffed. "No one walks in the Elwyer forest. You were chasing one of our foragers."

"I just wanted to talk."

"Somehow I doubt that."

"It's true. She was the first person I encountered in days." I chose not to mention Alissa. If my friend had survived I did not want these people out there hunting her. "Why does no one walk in the Elwyer forest?"

Red stared at me as if I was a simpleton.

"No one lives there. Now tell me the truth."

I considered my response carefully. My mission here was to assess the threat level of the Outside but I did not really care about the mission. I had just wanted to leave the Skylands but if I could do both at the same time then I would. Apparently no one lived in the forest so I could not claim to be a local, and judging by the difference in dress and technology she probably would not have fallen for such a lie anyway. I decided to tell some of the truth.

"I come from a place beyond the sea, on the other side of the forest. I am the first of my kind to ever come here."

"You lie. The ocean is endless."

My eyes widened in surprise at her statement. It was a ludicrous statement to claim there was nothing out there.

"I can assure you that there is. Where else would I have come from?"

"Any of the big cities. You carry weapons similar to theirs."

I was surprised again. Big cities? The Outside was supposed to be a desolate wasteland. Though given what I had seen so far I had no reason to believe the stories told back home. They were obviously false, intentionally or not. 

"Perhaps I do, but I wouldn't know since I'm not from there."

"Then how did you traverse the ocean?"

I went with another half-truth. "My people have just developed the means to cross the water and sent me here to scout."

"Alone?"

"No, there are others." I was sure that she would not believe that I had crossed the ocean by myself.

"Are they also in the forest?" I was not sure where the Pioneer had dropped off Raynard and the others but I chose to lie anyway.

"No. The rest spread out."

"You went into unknown territory alone, and the rest of you did as well?" Judging by her tone she did not believe me.

"No, we went out in pairs. I had another woman with me but we were attacked by a large brown furred monster. It did this, " I waved at my bandaged midriff, "and killed my friend." I managed to squeeze out a tear and Red's face softened somewhat.

"Describe this monster."

I did and her face paled at my description of our short fight.

"You killed a bear with a single shot?" I just nodded, trying to convey my sincerity with my eyes. Red regarded me in silence for long minutes and I could almost see the thoughts churning in her eyes. She stuck her head out of the tent flap and spoke softly before the rest of her body followed her head. A moment later a man entered and drew a large knife from his belt. I tensed, ready to evade if he tried to strike me but he merely took up a guard post inside the opening. He was tall and wiry and covered in furs. His long black hair was braided intricately and his eyes refused to leave me. I noted with amusement that his eyes was glued to my exposed breasts. I assumed that he would make the best out of his boring duty. I chose to ignore him and instead turned my attention to my manacles. They were not fettered to anything and I could move quite freely and I wondered what purpose they filled. I did not recognise the runes inscribed into them but then again, I knew little of runes. Perhaps the magic would confine me if I attempted to stray too far, or perhaps they would suppress my own magic to make me more manageable. My head was pounding too much for me to try them so instead I squared my shoulders and stared at the guard until he averted his gaze awkwardly. Apparently he had some decency after all. Red returned eventually and put a wooden bowl with some sort of grey sludge in it before me.

"Eat." She commanded as the guard left the tent with palpable relief despite a last lingering glance at my tits. I picked up the bowl and smelled the sludge. It smelled much better than it looked and I grasped the wooden spoon stuck in the mess. I took a hesitant bite and the flavour exploded in my mouth. It was really good and I shuffled it into my mouth, making appreciative noises as I did. I scraped the bowl clean.

"Red, this is really good. May I have some more?"

"Seriously? You liked it that much?"

"Yes! It's not better than meat but at least it is better than most of the things I've eaten."

Her eyes widened at that but she picked up the bowl and poked her head outside the tent and spoke to the guard. As she resumed her seat I heard her muttering under her breath.

"It's just porridge."

"Is that what it is called?" She looked up sharply.

"Surely you jest? You don't know porridge?"

I shook my head. Maybe if I volunteered some information about home she would be more talkative.

"Back home we only eat a fungus that lives in the caves beneath the city. It is utterly tasteless. I only tasted meat for the first time a few days back."

I neglected to mention that the upper class ate human flesh, I had a suspicion that that would not be greeted kindly. The guard returned with another bowl of porridge and I ate it more sedately.

"What is this tent made of?"

She stared at me incredulously.

"Well?"

"Leather. You don't know what leather is?" I shook my head.

"It is the hide of the buffalo."

"Buffalo?" I felt quite ignorant not even knowing what these apparently basic terms were. I guess I was ignorant when I thought about it.

"It is a large creature that we herd for meat, milk and their hides."

At least I knew what milk was, though none of us drank it after we stopped breastfeeding.

"Milk? May I have some?"

"Let me guess, you've never had milk either?"

"Nope. Not since I stopped suckling at moms teat."

She must have heard the longing in my voice when I spoke of mom for her face softened. She called for the guard to bring a mug of milk.

"Do you miss your family?"

"Yes, of course."

"Is it large?"

"Just my mom, and my daughter."

Her eyebrows tried to climb her forehead.

"You have a daughter? You don't look it." She gestured at my slim waist and my breasts that despite their size was still perky.

"Well, to be fair she is not mine by birth. Her father was a friend of mine and he died recently so I took her for my own."

Her fierce face softened further.

"What's her name?"

My eyes watered at the thought of the little dark haired girl. "Marissa." My voice was a soft whisper.

"What happened to your dad?"

"The government killed him when he was injured badly enough to no longer be able to work."

"That's horrible!"

I shrugged and winced at the pain in my ribs the motion invoked in my ribs.

"That is the way back home."

"I'm sorry."

"Don't be. It was many years ago."

The guard arrived with a mug that he handed wordlessly to me. I waited until he left before I took a small sip. Surprisingly sweet and went down smoothly and left a pleasant aftertaste. Much more pleasant to drink than water and before I knew it I had drained the mug. Regretting that I had not savoured it more I put the mug at my side and licked my lips.

"So, Red, what happens now? You can't keep me a prisoner forever. You must either release me or..." I left the other alternative unsaid but we both knew that the only other recourse was to kill me. 

"The Chief will return later today, or early tomorrow. He will decide your fate."

"That sounds ominous."

She offered no comment, merely nodded seriously at me.

"I suppose you won't tell me about your people before that?"

She shook her head. I felt suddenly tired, despite all the time I had spent unconscious these last few days.

"Then I think I'd like to rest now, unless you have more questions?"

"None that can't wait."

She would apparently remain to guard me so I simply stretched out on a thick mat by the edge of the tent and closed my eyes. Or at least that is what I wanted her to think. I kept them open a crack and watched her. When she relaxed back her entire body softened and transformed into a young woman instead of the fierce warrior attitude she had been maintaining for my sake. I suppressed a grin. She was not as hard as she tried to make me think. Perhaps tomorrow my head would have cleared enough for my magic to work and then I could maybe free myself of these manacles. I doubted I would be able to fight through an entire camp without my weapons, so perhaps I should bide my time for a better opportunity. Or maybe I should try to prove myself to them and live among them until the Pioneer returned to collect me. I slept.

## Chapter 12

When I woke up Red was gone and the black haired man was back to guard me. I caught him staring at my breasts again and without letting him know I had awakened fully I stretched with my arms above my head and my back arched. I glared at him and refused to cover myself with my hands until he looked away. Red barged into the tent unannounced with a grey dress slung over her shoulder. She dismissed the guard with a jerk of her head. Apparently she had some authority here, despite the man being her senior in years.

"The Chief returned in the night. He wants to see you but we gotta get you cleaned up. You stink and you can't meet him like that."

"I have not bathed in weeks."

She was surprised.

"But you came here in a ship!"

I realised that she thought that the ship had been floating on the water, apparently she could not conceive of a flying ship and I did not correct her. Instead I went with a truth that was not truly relevant.

"I can't swim."

"What about hauling water onto the ship?"

Damn, she had me there. I thought furiously for an explanation for entirely too long and eventually settled for a sheepish shrug. Strangely enough she seemed to accept that. She knelt next to me.

"Raise your arm." Puzzled, I complied and she started untying my bandages. Of course, I could not wear them if we were going bathing. I winced as she relieved the pressure and my battered ribs protested.

"Are they broken?" Despite my bravado my voice carried a note of worry. While I had broken my ribs many times before it was always a hassle.

"No, possibly cracked but not broken. You are lucky, bears are very strong and it must have been a glancing blow or it would have reduced you to a pulp."

I winced in pain. "I don't feel so lucky."

For the first time she chuckled and it was a pretty sound. Throaty and feminine. 

"I can imagine, but you are still lucky. The scratches look good."

I looked down and pushed my boob aside to see my wound for the first time. Neat stitches kept them tightly sealed and the skin seemed to be perfectly aligned. The scars I had thought would be impressive would be much neater if the stitches did not pop.

"This is very good work. Did you do it?"

"No, the shaman did."

"Pay my compliments. What's a shaman?"

She gave me an odd look.

"You truly know nothing?"

"I told you, I'm not from here."

"The shaman is our spiritual guide and healer. He speaks to the elements and heeds their council."

That sounded strange to me, but I was not really in a position to judge since I knew nothing of these lands. Back home the elements were kept at bay by the Great Barrier so perhaps we had just been cut from their voices. I had heard nothing from them since I arrived. Perhaps I simply lacked the affinity required. Red tossed my torn coat at me and I caught it. I noted that the pain had lessened when I caught it. I felt much better than yesterday. I shrugged into my coat and buttoned it to preserve my modesty, if I even had any to begin with. Red led me out of the tent and I squinted and held up my hand against the sudden bright light of the morning sun. The tent had become stifling during the night and the breath of fresh air woke me up superbly. I breathed deep of the air and noted an odd smell. It almost smelled like burning flesh and cloth but had other undertones. As two men, one of them the dark haired man who had guarded me earlier, fell in with us I turned to Red.

"What is that smell?"

Her brow furrowed in confusion as she breathed in deeply through her nose.

"What smell?"

"The smell..." I said eloquently. "It smells almost like burning corpses, but not quite."

"The woodsmoke?"

It was my turn to stare at her in consternation.

"You burn wood?" Then I remembered the overabundance of wood in the forest and it made more sense.

"What do you mean? Do your people not burn wood?" Her voice was laced with genuine confusion.

"No. We have no wood at home."

"Really?"

We passed through the camp that seemed entirely comprised of tents similar to the one I had spent the night in. There were people doing errands all around and all of them without exception stopped and stared at me. I noted them eyeing my purple hair and odd clothing. I saw none of them having dyed hair like I did and I must stick out like a sore thumb.

"Nope. We have nothing. We don't even have this shiny material my cuffs are made of."

"You don't have metal?"

"So that is what it is called. No, we don't have metal, or leather or whatever that dress is made of." I indicated the garment she still had slung over her shoulder.

"Wool. What are you making you things off? And what material is this?" She reached out and pinched the collar of my coat.

"The same thing everything else at home is made of. Materialised magic."

One of the guards coughed and sputtered and I glanced over my shoulder at him. His eyes were wide and his face was a picture of surprise. I returned my attention to Red and her expression mirrored his.

"You can materialise magic? But that is just a myth!"

I let out a chuckle.

"Not at all. Just a few days ago I thought trees were a myth and then I walked through a forest."

"I can't even imagine the amount of power that would require. It seems incredibly wasteful to me."

"Our entire city is made of the stuff. It is built atop a large magical geyser in the ocean."

She eyed me suspiciously.

"How large?"

"Hundreds of yards across."

"Your people must be like gods with that much power at the tips of your fingers."

"Not really. Quite the opposite actually. Most of the power is consumed to maintain the city, build buildings, manufacture things and to keep the Great Barrier up."

"Great Barrier?"

I winced as I realised that I may have said too much, but it could not be helped now. Might as well tell the rest, these people did not seem like a threat to the Skylands if they could not even traverse the ocean, much less the air.

"Our entire city is enveloped by an impenetrable barrier that even keeps the rain out. Nothing had entered, or left for centuries."

Red noted the past tense.

"Had? Are you referring to yourself?"

"Partly. We were attacked by powerful Mages. They broke through the Barrier and invaded but we managed to drive them away. They are the cause for my presence here. We were sent out to assess the threat to our home. We thought that there was nothing out here, that everything had died during the Apocalypse and that there was only dangerous magic out here." I glanced at her through the corner of my eye. "Obviously we were wrong."

"That would explain quite a bit," she turned to the guards, "wait here while we clean Kyra up."

"But..." She cut the man off before he could speak her name and I cursed silently. I really wanted to know her real name, though 'Red' suited her very well.

"I am sure I can handle one injured woman as she bathes, don't you think?"

He pinched his mouth shut, trapped. He could not deny her without indicating that she could not best me.

I followed her until the men were out of earshot until I spoke.

"Nicely handled. You caught him expertly."

She flashed me a pretty smile.

"Thanks. Here, clean yourself. Be careful, the slope is pretty steep."

I unbuttoned my coat and Red helped it off my wounded shoulder. Since I had walked barefoot I went straight for my belt and hooked my thumbs into the hem of my makeshift booty shorts and slid them down my legs.

"What on earth are you wearing?" Her voice was aghast, and was there an intrigued undertone?

I glanced down at myself, since I only wore my thong I supposed that is what she meant.

"Underwear?"

"But is goes all up in your crack! Isn't that uncomfortable?"

I let out a chuckle as I shook my head.

"Nah, it is actually quite comfortable. No bunching up of cloth. Besides, it makes my ass look fantastic."

I bounced it for emphasis and she let out an amused giggle.

"I have never seen anything quite like it. But you are correct."

I refrained from asking if she meant the part about my ass looking fantastic or the comfortability aspect.

"What do your people wear?"

"It is like a short skirt made of soft material."

I glanced down at her leg wear that was a sort of skirt of overlapping leather. I noted that the folds would open into slits as to not restrict her movement if she needed to fight. In fact, even the men wore the skirts.

"The men too?"

"Yes. Is that strange to you?"

I shrugged in response.

"Back home no man ever wears skirts. Except some Mages who wear robes."

"And the priests?"

"I am not familiar with that term."

"The men of who speaks with the gods?"

I narrowed my eyes. There were no gods.

"No. We don't believe in any gods. There is only mankind. Is there a difference between a priest and a shaman?"

She looked to the heavens in exasperation and she waved for me to return to cleaning myself before she responded.

"They are entirely different. A shaman speaks to the elements and the priests listen to the gods. We don't have priests, the elements are enough for us but there are men of the cloth in the cities."

Interesting. It seemed as if religion was rampant out here. I removed my thong and dipped my toe in the stream. It was colder than I had liked for my bathwater but warmer than I had expected.

"How deep is it?"

"About chest high."

I glanced at her chest to gauge the depth. I was quite a bit taller than Red so the water should only come up to my lower ribs. Excellent, I would be able to keep my stitches above the surface. I put a hand on the ground beside the stream and vaulted inside. I realised my mistake as my wound tightened as the stitches pulled but thankfully they held. My feet struck gravel and I hissed at the coldness surrounding me. I quickly adapted and the water was quite pleasant. The stream was neither swift nor strong and I could stand without any effort at all. Red tossed me a rough cloth and I soaked it in the water. I shifted my weight and raised my leg to be able to scrub my foot and ankle. The roughness of the cloth proved effective at rubbing a layer of skin and grime from my body and I realised that I would not truly need any soap. I might still smell slightly after this but no one would be able to accuse me of stinking. I scrubbed my other leg and then looked up at Red.

"Are you not going to bathe?"

"I bathed earlier this week."

"Seriously? You don't bathe every day if you can?"

"No. Why would I?"

It was an incredibly strange question to me.

"To get clean?"

"I am clean!"

I made a show of sniffing the air.

"I can smell you from here."

"You so can not."

"Can too!"

"Can not!"

I dipped my hand in the water and splashed at her. Perhaps displaying some playfulness would endear me to her. I needed an ally among these people, especially if I was to stand trial soon.

She sputtered as the cold water struck her face and chest and she blinked in consternation.

"Come in the water with me, it is quite pleasant."

"Fine, if it will shut you up."

With irritated movements she started to strip down, revealing a slender body. She was a small woman, even compared to the average but her lines were graceful and surprisingly full where it mattered. Her proportions were damn close to perfect and I felt a pang of jealousy. While I was no slouch myself I was somewhat over-endowed in the bust area for my frame and my thighs were not as graceful as Red's. The only thing marring her perfect pale skin was a wicked scar starting just beneath her left breast and trailing down her ribs to end by her cute belly button. It was curved and jagged and had obviously not been treated with the same care as my own. I pointed at it.

"Impressive. Must have been hell of a fight. I'd hate to see the other guy."

Her face contorted in fury but she swiftly schooled her face into a blank mask. The reaction surprised me. The fight must have been a painful memory but I decided to ask anyway. Not asking after pointing it out would have been weird.

"None of your business!" She spat the words angrily in response and I clamped my mouth shut. Everyone knew that angry redheads were dangerous. She leaped gracefully into the water with nary a disturbance to the surface and she vanished beneath the surface. She came back up and drew her hands through her hair to get it out of her face. The small waves on the surface just barely caressed her nipples that were rapidly stiffening from the cold. I tore my gaze away before she caught me staring. She scrubbed her arms furiously and avoided looking directly at me and I saw that she was visibly trying to calm herself. She drew a deep breath and let it out slowly.

"You have a set of impressive scars yourself."

"Thank you."

"How did you get them?"

I barked out a short laugh.

"There are too many stories to tell right now. I'm not even sure if I remember when I got each of them."

"You speak as if you have been in many battles."

"More than I can count."

She glanced at me, surprise and disbelief written plain on her face.

"But you are so young. You can't be that many years older than I."

"I'm twenty-seven. You?"

"Twenty-five."

"How many fights have you been in?"

"That I fought in? Not counting when I knocked you out, one. How have you managed to be in so many battles?"

"I'm a mercenary. I fought several times a week for years. It's how I earned my livelihood."

I carefully scrubbed the area around the stitches, trying to not pull on them too much.

"How could there be so much violence in one place."

Her words were not really posed as a question but I decided to answer anyway. Her reaction to my words would reveal much about the strength and values of her people.

"There are two and a half million people in my city and most of them are poor. Crime is rampant and policing practically non-existing. We mercenaries are hired for protection, assassination, 'protection' and sometimes outright battles between crime lords. Sometimes we are even hired by the police when they don't have the manpower for a raid."

"You said protection twice."

"Yeah."

"So?"

"The first one was actual protection, were we guard a person or deliver a parcel that is prone to be stolen."

"That is what I was expecting, and the other? I'm not sure if I understand how there is any other kind of protection."

"Well, it is like this. Imagine a shopkeeper. He obviously have some means. You offer your protection in exchange for money."

"How is that different from the first kind of protection?"

It felt almost bad explaining this to such a naive girl.

"If he doesn't pay you smash up his shop or even kill him to make an example for others. He is paying for protection against yourself."

"By the spirits, that is horrible."

I shrugged. "Such is life at home."

"Did you do this?" she asked, aghast.

"No," I lied. "I've never liked that kind of thing. I stuck with more honest work. Besides, my mom would kill me if I harmed innocents." I grinned to convey my humour. Of course mom would not kill me for something so simple as murder. Murder was almost a way of life back home.

"Your home sounds like a terrible place to live in."

"It ain't too bad if you just keep your head down and play by the rules. Break them and die."

She shuddered, and I was sure it was not from the chill of the water.

"But that was one of the reasons that I jumped on the chance to go on this expedition. If there truly was something out here I wanted to find it and if possible bring my mother and daughter here." I infused my last words with hope and hoped to garner some sympathy. It might have worked for she stopped scrubbing her chest and looked at me for a long moment.

"If you found such a place, would you stay there? Would you forsake your home and move somewhere else?"

Something in her voice made me stop scrubbing my own chest and I looked her square in the eyes.

"Yes." My answer was simple, but I realised that it was the plain truth. She nodded once as if making a decision and I felt hope for my current situation kindle in my breast.

"You better wash your hair, it is all matted with blood."

I reached up and touched it and true enough it was stiff with dried blood. I winced as my fingertips probed a tender area, the area where her spear had struck me. She noticed my wince.

"I'm sorry."

"What for?"

"For striking you. It's just that you frightened Jalani and you were armed to the teeth. Do all of your kind go armed so heavily?"

"It's fine. I would have knocked you the fuck out too if our roles were reversed. And no, most of us does not have as many weapons as I."

I did not mention that most of the inhabitants of the Skylands had anything other than melee weapons and the vast majority of those who had firearms only had single shot muzzle loaders that was both weak and inaccurate. They would kill you efficiently at medium range but anything approaching long range would be a pure gamble. A gamble with poor odds at that. The Guard and the special forces though were another matter. I was convinced that fifty, or maybe even half that, of the special forces would be able to wipe out Red's entire camp in an hour. They were armed with rifles like mine, but without the special bullets and they wore armour that was heavier than mine.

"I think I need some help with my hair, I don't want to submerge my stitches."

"Of course. Can you bend to dip it?"

I tried but failed. The stitches pulled to the point I was afraid they would pop and I told her so. She tapped her lower lip as she thought.

"Lie on your back on the edge of the stream, then you can tilt your head backwards into the water and I can wash it for you."

"Good idea."

Red had to boost me out of the water or I might have destroyed the shaman's good work. The edge of the stream was odd. The other streams Alissa and I had encountered had been shallow and the banks had gradually deepened. This one instead had an edge that was almost vertical as if it was cut from the ground. I asked her as much.

"It is an ancient canal. It was dug long before I was born, or even before my great-grandfather was born. No one knows who, or when, it was dug. It has just always been here."

I lay down on the soft grass and dipped my hair into the water. The sunlight burned on my watercooled skin and I closed my eyes against its glare until Red blocked it. Her fingers started working my hair, being careful to not rub my tender skull too roughly. For a fierce woman she had gentle fingers. I studied her upside down face as she worked and I caught her sneaking glances at my prominently displayed breasts. I chose not to comment but I think I caught a quickly suppressed expression of envy on her pretty face.

"I've never seen hair of a colour such as this."

"I'm not surprised. I did not see a single person in the camp with dyed hair."

"No, that is not our custom. I've heard that some people in the cities dye their hair when they are going grey. Are you grey haired?"

She peered down at me suspiciously.

"No."

"Then what is your natural hair colour?"

I smiled evilly up at her.

"That will be my secret for now. I dye it for a reason, you know."

She pouted slightly but did not press the issue.

"There, it won't get cleaner now without some soap but all of the blood is gone." I sat up on the grass as she climbed out of the water and I caught myself staring at the droplets of water dripping down her taught tummy. I tore my gaze from her scar. It truly was a thing of beauty and I desperately wanted to hear about the fight where she had earned it. 

As she sat down beside me I noted for the first time a tattoo on her arm, high up near her shoulder. I was surprised that I had not seen it before now. It was some sort of circular rune with thorns protruding from the centre and out through the edges. It was very pretty, in a savage way. It glimmered faintly of magic. I pointed at it.

"What is that?"

She glanced down at where I was pointing.

"It is my Clan tattoo. I earned it when I became a woman and was inducted into the clan properly."

"Clan?"

"Yes. We are all of the Clan."

"Does it mean anything specific?"

"It means Bizhjerai."

Well that was illuminating.

"It glows of magic. What does it do?"

Her eyes widened.

"You can see magic?"

It was my turn to be surprised.

"You can't?"

She slowly shook her head. "Only the shaman can. It is a gift granted to him by the elements."

That was not right. All humans could see magic, all it took was a bit of training. I told her as much and she was suddenly very excited.

"Can you teach me?"

"Perhaps. If your chief decides to kill me then obviously I won't be able to." She was pensive for a long moment and I let her think. Perhaps she would argue with the Chief that I may be able to teach her people things about magic that they did not know. That would be a powerful bargaining chip to tip the scales in my favour. She snapped out of her state of deep thought and looked at me appraisingly.

"So what does the Clan mark do?"

"You are not of the Clan, so I can't tell you."

"Fair enough. I hope that one day you may."

I left my words ambiguous and I hoped that he understood the hint that I may be willing to join her Clan. Anything to make her my advocate in the coming trial. The sun had dried us up but our hair was still wet and I looked around for a towel.

"Erhm, Red?"

"What?"

"You did not bring a towel. How will we dry our hair?"

She smiled slyly.

"Magic."

I rolled my eyes.

"I'm not sure if I can use magic yet. I am still concussed."

"I'll do it for you. Oh! I should have warned you already, you can't use magic. Not as long as you wear the cuffs."

She had confirmed my suspicions and I looked down at the fetters around my hands and feet.

"What will happen if I do?"

"It will absorb the power of your spell and turn it back on you. I'd recommend you not to test it. It will not be pleasant."

"How did you make them?"

I had never heard of such designs and in fact I had never even thought about it.

"We don't. We bought a set of them from another Clan. They have a blacksmith skilled in making magical metal items. Wait, how do you confine magic users where you are from?"

"We generally don't. Criminals, Mages or not, are usually summarily executed on the spot. For those who are not we simply drain them of their magic until they are on the verge of death and keep them in cells but that is a privilege reserved for the rich and powerful, if they are even prosecuted."

Her eyes widened. "You let criminals go free?"

"If you have clout or money then the police can't really touch you. No police would ever incarcerate someone who has a plan in place to send a hundred mercenaries after your family if you do."

She had apparently heard enough even though she seemed fascinated by my home. Her nose wrinkled in disgust and she changed the subject.

"Be quiet and let me focus and I'll dry our hair."

She closed her green eyes and her brows drew together. I watched her for several long minutes and my eyes kept returning to her scar. Suddenly I noticed that the top of her hair was dry and as I watched water started pouring out of it in an increasing torrent. It was an interesting approach, I myself would simply have heated my hair until the water evaporated but this seemed much more efficient though it must be more difficult given the time she had take to manifest the spell. Or maybe she was not that powerful and could not channel her energies as swiftly as I could. I was fairly certain that I would have been able to do it much quicker. I focused and drew on my personal power and shifted my magesense to my hair. Gently I coaxed the water to leave my hair and a shock went through my body. I convulsed and cried out as I fell to the side as my spell was drained of its power and fell in on itself. Shocks shot out from my collar and cuffs in an unrelenting stream of agony. As swiftly as it had come it left and I lay panting. When I finally opened my clenched eyes Red, her hair completely dry now, was watching me with a long suffering expression.

"I told you not to try to use magic."

"Sorry, I forgot. I saw your spell and wanted to try for myself. Drying my hair like that had never occurred to me."

"Really? How would you do it?"

"Heat."

"But that could set your hair on fire!"

I shrugged where I lay. "Only if you are careless." My leg, that was awkwardly folded under my hip, started to cramp and I sat back up and stretched it out to relieve the tension.

"Now shush and let me do your hair." She closed her eyes again and sat motionless for long minutes. I wondered if she would have been able to dry my hair with the same spell and my little episode had disrupted her focus. I sat there feeling ashamed as she worked and then I feel water stream over my shoulders and down my back. When it was dry I tossed it with a flick of my neck and a spike of pain stabbed between my eyes and the world wavered. Right, concussion. Don't toss your hair, Kyra. That was stupid. Red stood up and picked up the dress and tossed it at me. It fell gently over my head as I completely failed to catch it and I struggled out of its embrace. The, what had she called the material? Yes, wool! The wool was soft between my fingers and I rubbed my cheek against it. Marvellous that something not made of magic could be so soft.

"What is it made of?"

"Wool. I am sure I told you that before."

"Yes, you did. But what is wool?"

"Uhm. It is the hair of a sheep that has been spun into thread and then woven into cloth."

"Sheep?"

"It is a smallish animal with a great fluff of fur. I am sure you will see one soon, maybe even eat one."

She had referenced my inexperience with food that was not fungus.

"Oh, I would love that."

"Get dressed. The Chief will be waiting."

I stood up and stepped into the dress and laced it up the front. It was quite obviously one of Reds, though I could not picture her in anything but her warrior's garb, and it was fitted for her. Since I was taller it only came down to my knees while on her it would have gone to mid calf and I could not lace it up properly. My boobs strained against the confines on the cloth and it showed ample cleavage through the open laces. That could not hurt though when men would be deciding my fate in a matter of hours. On that thought I redid the lacing, tightening the lower ones and releasing the higher to make my cleavage really pop. I smoothed the cloth over my hips and made a simple twirl.

"How do I look?"

Red shook her head with an unreadable expression.

"How do you do that?"

"The dress is too small, and I have big tits."

"Not that. But how do you speak so casually about death and killing and then dress with the attitude of a woman preparing for a feast when you are actually heading to your trial?"

I had no real answer to that so I settled for a shrug that jiggled my breasts impressively. I would remember to shrug often during the trial. I gathered up my thong, coat and booty shorts. I had worn the thong for days now and the thin straps were soiled by blood on one side and I did not fancy putting them on so I stuffed them along with the shorts into the pocket of my coat. I would simply have to do without until I could reform them later. Assuming I survived until nightfall that is. Red had dressed swiftly and ushered me along.

"C'mon, the Chief is waiting. Let's get this over with."

With a sense of trepidation I followed her back to where the men was waiting. Idly I wondered if they had sneaked a peek as we bathed.

## Chapter 13

A short walk later and Red and our two male companions escorted us through the camp and everyone who saw us dropped whatever they were doing and followed us. It appeared that word of my trial had spread and it would most likely be a public affair. That may actually be in my favour since they then could not execute me silently. Perhaps I could win the crowd over somehow, though back home I was not known for my eloquence or influential manner. Red escorted me into a hastily erected pavilion. A foldable yet ornate chair had been set up in the centre and in it sat a man who looked somehow familiar. I was certain that I had never seen him before. He was quite obviously the Clan chief and he had just returned a few short hours before. Why was he so familiar? His hair was of a ginger colour that matched his bushy beard and he was a solidly build man. He did not look to be particularly tall, probably shorter than me but it was hard to tell with him sitting down. He was muscular but age had brought a layer of fat on top of the muscle and his waist and belly was as thick as his barrel chest. All of these details were made apparent by the skirt that was the only garment he wore. No, scratch that. It appeared to be a single long piece of cloth wrapped around his waist and tossed over one shoulder. The Clan mark on his shoulder was displayed proudly and the only jewelry he wore to indicate his station was a large cuff around his left arm made of what must be metal. It gleamed in the same way as my manacles but was of a yellowish hue. I glanced around and judged that the crowd around us must be hundreds strong. The Clan was larger than I had anticipated. Red bowed to the Chief and waved at me to sit down on a mat laid out before him. I did as she bade me and spent a moment arranging my skirts around my legs. It was rather tight on me and I sat awkwardly.

Red spoke without preamble.

"This is the prisoner."

The Chief nodded once and apparently dismissed her from his thoughts as his pale blue eyes regarded me intently. When he finally spoke his voice was deep and carried the tone of command. This was a man who would be right at home shouting orders in the din of battle.

"State your name."

"Kyra Zorantis." I wondered if I was expected to add some sort of honorific when addressing him but since Red had not warned me of any customary etiquette I chose to speak simply. If he took offence then his face did not betray it. It might as well have been sculpted.

"Where are you from?"

"I am from the across the ocean on the other side of the Elwyer forest."

A buzz of whispered conversation erupted from the crowd around us. Apparently Red had not spoken of me to the others.

"How did you get here?"

"A ship carried me here."

"Alone?"

"No."

"Where are the others?"

"I don't know, my friend and I was attacked by a," I glanced at Red for a moment to make sure I had caught the name of the beast correctly, "bear?" Red nodded.

"I was knocked out and when I came to my friend was nowhere to be seen. I tracked the bear by the blood and found it dead but still no sign of my friend. I fear she was slain before the creature died of blood loss."

"She killed the bear?"

"No, I did. I shot it before it struck me. Red here found me shortly thereafter."

His face twitched as I spoke the nickname I had given my fierce captor. Was that amusement? He changed the line of questioning abruptly. He did not try to argue any of my claims like Red had but his face was so unreadable that I did not know if it was because he believed me or merely hid his doubts. I suspected it was the latter.

"Why have we not encountered one of your kind before?"

"My people have been isolated for centuries, we thought that there was nothing left Outside since the Apocalypse."

"Do you mean the Cataclysm?"

"I don't know what you refer to. What we call the Apocalypse is the event that rent the world asunder with Wild Magic." He nodded slowly.

"It is the same event. Why did you suddenly leave?"

"My home were invaded. We have always been protected by a magical barrier but they managed to breach it and slay our citizens. We set out to scout and assess the threat level of the Outside."

"Who attacked you?"

"We called them Dragonkin. They were large and winged, led by a dragon with human Mages on it's back."

I held my breath, hoping that they would believe me. Perhaps dragons were common out here. Judging by the loud whispers from the crowd it was not the case.

"We call them Drakonids here."

I let out my breath in relief. At least they believed me.

"How large was this dragon?"

"It carried a dozen Mages on it's back. I don't know how many of the smaller creatures it had with it. I killed at least fifteen personally but many more were slain during the fighting."

For the first time his face betrayed a flicker of emotion, a tiny expression of surprise flitted across his still features.

"You killed fifteen Drakonids by yourself?"

I showed him my teeth in a not-quite-smile.

"I am not entirely without skills."

"What colour was the dragon and it's kin?"

"Gray."

"It sounds like Savistlin and her children. We have just heard that she was driven from her roost. She must have traversed the ocean for a new source of magic."

Dragons were rare enough to have names? And they were notorious enough for their movements to be known.

"She was one of the more powerful dragons of the Gray Flight, how did you manage to drive her away? You said that her Mages were guarding her?"

"I was leading a contingent of musketeers to fight her children who had a group of our elite warriors pinned down when Savistlin leaped upon us. I found myself beneath her and I cut the harness from her body before I climbed on top of her and killed several of her Mages."

Shouts of denial rang out from the crowd and even the impassive Chief regarded me with open disbelief. He raised an arm for silence and they slowly obeyed. Reds head had snapped around in a whirl of red tresses and she stared at me through wide eyes.

"They call me Dragonbane back home." I added swiftly before the Chief could speak.

"Are you claiming that you single handedly killed Savistlin?"

The silence was oppressive as the crowd awaited my response.

"No. I was just fortunate enough to survive her charge and get trapped within the shield her Mages erected. I distracted them enough for their shield to fail and our elite warriors chased her off."

"How did they manage that?"

"Without her shield our weapons wounded her gravely, or at least I think they did judging by the amount of bleeding. She fled into the night sky and her children followed."

I glanced around and was faced with disbelieving expressions. Apparently people did not fight dragons out here. The silence stretched out for long moments before the Chief broke it.

"I find your tale hard to accept. No healthy dragon has been killed in centuries, except by other dragons, and that took the concerted efforts of an alliance of cities. Granted they faced a whole flight but dragons are tough to kill."

"Be that as it may it does not change what happened. We have powerful weapons of our own, as well as our magic."

His eyes narrowed.

"How many Mages does your people possess?"

"Trained Mages? Tens of thousands but almost all of my people know at least some sort of rudimentary spell."

The crowd went wild and I heard several cries of "Ten thousand Mages? Impossible!" and similar. The Chief raised both of his hands this time and it took a solid five minutes before the din died down.

"And how many people are there in your Clan?"

"It is not a Clan per se, but at the last counting there were about two and a half million people on the Skylands."

I clamped my mouth shut as I spoke the name of my home but I needn't have bothered, the crowd went wild again. Apparently it was not possible for that many people to live in a single location. Apparently they did not have access to the same kind of old records that we did. They told of cities that had held tens of millions of people before the Apocalypse.

The Chief carried on the interrogation but the questions were mostly variations of those he had already asked me, presumably in an attempt to make me contradict myself. As the sun reached its zenith I was exhausted and sweat was dripping down my back. I hoped that there were no visible stains on my dress on display for the crowd or they may pick up on my nervousness. Eventually his questions dwindled and he stared icily at me in silence for long tense minutes. It was almost a relief when he spoke again but his voice had a tone that clearly indicated that he had started uttering my sentence and a weight appeared in my stomach. I squared my shoulders, resolved to meet my fate with dignity. I felt a fleeting disappointment that his icy blue eyes did not dip to my cleavage that heaved with the motion. My tits had apparently garnered me no sympathy at all. They had rarely betrayed me like this before. 

"I found your story outlandish and hard to believe, but we have little knowledge of anything beyond the ocean. It may be true, it may not. You will remain here while I consider your words and I will consult the Elements," he nodded toward a tall figure standing in silence beside him. I had not noted the man before, it was as if he had suddenly appeared before me from the thin air but I had sensed no magic in play. I realised that I had not sensed any magic since I was cuffed. Perhaps these magical manacles suppressed my senses. I did feel magic in the air though and with some focus I could 'see' the crowd behind me so it did not disrupt my magesense. The man who had appeared were covered from head to toe in leather and bones. His face was obscured by the skull of a horned beast and I saw only his glinting eyes gaze intently at me through the empty sockets of the skull. Pauldrons of what appeared to be shoulder blades covered his shoulders and a light breastplate of ribs covered his torso. The rest of his clothing was festooned with bones and feathers that rattled in the breeze. Breeze? I felt no breeze on my sweating skin and the air was stifling. I realised that this must be the shaman and apparently his powers were no myth. The Elements truly played at his whim.

"Until then you may move freely about the camp under the protection of my daughter. You will remain fettered and will not be allowed to touch weapons. Do you understand?"

Daughter? Before I could respond in the affirmative, for what other choice did I have, Red took a step forward and I could read surprise and anger in her posture.

"But I am supposed to join the hunt tomorrow, Father! Gaelon can babysit her."

The pieces finally clicked into place in my head and I understood why the Chief looked so familiar.

"Gaelon will take your place in the hunt. You captured her, you will guard her."

"But..."

"My word is final."

There was a tone of finality in his voice and I could hear Red's teeth click together as she bit back her retort. 

"Do you understand me, Kyra Zorantis?"

"Yes, Chief. I will remain here unarmed under the guard of your daughter."

With that the crowd started to disperse as they talked to one another excitedly and I could just barely make out bits and pieces of my own story being repeated. Red motioned for me to follow her and I did. Her small frame radiated rage and I chose not to speak until she did. She led me into the now familiar tent and I sat down on my cot as Red started pacing. Eventually she sat down and rubbed her face. I was mildly offended, was it such a chore to guard me? I had found our conversations quite pleasing and she had seemed quite interested in my home. Since she did not seem inclined to talk I let her fume in silence.

## Chapter 14

The next few days was quite pleasant even though my forced idleness grated on me. There were enough things to take my mind off of it though and I dragged Red around the camp, asking endless questions about every detail. I learned the terms for many of their items and customs and before the day was up Red had shed her rage and my curiosity seemed to infect her. Eventually every one of my questions was followed by a question about a similar item or chore from the Skylands. I answered as honestly as I could but withheld some information that may be dangerous for Outsiders to know. Red carried her spear with her at all times and had an ax in a steel ring on her belt and when I asked about her armament she looked at me as if I was an imbecile.

"I am supposed to be your guard," as if it explained everything. Come to think about it I guessed it did. She would have to at least appear to take her guarding duty seriously since it was a direct command from her father, the Chief, especially since she had been saddled with me against my will. 

The Clan did not seem to use much magic in their daily life and every instance of spellwork I saw was some small cantrip such as lighting fires or produce a magical light during the evenings. They actually cooked by burning stacked wood and holding the meat in the flames with sticks or other more sophisticated tools. It was quite extraordinary. When I first tasted the meat grilled over wood I almost passed out in pleasure. It was so much better than the meat Alissa and I had cooked with magic that it tasted positively stale in comparison. The taste of the smoke and charred flesh was exquisite. I ate until I felt I would burst and then I ate even more. Say what you will about my hosts but they were generally friendly and generous and they seemed very amused at my appetite. On the second night the word of my inexperience with food had spread around the camp and both men and women approached me to offer me a morsel of a special dish they had prepared. I gushed over them and complimented them and in return I told them some mundane tidbit about home that they seemed to find incredibly interesting. When I told them about the magic dispensers most people had at home their eyes went wide. Out here people just pulled magic from the air, what little of it there were. They had heard stories of a similar system in the cities but very few of them had ever been to see it. None of the cities seemed to do it at the scale that we did back home. I still had not revealed that our home was floating thousands of yards in the sky though, I think that may have be a little to much for them to accept right now. I'm not sure if they believed my story about the dragon but at least they did not call me a liar to my face.

On the third day Red wanted to train with her weapons and she brought me to the outskirts of the camp were there was more room. She had brought an assortment of weapons, among them a relatively slender and short staff with a string between the ends. I wondered at its purpose and Red rested a shield against a small solitary tree on the plain and walked away from it.

"What is that weapon?" I asked her with interest.

"It's a bow. We use it to shoot arrows."

She smirked at my confused expression.

"Watch."

She drew a slender stick from a cylindrical bag made of stiff leather and put the end against the string. She raised the bow and bent it using her entire torso and both arms. It looked heavy and she grunted with the effort. Then in the same smooth motion she released it and the stick sailed through the air. It embedded itself right next to the metal boss of the shield. I looked back at Red, completely unimpressed. She pouted a little at my lack of reaction.

"You don't have bows in the Skylands?"

"Nope. Never even heard of one."

"What kind of ranged weapons do you have?"

"Muskets and pistols, mostly. Some of the elite soldiers have rifles but most people only have melee weapons."

She loosed another arrow at the shield.

"May I try?"

She bit her lip uncertainly before she finally decided that giving me a single arrow to loose would not pose a significant threat to anyone and she handed me the bow and an arrow.

It was indeed heavy to draw, even with my superior strength and I took careful aim. My arm tired swiftly and I almost dropped the string when I let loose. The arrow went wide and vanished into the grass beyond the shield. Red laughed at my failure.

"You were aiming too long. The draw weight is much more than you can sustain, you need to draw, aim and loose in the same movement."

She handed me an arrow and I tried again. This time I did not get as tired in my arm and shoulder but the arrow went wide anyway. She gave me a few additional pointers and my next arrow came much closer to the target. I only missed by a couple of yards.

"Here, let me show you."

She stood right behind me and reached around to put her hands on mine. I pushed the feel of her supple body against my back aside and focused on her words as she breathed them into my ear. She had to stand on her tip toes to see over my shoulder. She guided my hands to nock the arrow and then she pulled on my wrists to guide my movements. I let loose and the arrow bounced off the metal rim of the wooden shield. I glanced over my shoulder at her and found her face inches from mine.

"I thought you were good at this thing?"

"It is difficult when I am not doing it myself. Try one more time, then lets move on to other weapons."

My next shot was the closest yet but I gave up to never be good with the bow. Give me a good pistol any day and I smirked at the thought of the effect that my rifle would have on the shield. One of the exploding shots would reduce it to so much kindling.

"What are you smiling about?"

I shook my head. "Nothing." I offered her an enigmatic smile. She tossed me a metal sword and I jerked in surprise but still managed to catch it.

"Relax, it is blunt."

I glanced at the edge and saw that she was correct. It was not heavy enough to inflict significant harm either. I might be able to crack a skull or shatter a collarbone with a well aimed strike and the point would still be dangerous with enough force behind it but otherwise a blow with it would be a mere distraction.

"Let's do some slow work, I have a few techniques I want to practice."

I nodded. I was familiar with slow work. It was when you sparred with the blades but you toned down the speed of your movements. The point of the exercise was not to win but to refine your technique. I swung the blade to get a feel for the balance. It was weighted farther toward the point than I would have preferred and it pulled to the right when I swung it. I guessed metal would be more difficult to shape than just growing a blade from magic so I excused the blacksmith for the poor balance. See all these new terms I'm already using? Red sank into a guard position and I emulated her. We traded a few slow strokes to get a feel for our weapons and each other before we launched into more intricate manoeuvres. Her inexperience showed in her movements and I decided to take advantage of it. I feinted a thrust to her thigh and she went to block it. I halted my thrust and twisted my wrist to flow into an elbow cut at her shoulder. With her blade completely out of line and her body leaned forward she was completely open and I left her with only one recourse. If it had been an actual fight and I had used my full speed I would have cut her shoulder open, effectively ending the fight by disabling her sword arm. She took the only way out she had and stepped forward to come around behind me. I knew exactly what she would do and was already moving forward and in behind her. She had guessed that I would press the advantage and had brought her sword into a defencive guard to her side but I was suddenly behind her. I spun on my heel and swatted her with the flat of my blade on her bottom before I danced away. She yelped and spun around, her face turning almost as red as her hair.

"Don't block strikes for your legs if you don't have to. Slip the leg instead. Your parry left you wide open, otherwise you did a good job!"

She visibly bit back a retort as she accepted my advice. "I'll show you, thrust at my leg as I did."

When she did I tried to sidestep but I got caught up in my skirt. I still wore the dress Red had lent me for the trial and it was still way too tight for me. I grunted in surprised pain as the point of the weapon impacted solidly on my thigh and pushed the muscle into my femur.

"Hold on." I tucked my sword under my arm and reached down and tied the skirt to my side. It left my legs exposed from mid thigh but that could not be helped.

"Again."

She thrust and I simply dipped my leg aside. In the same tempo my sword arm flicked out and thrust from above and from the right and my point brushed lightly against her shoulder.

"You overextend slightly and it leaves you off balance. It would have been fine if I had not been taller and had greater reach. I could strike you even after my retreat. Since you are short you need to close the distance before you can strike and maintain your balance."

She nodded and her face set into a focused grimace.

"Go in for a feint first and when my sword leaves me open you can get close. Only then attack."

She thrust at my open shoulder and I moved to block it and she tried the same elbow cut I had. I blocked it and counter thrust at her face but she leaned aside and I missed. She slipped her blade low and went for a push cut across my ribs but I merely folded my arm back down and trapped her sword against my ribs. With my weapon occupied to lock hers I simply reached out and grabbed her throat. Reluctant to let go of her weapon she was unable to dodge my grasping fingers. I squeezed firmly to hammer home my point.

"Always be prepared to ditch your weapon, and always carry a backup. Now that I have you I can..." I let my words trail off and yanked her close and before she knew it I had released her blade and had my point pressed into her right breast. Her own weapon and offensive arm was behind my body and she would be unable to harm me. I smiled into her face and pushed her away.

"Don't get me wrong, your technique is really good and if we had been fighting for real I would not be this confident but at the slow work I can beat you with experience."

"You don't need to try make me feel better."

Despite her words I could tell that she appreciated my compliment. We sparred for a bit and she landed a few solid blows on me but I still won more than two thirds of our bouts. She was getting frustrated and I suggested that we take a break for water.

"How are you so damned good at this?" Her voice was a bit petulant and I could tell that she was angry at herself for her failures.

"I have been fighting for my life constantly for years, and you have only been in a single fight by your own admission. A fight you have yet to tell me about."

Her lips pressed together and she refused to answer but she did seem a little bit less frustrated.

"Let's do some unarmed sparring."

"Alright."

We took up positions and she assumed a boxers stance. I emulated her, but I had no intention of boxing. I fought dirty. She kept bouncing on her feet, shifting her weight between her legs which struck me as odd. I identified the pattern of her shifting as we circled and as her weight was on her back foot I surged forward, throwing out a light jab more to test her defense than to actually strike her. What happened next surprised me and I was not sure what happened. She was blindingly fast and my jab struck nothing but solid air. Her fist thundered into my midriff and I doubled over with the breath streaming out of me in a whoosh. Her arms may look smooth but she packed a serious punch. Her knee struck me in my wounded ribs and I fell to the ground panting. She smiled evilly at me as she kept bouncing, face flushed with victory.

"What happened to the proud Dragonbane?" she mocked. I slowly regained my feet and gingerly touched my side and checked for blood. My stitches may have ripped from such a blow. Her expression turned into one of horror as she realised what had happened and she moved closer in concern.

"I'm sorry, I did not think of your wound!"

When she got close enough I drove my shoulder into her chest and wrapped my arms around her and tackled her to the ground. Much of my pain had been feigned. I managed to turn her on her belly and force her arm onto her back. She squirmed and yelled in frustration.

"You don't fight fair! I thought I had hurt you."

I leaned in to whisper in her ear.

"Fair is bullshit. There are no rules in a brawl, only victory." My snicker was cut off when she threw her head back and smacked it into my face. The distance between us was too small for her to gain proper momentum and I was more startled than hurt but my grip weakened enough for her to scramble away and up to her feet.

"Thanks for the tip. I'll keep that in mind." Then she vanished in a blur and I felt her fist strike my uninjured side. I was prepared for it and merely grunted. Then the fight was truly on. She was blindingly fast, much quicker than me, and she packed a punch. In an outright fistfight she was more than a match for me but I did not fight like that. I went in for a grapple and if I got a grip on her slippery body I would win. When we both breathed in hard pants and were covered in sweat I was covered in bruises from her small fists but we had won roughly the same number of bouts. I won grappling almost instantly but she was adept at avoiding my grip. Eventually we called it quits and went to wash the sweat from our bodies.
