I washed the dress in the water and Red dried it for me. I mentioned her scar again in an attempt to get her to tell me about it but she clamped up stubbornly. I offered a few stories about some of my more interesting scars but she was in no mood to reciprocate. I left it alone for now but my curiosity had only increased at her reticence. Our sparring set a pattern for the rest of the week. I would gorge myself for breakfast and then we sparred for a few hours before a bath and then I gorged myself again at lunch. The afternoons I pestered her with questions and I offered more information about my home. Eventually I started to wonder if the Chief had forgotten about me. I found it slightly odd that I had not yet heard anyone address Red by her true name and I was too stubborn to ask her again. I had asked her once and she had refused to answer and thus I would keep using the nickname I had given her. In fact, I did not see many people talking to her at all, at least not in my presence. Red showed me that the Bizhjerai did indeed have firearms. Roughly half of their warriors could be equipped with muskets but the black powder they used to load them with had to be purchased from merchants from the cities at a high rate and thus they saved it for major battles. For hunting and skirmishes against the other Clans they used their bows. The bows they could make themselves and there were plenty of wood to make arrows. She showed me the powder itself and described how it burned swiftly and generated much smoke. It was similar to the magical flash powder we used at home and I realised that our weapons had been designed to replicate these weapons. We had merely substituted the wood, metal and black powder with materialised magic. I hefted one of the muskets, unloaded of course, and aimed down the barrel. It was similar in weight to the muskets from home, slightly heavier and weighted a bit differently. I desperately wanted to shoot one to see if the were more or less accurate than ours but I did not even ask. I knew Red would not allow it, not until her father decided to either free me or kill me. And perhaps not even then. I was starting to lose my patience with waiting when disaster struck.

## Chapter 15

I awoke to the unmistakable sound of a gunshot and was instantly on alert. A moment later a multitude of voices rose in alarm and I pushed to my feet. Were the camp under attack? My guard, who I learned was the man Gaelon that had replaced Red on the hunt, stared intently out the opening in my tent. He usually guarded me during the night when Red went to her own tent to sleep. It was the same dark haired man who had been so fascinated by my boobs and he seemed to whole heartedly approve of the dress I still wore. For once though his eyes were not glued to my cleavage and I could see the muscles of his jaw clench. He glanced over his shoulder when he heard me sit up and he waved for me to remain. I ignored him, as he had ignored me whenever I had tried to speak to him, and joined him at the opening. If we were attacked I wanted a weapon. Just sitting here I would be a at a severe disadvantage if any invaders found me. More gunshots rang out and Gaelon spoke to me for the first time.

"Stay here." He started to leave and I began to follow. I would not sit idly by, waiting for someone to come by and slit my throat like one of the buffalo at the slaughter. He spun around and put his hand on my chest and pushed me back inside. I stumbled back when he spoke a single word.

"Kyrtos!"

I had no idea what it meant by my manacles blazed into magical light and my arms were inexorably drawn to my legs. I folded under the pressure and was swiftly neatly bundled up on the ground. My legs folded up behind me and my wrists reached back to rest against my ankles. It was seriously uncomfortable but it effectively rendered me motionless. Gaelon left me like that and I yelled after him to let me go but as usual he ignored me. Distant sounds of fighting reached me and I yelled in impotent frustration. I wiggled and tried to roll toward the tent flap but realised that I would be even more exposed outside in my current state. Instead I yelled whenever I heard footsteps nearby.

"Hey! Let me out! I can help!"

No one arrived to set me loose on these invaders. Despite my being a prisoner here these people did not seem like bad people and they had indeed treated me well even though they had nothing to gain from it. If I could help them, I would. I don't know how long I lay there but I was sure that people were dying out there. Someone burst into the tent and I tried to roll away from them. If it was an invader I wanted to get as far away from them as possible to buy myself some time. Hands pushed on my shoulders and rolled me to my side and I let out a relieved breath when familiar red hair glinted in the moonlight from outside.

"Sytrok." The voice was familiar but with an edge of fear and excitement that I had heard many times in the voices of mercenaries before a fight. I was very suddenly released from the magic binding me and I stretched and rolled to my feet. Red stood before me, geared for war. A pistol was in her belt in addition to her normal weapons and plates of stiff leather and metal protected her forearms, legs and thighs.

"We are under attack. Now that I know you are safe I need to get out there. Stay here."

I grabbed her arm as she whirled about to leave and I pulled her back around.

"I can help. Give me a weapon, or better yet give me my weapons."

She searched my face as if uncertain of my intentions.

"For fucks sake, Red, we don't have time for doubts. Arm me and let me loose, you know I can fight them!"

"Will you surrender your weapons after the fight?"

I could tell that she wanted to add "if you survive" but she did not want to insult my prowess.

"Sure, fine."

"Do you swear?"

I looked into her eyes and tried to convey my sincerity.

"I swear." I was surprised to realised that I meant it. I had never before even considered willingly surrender my weapons but I would if she asked me.

She stared into my eyes for long moments but a sharp crack of a nearby gunshot snapped her out of it. She touched my collar and spoke a short incantation and it fell to the floor along with my bracelets and ankle fetters. My magic returned in a surge and for the first time I realised how much I had missed it. It was like drinking water after almost dying of thirst, or finally scratching that itch that you had been unable to reach for days.

"Hold on."

She watched me with consternation as I undid the lacing of my dress and shrugged out of it. My choker still lay on a small foldable table in the corner and I snatched it up and put it on. I gathered up my torn and bloody clothes that still lay where I had discarded them and bundled them under my arm and set my choker to manifest my full armour and dissolve the bundle.

"Alright, I am ready. Take me to my weapons."

Red did not question my nakedness and instead she pulled the axe from her belt and handed it to me. I was not experienced in the use of axes but it would do for now.

"Follow me!"

She dashed from the tent and I hurried after her. We rounded a tent in the opposite direction of the sounds of fighting.

"What is happening?"

"Grasax' warriors are to the south, engaging our main force. A group of flankers attacked from the east and they are already in the camp. We have warriors searching for them but be ready."

She bent down and put her fingers to a woman lying on the ground but swiftly moved on. I could have told her the woman was dead already but she seemed to want to make sure. A spear launched out of the darkness to my right, aiming for Red's side but I knocked it to the sky with my axe and leaped toward the man who wielded it. He looked like any of the other men in the camp but his hostility was plain on his face. I found myself within his guard and he danced back to bring the point of his spear to bear. I dropped my mostly dissolved clothes and grabbed the shaft to keep him from retreating. Red's spear whistled by my ear and the man was forced to let go of the spear and twist to the side to prevent his face from being impaled. It gave me the opportunity to sink the axe into his thigh and he fell to the ground. A quick chop into his skull put and end to his struggle, and his life. I put my bare foot on his face and twisted my axe free. I glanced at Red and she nodded in thanks. Her eyes were wide and wild and showed whites all around, from fear or bloodlust I did not know. She set off again and I followed. My armour was partly manifested when we came upon two more of the flankers, one wielding a wooden club and the other a short sword. I charged the sword wielder as Red engaged the clubman but I could not spare any attention to her fight. The axe was much shorter than my favoured backsword and I found myself at very close range with the swordsman. His sword was much more nimble than my axe and he managed to get in a few shallow cuts on my arm and shoulder before I managed to hook the axe around it and pull it out of line. He tried to reclaim the blade and did not see my free hand soar toward his throat. He stumbled back, gasping for breath as the heel of my palm struck his larynx and it gave me the opening to put my axe into his neck right were it joined his shoulder. I wrenched it loose and blood poured from the gruesome wound. He was still not down yet, even though the wound would prove to be fatal and he scored my corset with the edge of his sword. I danced back and assumed a purely defensive pattern. I just needed to outlast him. Sure enough, his blows weakened as he swiftly bled dry and when he stumbled I struck him with the axe in the head. My edge alignment was off and it did not bite into his skull. Instead it folded and struck him above the ear with the flat of the head but it was enough to put him on the ground. He tried to rise weakly but the blow and blood loss made him clumsy. He would not get up again and I dismissed him from my thoughts and whirled to aid Red. She did not need my help as she twirled her spear and struck her foe over the ear with the butt of the shaft. It was the same move that had knocked me out the previous week. He reeled back and was wide open. He swung his club in a blind defensive movement and Red watched it sail past her harmlessly. She stepped back, brought her spear neatly into line and thrust flawlessly to impale him through the neck. He fell limply and silently, she must have damaged his spine with her perfect thrust. She stared at the corpse with a wild expression.

"Nicely done."

She stammered something unintelligible at me.

"What?"

"That was my first."

I was puzzled. "First what?"

"My first kill."

"Really? That thrust was perfect, very practised."

"It was so easy. I had thought it would be more difficult but he stood no chance."

I squeezed her shoulder but she seemed unable to tear her eyes from the corpse that stared blankly at the moon.

"I told you before, you are very good. Let's talk about this later. Now take me to my weapons."

She snapped out of her fugue and flashed me a wild grin before she launched into a jog. I hurried to catch up. She stopped just a few tents over and ducked inside. I followed her and summoned a magical light. We did not have time to let our eyes adjust to the murk inside. My weapons lay neatly laid out on a small table and it was quite clear that someone had been studying them. Red, maybe? Or someone else? I put the thoughts from my mind, we had a battle to join. I put on my gauntlet and loaded my revolvers and slung my weapons belt around my hips. I made sure the sword was loose in its scabbard before I picked up my rifle. I hesitated for a moment before I slammed the magazine with the simple kinetic rounds into the weapon and racked the slide. My armour finished manifesting as I did and I looked up at Red through the slits in my helmet.

"I'm ready. Let me go first, then you can lead me to the battle."

She nodded and brandished her spear with both hands. She was as ready as she would ever be and I extinguished the light. I waited for half a minute for our eyes to adjust to the sudden dark before I burst out of the tent. Three men whirled around at my sudden appearance. One was armed with an axe and shield, one with a spear and the third held a bow. He drew an arrow and loosed it at me before I had assessed the situation fully. The arrow was slow and I twisted to the side and the arrow glanced off of my armoured corset. He drew another arrow and I aimed my rifle centre mass. The weapon spoke and he reeled back with a hole in his heart. His fingers slackened and the bowstring sang. He managed to maintain his aim and the arrow punched into my corset perfectly. The crystal proved too hard and the arrow shattered in a rain of splinters. I racked the bolt and ejected the spent casing. The two remaining men howled and charged as the next round chambered. Red darted around me to engage the axeman over whom she had the advantage of reach. I aimed at the spearman and evacuated his skull in a spray of blood, brains and bone splinters. Red jabbed her spear into the shield of the axeman and he hooked his weapon around the shaft to lock it. He twisted his shield and ran up the length of her weapon, keeping it locked against his shield. He had not understood yet that his friends were dead or he would not have ignored me in this manner, I was sure of it. They had underestimated my weapon. Red had heeded my earlier advice and let go of her spear and reached to her side for her axe, the axe that she had given me and we had forgotten in the tent. She yelped and ducked beneath the swing of his axe. I stepped close and almost laughed at his surprised face as he saw me unexpectedly appear in his field of vision. I demolished his surprised face by slamming the butt of my rifle into it and he stumbled back. I hooked my foot around his knee and pulled and he fell heavily on his back. I leaped forward and drove my sharp heel through his temple and he stopped moving instantly. I wrenched my foot clear and shook of the memory of how I had used that very same move to put a small child out of her misery. Red scrambled to retrieve her spear and darted into the tent to get her axe. She was sliding it into the ring on her belt as she returned. She was looking a bit embarrassed when she did. I racked the slide on my rifle.

"How did you reload that swiftly?"

I grinned. "I'll explain later. It is actually an incredibly clever design, but there is no time. We need to help your people."

She did not respond, instead she led me through the camp back the way we had come toward the sounds of fighting. We encountered another group of three invaders but I dropped them with precision shots of my rifle. I reloaded, slotting the magazine of special rounds into the weapon. I racked the slide and pressed my thumb lightly against the selector gem and the rune flashed as a spell was infused into the chambered round. I grinned evilly, I really wanted to see how effective this one would be. We emerged from the camp and I surveyed the scene before me. The opposing forces were arrayed a hundred yards from one another. The attackers outnumbered us two to one so far but the Bihzjerai had one advantage. The front row were not armed with muskets, instead they shouldered large shields plated with metal to shield their gunmen from the incoming fire. The Bizhjerai behind reloaded and fired with impunity, but their shots were not very effective. At that range the majority of the shots would go wide, either slamming into the ground between the forces or go high above the heads of the enemy. Red and I was to the side of the line and so far we appeared to be unnoticed. I dropped to my belly to present a smaller target and lined up my sights as I heard Red assume the same prone position next to me. Even over the din of battle I could hear her father shouting orders to his warriors. I had guessed correctly about his voice.

"Shield up!" I hissed at her and she awkwardly scrambled to loose her shield from her back from her lying position and held it before her. I aimed at the closest flank and aimed at the chest of a man raising his musket. They were not firing in volleys and as I watched the muscle flash of the man ignited the flashpowder on the man next to him as he was ramming the shot home. His weapon discharged and completely destroyed his hand as the ramrod launched into the sky and the shot ripped off his fingers. He stumbled back, screaming as he cradled his hand to his chest. I shifted my aim at the man next to the shooter who had just finished reloading. He was a more imminent threat than he who had just fired who would be reloading for at least ten seconds. I squeezed the trigger and the rifle bucked against my shoulder. The man fell back, a bloody crater torn in his chest. Flames of magic spewed from the wound as he fell but I did not wait to inspect my handiwork. The spell would take a few moments to ignite so I shifted my aim farther down the line. I thumbed another spell into the round I chambered and fired as soon as I lined up my sights. I did not fire directly at a warrior this time, instead aiming at the ground between the first and second rank. The round whistled past the legs of a man assuming firing position and struck the ground in shower of dirt. Before I could even rack the slide the round exploded in a ball of flame. The man lost his legs and the man beside him was thrown back in a shower of shrapnel. Their formation broke in the centre as several men was thrown from their feet and the rest scrambled to put distance between themselves and the explosion. I fired another such round at the right flank and it dissolved into similar disarray. A shot whistled past above my head and I knew then that my position was compromised. As long as I was lying prone I did not really fear getting hit, and even a lucky shot would probably not pierce my helmet but it would knock me senseless for precious minutes if not put me out cold directly. I glanced at the first man I shot and saw him crawl back onto his feet. Blue flames of magic burned in his eyes and he raised his musket like a club. No one paid him any mind, even when he brought the butt of his musket down onto the head on one of his fellows with what must have been a sickening crunch. The man fell heavily to the ground and it was obvious that he would not rise again. He killed two more in quick succession before his companions noticed that anything was awry. They turned to him with hesitant movements, obviously uncertain what to do. Their hesitation vanished when he lashed out at them and several drew short swords from their belts. One man was about to stab him in the back and I shot him with a similarly imbued round. I racked the slide and squeezed off my last shot, this too imbued with the same spell of temporary undeath. It was one of the most complex spells I had ever seen and I briefly wondered how Kendall had gotten access to it. It was not a common spell and must have cost him a small fortune. Then I did something stupid, but entirely necessary. I slipped the sling of my rifle over my head as I stood and launched into a sprint.

"Kyra, wait!"

I ignored Red as I drew my revolvers, the small one in my left. I held my left forearm across my body and manifested my shield. It was large enough to protect my torso and upper thighs but I did not want to spare power to shield my legs. It would be a lucky shot indeed to hit them. A flash of red at my side announced that Red had joined my suicidal charge. Fuck, I'd much prefer her to stay back. I was heavily armoured compared to her and may be able to fend for myself once among them but her light armour would make her easy pickings. Shots flattened against my shield as I charged. I summoned up my limited blood magic to push my legs further and swiftly outpaced my friend. I would pay for this expenditure of energy later but for now I had reserves to spare. I dashed across the space between the two opposing forces and I fell into a long loping gait, each step twice as long as they would have been without my blood magicks. I just hoped that the Bizhjerai would take advantage of the disarray I had sown and join me. If they didn't I'd soon be dead, and Red along with me. I was almost halfway to them when they put their undead friends down. Undead were hard to kill, and only the destruction of their brains or hearts would truly put them down but dismemberment would still incapacitate them. I was within revolver range but I kept my shield up. I had spotted several men raising their muskets at me in concert and a fusillade such like that would ensure at least some of the shots hitting their intended target, yours truly. The shots rang out and two struck my shield. A wooden thunk from my side told me that Red had been hit too but I could not spare her any attention. As the musketeers started reloading I dropped my shield and raised both of my arms to aim at them. At this range, and with them so tightly packed, accuracy was a moot point. I fired almost blindly into the mass of warriors with both revolvers. I wasted shield breaking spells on these normal warriors but the kinetic impact was enough to drop them regardless. Two men fell to the blood poison and they started melting almost immediately and two more fell as their entire torsos burst open from the inside as my explosive rounds found their marks. My left hand revolver was less impressive, but no less efficient. I holstered my revolvers and drew my sword just a few steps before I struck their line. They had started backing away at the sudden death and maiming of almost a dozen of their compatriots. Two brave men stepped into my bath, bracing their feet to receive my charge and raising their muskets as spears, holding them horizontally to block my body. Instead I dug my heels into the ground and stopped right before them. They blinked at me in surprise, apparently having expected me to charge bodily into them. They were so surprised at my sudden halt that they let me kill them. I slashed the throat of the leftmost one with a backhanded elbow cut and let the blade carry on as he dropped his musket and raised his hand to his partly opened throat. Cutting throats is not easy and my slash had gotten stuck in his larynx, it did not matter for he would pass out from blood loss to the brain within moments and would die shortly after that. The slash brought my weapon into line for a thrust through the chest of the other man and that was exactly what I did. My enchanted blade pierced his heart in a perfect thrust and I shouldered him aside before he could strike me with his musket like a club. Even a fatally wounded warrior would be dangerous for a few more moments. I came face to face with a woman aiming her musket square at my face. At this range there was no possibility that she would miss despite the inaccuracy of her weapon. She would hit me straight in the face. I started ducking aside and raising my arm as my shield winked into being but I knew that I would not have the time to properly infuse it with power. I needn't have bothered for a spear launched from my side and knocked the musket aside. The woman's finger clenched reflexively on the trigger and she fired her one shot into the sky. The spear carried on and slashed her startled face open before it was swiftly withdrawn back into line. The spear lashed out and took her between the breasts. She stumbled but did not fall and she dropped her weapon and grabbed the spear to trap it even even as she was dying. To my relief Red ditched the spear, she had remembered my lesson, and raised her shield as she reached for the axe on her belt. Good thing she did for a sword embedded itself into the wooden surface a moment after she had ducked behind it. The attacking warriors were circling around us and I reached beneath my coat to crab a crystal from a snug hoop on my belt. I pressed my thumb against the large facet on the top and I felt a surge of magic. I lobbed it over the heads of the warriors and manifested my shield. I found myself back to back with Red as we fought but we were at a disadvantage. The warriors had superiour reach when they used their muskets as clubs but the ones with swords had to come within striking range to attack us. I dared not go on the offensive at the men with longer reach or I would leave Red exposed from the back. The crystal I had thrown detonated and men were thrown through the air as the violent death was unleashed. The explosion was not the primary effect of the spell embedded within though and I could see the bodies of those struck burst into blue flames as their souls and magic was ripped from their bodies when their mortal frames weakened. The ethereal, screaming forms was pulled through the air as they were devoured by the spell. I lashed out with my blade, cutting a bloody groove down the chest of an attacking woman and I smiled grimly as bloody fat poured out of her bisected breast. She fell back and was replaced with a large man whose fists where blazing with fire. Apparently these guys did know some magic after all. Before he could launch any of the flames at me I sensed the soul draining spell reaching its peak and I spun around and dropped to the ground. My feet swiped Red's legs and she joined me on the ground with a startled yell. She kept her cool and covered her body with her shield and curled her legs beneath. The spell ignited with the power of the souls it had devoured and a ring of crackling power erupted in an expanding circle. A few who noticed were quick enough to drop beneath it but many more were caught unawares or were too slow to evade it. The ring was at about waist high and it cut through them. The power burned brightly and sizzled as it cut men and women in two. Bisected bodies struck the ground around me and the battlecries turned into screams of agony as the still living upper halves writhed in pain and panic. Most had passed out of shock but many still retained consciousness. I leaped back to my feet, swiftly joined by Red. Those outside of the range of the spell stared at the carnage with wide eyes. Experienced as they were they had not faced a Skylander before and had not expected the swift death available at my fingertips. An evil smile curled my lips and I barked out a short, cruel laugh. Our opponents backed away from us but I would not let them. I ran toward them with my sword ready to strike. I was out of surprises, but they did not know that and bloodlust had overcome me. I used my personal energies to set a pair of them on fire with a tongue of flame from my palm. A woman dropped her weapon and fell to her knees in front of me in surrender and I nearly severed her head in one stroke. Instead my blade caught on a vertebrae and she fell to the side as she started to drown in her own blood. A loud keening sound permeated the air and men struck the line from my right. The rest of Clan Bizhjerai had joined the fray. The attackers were already in disarray and not in any shape to receive a charge and the battle swiftly turned into a mixed melee. Friends and foe were on all side and I found it difficult to tell them apart. I let Red take the lead and supported her. She seemed to have no problems finding enemies and I attacked those she did. We proved a deadly team. She would engage an enemy and I would keep others from her back or attack her target as she kept them engaged. I suffered several heavy blows on my armour but none did more than rattle me. I suffered a number of minor scratches on the insides of my arms that were not protected by crystal plates but they did nothing more than make the grip on my sword slippery. Before long the blood started to dry on my hands and actually made my grip more secure. Suddenly the ground heaved and I was almost thrown off my feet. Several others were not so lucky and tumbled to the ground. A crack appeared in the ground and molten rock poured forth. Somehow none of the Bizhjerai warriors were touched by it, only the invaders were burned by the raging inferno. Had the shaman joined the battle? The enemy broke and turned tail and fled in a disorderly rout. Many where cut down from behind and I torched a fleeing man with magic before he got out of range. I sheathed my sword, disregarding the blood and other more fleshy bits that would get lodged within, and unslung my rifle. I reloaded with my spare clip of kinetic rounds and started picking off fleeing warriors. I ejected the last casing and cursed. I had no more magazines before they recharged and I hadn't had time to fit the first one into the charger. The magic field here might not have been enough to recharge them in time anyway. Several of the Bizhjerai warriors had given chase in their bloodlust but the Chief ordered them back.

"Let them go! We need to secure the camp!"

I followed Red back into the camp and joined the search for any lurking invaders. We found small groups of them here and there setting fire to tents or supplies but they did not put up much of a fight. Many tried to flee when they realised that their fellows had been defeated but none made it out of the camp alive. The sun was rising as we killed the last one but one more hour passed before the camp was proclaimed safe. Red smiled at me, her face flushed with the thrill of combat and victory.

"We won, Kyra!"

Feeling suddenly exhausted I merely nodded and pulled her into a one-armed embrace. I noted many of the Bizhjerai around me looking at me with fearful eyes, several of them tightened their grips on their weapons. I could sympathise with their fear, they had all seen me in combat and I was still armed and was after all an outsider. The Chief pushed past his warriors and faced me without fear. Either he trusted his daughter's judgement, he was not afraid or he hid it well. Remembering my promise to Red I unslung my rifle from my shoulders and the warriors tensed, several going so far as to raise their reloaded muskets at me. They did not aim directly at me, probably because Red had stepped in front of me to block their line of fire. She glared at each of them in turn until they looked away before she faced her father.

"Father. I think that our 'guest' have proven herself tonight."

I put my hand on her shoulder and pushed her aside. Or rather I tried to push her aside. Her body resisted and I was unable to budge her.

"It's fine, Red, I did swear an oath after all."

I dropped my rifle and let it gently soar to the ground on a cushion of magic. It was much more intricate than my revolvers and I did not want to handle it with any undue force if I could avoid it. I unbuckled my weapons belt and it joined the rifle on the ground before the Chief. With a thought my armour started to dissolve and transform into my usual outfit with the corset, choker and coat. I hoped that they would let me keep my choker so that I would not be forced to wear that too small dress again. While I did enjoy the way it made my boobs look it was far from practical. I held out my hands for the manacles, more like a gesture of good faith than actual necessity since they most likely still lay on the floor of the tent I had been held.

"I believe you are right, Anjali, but she is still an outsider."

Anjali? Had I finally heard Red's true name? I much preferred my nickname for her. It was also weird that he called me an outsider, when he was quite literally an Outsider himself from my perspective. Though from his perspective I could see his point. I decided to rejoin the conversation and I spoke loudly to make sure that all present heard me.

"I mean you no harm, you have my word. I pleaded with Red to unleash me when I heard the gunshots and she did so after requesting my oath that I would return to captivity once the threat was over. I will gladly do so while I await your judgement." I shook my hands to indicate that I was willing to be cuffed once more. I realised that I meant it, normally I would have lied or done whatever was required to ensure my return to freedom. But these people had impressed me with their generosity and simple enjoyment of life and I was filled with sudden admiration for them. They had just been attacked by a foreign Clan but calm had already returned to the camp. Wounded were carried from the battle and were treated with familiar hands. Raids such as these must be somewhat common. The Chief seemed to come to a decision and he nodded once, firmly, before he spoke.

"Very well, I have come to a judgement. Kyra Zorantis proved invaluable in this latest incursion by the Outcasts and I thank her on behalf of Clan Bizhjerai for her aid. She will remain with us and her weapons will remain in our care but she is free to move freely in the camp under the escort of my daughter, Anjali. She is a friend of the Clan and is to be treated as such."

The warriors around us relaxed visibly and Red offered a beaming smile at me. For the first time I noted the blood trickling down her face from a slash above her temple. The blood made her already fierce features even more striking. More blood ran down her thigh from a nasty gash and concern washed through me. Before she could react I had knelt beside her and pushed her leather skirt aside to reveal her pale, smooth skin beneath. The only thing marring her was the oozing wound. It was a neat wound, a glancing thrust from a sword at my best guess. She started to pull away but my grip on her thigh was firm.

"Don't, let me look at this."

I wiped blood away with my palm before I glanced up at her with a grin.

"This will be your second impressive scar."

She returned my smile hesitantly but she allowed me to inspect her wound. How she had managed to be slashed on the inside of her thigh was beyond me. You rarely thrust at the legs, they were too easy to pull aside. Cuts was much more effective. I pinched the wound shut with my fingers and I heard her hiss in pain.

"Sorry."

She did not offer a reply so I got to work. I aligned the edges of her skin as best I could and then clamped the wound shut with telekinetic staples. I was almost like stitches, but tighter and the blood flow stopped almost immediately. I poured water onto the wound from my canteen to wash her skin before I applied a band of force around her leg to put pressure on the gash.

"There, should be good as new in a couple of weeks, if not less. Though I can do nothing for the pain."

"I'll manage. Thanks."

"Don't mention it. You saved my ass back there, this is the least I could do."

"I remember you saving mine as well."

I shrugged. "I was armoured, I could afford it."

"Speaking of armour, how does that work? It just appeared on your body!"

"Magic." I bared my teeth in a wicked grin and she rolled her eyes. Before she could respond her father approached us. He had been watching the whole process intently.

"You are a resourceful woman, Zorantis."

"Please, call me Kyra. And you learn a few things about survival when you are a mercenary in the Skylands. Danger is all around and those who does not learn swiftly die young."

"You are not that old yet."

I smiled without mirth. "No, but I learn quick."

He pointed at his daughter's leg.

"Can you do the same for the rest of the wounded?"

"I can treat lighter wounds easily enough, but anything too serious is beyond my power."

"Do what you can, please, the shaman can deal with the worst. Anjali, watch her. The rest of us have cleaning to do."

With that he walked away, followed by most of his warriors. They did indeed have a field of the dead to take care of. Red and I found the shaman at work next to a long line of wounded warriors and he barely glanced up as we approached. He offered a grunt in greeting before he turned back to pushing the entrails back into the belly of a wounded man. I was astonished, did he really think he would be able to fix that? Only the most skilled of the healers back home would be able to bring someone back from such a gruesome wound. It would be much kinder to just put a bullet in his brain and get it over with. I decided to give the shaman the benefit of the doubt. He would not be wasting his time after all. I walked down the line of the wounded and treated the lighter wounds much like I had Red's and before long only those who were beyond my power remained. I stood up and wiped my eyes before I realised that I had just given myself bloody eye shadow. All I wanted was to sleep but I squared my shoulders and started walking toward the battlefield.

"Where are you going?" Red jogged to catch up.

"To help with the cleanup."

There were a lot to do before any of us could rest.

## Chapter 16

It was almost noon when we had gathered all of the fallen Bizhjerai and laid them out in a long row. Only fifty of the clansmen had fallen during the short battle but almost the same number of non combatants had been killed within the camp. Even children had been murdered and several of the corpses were charred from when they had been trapped inside their burning dwellings. I hoped that they had died quickly. The invaders were left where they lay to rot and be feasted upon by the carrion. I carried the last of the fallen on my own even though I staggered beneath the dead weight. Red had moved to aid me but I waved her off, I wanted to carry him to his final resting place myself but I was unable to put him down with any grace. The back of his head smacked into the ground with a dull thump, but he was beyond pain now. Even though he had hardly spoken to me I had spent many a night with his watchful gaze upon me. I had found Gaelon outside a tent and he was covered in wounds from head to toe but it was the shot through his head that had finally put him down. We had found several children, women and young boys inside the tent and seven dead invaders around his corpse. One invader lay inside the tent and one of the women told me she had killed him. She would not have had a chance if Gaelon had not wounded him severely first. I knelt next to the fallen warrior and looked into his glazed over eyes. He had given his life in defence of the helpless and I could not help but admire him. I had never done anything even close to that noble. I killed for money, necessity and sometimes the for the hell of it. Such was life at the Skylands but these people were starting to show me another way to live. On a sudden urge I lifted the fallen mans hand and cradled it in my own before I opened his slack fingers and used his still warm flesh to cradle my breast.

"What are you doing?"

I did not look at Red, unable to tear my eyes from his dead gaze.

"He had been thinking about these for days, he must have wanted to touch me."

"Undoubtedly. In life Gaelon was a hopeless womaniser and he always had a fondness for ample bosoms."

I put his hand gently on his own chest and reached out to forever close his dark eyes.

"Did you ever?" I let my voice trail off, it was not my place to ask her that.

"No, though now I kinda wish I had. He died heroically."

I stood up and faced my friend.

"He did, though I don't know why. He must have known that he could not defeat eight men on his own."

Her graceful eyebrow arched.

"He nearly did, if that last man had not had a pistol he might have. Besides, he did whatever any of us would have. He protected his family, even with his life."

"But you said he was a womaniser? I did not realise that he had a wife and kids."

"He didn't. They are Bizhjerai."

They way she made the pronouncement finally hammered home what the Clan meant to these people. They were one big family, no matter their relative interpersonal relationships. I nodded slowly in understanding.

"Come, let us find my father. I am sure he would like to speak to you more."

I followed Red back into the camp and when we entered the rows of tents we were met with a small panic. People were bustling around and searching and cries of dismay sounded from within tents. I saw a panicked woman screaming for her child, a wild look on her face.

"What is going on?"

Red shook her head. "I don't know. We need to find father, quickly."

She started to run and I pushed my tortured muscles to follow her. We found the large warrior in the middle of camp. The state of his mind was obvious by the way he was pacing back and forth as he listened to a steady stream of warriors approaching to report to him.

"Father, what is going on?"

He faced his daughter with a weary expression.

"The attack was a distraction. The Outcasts have abducted our people. We don't know how many were taken but judging by the footprints it must be almost seventy people missing."

Red was stunned for a moment, an expression of shock twisting her pretty features.

"We need to go after them, now! Before they gain too much of a head start."

The big man shook his head.

"It is too late, we will never catch up to them before they reach Dun Traelak, not if we want to be in any state to fight them. They are lost."

Red sputtered but I could see the sense in his words. I did not understand, why would these Outcasts sacrifice so many of their own to just take a few scores of the Bizhjerai? What was Dun Traelak? I held my tongue but made a mental note to ask Red about it later.

"We can't just leave them there! Who knows what Grasax will do to them!"

There was that name again. Grasax. Who was he?

"We can't take Dun Traelak. Many have tried and all have died. The place is impenetrable. My word is final daughter. Go. Rest. We will speak more about this later."

Red opened her mouth to retort but I put my hand on her shoulder and she turned her head to glare at me. It was the first time she had looked at me with anger, and I did not like it. I shook my head slightly. Her face reddened to almost match her hair and she pulled her arm out of my grip and stalked away. I hurried to catch up to her.

"The fuck are you doing here? Aren't you going to stay with my father, doing nothing?" She spat the words with vehemence.

"You are my watcher, remember? I would not want you to get into trouble for leaving me without a babysitter."

My attempt on humour was the entirely wrong thing to say and she pressed her lips together. I decided to forge on anyway.

"What are you going to do?"

"I'm going after them with whoever will follow. We can't leave our Clanspeople to their fate!"

I grabbed her arm again and pulled her to a halt. She tried to struggle free but my grip was like iron.

"Listen to me, Red! Your father is right."

"So we should just leave them to Grasax and his vile tortures? Is that what you are saying?"

I drew a deep breath to calm myself down and bit back an angry retort. It would not do to snap at her right now.

"Of course not, and of course we will go after them. But we have to be smart about it. It would be pointless to just throw ourselves at them. You are exhausted, and so are everyone here. We should rest and recover and then plan with a clear head. I will go with you, even if no other will."

I tried to convey my sincerity with my eyes and I seemed to get through her angry haze for her shoulders relaxed.

"You would?"

"Yes. I'll follow you right now if you still want to go but I would much prefer to do this properly instead of running off half cocked and getting us both killed."

She drew a deep breath and let it out slowly. "What do you propose?"

"That we go clean ourselves off, then rest. The funeral is tonight and we should be there. Tomorrow we can start making plans. How long before the Outcasts reach Dun Traelak?"

"Not long, a week at the most."

"Then we have at least a week before Grasax does anything to them."

I was speculating widely with my limited knowledge but it would seem that I was correct since she did not object. Without a word she spun and started walking.

"Where are you going?"

"Bathe. I want this blood off of me."

I followed her wordlessly and set my clothes to dissolve. I wanted the same thing. We walked in silence to the stream with the steep edges and stripped down in silence. I left my partly dissolved clothes on the shore but kept my choker on. The tightness around my throat was reassuring. Red watched me as I removed my corset.

"What?"

"Something looks different about you..." her eyes widened in sudden realisation, "your boobs! They've shrunk!"

I glanced down and saw that I could see the tips of my toes peeking up around my breasts, something I normally would not have been able to.

"Yeah, blood magic will do that to you."

"Blood magic?"

"Your people doesn't use it?"

"Never even heard about it."

I gathered my thoughts as we stepped into the water, trying to figure out how to best explain the concept.

"It is a magic that is fuelled by your body, by the energy stored within," I reached up and cupped my breasts, "like fatty tissue, for instance. It can only, with a few exceptions, affect the body and I used it in the battle to run faster. I temporarily increased the efficiency of my muscles, but it comes at a heavy cost. See, you can almost count my ribs too. Not only fat from my breasts were used and my legs are killing me right now."

"Why?"

"The stress on the muscles and joints. They were not built for that kind of work. Think of it this way, if I push against the ground when I run with twice the strength than I usually do it is as if my body weighs twice as much. My knees were simply not built for that."

Her face furrowed in confusion as she absently scrubbed blood from her abdomen.

"You made your body twice as heavy?"

"What? No! I pushed with twice the strength."

"How does that make your body heavier?"

"It didn't, but the effect was equivalent."

It dawned on my that she knew little of physics.

"I push twice as hard against the ground, and since the ground won't move it will accelerate me forward but due to my momentum it is as if I had doubled in mass. Do you follow?"

"No, but I will take your word for it."

"It's not important right now. Tell me about these Outcasts, and Grasax."

She was silent for a long moment and I took the opportunity to dunk my head beneath the surface and scrub at my scalp. I resurfaced in a wash of water and I wiped it from my eyes before she spoke.

"Let's start with the Outcasts, they are easier to explain."

"Fair enough."

"Some crimes that is irreconcilable among my people but does not warrant death results in exile."

I connected the dots quickly enough.

"And they are the Outcasts."

"Yes, and most of them join Grasax. He is the only one in the region who will take them in. That is what differs the Outcasts from the Clanless. The Clanless lives solitary lives in an attempt to regain their honour. There may be hope for them to someday rejoin their Clan."

"Who is Grasax, and why does he accept these Outcasts?"

Red dipped beneath the surface and I waited patiently for her to finish with her hair.

"No one knows who he was before, he has lived in Dun Traelak for as long as anyone can remember. He is a liche."

I was not familiar with the term and I told her so.

"An undead Mage. He sacrificed his humanity for immortality. He needs mortals to sustain his unlife. That is one of the reasons he raids for slaves."

"And the other reasons?"

"He experiments on them. The area around Dun Traelak is filled with monsters of his creation. Some are pure magical constructs, others are the twisted bodies of his victims."

We lapsed into silence as we finished cleaning ourselves and we climbed back onto the bank to dry in the midday sun.

"Are these monsters the reason why Dun Traelak is considered impenetrable?"

"Partly, but it is also surrounded by a barrier that none have been able to breach. Once, several hundred years ago a group of shaman gathered to entreat the elements to tear down the fortress but they were unable to breach the barrier. They had to give up the siege eventually."

I wondered if the barrier was the same kind of shield that protected the Skylands. If so it would require some sort of generator on the inside, and would need a source of power. Such a barrier would block the magic field from entering and recharge the spell. Unless the barrier was raised when enemies were nearby, and in that case you could sneak in and disable it or simply wait it out. If there was an internal source it would get much trickier. Could there be a magical geyser in the old fortress? Was that why the liche had taken up residence? No, Red had told me that he needed mortals to fuel his power so that could not be it. That was not completely true when I thought about it. She had said that Grasax needed mortals to sustain his unlife, not to power his magic. When I asked her about specifics she seemed confused about the distinction. I cursed her peoples lack of magic and the associated engineering. While I myself was no savant in the subject most people on the Skylands understood the basics of magic. It was too central in our survival for it not to. I lapsed into silence, my thoughts churning over what I had learned. I had no doubt that Red would make good on her promise and try to flee her Clanspeople and before she did I had to figure out some way for her to survive and if possible succeed. What I needed most was knowledge about Dun Traelak, but most of what Red told me seemed to be second hand knowledge, if not worse. I needed to see this place, preferable the insides to gauge any weaknesses but time was against us.

"If the barrier goes down, do you think we can take the fortress?"

Her answer was immediate, and full of certainty.

"No. Not alone. Even if we gather the whole Clan we would not be enough. Dun Traelak is not large but it is very well fortified."

I was surprised, I had thought that this camp was the entirety of Clan Bizhjerai.

"Are there more of you?"

"Yes, there are several more camps like this, as well as the main hold."

I was astonished, that was more people than I had expected. Just to make sure I asked her how many warriors they could field.

"Around a thousand trained warriors, possibly twice that if we arm the women and untrained men. But even then we would have no chance of breaching the fortress, not even with the barrier down."

"Then we need allies. Are there any other Clans that would join us?"

Sudden hope brightened her eyes.

"Possibly Clan Ithlak. They have suffered greatly at Grasax's hands, but it would be difficult to persuade them to sacrifice their warriors in an assault. The only reason that Grasax is tolerated is that it is much more expensive in lives to oust him than defend against his raids."

"That and the barrier."

"That too. Do you think you can bring the barrier down?" I tried to not take offense at the doubt in her voice.

"Not with brute force, but it sounds like the same kind of magic that we use back home to guard the Skylands. If it works similarly I might be able to figure out how to bring it down."

"That is a big 'if'."

"Do you have any better ideas?"

"No," she said reluctantly.

"Then the first step is to rally the Clan and find Ithlak. How long will that take?"

"If we send word immediately, perhaps two weeks to gather the Clan. Persuading Clan Ithlak? I don't know. Their lands are closer to Dun Traelak so they would be able to muster more swiftly than Bizhjerai."

My clothes had finished manifesting on my body and I stood up.

"We need to speak to your father, now."

"It is better if I speak to him alone. I'll leave you in your tent on the way."

Her words surprised me.

"My tent?"

"Yes, you've earned it. And we have many to spare after today."

Despite her grim words I was pleased. I had a home from home now, something I had never before imagined. Red dressed swiftly and we returned to my tent. Despite my agitation of her pending conversation with her father I fell asleep almost as soon as I stretched out on the bedroll. It had been a long day, even though it was still early in the afternoon.

I woke up as night fell, still feeling tired but such was the price of blood magic. It may still be several days before I felt restored. Red sat leaned against the central support of the tent and she was quite obviously asleep. I watched her for long minutes as she slept peacefully. She had exchanged her torn and bloodied leathers for a fresh set and her axe was cradled across her thighs. She was taking no chances even though I doubted that the Outcasts would return. They had paid too heavily in blood, despite their prize. She awoke with a start and her eyes found mine.

"How did it go?"

"He and the Elders were not entirely convinced but they all saw you this morning. Your magic is powerful and they are desperate to get our people back. They have already dispatched messengers to the rest of the Clan and to Clan Ithlak. We break camp in the morning and move speak with them."

I was surprised at the alacrity of the decision. Back home the discussion would have carried on for weeks and possibly getting lost in the bureaucracy.

"They trust that I can bring the barrier down despite several failed attempts in the past? Just like that?"

She smiled ruefully.

"No. But they are willing to take the chance. If you fail we can always leave again and nothing would have changed except for an unnecessary campaign."

I could not fault their logic. I glanced out through the tent flap. It was getting dark and it was time for the funeral.

The entire camp was gathered outside by the row of bodies and a large pyre had been built as I slept. There were little ceremony, the Chief walked down the length of the row and stopping by each body and spoke about each person. He knew each of them by name and described their deeds in life before they were gently put on the pyre. The pile swiftly became macabre as they were piled on top of one another. The shaman approached and wordlessly raised his fists to the sky. Flames erupted along his arms and he ignited the wood with streamers of flame. Everyone had lost someone today and not a single face was dry. I reached up to scratch my cheek and was surprised that my fingertips came away wet. Not even my hardened heart was immune to the sombre mood it would seem. We watched the pile burn until the corpses were unrecognisable and people started to drift back to their tents. No one celebrated the victory for it was cloaked in such sorrow.

## Chapter 17

We woke up early the next day and the camp was taken down with a swiftness that surprised me. The tents were loaded onto wagons pulled by the hairy buffalo and off we went. Most of the people were on foot but many of the warriors sat astride long limbed beasts that Red had called horses. I did not trust them and I refused to sit astride something with a mind of its own. Instead I walked next to Red as she sat atop a glossy brown horse. I glanced between it's legs and I assumed it was female. Maybe horses did not have the same parts as humans? I looked at a few of the others and that suspicion was swiftly dispelled. They had quite impressive members and I almost felt sorry for the females of their species. The closest camp of Clan Ithlak was only a few days away and the Bizhjerai knew of its location only because the two clans had a friendly relationship though they were not allies. They had not raided one another for decades and they traded goods regularly. Red told me of the history of the Clans and it seemed as if they had an oddly conflicting past. They were a peaceful people, for the most part, content to herd their large beasts and live off the land but conflicts between the different Clans were common. All Clans had bloody feuds with one or two of the others and some were allies and the resulting mess of allegiance and hostilities made my head spin. There were even some instances of allies fighting each other because they were allied to Clans who had a feud. Somehow that alliance had not been broken even though their people killed each other. The honour involved in alliances and feuds had very strict rules and as long as you respected the code of battle even allies could fight and kill one another. When I suggested that a Clan simply conquer the others Red looked at me as if I was simple, but she failed to explain to me why that was not possible. I simply could not wrap my head around their concept of honour. If the Skylanders ever came here these people would be subjugated in short order and the peace would be strictly enforced. At least until the resources, mainly the buffalo meat, was exhausted. Then the place would fall into the same anarchy as the Undercity back home. We arrived at the camp of Clan Ithlak with little ceremony. Their clansmen did not look or dress any differently to the Bizhjerai, the only difference I could spot was they all sported another tattoo on their left shoulder. Where the Bizhjerai clan mark was jagged and feral the Ithlak mark was more rounded and graceful. Just as with the Bizhjerai Mark the rune seemed vaguely familiar to me but I could not put my finger on it. Luckily for us the Ithlak chief was in residence, apparently he had travelled with this camp in the hopes of meeting the Bizhjerai chief and discuss some trade deals and the two chiefs retreated into a large pavilion along with their Elders. Red and I helped setting up camp only a hundred yards from the Ithlak camp. Ithlaki and Bizhjerai travelled freely between the two camps but there were no doubt in my mind that it was indeed two separate camps. Everywhere two or more of members of the different clans met I could overhear stories of our recent battle and it was plain that the Ithlaki shared our outrage. Several young men spoke with Red and she grew increasingly agitated. I could not really understand why but their furtive glances in my direction and guarded words perplexed me. As soon as we had some privacy from listening ears I questioned her about it.

"Gah! It is so stupid. They all want to garner favour with me for being the chief's daughter."

"Would friendship with you make them more powerful?"

"Not really, but those were the sons of the Ithlak Elders. Marriage to me would put them in a position to lay claim to both Clans when father dies."

Realisation dawned on me, along with an unexpected surge of jealousy. I squashed the feeling brutally and spoke the first thought that popped into my head.

"Would such a marriage make them more inclined to help us against Grasax?"

She stared at me with a hurt look on her face. I racked my mind to see where I had gone wrong but came up short. Obviously my suggestion had offended her somehow.

"Possibly, but I don't want to marry any of them."

"Why not? They are handsome and you said yourself that they are skilled warriors."

"I'd rather not talk about it."

I decided to respect her wishes and changed the subject. Something the Chief of Clan Ithlak had said to her father before they retreated into the pavilion had been nagging at the edges of my thoughts.

"Why did Chief Ithlak say that your family especially deserved vengeance upon Grasax?"

Her face set into the familiar expression that she got whenever I asked about her scar but this time her face softened.

"I suppose that you have deserved to know." She traced her scar over her clothing. "The night I got this, the night of my first battle. It was Grasax."

A surprised gasp escaped my lips.

"You've met him?"

"No, he was not there personally but it was his underlings who hurt me. I was eleven years old when they came in the night. We should have learned from that night, they used the same tactics a few days ago. They attacked the camp and as my father and the warriors rushed to defend the camp a smaller force attacked the camp from the flank."

She swallowed and continued in a dead voice but her eyes blazed with emotion, a mixture of grief and fury and I had an inkling about what she was about to tell me.

"Mother did all that she could to protect my brother and me."

Brother? She had never spoken of him.

"She was a gentle woman, not a fighter but she killed the first who entered our tent. The second cut off the arm that held the knife and would have gutted her if I had not intervened. The blow meant to take her life instead cut me." Again she traced the scar over her clothes, a gesture that had become familiar from all the times I'd seen it.

"I only bought her moments for he killed her directly afterwards. I was knocked senseless and he must have thought me dead or else he would not have left me there. He took my brother."

Her voice broke and she pressed her lips tight and averted her face. I reached over and put my hand on her thigh in compassion. I had heard enough.

"We will kill him. I promise you that."

She did not offer a reply and I waited for her to regain her composure. I found myself telling her in a quiet voice about my own tragedies. I had already told her about Greg but I had suffered enough to speak through the night. I told her about Raynard and the strange effect he had upon me. I even told her about the way we had fucked after that raid on the Stardust dealers, how I lain on the body of a woman I had slain with her slick guts against my naked back. I told her of my murder of Markus. Through it all she listened, her eyes never straying from mine even when I had to avert my gaze in shame. I wanted her to know me, even the dark parts. She offered no judgement but before long her cheeks glistened with tears. I had expected condemnation, or disgust but her eyes were full of compassion. I had lived a life so far removed from the code of the Bizhjerai that I would expect her to shun me but to my great surprise she didn't. When I finished she reached out her hand and I hesitantly put mine in hers. She squeezed it tight as tears kept pouring from her eyes. My own were surprisingly dry but it was a great relief to confess my sins to another person. Not even Kendall knew all of these details. Before we could resume our conversation yet another of the young men sat down next to us. He was very handsome and by the way he moved it was clear that he was very well aware of it. He had long tousled hair and his face was stern but softened by an ever present mischievous smirk. He introduced himself to me as Iolan and he politely ignored Red's silent tears. Instead he made menial small talk with me and I hated every second of it. I had never been fond of small talk, but his tactic was obvious. It was an old pickup trick that Greg had taught me, mostly so that I would be wary of it. Ignore the object of your affections, Red in this case, and engage one of her friends to make her insecure and jealous. Red had already told me of her dislike of being courted by these men and I kept my answers short and cold. He refused to take offence of my answers, never letting that infuriating smirk off his face.

"Kyra, be nice," Red had composed herself to remind me not to be rude.

I clamped my lips shut, withdrawing from the conversation.

"Oh, she speaks." His smile was way to friendly for my taste but I bit back the retort.

"Yes, I am sorry for my silence, Iolan. I've had a lot on my mind."

"Yes, terrible tragedy about the attack. I assume that is why you are here to speak to father?"

It dawned on me that Iolan must be the son of the Ithlak Chief.

"Yes, we need help if we are to have a chance of freeing them."

For the first time his apparent mirth was washed away by an incredulous expression.

"Surely you can't mean to attack Dun Traelak?"

Red nodded.

"Kyra here recognised the barrier spell and she may be able to bring it down."

He turned back to me, obviously reassessing me. He clearly thought the claim was bogus and he changed the topic back to that of raids.

"We've had increasing problems with raids of our own."

"How so?"

"Clan Kriath has made overtures on our lands."

"Business as usual then," she responded with a smirk. Iolan nodded in agreement.

"It would have been, but they have recently adopted a group of Reavers and their combined forces have proved to be troublesome."

Reavers? I asked the question aloud and Iolan cast me a disdainful glance at my lack of knowledge.

"Dangerous warriors, they drain the magic straight out of the air around them and from the foes they face. Each man they slay feed their magic and they grow stronger the longer they fight."

That sounded like a useful skill. Was it possible to figure out how they did it?

"Why don't you just learn to do the same? That would even things out."

Iolan cast a frustrated glance at Red.

"Where did you find this one? She knows nothing!"

"She is from a place called the Skylands, on the other side of the ocean."

"There is nothing over there," he scoffed. I was getting sick and tired of that phrase but I did not have the energy to correct him.

"Think what you will, but that is where I am from." I almost winced at the petulant tone of my voice.

"Very well. We can't just learn how to become Reavers, they are born with the trait. The legends said that they were among the first of Grasax's creations but they are not bound to his will. With the help of Clan Bizhjerai we might be able to crush them."

We were interrupted by Red's father who approached his daughter.

"Clan Ithlak has agreed to help us, on one condition."

Somehow I already knew what he was going to say and I was not surprised as he continued.

"That we help them defeat Clan Kriath and their new allies first."

"But father, that will take weeks, months possibly! We don't have the time!"

"Not necessarily, the key factor behind their recent confidence is the Reavers that have joined them. Remove them and they should return to their normal behaviour."

Iolan spoke up in rage.

"You can't expect us to just let them be after that? After all they have done to my Clan?"

"That is precisely what I expect, young Iolan. If we help your people destroy the Reavers then your father has pledged Clan Ithlak to aid Bizhjerai against Grasax. When that is done you can return to your feud with Kriath for all I care."

He turned to his daughter. "You should get some rest, we break camp at dawn."

I was impressed. The Clans did not waste time once they made up their minds. Red and I extricated ourselves from Iolan's presence and retreated to my tent.

The next week passed in a blur of marching and preparations and we fought a few skirmishes with the warriors of Clan Kriath. They had no chance at all against the combined might of the two Clans and we let many of them flee. We wanted them to gather for a defence so that we could crush them in one fell swoop. We encountered one of their camps and we killed more than a fifth of the total strength of Clan Kriath, but not without losses of our own. We were joined by one of the other Bizhjerai camps as well as one of the Ithlaki after a few days and one more camp of each clan at the start of the second. Almost fifteen hundred warriors, two thousand if we fielded armed civilians as well were arrayed against the estimated might of Clan Kriath that was around a thousand men. If not for the Reavers victory would have been assured. As it stood now victory was only probable, but we could not afford to sustain heavy losses. The plan the Chiefs had concocted were simple, Bizhjerai would provide the bulwark, a line of muskets and spears to draw the Kriath warriors out into the open, away from the housing that would shield them from the Ithlaki cavalry. Remembering the devastation left by my magic weapons I had been tasked with holding back and when the Revers revealed themselves I would rain down hell upon them. The Reavers were only dangerous at close range and they would not risk themselves charging into a hail of musket fire. They would strike where we least expected and when they were among us the odds would be stacked in their favour. As many men as possible who would be on the flanks had been equipped with pistols to defend themselves with if the Reavers tried to flank us, which the Chiefs deemed probable. I could do nothing but agree with them. The Reavers were not known for using shields, but it had been encountered in the past. If I had been the Kriath commander then I would have mixed the Reavers into the rear ranks of my own and shield them with the bodies of the front ranks so that they could join the melee in relative safety but the Chiefs stared at me with horror when I suggested it. Apparently the Chiefs valued the lives of their own to much to sacrifice them in that manner. While commendable, war was grisly business and people would die regardless. I found it more prudent to protect your best assets, even if it cost you some of your other assets. Victory was all that mattered in war, after all. Before I knew it the hour was at hand and we stood arrayed not far from the Kriath main hold. It was different from a normal camp only by its size and that the housings were more permanent than a cluster of tents. Most houses were built of wood, but some leather hovels were clearly visible at the outskirts. The hold was a flurry of activity as they prepared to defend themselves and warriors trickled out in clusters to assume their formations. I tried to identify the Reavers but they all looked the same from this distance. I checked my weapons to make sure that I was ready and I exchanged a glance with Red. She returned my nod, she was as ready as she would ever be. The bulk of the Bizhjerai warriors was arrayed to either side of us in their customary four ranks. The front rank carried spears and the large shields and the other three ranks were armed with bows or muskets. They did not own enough of the powerful weapons to arm all of their warriors, not even with the loot from the Outcasts, but the bows had proven their usefulness to me in the recent skirmishes. I lamented the fact that I had been unable to replenish my nova grenade, but the magic field out here were not powerful enough to do it in the limited time we had. Materialising magic required a tremendous amount of power but at least I had been able to recharge my weapons. My rifle was loaded with the magical rounds and I had prepared several nasty spells that were already loaded into the crystals within the stock. We also had three shaman behind our ranks, their kind of magic worked too slowly to be of proper use in battle but they would do what they could. Their elemental magic had proved itself in the last battle where it broke the morale of the Outcasts. The day dragged on without a single shot being fired. Clan Kriath seemed content to wait in the outskirts of their hold. They had shelter and supplies, we did not. They would not come to us. Around noon Red's father sent a contingent of Bizhjerai supported by Ithlak cavalry to flank the hold and I approved of his tactics. Either the Kriath would be attacked in the flank or they would have to divert part of their force to defend it. Either way our superiour numbers worked in our favour. Before long plumes of fire rose above the far side of the hold. The small force of Ithlak cavalry that had sneaked around the hold under cover of night had attacked. The warriors of Clan Kriath noticed the smell and started to glance back nervously. I am sure that all of them had families back there. Some turned and ran toward the flames and soon the trickle of men turned into a torrent. I smiled evilly. Attack a mans family and he would break ranks. It had my idea to attack the non combatants and the Chiefs had not liked the idea. They were not ruthless enough to kill innocents to win a battle, but I knew better. Eventually they had given in to the suggestion, given the time constraints we were under and they had ordered their warriors to let anyone who did not lift a weapon to flee and only burn their dwellings. Homes could be rebuilt but once dead there were no return. The Kriath did not know that their families would be relatively safe though and they rushed to the defence of their civilians. The enemy commander realised his precarious situation and retreated into the hold. It would seem that our neat plan to wipe them out with cavalry would come to nought. House to house it was then. It would be bloody and brutal, but war always was. Red's father seemed to realise the same and the call to advance rang out in his powerful voice. We still had not seen any trace of the Reavers, and their absence worried me. When inside the hold proper the range advantage we had would be lost and they could be upon us before we knew it. The Ithlak cavalry set off at a gallop to circle the hold to attack from the flank since their charge was effectively cancelled and I marched along with the Bizhjerai infantry. We entered the area with leather hovels at the outskirts and met a weak resistance. Whoever came at us was quickly shot down by our bowmen. The bows were much more accurate than our muskets and we only had a few volleys before the bores would be too fouled up by the residue left by the black powder. Yet another weakness of the weapons that we did not have in the Skylands. The magical flash powder burned utterly and completely, leaving nothing behind but a purple smoke. I saved my rifle shots, searching for Reavers with Red by my side. I reached out my free hand and set fire to a leather tent.

"Burn the houses, don't let them hide inside and take us in the rear!"

My command was met with grimaces from my fellow warriors but they heeded my advice and reluctantly set fire to houses lovingly crafted by parents for their children. A small group of men burst out of a tent right in front of us as they overheard my command and they were quickly put down by the archers. A man charged at me with several arrows through his chest, howling in blood-lust. The arrows had nowhere near the stopping power of a musket shot and they did not die swiftly. Red's spear took him in the throat and he collapsed at our feet. I stepped over his corpse without a second glance and continued the advance into the hold. A short while later the resistance intensified even as the Ithlak cavalry attacked from the west. Our advance came to a halt and we started trading volleys with the defenders. They had constructed makeshift barriers by whatever materials was on hand but our shields, designed for the purpose, proved more effective. I was tempted to open fire but my magical shots were precious and I did not want to waste them. I ducked behind a shield bearer, gritting my teeth in impotent frustration. It was a good thing I did, if I had been focused on firing I would not have heard the low command from behind us and I glanced over my shoulder. Silent as death itself the Reavers waded into the fray. Somehow they had gotten behind us and were nearly upon us. I shouted a warning and raised my rifle to squeeze off a shot. The ground erupted in front of the leading Reaver and he and his closest fellows fell with mangled legs. I racked the slide and repeated the action farther down the line. The men around me had barely turned around when the Reavers hit us and many were cut down before they could even raise their weapons in defence. A pull on my personal energies warned me of their dangerous powers as my energy was leeched from me against my will. I threw up a shield around me and the pull lessened but the power I put into my shield was leeched away instead. The long blade the Reaver opposing me wielded flared into magical light with the stolen power and the edge cut through my shield effortlessly. It popped and cracked in a flare of blue and I blinked at him in astonishment. His next swing nearly took my head off but I twisted aside and the blow glanced off of my helmet. At least the spell on the sword could not cut through my armour as easily as it had my shield. I thumbed the selector gem on the rifle as I used it to bat his thrust to the side and the action brought the muzzle of my rifle into line. I fired. The shot erupted into dozens of sharp shards mere inches from the muzzle and struck his chest in a wide spread. His leather vest proved completely ineffective against the force and he fell back, bleeding profusely. I could see his slick organs beneath the ragged mess his chest had become. The warriors we had previously exchanged volleys with took advantage of the distraction and charged with a wild roar. We were trapped. I put down two more Reavers with the same scatter shot spell before my rifle went dry and I drew my revolvers. These assholes weren't so tough after all, even though I was rapidly weakening from their draining aura. I saw a Bizhjerai warrior get impaled on a long sword and as the Reaver pulled it free the man erupted in blue flames as his soul was violently torn from his body. His soul was still entrenched in his body but the shock of the fatal wound had weakened its hold enough for the Reaver to pull it forcefully from his body. The power coursing unnaturally from his body was burning it up from the inside and his blackened skeleton fell to the ground. The man's murderer was suddenly enveloped by a shield and before my eyes I saw it stop a point blank musket shot dead in a flare of blue. Shit, they were getting stronger by the moment. The crackle of flames brought my attention back ahead and a Reaver flung a bolt of fire at me. I crouched down and turned my head and the flames roared around my helmet. It heated up significantly but I suffered no more damaged than a sweaty brow. He too raised a shield with his stolen power. Luckily my sword was enchanted with the same kind of shield-cutting effect that they enspelled their weapons with and I channelled power into the weapon. Some of the runes on the edge blazed blue with my power and the edge was limned in ghostly flames of the same colour. Why was magic almost always blue? I pushed the random thought aside and charged the Reaver. He grinned evilly at me and I saw that his teeth were filed down into cruel points. I had seen worse among the brutes deep in the Undercity and did not let it affect me. He did not even try to defend himself, trusting his shield and he swung at me. I leaned to the side and thrust at his unprotected belly. The point of my sword popped his shield like a bubble of soap and sank deep into his liver. Now it was my time to smile into his startled face. Two could play at this soul drinking game. I activated another enchantment on the blade and used it to rip the soul from his body and he erupted in the same flames that my poor fellow had just moments ago. I drank the power to replenish what had already been stolen. His charred corpse fell at my feet and I found myself fighting a group of Reavers rushing to join their friends. They had not yet stolen any power and I reached down and pulled my small revolver. They were too close for me to miss and I fired until the hammer clicked on an empty chamber. Six Reavers fell to the ground, completely helpless against the kinetic rounds. Those already among the Bizhjerai where a completely different matter though. They were all protected by shields and only used their weapons when someone got too close, instead they used their free hands to fling death and destruction into the Bizhjerai. The shield wall on the other side of our ranks still held against the Kriath warriors, their muskets was too short to strike without braving the sharp points of the spears poking at any who dared to come too close. The archers were wreaking havoc amongst their ranks but we had serious problems with the Reavers. I was sure that had we not been surrounded the Bizhjerai would already have turned and fled. Or maybe not, I amended when I saw expressions of fierce determination instead of fear and panic on their faces. Their weapons bounced off the shields of the Reavers and more often than not they were either incinerated, cut down to feed the Reavers, or worse.
