I saw one man erupt from inside as his blood boiled and gore and viscera covered the men closest to him. I realised that I had to focus on utility. I was the only one able to pierce their shields and their magic would only grow stronger the more souls they claimed. Luckily I had prepared for this and had loaded my large revolver with only shield breaking spells. I unleashed a blast of magic that threw two Reavers to the ground but otherwise did not harm them. I darted through their line and emerged into the relative calm behind them. I stabbed my blade through his shield and an instant after into his chest. I claimed his soul for my own but it was more than I could hold. Magical sparks coursed across my armour as the overflow power started to leak out of me and my skin burned all over from the discharge. It was a similar effect that the Reaver was suffering as his soul was ripped out of his unwilling flesh, only on a lesser scale. I had to use the power flowing into me or I would burn just as surely as he did. The other Reaver was scrambling to his feet and I used the power coursing through my sword arm to lash out at him. Dark coils of magic surrounded him and squeezed his shield like a vice. He gritted his teeth and strengthened his wavering shield. I just hoped he had not claimed more power than I had. In the back of my mind I wondered how they were able to hold more than their natural storage capacity without burning. I intensified my grip as the flow of power into me lessened. I had used the power I had stolen and started pouring my personal power into the spell. I clenched my fist as I tightened the coils around his shield. Sparks flew as the two opposing forced struggled but in the end I won. His shield buckled and bent before it cracked and the pressure I had put on it with my coils, now without resistance, shrank inward and neatly cut him into several smaller pieces. It was not a pretty death, but a quick one. I had no time to gloat and spun around. The Bizhjerai were in a bad way. Luckily the Reavers had disregarded my presence behind their lines, if they had even noticed it, trusting their fellows to deal with me. Their hubris became their undoing as I summoned my revolver from the ground where I had dropped it. It smacked reassuringly into my hand and I cocked the hammer with my thumb and aimed at the back of a Reaver a way down the line. I took the risk of missing and striking one of my own and squeezed off the shots as fast as I could. Shields sputtered and winked out and the Bizhjerai took advantage of the stunned Reavers. The six warriors was clubbed or cut to death in short order. They had been dazed by the backlash of their failing shield and were no match for the stalwart warriors of Clan Bizhjerai. I holstered my revolver and charged the closest Reaver. My enchanted blade cut through his shield from behind but I did not stop to finish him off. I pushed with my blood magic and darted down the short line of Reavers and poked their shields one by one. The Bizhjerai made short work of them as I left them in the dust of my rampage. With our rear cleared the Kriath warriors that had just managed to break the shield wall faced our full might and they wavered at the renewed assault. They started to fall back but the Bizhjerai did not let them. They fell where they stood, shot or speared without mercy. I surveyed the scene and was appalled at the number of dead. The Reavers had killed almost half of our force before they were finally slain. If it were not for my enchanted sword I had no doubt that they all would have died. A hundred dead Bizhjerai and Ithlaki lay scattered but I was relieved that Red was still among the living. She had been in the front rank, lending her spear to keep the Kriath at bay and she sported a minor cut on her cheek as her only wound. I was sure that most of the blood on her face was not her own. I was unable to muster a smile for her amidst the carnage of her clansmen but I gave her a thumbs up. A few of the fallen warriors yet lived and Red commanded a small group of our diminished forces to take care of them, we needed to rejoin the advance through the hold and if there were more Reavers around I needed to deal with them. I cringed at the thought of how powerful they must be by now. We rejoined the advance and were greeted by startled faces at our severely diminished numbers but none of the clansmen wavered. We fought for hours, each inch won by blood. The Kriath was getting desperate and further into the hold I saw a line of Kriath get demolished by Ithlaki cavalry. I was suddenly faced by a woman brandishing a knife and I noted that she wore the dress of the non-warriors. Shit, the Kriath was sending out their civilians. With a small twinge of regret, swiftly quashed, I cut her belly open with a flick of my sword and then I ignored her. She cradled the guts spilling from her torn stomach as she collapsed to her feet but she was put out her misery swiftly enough by an axe to the head. A line of Reavers surged from behind a house and charged us with gleeful howls. I could see shield enveloping them and fire wreathed their free hands. Red reacted faster than me and called out the order to form a shield wall. Shots rang out but were stopped by their shields, shot and arrow alike. One of the Reavers stumbled as his shield was struck by four musket rounds and cracked as it was overloaded. An opportunistic archer but a shaft through his eye and he fell bonelessly to the blood soaked ground. The battle had already raged across this area and the ground was littered by corpses, friend and foe alike. Behind the line of Reavers rapidly approaching I saw two men silently staring at one another. They both wore the garb of shamans and I assumed that they were in some sort of invisible battle. The Reavers thundered into our shield wall a moment after their flames set the majority of the shields ablaze. Several others were torn from the grips of their owners by invisible bands of force and then the Reavers was among us. The carnage was absolute, these Reavers were far more powerful than the ones we had faced before. There were still ten of us for every one of them but the clansmen had no hope of hurting them. I saw one brave Ithlaki warrior throw himself over the shield of a Reaver and even as the discharge of the shield burned him he clutched the crazed warrior tightly as they fell. Several of his friends stabbed at the downed Reaver but their strikes proved ineffective. The Reaver ripped the man apart with disdainful ease with his mind and regained his footing. The distraction had let a group of Bizhjerai draw their pistols and the Reaver found himself staring into half a dozen muzzles. His shield was overloaded by the first four shots and the remaining two found a resting place within his flesh. One of the shots struck his shoulder and the other right in his brain. The Reaver fell and the excess power within him vented violently. His body erupted in a gout of flame that consumed his body and as it failed, the rest of his stored power erupted in a powerful blast. Men were thrown to the ground but those closest to him was his own kind. Their shields overloaded in the inferno and one was immolated by the blue flames. The thrust of a spear took him in the chest and he erupted similarly, taking the spearman with him in his explosive death. Damn, even in death these bastards were deadly. The remaining Reavers spread out and started destroying our warriors. I blocked an expert swing of the Reaver facing me but it had been a feint. His sword yielded and he folded it around to send it at my head from the other side. I threw up my left arm in desperation and hoped that their increased power would not let their weapons cut cleanly through my armour. My gauntlet was made of stern stuff and it held. The Reaver stared in amazement, he had obviously expected to cleave my arm neatly in half. I showed my teeth through the vertical gap in my helmet and wrapped my fingers around his blade, trapping it firmly. Unable to defend himself my blade popped his shield and his eyes crossed hilariously at the feedback before the point of my sword found his heart. I pulled heavily on his Soul and channelled the power directly into my large revolver. The shield breaking spells started recharging rapidly from the huge influx of power. This Reaver must have claimed the souls of many before he faced me, and his death. His burning body crumbled into ashes but both of my revolvers were reloaded before the flow of power lessened and petered out. I saw several clansmen around me stumble as their souls were drained by their aura and I saw Red fall. I shouted a denial and moved toward the Reaver preparing to take her soul. I snatched out my revolver and shot him. His shield popped and he stumbled before my blade sang out and separated his head from his shoulder. The enchanted edge cut cleanly through sinew, flesh and bone. I raised my leg and kicked his body into two of his fellows before he could vent his power and the trio vanished in a huge blast of power. The only thing saving Red and me was my own shield. The raging storm incinerated everything else around us, including several clansmen and the blast drained much of my personal energies. The storm vanished as quickly as it erupted and I found myself blinking in the sudden relative darkness of the afternoon sun. Two Reavers remained and they watched me uncertainly as I stepped out of the residual flames. I was sure that they had never fought anyone like me before. The Skylands bred tough children, and I had led one of the toughest lives there was. I was also armed and armoured by a genius. They may be more powerful than I, but I had fought Mages and warriors alike. They were still only human. I still held my revolver in my left hand and I raised it. Four shots rang out and their bodies erupted in flames as they were consumed by their own stolen magic. It was a waste of shield breaking spells to use them as kinetic rounds but it did the trick. With their draining aura gone Red and a few more survivors slowly picked themselves off the ground. They watched me with awe where I stood among the charred remains of Reavers and friends alike. It pained me to see the expression in Red's eyes, the others did not bother me in the slightest. I wanted to be her friend, I did not want her to look at me like that. An arrow struck my armoured back and splintered and another embedded itself in Red's thigh. She cried out and fell to her knee. The other survivors were not so lucky and fell with several arrows each in their torsos. I spun around and strengthened my shield as a musket ball struck it. My power was weakened and the shield collapsed even as it saved me. I stumbled as darkness fell when the feedback threated to knock me out but vision returned and I straightened myself just as the Kriath warriors charged. I backed up to protect my wounded friend but we were severely outnumbered. Our only choice was to run. Red was in no condition to run and the thought of leaving her floated through my head. I refused to let the thought take root. I would not leave her behind. Those days were behind me. It was time to take a stand, to act like a Bizhjerai even if it cost me my life. I raised my weapon and prepared to fight until death claimed me. Red pushed to her feet and joined me. I glanced at her face and winced at the rictus of pain and weariness painted on it. She looked at me and it was as if time slowed down. There were nothing except for her pretty face and her startlingly green eyes. They glinted in the sunlight and seemed to glow of an inner light. It was a sharp contrast to her fiery hair. She was so fucking beautiful that I wanted to weep. An arrow whistled between our faces and broke the spell. Time resumed its normal pace, if not even faster, and the Kriath was upon us. I shot the first with my small pistol and deflected the axe of the second. Red's axe took him straight in the face. We fought like possessed, revolver, sword, shield and axe working in tandem. We played a cruel symphony of death and I had never felt more alive. I could hear Red laughing maniacally beside me and I joined her with an exultant howl. We were weakening though and I knew we had but minutes left, at best. With Red at my back I was not certain how badly she was wounded but her lighter armour would have been pierced by now. Even my armour had its weak spots and I bled from a dozen wounds. Soon blood loss and fatigue would let them hurt us even further and then it would be over shortly thereafter. I did not care. I was doing what I did best, killing. And I did it with a friend that accepted me, despite all I had done. There were worse way to die. My only regret was that I would never see my mother again, or Kendall or Marissa. The thought of Marissa galvanised me and a surge of strength suffused me. I tried to steal the soul of the warrior facing me but when my blade found a home in his flesh I was forced to rip it free to defend myself. They did not allow me the time and focus required to drain him. My sudden strength was already waning and an axe clipped my helm. I was thrown off balance, head ringing and I heard a feminine cry from behind.

"Red!"

I spun around and tried to see through my blurred vision. She was still standing but her back was cut open in a long gash. I lashed out at the man who had struck her but he danced out of my reach. Then he dropped to the ground and lay still. I stared at him, dumbfounded. What was he doing? My vision cleared and I saw the arrow driven into his temple. Another Kriath warrior fell at my side and I searched for the source of the arrows even as I deflected an axe headed for my ribs. Ithlaki archers were loosing arrows as quickly as they could into our attackers. I killed the man with the axe with a wicked thrust through the underside of his chin and through the top of his head at the same time that two arrows thunked into his back. I ripped my blade free as he fell and crouched into a defencive position. There were no more enemies to fight. I looked back and saw Red turning to face me but she stumbled on her wounded leg and fell. I dropped my sword and caught her and her face ended up inches from mine. I stared into her weary eyes that yet shone with the thrill of combat and the realisation that we still lived. Jubilation surged in my throat and I laughed at her astonished expression. Despite the pain of her wounds she joined me. Her laugh was the most beautiful sound I had ever heard and I leaned in and kissed her. Not a light, friendly peck but a deep kiss of passion. She stiffened in my arms and I froze hesitantly. What the fuck was I doing? Then her body melted into mine and she responded in kind. A loud noise finally permeated my fuzzy mind and I realised that the warriors who had saved us were cheering. If their cheers was for us or in victory I did not know, nor did I care. All I cared about right now was the small woman in my arms and the wondrous taste of her mouth. We reluctantly ended the kiss to come up for air and I pressed my forehead to hers.

"Can you stand on your own?"

"I don't know if I could have after that even with intact legs."

We both giggled at that but I helped her onto her feet. She did manage to stand on her own but walking proved difficult so she put her arm around my waist for support. I liked that.

"Victory is ours, Anjali. The Kriath are defeated."

The man who spoke was tall and covered in blood.

"My father?"

"Wounded, but not badly. He awaits you in the centre of the hold with the prisoners."

We did not speak as we slowly made our way through the corpse-littered streets. Streets was too strong a word for it though, they were more like gaps between housings. Everywhere I looked the ground was turned into a bloody mud and the vital fluid ran in thick rivulets at places. Many people had died today, I just hoped that most had been of Clan Kriath and not those who would have fought Grasax with us. I slipped on the guts of a child that lay in my path and I quickly averted my gaze. She reminded me too much of the little girl I had murdered. I would kill anyone for the right reasons, but not children. Never again. The Chief was indeed waiting, along with the Chief of Clan Ithlak. There were pitifully few prisoners, mostly women and children and some of the elderly men too weak to fight. Either there were more prisoners elsewhere or Clan Kriath had died today. I led Red down the line of prisoners toward her father and the shaman when a familiar voice spoke my name.

"Kyra? The fuck are you doing here?"

My body froze as a familiar warmth bloomed between my legs. That damn smooth voice was one I had never wished to hear again. I turned my head but could not deny what I saw. Raynard was kneeling in the row of prisoners. I left Red standing and approached him despite my attempts not to. He was just so hypnotic. His handsome face turned into a hopeful smile.

"You with these assholes? Get me out of these manacles will you? We need to get out of here, these people are crazy."

I marvelled at his audacity to insult the people holding him prisoner. I refused to respond even as my body yearned for his. I stared at him for a long moment and his smile wavered but did not leave his face.

"Kyra?"

The pieces of the puzzle fell into place. His presence here. The Reavers.

"You!"

"What?"

"You did this?" I made a gesture that encompassed the carnage all around us.

"What? No! You attacked us!"

"Don't lie to me! We were sent here to destabilise the region so you brokered the alliance between Clan Kriath and the Reavers. You made them bold enough to step up their raids, and triggered this war."

My gaze was drawn to the tattoo on his shoulder. It was the Mark of Clan Kriath.

"They let you into the Clan! The alliance was the price wasn't it?"

I could easily see someone of Raynard's charisma convincing the brutal Reavers to ally with Clan Kriath in exchange for the promise of carnage. Raynard chuckled.

"You always were a smart one, Kyra. Now c'mon, tell these idiots to let me loose so we can return home. It is obvious by the way they look at you that you have some clout here."

I almost moved to do as he said, such was his power over me, but with a tremendous effort I stopped myself. I felt a hand on my arm and glanced over my shoulder at Red. The obvious question was plain on her face, even beneath the mask of blood. I answered with a single word.

"Raynard."

Her face went through a series of expressions, surprise, shock, and fury in that order.

"I see my reputation precedes me. Who is this little morsel then?"

I refused to answer. This was the man responsible for all the death and destruction today. A thousand men had died as a result of his actions. And mine. I quashed the traitorous thought, but it was correct. It was my actions that had brought this war along. If I had not proposed the attack on Grasax then we would never have sought the aid of Clan Ithlak and they in turn would not have requested our aid in this attack. The Clans had lived a life of balance here on the plains, suffering the raids of each other and Grasax but nothing on this magnitude. An entire Clan had been wiped out and the survivors were sure to be Clanless or worse, Outcasts. They could all have carried on with their lives, granted the prisoners that Grasax's men had taken would be lost but were the lives of seventy-odd people worth this carnage? They had lived comfortably here and then we had come along and disrupted their way of life. We did what Skylanders always did. We destroyed and corrupted everything we touched. We had turned a wondrous magical technology, a safe haven after the Apocalypse, into an oppressive city state that cared nothing for its inhabitants unless they were rich and powerful. They would do the same if they ever came here. I slowly drew my small revolver and held it along my thigh as I stared into his brown eyes. A flicker of uncertainty on his face betrayed his surprise but it was quickly covered by a confident smile. He had had me wrapped around his finger for so long that even I was uncertain if I would ever uncoil. I struggled to raise my weapon but my hand remained stubbornly by my side.

"C'mon, Kyra. You won't kill me, not like this. You want me. You need me."

He poured his charisma through his words and I wanted to fuck him as much as I wanted to kill him, like I usually did. The small hand returned to my arm and I looked at Red. Tears were streaking down the blood on her cheeks but her eyes was full of understanding. She may not understand what was going through me but she knew of it. I had told her of the effect he had on me earlier. She nodded, giving me her silent support to whatever course of action I chose. She licked her lips and I focused on their graceful arches. The memory of the jubilant kiss we had shared after the battle slammed into my mind. What did it mean? Was that just a spur of the moment in the exultation of survival against all odds? The heat between my legs changed. I am not sure how, for it felt exactly the same as I stared at her lips. I ripped my gaze free of their hypnotic spell and I returned my attention to Raynard. He looked different now, less enchanting than he had previously.

"Kyra?"

His voice had lost its smooth timbre and I felt nothing when it reached my ears. I smiled at him, knowing what I must do. His cocky smile returned at my expression but I wiped it away when I raised the revolver to his face.

"Kyra, don't!"

I squeezed the trigger and killed my previous life.

## Chapter 18

I felt empty inside and the scene from just a few hours ago replayed before my minds eye. It was as if I watched through another person's eyes as I squeezed the trigger. Raynard's astonished face went slack when his brains evacuated through the back of his skull. I could still hear the sound of him striking the the ground with a dull thud and his body erupting in the spasms of death. Not even the plate of meat set before me could rouse me from my stupor. Red had left me here in this tent with the food while she spoke to her father. The scene replayed once more before my eyes, and then again and again until I lost count. I don't know how long I sat there, it could have been minutes or hours but a gentle hand on my shoulder roused me. I looked up at Red as she sat down next to me. She clutched my hand in silent compassion as the silence stretched out between us. It was a comfortable silence and her reassuring touch grounded me. Almost mechanically I picked up the meat and bit into it. The cold meat was tough but I ripped off a piece with teeth and chewed it absently.

"I am proud of you."

"What?"

"I will not claim to understand what you are going through, but I want to. Just let me in."

I squeezed her hand but did not offer a response. None of the words that sprang to my mind seemed appropriate.

"I understand that what you did was difficult, and I am proud of you."

"Did I do the right thing?"

"Did he deserve death?"

I nodded slowly. "He has done nothing worse than I have. Do I deserve to die as well?"

"I don't know. Maybe."

Her response surprised me, I had expected her to defend me and my expression must have betrayed my shock for she smiled reassuringly.

"Maybe you do, maybe you don't. I will not judge you, and I will kill anyone who suggests that you be put down. I will have your back." She paused before continuing. "Were you truly sent here to destabilise the region?"

I was sick of lying and covering up so I merely nodded. A knot formed in my belly when her expression hardened, despite her previous words.

"Were you going to? Was your aid only a means to gain our trust?"

Her words felt like a knife twisting in my belly.

"Yes to the first, no to the second. But that was before I was got to know your people."

"So now you no longer plan to destabilise us, but your aid was to gain our trust?"

I looked at her sharply, not understanding her meaning. Her sly smile betrayed that she was just teasing me and despite my numbness I felt a small smile tug at the corners of my lips. She stood up to leave.

"You should rest, we will speak more tomorrow. It has been a long day."

I refused to let go of her hand and she was pulled to a stop.

"Please stay. I don't want to be alone right now."

Her pretty face softened and we curled up next to each other on the bedroll. I set my armour to dissolve as she curled up against my back. She had discarded her own armour and wore only soft leather and her firm body pressed close as she wrapped her arm around me. Despite my churning thoughts I fell asleep swiftly.

## Chapter 19

I peered at Dun Traelak in the distance. I, Red and a small contingent of Ithlaki cavalry had ridden ahead of the host to survey the lay of the land and the fortress and we would have a few days to find a weakness before they became alerted to our invasion. I had initially refused mounting one of the slender beasts but necessity had forced me. When Red had mounted and started to ride away without me I had reluctantly joined her on her beast. She would not let me ride on my own, and I was silently glad for it since I had no idea how to get the creature to behave. My whole body ached from the experience, but my legs and crotch was really killing me. How could they do that willingly? I glared at Red beside me. She seemed to suffer no pain at all from our swift ride. She sensed my glare and smirked in my direction. That bitch! She knew how much pain I was in and now she was gloating. I grumbled under my breath but returned my attention to Dun Traelak. We were in trouble for the barrier was up. I squinted at it and focused my magical sense on it. It was indeed very similar to the Great Barrier and it seemed to be activated perpetually. It extended to just beyond the outer walls of the fortress so there were no possibility to get close to inspect it further. The Dragonkin had pierced the Great Barrier with stupendously powerful blasts of magic but we lacked the raw magical power to do so ourselves. Not even if I claimed the souls of all of the warriors accompanying me I doubted that it would more than dent the shield temporarily. A small patrol was returning to the keep and I watched them with keen interest. They had not seen us lurking at the edge of the forest. How were they going to get inside? Were there a portal in the barrier somewhere they could use like the one installed in the Great Barrier after the Dragonkin invasion? Or would they deactivate the whole thing to let them pass? The patrol approached the gates but they did not halt before the gates. They closed in on the edge of the barrier and then... Nothing. They walked straight through it. Red nudged me in astonishment.

"They just walked inside. Is the barrier down?"

I glanced at her. "No, it is right there. Can't you see it?"

"No." Her voice was petulant and I kicked myself mentally for forgetting that she had not been taught to see magic with her magesense. I had to remedy that as soon as we had time. It surprised me that she managed to perform the few basic spells she knew without being able to see the runes. Well, to be fair the spells the Bizhjerai used was very easy and could be invoked with little more than a thought.

"Perhaps the barrier is permeable when they are not under attack." I mused aloud.

"Then why have it up in the first place? Wouldn't that just waste power?"

She had a good point, though I had an answer.

"Yes, but it could also be due to necessity. A barrier that large would take time to erect from nothing but having something there would cause it to become impenetrable much quicker. It is much faster to change the aspect of a shield than erect it."

"Why?"

"The power is already there, or at least most of it is. Funnelling the new spell across the old one is quicker than casting it from scratch. Think of it like pouring water over a crystal. If you trail a bit of water across the surface then the following water will be much more likely to take that route than any other."

"Why would you pour water over a crystal?"

I huffed in exasperation.

"You wouldn't, unless you were explaining magic to a student. A thick student." I grinned at her to take the sting out of my words. She ignored my jab at her intelligence with a surprising lack of her usual willingness to banter.

"So. How do we breach it? You said you may be able to do something about it from the inside?"

I watched the zenith of the dome above the barrier and saw the torrent of power shooting up from the central tower to feed it.

"Yes, there must be a generator in that tower," I pointed it out to her, "if we can get to it we may be able to destroy it."

"Generator? I am not familiar with that word."

"It is a spell, a focus for the power. It probably contains a store of power as well to feed the barrier in times of extraordinary stress. That is how we built them back home."

"You have things like this? Apart from the giant one around your lands?"

Her voice no longer held an undertone of doubt when she spoke of the things of my homeland. She had come to trust me on that after she had seen my weapons in action.

"Yeah, my armour has one actually. This choker I wear to control it contains the power to manifest the armour and clothes I wear."

"What happens to the power stored within if we destroyed it?"

That was an excellent question indeed, most likely it would be released and depending on the amount of power stored within there may be some manifestations of Wild Magic. Most likely things would burn, and burn violently.

"Lets just say that we don't want to be anywhere near it. It could possibly bring the entire tower down."

"But first we need to get to it."

"First we need to get to it." I agreed grimly.

"Now that you have seen it, do you have any suggestions?"

I shook my head mutely. I was totally stumped. My first instinct had been to batter the barrier down with magic but that was not an option. Not if not even the concerted efforts of the shaman had managed it. Kendall knew more about this kind of magic than I and I desperately wanted him by my side right then.

"This is probably a stupid idea, but why don't we just walk inside?"

I stared at Red, dumbfounded.

"What?"

"That patrol just entered like the barrier was not there. If Grasax is not alerted to our presence, why can't we just walk inside? Pretend to be a patrol to get through the gate."

There were a number of ways to prevent that, most of them relying on disciplined watchers at the gate. If they did not recognise those who approach, surely they would raise the alarm. I said as much but Red was not quite ready to drop the idea.

"Then we climb the wall at night."

"These assholes have not held this position for centuries by being that lax in their security."

"Fair point. I just wanted to float the idea at least. What? Why are you looking at me like that?"

"Red, you are a genius! I could kiss you!"

Her face reddened as an odd expression crept across her face but I barely noticed. He words had sparked an idea in my mind. She muttered something under her breath. We would not be able to cross the gates unnoticed, but if we managed to distract the guards then maybe. Now how to distract them? Another idea struck me with the force of a hammer.

"Red! You said that there were monsters out here that Grasax had created but not bound to his will, like the Reavers?"

Her brow furrowed in surprise at the unexpected turn of my question and she opened her mouth to answer when her previous words filtered into my awareness. She had muttered "Why don't you?"

Wait, what? She wanted me to kiss her?! Now?! Had the kiss we shared after the battle not been a spur of the moment? We had not spoken of it, even though I wanted to but the right moment never seemed to appear. Or maybe I had chickened out once or twice when I could've. Alright I chickened out a bunch of times.

"Yes, there are several such monsters though none that I know of that are as intelligent as the Reavers. Why?"

Again, the moment was lost and I pushed my thoughts of kissing her full lips aside regretfully. They were quite pleasant thoughts. I could suddenly taste the memory of her again and I almost lost my train of thought.

"Do you think we can lure one to the walls?" I asked her.

"It would be risky. They are dangerous. Why?"

"Think, Red, think!"

I waited for her to come to the same conclusion I had. I had given her clues aplenty.

"You want to use it as distraction?"

"Precisely! If we get one of the beasts close enough to the wall we can come and 'aid' the defenders who will surely come out to drive it away. We can slip through the gates in the confusion."

She was doubtful.

"It will be dangerous and they are sure to notice us if we herd a beast up to the wall."

Damn, she was correct but I wouldn't be dissuaded so easily. It was the best plan so far and it was worth hammering out the details a bit before we discarded the idea.

"Look at the grass over there, it is quite tall. If a few of us, not all obviously, crawl through the grass and hide near the gate the rest of us can herd the beast here to the edge of the wood. I'll draw it close, I can run faster than the rest of us with my blood magic."

Red judged the distance between our current position and the walls. It was several hundred yards. She glanced down at my cleavage and I ignored my heating cheeks. It was a pleasant warmth, entirely unlike the heat that would creep upon me when Raynard did the same. Again I saw his emptied skull strike the ground but for the first time the image was not a painful one. Instead it was full of relief. I wanted to think that I had killed him in vengeance for what he had done to the Ithlaki and primarily the Bizhjerai but to be totally honest I had done it for me. I was finally free of him. I could not have done it without Red, only her support had made me strong enough to resist his strange hold over me.

"It is quite a distance, are you sure you can do it? Just the short charge the other day drained your reserves heavily."

Again she glanced meaningfully at my cleavage. Luckily my corset had adjusted its cups for my smaller size. In time I would recover with proper sustenance.

"Yes. I won't have much left after but I can do it. We will have to find a beast I can outrun though. With the dark colour of my armour they may not even see me in the night. What do you think?"

She looked dubious but nodded slowly.

"Maybe, but I don't like putting you at such risk."

"Neither do I, but it is the best idea that we have. We still have another two days before the host arrives so we may figure something else out. We need to get inside the night before the host arrives so that they can be ready to strike when we attack from within."

"Very well. Let's say this crazy plan works and we take the barrier down. How does the Clans get through the walls? They won't have time to build ladders if they have to attack almost as soon as they arrive."

"Fuck."

"Fuck, indeed."

"The shaman?"

"What about them?"

"The night when the Outcasts attacked the shaman opened a rift in the ground."

"Yes. It is difficult and takes time but it is within their power."

"What if they open a rift beneath the wall?"

"Without the barrier and protection from arrows and shots from atop the walls to allow them to get close? Yes they should be able to do it. But then there will be a small rift beneath the wall, then what? The Clans crawl through it?"

"No, of course not. Make the crack wide enough and the wall will fall."

"Are you sure? Won't the wall just span the rift?"

I had forgotten how little the Bizhjerai knew about physics and architecture. They had no use for it in their way of life. I launched into an explanation of foundations and the pull of the earth. That led into an explanation of fulcrums and torque and before long Red had a thoroughly confused look on her face.

"Slow down, I don't understand half of what you are saying. I'll take your word for it as I have so much else." She was pensive for a moment. "Do all of your people know these things?"

"No. Most people above the Undercity have at least basic understanding but I am friends with a genius who won't stop talking about things like this."

"Is this the friend that had you murder that whore?"

I nodded with a wince. The memory of that murder was not a pleasant one, but I had far worse memories. An image of a crushed face surrounded by red hair flitted through the back of my mind.

"Your people sounds terrifying, if they ever come here in anger I fear that all of the Clans are doomed. But they brought you to me and for that I will be ever grateful."

Unexpected tears stung at the corners of my eyes at her words and I clasped her shoulder.

"Thanks. That means a lot coming from you. But why do you think they are terrifying?"

She shrugged. "You know all of these things, and your weapons." She shuddered before continuing. "I am just glad that they are pointed in the directions of our enemies."

"You and me both."

"So. We have a plan for the barrier, however dubious that plan may be, and we have a plan for the walls. What about this 'generator' you spoke of?"

"That is the least of our problems. I can hopefully cobble together a spell to destroy it once I have inspected it. It is sure to have a weak point."

"But you said that the tower may topple in the following release of power, how do we survive it?"

"My friend gave me a book on spells, I am sure I saw one in there that would delay the explosion until we can get clear. Let me study it before we go hunting for a beast tomorrow. Tell the men about the plan while I work, will you?"

"Of course."

We retreated back into the forest and joined the Ithlaki cavalry waiting for us. We went deeper into the forest before we made camp for we did not want to be spotted by any patrols from Dun Traelak. Red left me to inform the men as I settled down with the book Kendall had given me. I skimmed the pages and found several interesting spells but none that would help us in the upcoming battle. There, I found the spell I had mentioned to Red and I inspected it more thoroughly than I had the others. It was a timer spell that would ignite after a certain amount of time as long as you connected it as a triggering condition on the main spell. I did not understand how that was achieved so I had to flip a couple of pages back toward the start of the book to study the part of composite spells. That part led me another page to learn about temporary power holding spells. My head started to spin. The usual spells I used were simple, they were constructed as a simple concept, heat for instance, and was charged with power until it ignited. When it did it would not accept any more power, the spell was closed so to speak and it would burn until the power was consumed to such a degree that the runes binding the power no longer could maintain coherency and the spell fizzled out. Using the timer spell would require the timer to contain enough power to maintain itself until the timer ran out to trigger the primary spell. That spell though could not contain enough power to ignite, or it would burn out long before the timer triggered it. That meant that the power would have to be contained in another spell that would not consume the power during it's own lifetime. Each of the spells I wanted to use were easy enough to understand on their own, isolated from the others. It was how they were supposed to be bound together that eluded me and the book failed to explain it. I guess it should be obvious but it was beyond me. Red plonked her behind down next to me and peered at the text in the small book in the waning light.

"Do you understand that?"

"Nope. Not all of it."

"Try to explain it to me. Sometimes it helps to try to explain things you don't fully understand."

Damn, this girl was more insightful than she had let on. Kendall used to say the same thing to me when I complained about not understanding his long monologues and more often than not he thanked me for helping him understand. Then he usually left me tired and confused to hurry back to his projects.

"Alright. Prepare to be bored."

"I doubt it. You are never boring."

The speech I had hastily prepared floundered at her words and I felt myself blush. I shook myself and started explaining the timer spell. When I finished I had gained no new insights but Red watched me expectantly.

"Show me."

"What?"

"Show me. Try it out with an example. You can be told for eternity how a bow works but you will never be able to hit your mark without actually loosing an arrow. Remember how you improved your aim when I showed you?"

I thought back to our archery practice but my mind returned to the moment when she had stood pressed against my back with her arms around me as she guided my hands on the string. 

"All right. Let's use a simple light spell as the primary effect and we want a five second delay."

The light spell was very simple and I could achieve the effect with but a thought but for this purpose that was not possible. I invoked the spell and the simple rune manifested above my palm. I was careful to only channel a tiny trickle of power into it, barely enough for the rune to maintain coherency.

"Here is the light spell, now we need the temporary holding spell for the power to light it."

"Uhm, Kyra?"

"Yeah?"

"I can't see magic. You promised to teach me but you haven't."

Was that a tone of rebuke in her voice? We were at war! There was no time for education.

"Shit. That's right. Uhm, here. Look at this."

I picked up a twig from the ground and ripped the grass out of the ground in front of us along with its roots with a twist of my magic. A sweep of force flattened the soft soil beneath. I used the twig to draw out the rune in the dirt. It looked much more complex than it actually was when it was drawn on a surface since it was impossible to draw three dimensional objects on a flat plane.

"This is the rune for the light spell."

"All that for a bit of light?"

"Yeah, if you want to do it formally. It is such a simple concept that a mere thought is enough normally. But this is the actual incantation. Try it, channel some power into it and it should obey you even though you did not draw it yourself."

Her brow furrowed as she focused and within half a minute the rune started to glow faintly. Gaining confidence she poured power into the rune and it soon shone with a harsh brilliance. The light winked out when she cut off the flow of power. Her expression of intense focus turned into one of exaltation.

"I did it!"

I wanted to kiss her then and there, she was so adorable in her jubilation, but I controlled myself.

"Indeed you did. Good job."

A small trickle of sweat dripped down her cheek. Channelling power into a rune was much more difficult than invoking a spell of your own since your mind had no intuitive way to find the way for the power and the crude symbol in the dirt would resist and leak in unexpected ways. If it had been precisely drawn with ink on paper it would have been much easier. Best of course would have been to inscribe the rune properly into a three dimensional medium like a crystal with clearly defined entry points for the power, like the grenade stone I had used against the Outcasts. That had been almost effortless.

"Now, this here is the power holding spell."

This spell was not a single rune, it was much too complex to be expressed so easily and I carefully copied the runes from the book onto the ground.

"Can't you just use the design in the book? Wouldn't that be easier?"

I was impressed by her conclusion, I had not told her about the effect various mediums had on the spell inscribed on them.

"Sure, but the power coursing through it is likely to destroy the medium and I am not ready to part with this book yet. Now let me focus for a bit."

It took several long minutes to copy the spell and Red watched me intently as I did. Every move I made was followed by her intense green gaze. I pointed at it with the twig when I finished.

"This will hold power for a while."

"How long?"

"Uhm… Until it runs out? You see, as long as the spell is ignited it will feed from the power within to sustain itself. When the power is out the spell dissipates."

"So the more power you put into it, the longer it will last?"

"Yes, but at the same time the power will dwindle faster."

"Why?"

"The more power it contains, the more power it requires to contain it. Think of it like a pouch. The more you want it to hold the more leather is required to make it."

"But the volume of a pouch increase quicker than the surface area."

I glared at her suspiciously. "I thought you knew little of geometry?"

"What? I thought that was obvious."

"Clever girl." She blushed prettily at my compliment. Her intuitive grasp of the relation between radius, volume and surface surprised me. She would learn magic swiftly, she just needed a lot of training to make it easier for the power to flow through her. It was like running, the more you ran the faster and longer you could keep it up and she had used precious little magic in her life. Instead she had focused on physical training.

"Anyway, this spell here holds the power, and this one consumes it. Now let's do the timer spell."

It was much simpler than the power holding spell and I copied it quickly.

"Now, power goes into the timer here," I pointed at a trailing end of the rune that would form a channel when expanded into three dimensions, "and when it triggers a surge will come out here," I pointed on a similar channel on the other side. I pointed out the input to the light spell, which had no output since the spell itself was the output and I indicate the input and output of the power holding spell.

"What I don't understand is how to link them together."

"I see." Red studied the runes intently for a long while before she glanced at me hesitantly. She reached out and dug her finger into the soil and drew a line from the power spell to the light spell.

"It can't be that simple, can it?"

"Only if we wanted to feed the power directly into the light." I made a small adjustment to the connection, adding another line parallel to the first. "But we want it to start feeding power when the timer triggers."

"Oh." Without hesitation she drew two parallel lines from the output of the timer to join the channel between the power and the light spell. "Would that work?"

"No, that would only cause the power from the storage spell to be channelled into the output of the timer spell. At best that would simply just not work, at worst it might destroy the timer with unpredictable results."

"Why unpredictable?"

"The meaning of a rune is dependent on the direction of flow of power, reversing the direction does not directly reverse the effect since the runes are not perfectly symmetrical, instead they are turned into a completely different spell."

"Well, fuck."

"Right now? I thought we were doing magic." My eyes widened as I realised how my joke may be interpreted. I silently cursed my dry humour, especially considering the weird tension between us. She bumped my shoulder lightly with my own.

"Maybe later, but let's focus."

Had I heard that correctly? Had she just offered herself to me? Should I kiss her? I stared at the back of her head as she leaned toward the runes to study them. Eventually I chickened out, yet again, and leaned forward to join her.

"We need a dam."

I blinked. "A dam?"

"Yes. It is a sort of gate in a canal that you can lower to cut off the flow of water."

"Yes I know what a dam is, you idiot. How does this apply here?"

"Now who is the idiot? Do you seriously mean to say that I understand something about magic that the great Dragonbane herself does not?"

"Careful, Red. It is not becoming of a student to mock her teacher." I punctuated my words with a playful growl.

"Yes, Mistress. Please don't punish me," she looked up at me under lidded eyes and added under her breath, "Too much."

"You are not too old to spank, young lady!"

She stiffened and I worried that I may have gone too far. The corners of her mouth tugged uncertainly and her eyes were wide. She shook herself and turned back to the runes and pointed at the join in the channels between the three spells.

"We need a dam here, and here. This one should be open," she indicated the output from the timer spell, "and this one should be closed," she pointed at the output of the storage spell. "When the timer triggers and the power flows here, the dam from the storage opens and the one from the trigger closes," she frowned before she continued, "perhaps it would be better in the opposite order."

Now I was confused. "How so?"

"If the one from the storage opens first, before the timer output is closed there may leak some power from it into the output. Didn't you say that was bad?"

"Well, yes. But what makes you think that the power will flow in that direction? There will already be power coming from the timer spell."

"Yeah, but isn't the pressure in the storage greater? It may push the power back into the timer. Besides, what happens if the output from the timer is open when the timer dissipates. We can't ensure that it survives until the stored power is exhausted."

"Are you sure you are not a master Mage? I had not thought of that myself."

Red beamed at me. "We make a good team. You provide the raw power and the knowledge, I bring the brains. Also I am cute."

"Are you implying that I am not 'cute'?" I infused my voice with a dark tone, but I was only joking with her.

"Of course you are not cute."

Now I actually bristled.

"I'd describe you as beautiful. Fierce. Dangerous. But never cute."

"Good save." I was mollified. I could live with not being cute. I particularly liked her describing me as fierce. I returned to the subject at hand. It was getting difficult to see in the darkness so I took out my light gem from my pouch and set it to hover above us. With a thought I dimmed the blinding light to a more comfortable and, more importantly since we were hiding, discreet level. Red had not seen it before and her eyes went wide with wonder.

"Where did you get that?"

I could not keep a smug smile from my lips.

"I made it."

She stuck her tongue out at me. "Show off."

"Impressed?"

"Yes," she said reluctantly and she crossed her arms and glared at me but a smirk tugged at her lips.

"Good thinking about the dams, I think that may actually be the solution to the problem. Now we just need to figure out how the fuck to do it."

I was getting distracted by the smell of roasted meat as one of the Ithlaki was heating a haunch of venison with magic. We dared not make a fire in case the watchers on the walls of Dun Traelak saw the smoke over the treetops. I really preferred cooking the meat over a fire, it tasted so much better than eating magically cooked food. I spared Alissa a thought. We had shared our first bite of meat together and I hoped that she was well, if she still lived. Somehow I doubted it after all this time alone in the wilderness. Perhaps she had come across one of the other Clans but if neither the Bizhjerai or the Ithlaki, being the two Clans closest to where we had disembarked from the Pioneer, had encountered her I deemed her chances of survival low. It saddened me to think of the green haired womans demise so I chose to assume that she lived until it was proved otherwise.

Red threw up her hands.

"I have no idea. There must be something in that book of yours about some sort of decision making. I'll go fetch you some food."

"Thanks."

I dove back into the book in the light of the crystal and found a few bits and pieces that may be relevant but I could not make sense of them. I decided that I was too tired to understand it now and I put the book aside when Red returned with supper. Shortly afterwards we decided to call it an early night. I'd give it another try tomorrow before we started hunting for a suitable beast. Three of the Ithlaki would take the first watch and I bedded down next to Red beneath the low boughs of a tree. Runes and thoughts about spell conditionals spun before my minds eye and sleep was slow to claim me.

## Chapter 20

I tightened my grip around the waist if the Ithlaki warrior in the saddle in front of me. We had found traces of a beast an hour ago. Or at least the Ithlaki claimed that they had found traces. I saw no difference between the ground that they were so interested in and all the other surrounding it but they were quite certain. We carefully threaded our way through the underbrush in search of the beast and I was getting bored and so my mind drifted. Mostly it strayed with some worry towards Red. She had been torn between joining me on this hunt and joining the group that would crawl toward the fortress. In the end she had been decided by the fact I was the only member of this party that would enter the fortress and she simply would not hear of staying on the outside. The rest of my group here would break off while still in the forest as to not alert the defenders of our presence. The whole plan hinged on the residents of Dun Traelak believing that the beast was straying too close. If they saw any of us they were likely to just lock up and wait it out. The risk of them getting caught in the open was an ever present worry in the back of my mind but it was out of my control and I tried to not let it rattle me. I forced myself to consider the concept of the dams and conditional spells that Red had suggested the evening before but I had not yet figured it out. I felt that I was close, but close would not cut it. If I could not figure it out in time I would simply have to destroy the generator directly, even though it might kill me. No, it would definitely kill me. With sudden clarity I realised that there were no hesitation behind my decision, I was truly ready to die for these people. No, not for these people. For Red. Somehow she had found a way into my cold, empty heart and filled it with her warmth, and I owed her everything for that. Despite being a captive for almost my entire stay with the Bizhjerai it had been among the happiest times of my life since I got old enough to understand the darkness of my homeland. At some unspoken communication the Ithlaki all froze and halted their horses. One of the beasts snorted and the rider patted its neck soothingly.

"What is it, have you found it?" I whispered the question softly into the ear of the man before me and I could see his long braids bob as he nodded. He twisted to face me and responded just as softly.

"Right ahead, beyond these trees." He carefully nudged the horse forwards and it stepped gingerly around a large shrubbery. I could almost feel its apprehension through its flanks and then it rounded the tree. The beast was like nothing I had ever imagined and it was not just its size that amazed me. It was easily twice as high as the bear that had attacked Alissa and me but it walked on two legs. They were short and stubby, unlike its arms that almost dragged over the ground. Each finger was almost as thick as my wrist and its body was covered in patches of long fur, the rest was composed entirely of wrinkly pinkish-gray skin. It sat on the ground and reached out to a nearby bush and ripped it out of the ground seemingly effortlessly. It crammed a large portion of the bush into its wide mouth and bit down. The crackle of breaking twigs disguised the hoof beats of our horses but it must have heard us even so. It turned its head, still chewing slowly as it glared balefully at us. Its eyes bulged out of the sides of its head as if from an internal pressure. It lowered the bush from its face and I recoiled in horror from what I saw and understanding struck me full on. I had thought that I had become inured to the horrors of life after all I'd seen and done but this monstrosity was too much even for me. The face was distorted and brutal but there was no doubt that it had once been human. This had one day been a young babe, beloved by its mother, and Grasax had turned it into... Whatever this was. It did not seem to consider us a threat and was content chomping along on its shrubbery, grinding the vegetative matter with its flat teeth. Only its front teeth that was a sharp and vicious betrayed any sort of carnivorous tendencies. The Ithlaki around me exchanged nervous glances and I saw a few of them swallow with trepidation. I wondered if they had ever seen a creature like this before but I dared not raise my voice in fear of startling the creature into action. I felt almost bad to disturb the creature and possibly sacrificing its life for my own ends. I pushed the feeling aside, I had done worse before. I had sacrificed actual people for my own ends before. This creature was no longer human, just a beast and it would do nicely as a distraction. I leaned forward and whispered to the Ithlaki again.

"Will we be able to outride it?"

"Probably."

"Probably?"

"I've never seen one of this kind before, but look at the legs. They are short and thick, he is not likely to be faster than our horses."

I glanced around at the other men and they turned their horses, prepared to launch into a gallop. I twisted around to face the beast that was now behind me. It stared at us placidly as it finished its shrubbery. I traced a rune in the air and charged it with power. Hesitating just a moment I sent it streaking toward the creature. To my surprise its eyes traced the spell with something that might have been concern on its distorted face. It could see the magic! The spell struck it squarely in its wide chest and it jerked as corposant lightning flickered across its torso. It spasmed slightly as the magic sent tendrils of pain through its nerves and it roared in fury. Quicker than I had thought possibly for a being of that size it surged to its short legs and charged us. With a lurch that almost threw me off the horse the Ithlaki galloped away. I looked backward and saw the creature come hurtling closer, running on all fours now.

"Faster!" I shouted the command, all subtlety forgotten in our mad dash. Our horse was the slowest, carrying two riders, and the beast was catching up. Two of the Ithlaki had fallen back to ride alongside the beast. They dared the reach of its long arms and jabbed it with their spears. It snorted and lashed out with its arms, throwing horse and man end over end. It stopped and pounced on the fallen horse and ripped it apart with a single massive jerk of its arms. The rider had vanished into the undergrowth and our quick dash swiftly left him behind. I hoped that he had survived and would stay hidden until danger had passed. The beast crammed horseflesh into its mouth and seemed content to feed so I threw another of the pain spells at it. We had almost travelled outside of my range by then but the spell provoked the beast to charge after us again. Before long it had caught up to us and I could hear its great heaving breaths almost on my neck. The Ithlaki fell back again but this time they approached from behind before they poked it with their spears again. This time the wide swing of its arm missed completely but the motion threw off its gait and we gained some ground on it. The pattern established itself a few more times and another Ithlaki fell when his horse snagged a hoof on a root or rock hidden by the foliage. This time I could hear him die as his neck broke with a loud crack when his head struck a fallen log. The beast ignored the fallen man and charged after us, obviously too enraged to feed. The blood of the horse it had slain covered its torso and dripped from the shaggy fur on its chin and steam billowed from its wide nostrils. We rounded a tree and the beast did not bother to dodge around it. The trunk splintered as it merely shouldered it aside with seemingly no effort. It did slow down significantly, robbed of momentum by the impact. My rider noticed and used the tactic several times more when the beast got to close rather than risk the lives of any more of his Clansmen. They still had to do it once more to distract the beast so that my rider could slow down enough for me to dismount at the edge of the forest. Even though I was on my own against the towering monster I was relieved to be off the horse and back on my feet. I trusted my legs more than the horse for they would at least obey my every command unlike the fickle horses. I jumped from the back of the creature and spun to face the beast. I had to work quickly. Even as I watched the beast grabbed a horse by the head and flung it over its shoulder along with its rider. They vanished into the thick foliage with loud screams. I traced the rune of the pain spell as the beast lashed out and swiped the head off one of the three remaining Ithlaki. My rider kicked his horse and lowered his spear. It struck the beast in the shoulder and lodged there and his action saved the life of his remaining friend but it cost him his own as the beast caught him around the chest with its other arm. My spell of pain struck it in the side just as its teeth clamped down around his head and ground his skull into fragments. It dropped the limp body when the spell ripped through its nerves and it roared and charged me. Time to get the fuck out. I prayed to the Elements that there would be no keen eyed watchers on the walls and I turned on my heel and ran. I pulled heavily on my blood magic and I shot across the open ground faster than the horses had. Granted, the horses had been encumbered by riders and the rough terrain, out here they may have outrun me. Especially across longer distances. My feet and knees screamed at the torturous weight I forced upon them and I pulled even harder on my magic. Energy surged through me and I loped with long strides. I dared not look across my shoulder to see how close the creature was for a single misstep would cause me to fall and tumble. If the breakneck speed of the fall would not kill me then the beast surely would just moments after. The Fortress loomed in the distance. In truth it was not more than a few hundred yards between the edge of the forest and Dun Traelak but with a crazed monster more than ten times your own weight even such distances seemed incredibly long. My mind shrunk until only three things existed; the pounding of my feet, the slowly approaching walls and the wheezing beast behind me. The wall inched closer and I could barely make out people on its walls. They were not scurrying about so they must not have spotted the beast and me in the dark of night but it was only a matter of time before they would be able to hear its heavy footfalls. I could almost feel its breath on my neck as I neared the wall. This was the most critical part of this stage of the plan. They must not see me, but they must see the beast. My dark crystal armour camouflaged me well against the dark grass and I angled my face down to remove the possibility of any reflected torchlight in my eyes. Again I prayed to the Elements to let this work. I slowed down to avoid slamming into the wall at full speed and just a few steps from it I threw myself to the side and rolled through the grass. The beast was too heavy, and too stupid to have slowed down and it slammed headfirst into the wall with a great thud. It roared in pain and stumbled back onto its rear. I crawled through the tall grass, heart pounding and breath heaving. My legs were killing me and I doubted I could stand even if I wanted to. As long as I had been in motion I could stay that way but now my legs were thoroughly exhausted. I used my elbows to drag myself into cover. I was in the gap between the shield and the wall and as soon as the beast recovered its senses it would be on me in a flash. My gamble had paid off and the shield changed to become impermeable. The beast had reared back outside it and I was safe from it, for now. I scrambled to put more distance between me and it, closer to the great gates where Red and her Ithlaki would be hiding. At least I hoped they were. The beast roared and shouts in response erupted from atop the walls. Light blazed as they cast spells of lighting on the walls and I hunkered down in the grass. Orders rang out and the shield turned permeable again. The beast was not a threat to the walls. The great doors opened slowly and a great many men carrying heavy spears surged forth. The column of men passed me within just a few yards and I held my breath and tried to will my pounding heart to slow down. I was sure that if they just stopped and listened they would hear it. Instead they fanned out and cautiously approached the beasts. It whimpered and eyed the steel points with apparent familiarity. The multitude of scars on its hide made much more sense to me suddenly. Dark shapes on the other side of the gates rose from the grass and I almost let out a cry of relief when the light reflected off a mane of red hair. No one was watching the gate, all of the eyes above were fixed on the struggle against the monster.

"Kyra?!" The cry was more of a loud whisper.

"Over here. Can't stand."

Red rushed toward my voice and found me lying in the grass.

"Are you hurt?"

"No. Just exhausted."

Red pulled my arm over her shoulders and motioned for one of the Ithlaki to take my other arm. They lifted me between them and dragged me toward the gate like a prisoner. The ten Ithlaki in our group hurried through the gate. A small group of men met us on the other side and they drew up short in surprise as they saw us. The Ithlaki tightened their holds on their weapons. No, no, no, no! We can't fight them, that would give us away! I could not say anything or we would be found out for sure. Luckily one of the men were quicker in thought than the others and stepped forward.

"The beast broke our spears, and we have a wounded."

He waved in my direction. The man threw me a disdainful look where I hung but Red had dragged me into a shadowed spot and he must have not been able to see my strange armour.

"Take her to the pit and rearm yourselves. I'll see you outside."

He led his troops through the gate without a second look at us. I blinked in surprise. That was easy. Almost too easy. And what was this about a pit? Did they not have healers here? We wasted no time and Red and the Ithlaki man dragged me away from the gate, into the deep shadows between the buildings inside. There were not many buildings aside from the main keep and the shield tower and one of the men peeked carefully into each one. We found one that was a warehouse and we rushed inside and closed the door carefully behind us. I conjured a weak light so we could see our hiding place. The walls were lined with muskets, hundreds of them, and barrels of what must be black powder. Neat pyramids of cannonballs were piled wherever there was space. There were plenty of places to hide and they were unlikely to come here before the host of Clans Bizhjerai and Ithlak arrived tomorrow. As soon as the host arrived and the defenders started to prepare we needed to move. This armoury would be swarming with enemies. Red put me down and I leaned back against the pile of cannonballs. My legs ached but at least my heart had slowed down to more normal levels. Now we just had to survive in the keep for twelve to eighteen hours. That should not be that hard at all.

## Chapter 21

None of us had gotten much sleep during the remainder of the night. At first the roars of the beast and the men fighting to drive it off kept us awake but as the silence of night dragged on we grew increasingly nervous. I tried to distract myself, both from the pain in my legs and lungs but also from my increasing sense of trepidation, by studying the book on spells. Red sat next to me, staring at me with wide eyes. If not for our precarious situation her attention would have pleased me immensely.

"Kyra." Her voice was so low that I barely heard it, she scrambled closer to sit next to me.

"What?"

"Do you think you can cast that timer spell yet?"

"Probably. Maybe. I think so? Why?"

"The powder in here. If we can destroy it before we make our move it could save the lives of many of our people. It would also be a fine distraction when we move for the tower."

I froze at her words. 'Our people'. She had said 'our'. I ignored the warm feeling in my belly.

"That is an excellent idea, robbing them of their weaponry would put the Clans at an advantage, though it doesn't feel right."

Her face was a picture of surprise.

"Are you getting squeamish on me? Your ruthlessness was one of the things I admired about you."

"No, not that. Just think about what kind of army the Bizhjerai could field if we claimed these weapons."

"And there is the Kyra I have come to know and like," she said with a smirk, "even so, we better make sure to win this battle first. If we keep these weapons in the hope to claim them and then fail..." She let her words trail off.

"Yeah, I hear you. Let's experiment some while we wait, find me a splinter of wood or something."

She did not question why I wanted a piece of wood and she started to stand but dropped down again almost immediately as the door opened. We had positioned ourselves to be out of sight of the door and every one of us froze. Cheerful whistling announced the man who had entered and the soft light of a lamp spread from the entrance. It was dawn but he still needed the lamp to see properly. I glanced at the Ithlaki hiding on the other side of the aisle and he pulled a dagger from his belt. I would rather we not kill this intruder but if we had to we could stash his body in the shadows and hope that he was not missed too soon. None of us breathed as I heard the footsteps come closer. I dared not prepare a spell in case he would be able to sense it so instead I followed the example set by the Ithlaki and curled my fingers around my dagger. I pulled my legs slowly in beneath me to be able to spring into action. A small gasp of pain escaped me as my tortured legs curled and my heart stopped. The whistling cut off immediately. After a few long tense moments it resumed again and I relaxed slightly. My thighs were starting to cramp up from my awkward position but I dared not move again for fear of making more sounds. I heard the familiar sound of a hammer being cocked. Was he loading a weapon? Was his whistling a ruse? He must have heard my gasp of pain. A thunk of metal on wood announced that he had put the weapon aside and then the faint rasp of steel against leather reached my ears. The metal whistled through the air as he tried the balance of a sword. With a satisfied grunt the footsteps receded and the door closed behind him. A chorus of relieved sighs thundered through the silence and a hysterical giggle escaped Red. I could not help but grin back at her. She rested her head on my shoulder as her own shoulders shook with barely suppressed, and slightly hysterical, laughter and I stroked her back until she calmed down.

"The wood, quickly before another arrives."

She quickly returned with what must be a large splinter from one of the shelves. I decided to risk a bit of magic, it would not require much and would not be perceptible far beyond these walls. I cradled my free hand around the end of the splinter and it burst into flame. I let it burn until it went out of its own and I waved it through the air to cool the remaining embers. I tested it by dragging it across the stone floor and it left a smear of coal.

"Look at you. Just a few weeks ago you had never even seen wood and here you go making a stylus just like that."

I ignored her comment and drew out the rune for the light spell. I started drawing the timer spell but I had not yet managed to memorise it properly so I had to consult the book. Then I went on to the storage spell and then I connected the three. I flipped to the page about composite spells and considered the runes. I had already decided what to try first but I reconsidered the runes. I drew out the final conditions. It was not obvious how it was supposed to go together and there were no examples in the book to base the design on. Each condition was unique to the sought after effect and the construction of the runes depended on understanding their nature. My work was equal parts instructions and improvisation and I had no idea if it would work. I glanced at Red.

"Ready?"

"Yeah. Do it."

I channelled a tiny trickle of power into the store spell until the the runes glowed faintly. The small amount of power would be consumed by the storage spell itself in short order but it did not need to last long. I charged up the light spell until it was just about to ignite and then I charged the timer spell. Now it was just a matter of waiting until it triggered and observe. I had set it for five seconds and I counted under my breath. Nothing happened. I waited another five seconds, just to make sure that I had not set it to more time than I had planned. The spells faded.

"Shit."

"Don't worry. You have more ideas, don't you?"

I nodded and smudged out the connection runes and started over with my next idea. I did not tell her that that had been the most promising solution. Again I started charging the storage spell, then the light spell and then the timer. Again nothing. It would appear that I would have to destroy the generator myself. The thought saddened me, for I did not want to leave Red behind. I would have to convince her to leave me in the tower somehow.

"I have a question."

"Ask it."

"Why do you charge the timer and light spell before?"

"They must be invoked first or else there is nothing for the power to work on."

The question baffled me, she must have known this by now after our discussion yesterday.

"Well, yes. But why not connect them to the storage spell instead. That way the entire spell will be connected to the power source. What if the timer is set for such a long time that the power in the light spell fades?"

I stared at her and her face fell.

"That was dumb, wasn't it?"

"Quite the contrary. It was brilliant. Despite your lack of knowledge your insight amaze me." I handed her the makeshift stylus. "Show me."

Uncertainly she accepted the stylus and peered at the runes with an adorable expression of concentration. I forgot the dangerous position we were in as I watched her. Despite her uncertainty her hand was firm and she drew the connection channels without hesitation.

"Why did you make them this way?"

I pointed at the unfamiliar shape of the channels.

"They don't need that much power, I felt as if that shape would choke the flow. Is it wrong?"

"I don't know, it just looks unfamiliar. Lets try it."

This time I channelled power only into the storage spell and the other two charged on their own shortly thereafter. The runes came to light as the power coursed through them, invoking the spell as it went. I was amazed.

"Did it work?"

Yet again I had forgotten that she could not see the effect for herself.

"Yes. You are a fucking genius, Red, are you sure that you've not had any training?"

Her cheeks reddened at my praise but I was sincere. My eyes were on her face and was surprised by the sudden gasp that escaped her lips. I turned back to the spell and let out a gasp of my own. The light spell glowed with a faint white light. The runes winked out along with the spells as the power in the storage ran out.

"It worked." I'm not sure if it was I or Red who gasped out the words. Relief surged through me. Perhaps I would not have to give my life to take the shield down after all. A sudden pressure on my lips surprised me as she darted in and pressed a quick but firm kiss on my lips.

"It fucking worked!" She exclaimed jubilantly.

"Yeah," my voice was as excited as hers and not only at the success of the spellwork, "I would never have been able to figure it out without you."

"I am sure you would have figured it out eventually."

I did not contradict her, I was too stunned by her sudden kiss. I licked my lips to taste the lingering sensation and a shy smile tugged at my lips. Her green eyes watched my tongue and her own darted out to wet her own lips. I fished out the small grimoire from my pouch and hastily copied the runes with the stylus. I wanted to have the template ready for when we reached the generator. I put the grimoire in my inner coat pocket for easy access.

The rest of the day passed slowly and we waited with increasing trepidation. Twice more someone entered the warehouse but we avoided detection. We were in the process of eating the last of our rations, forcing it down despite our trepidation, when the door opened again. We stopped chewing and waited for him to leave like the others. Unfortunately this fellow was on a mission and he strode confidently toward the far wall. I could hear his footsteps coming closer and his path would bring him past the place were Red and I hid. I exchanged a glance with her and I noted her quickened breath. He may not see us going in, but he would without a doubt see us on his way out and there were no way we could move to another hiding place without him hearing us. Red drew her dagger and I emulated her. We moved slowly to make as little sound as possible. I pulled up my protesting legs to my chest to present a smaller surface but I doubted it would be enough. The man walked past us and luckily his eyes were fastened to a particular weapon on the far wall. When he was past us Red surged to her feet and slammed her dagger into his back, straight through his kidney. Good girl. Most people would go for the throat when they sought to kill silently but it was much easier to react to. Besides, cutting a throat could be loud if you missed the larynx and you had to place the blade perfectly. Cutting throats was not something you did in a single swipe. The kidney though was a whole other story. Being stabbed in the kidney was so painful that the entire body tensed up, so much so that it was impossible to breathe and much less so to scream. I'd even seen people knocked out cold by a mere punch to the kidneys. The man stiffened in pain and only a strangled huff of air escaped his mouth as his lungs seized up. Red was not content to end there though and she quickly withdrew her blade and sank it between his ribs to puncture his lung, systematically removing his ability to make noise. Only then did she go for the throat, grabbing his hair and pushing his chin down toward his chest. I had learned from experience that pulling someones head back to slit their throats only made the relevant blood vessels retreat back toward the spine. Pushing the head forward did the exact opposite. The man was still paralysed by pain and was unable to resist her as she slid the point of her long dagger into the side of his neck. I could hear the soft scrape of steel on bone even through the flesh. Now was the time to pull his head back and force his jugulars against the edge of her blade. She sawed back and forth in welters of blood until her blade ripped through his skin. She had nearly severed his head and it fell back onto her shoulder as his life spurted over her in thick pulsing gushes. She did not flinch and held him the short moments before his knees weakened and she lowered him to the ground. The stones was covered in blood, but that could not be helped. I myself would have been content with the stab to the lung. Id have poked a hole in the other lung for good measure and then stash the body somewhere do die on its own. Now it would be nearly pointless to hide the body for all the blood. I did not rebuke her though, just made a mental note to give her the advice later if we both survived the battle.
