I stood up and spoke in a loud whisper.

"No point in hiding any longer. Anyone who comes in will see the blood. Take up positions by the door. Let them come in before you kill them, lets hope that they come one by one otherwise we will have to make our move earlier than expected. Without the distraction of the host our mission will be nigh impossible but we will have to try."

Grim silence answered me and we took up positions. I spent a few minutes drawing up the spells on one of the barrels of black powder. Instead of a light spell I inscribed one that would generate heat. I'd charge it up before we left for the tower, or if we were overwhelmed. I'd rather blow this armoury up with us in it than let them have it, out of spite. It would be a pointless gesture since if we could not bring the shield down then it would not matter how well armed the defenders were but it would be a last insult to Grasax and his slaves. We settled down to wait, but the tension had increased tenfold.

## Chapter 22

A blast of a horn rattled us all. The alarm could only mean one thing, the Clans were here. We had to move, swiftly. The Ithlaki we left behind in the forest must have already found the host and informed the Chiefs of our plan. They would have no choice but go along with it and despite their weariness after their march they had to prepare for battle. There were only one door to the armoury and we would have to risk using it. I was sure that a number of defenders were coming here to arm themselves. We had already helped ourselves to as many weapons that we could carry. All of us had several pistols in our belts and carried a musket. I'd have liked us to carry more than one but the longer it took for them to identify us the better it would be. I had a sudden stroke of genius and ordered the men to gather up as many muskets as they could. I explained my plan quickly and several chuckled. A few paled but even they had wry grins on their faces. There were nothing else to do so we huddled up around the door. I stood in the middle of the group, slouching my back and bending my knees, so that their bodies would obscure my distinctive armour. I had argued with Red, claiming that I should not wear it and instead wear the armour of the man she had slain to blend in better. She had won the argument, arguing that we were inevitably to be spotted as hostiles and once that happened my armour would be worth more than the few extra moments its absence would buy us. The door was opened and we rushed out, trying to look as hurried as possible. With our state of mind it did not take that much acting. Two men immediately jumped back from the door and looked at us with surprise. The armoury had been expected to be empty. Each of the Ithlaki carried many muskets in their arms and they hurriedly pushed a musket at the men.

"Quickly, arm yourselves! These are loaded."

The men accepted the muskets and before they could react further we had hurried along. We distributed more of the empty muskets as we made our way toward the shield tower. I was surprised at how effective the plan were. They did not even check the load of the weapons. Their lack of discipline disgusted me. The two guards on each side of the door leading into the shield tower watched us with bemused expressions. They were already armed but they still reflexively accepted the muskets that were thrust into their chests. With their hands occupied with the useless weapons they were defenceless at the sharp blades that followed a moment later. They died silently, but their corpses would alert anyone who glanced our way. I got to work on the lock, expanding my senses into it. It was good one and I had barely started figuring out how to open it when a voice rang out behind us.

"Hey! What are you doing? Get onto the walls!"

The Ithlaki had arranged themselves to block the line of sight to me and the two dead guards but the officer who had spotted us was coming closer. He must have spotted the dead guards, or been otherwise tipped off for a moment later his voice rose in a warning. One of the Ithlaki shot him and for once the smooth bore muskets proved accurate for I heard his body hit the cobbles a moment later. I gave up on picking the lock, we would be overcome in moments. Instead I blasted it apart from the inside with a loud sound of tearing metal and withdrew the now slack bolt before I pushed the door open. We hustled inside in a rush and for the first time I beheld the generator. It was made of stone and its surface was covered in runes that shone brilliantly. The tower was empty on the inside and had no floors or furnishings and the inside was inscribed with large runes all the way to the top.

"Bar the door, hold them off me!"

I trusted that the Ithlaki would protect me and I rushed to the generator. It was protected by a smaller version of the barrier that surrounded the fortress and I launched a bolt of force at it. The bolt slid off the shield without making a dent. I looked closer with my magesense and what lay below astonished me. It was a magical fount, like the one below the Skylands but much smaller. That was the source of Grasax' power. I suddenly understood the reason for the semi-permeable shield around the fortress. It contained the power within, creating a much denser magical field within its confines. Without it the power from the fount would dissipate over the plains. It also meant that this smaller shield would be very powerful and nothing I could do would be powerful enough to breach it. It would take far more than I could store inside me to even put a minor pressure on it. The tower itself was shielded to keep the magic field from outside leak in and disturb the enchantment, the interior was a magical desert. Red stared at me.

"What are you waiting for?"

"I can't break this, it is too powerful."

"What?!"

"It is powered by a fount, it will recharge near instantly unless completely overloaded. I don't have enough power for it."

"But you said..."

"That was under the assumption that it was fed by a capacitor stone, not being directly fed by a fucking fount!"

She stepped close and lowered her voice.

"Use us. Take our souls as power."

I looked into her eyes and shook my head. I couldn't kill her for this. The Ithlaki I could sacrifice, even myself, but never her. But I already had. The realisation struck me in the belly like a musket shot. I had led her inside the fortress. If this generator did not fall we would all die within minutes. Even so I could not bring myself to drink her life for my spellwork. My thoughts churned in vain attempts to find a solution. Instead I lied to her.

"I'm not sure it will be enough."

"Do it anyway. If we don't succeed we are dead anyway."

Her courage and determination was admirable and I reached up to cradle her face. I wanted to touch her one last time before we made our last stand. I lamented that my gauntlets kept my skin from touching her soft cheek. I withdrew my hand and stared at my gauntlet. Red's eyes widened in sudden hope.

"You have that face."

"What face?"

"That face you make when you have an idea."

"I do."

I had found my answer. I set my armour and clothes to dissolve and fished out my grimoire. I flipped the pages to the page with the template and drew the stylus from the back. A loud whoosh and a series of loud booms echoed through the door. The walls shook as the armoury went up in flames and a hysterical giggle escaped me. The door pounded once as something massive struck it. The Ithlaki had braced it with their bodies but they stumbled from the impact. The defenders had brought a ram to get inside. I ignored their plight and drew a test line on the shield around the generator. The ink stayed where it was. The shield was strong enough to draw on. I chuckled, this would actually have been more difficult if the shield had not been quite this powerful. I copied the template and made some on the fly adjustments, I just hoped that they would work on the first try. I drew my large revolver and ejected the cylinder, I chose a shield breaker round and put it in place and locked it in place with a telekinetic cantrip. I drew a containment spell around it that I connected to the storage spell before I ejected the magazine of explosive rounds from my rifle and even ejected the one already in the chamber. I emptied the magazine into my hand and affixed them all in different angles outside the containment spell and connected their primers to a conditional spell I drew on the side. The door behind us cracked and fell off its hinges and warriors rushed inside in. The Ithlaki carried several pistols and a musket each and I ignored the boom of gunfire as they killed the first group of warriors. A shot flattened against the shield next to me and Red crouched behind me, protecting us both with her metal plated wooden shield. I should probably have performed my work on the opposite side of the generator where we would be protected by it, as it was they could shoot freely at us through the door. The Ithlaki scattered to the sides, out of line of fire.

"Hurry up, Kyra! My shield won't hold for long."

Magic drifted inside through the doorway where the wards keeping it at bay had broken and I sucked it inside greedily. I was already at full capacity and the extra magic started leaking out painfully. I strengthened my personal shield to keep the power in but the pain did not abate much. It was not healthy to hold more than you could. In fact, it was downright dangerous. I surrounded the suspended rifle shots with another spell and yet another containment spell went around it. My clothes dissolved as I worked and I was nearly naked when the Outcasts attacked again. Several fell as the Ithlaki expended their shots and then joined the melee with short swords and spears. The door proved an effective choke point and they held it for long minutes. I double checked my work. It was sound, I hoped. I started channelling power into the storage spell as I reached up and undid my choker. The large blue crystal in the front shone brightly with the power that fuelled my armour. I affixed it in the centre of the storage spell and connected it with two swift swabs of the stylus. I replaced the stylus into the grimoire and put it in my belt pouch. I focused on emptying my power into the storage spell. A man stumbled and fell next to me and drew my attention. It was one of the Outcasts and he was bleeding through a large cut in the side. He reached for my throat with his fingers curled into claws. I stuck my hand into his wound and grabbed at his soul. I started drawing on his soul and fed the power into the spell. I turned my head over my shoulder and shouted at Red.

"Get me another one, alive!"

The man in my grip was weakening swiftly and was not a threat to me. Red understood and stood up and grabbed a man engaged with one of the Ithlaki. She clubbed him on the back of the head and threw him to me.

"Cut him! I need to get beneath his skin."

Her axe lashed out and opened his throat. I stuck my fingers inside, feeling the slippery inside of his throat, and started to drink his soul. His wound was fatal and his body relinquished his soul at almost the same time as the first man. Both men started burning as I ripped their souls free and the skin on my hands burned in agony. I withdrew my hands, holding their souls in my grip and I consumed them entirely. Their power went into the spell. The storage spell was close to overloading, I had not drawn it to contain the power of two entire souls as well as most of my own power. When the edges of my vision started to darken I pulled back. I estimated that I had one or maybe two blasts left in me before I was in danger of passing out. I straightened up and just barely managed to avoid stumbling. I set the timer for five minutes and connected the storage spell. I drew my revolvers and turned to the fight. The Ithlaki was pushed back into the room and would soon be completely surrounded. Only seven of the ten men we had brought with us was still standing but the door was choked with corpses.

"We need to get out, now. This place will go down in five minutes."

I shouted the words and charged toward the door. The Outcasts were not ready for me to join the fight and I distracted them from the back and the Ithlaki dispatched them. I was almost at the door when one of the men surged out in front of me. I had forgotten that I was naked apart from my weapons belt and left control gauntlet and could not charge into a rain of musket balls with relative impunity. I did not even have enough strength to muster a proper shield around myself. The Ithlaki took a single step outside and was instantly riddled with shots and he fell on his face. I leaped his corpse and squinted at the sudden brightness of the daylight. The defenders were as undisciplined as the others had been earlier and they had all fired their muskets. The rest of my party made their egress unopposed while the enemy reloaded and my vision adapted. I raised my pistols and smiled grimly. Before the Ithlaki had exited eleven men had fallen to my precision shots. I holstered my revolvers and drew two of the single shot pistols. At this range it would be near impossible to hit with any reliability so I charged along with my fellow warriors. Red whooped loudly by my side. Her face was frantic when I glanced at her and I could see her certainty of our impending death clear as day. Our mission was complete, whether the spell I had built would be enough to take the shield down no longer mattered. All that was left to us was to sell our lives dearly. The defenders looked around in shock at the sudden carnage my revolvers had wrought and their hesitation proved their undoing. I charged one man even as I shot his companion in the belly. I chose my opponent and shot him through the forehead at point blank. Even as he fell I dropped the spent pistol and darted two fingers into the large hole. The jagged edges of his skull cut small wounds into my fingers but I did not care. I curled my fingers through the mushy remnants of the contents within to maintain my grip as he fell and I grabbed at his fleeing soul. I ripped it out as his body combusted and I drank him down in a large gulp, like a woman dying of thirst that had finally found water. I was still far from my full strength but I was no longer almost helpless, magically speaking. Our sudden charge had bought a moment of respite but we were standing in the open. The air was thick with smoke from the burning armoury and obscured the sight of the men manning the wall. The smoke was the only thing keeping them from riddling us with shots for fear of hitting their own. We desperately needed a more defensible position. Red dashed past me.

"This way!"

I followed her without hesitation, trusting her judgement. The remaining Ithlaki followed her and we soon found ourselves between a smaller warehouse and the main keep. It was a good choke, but they would have a clear line of fire if they simply chose to stay outside and fire down the narrow alley. The Ithlaki started to reload the pistols they had pilfered. At least we would be able to return fire initially but if they were smart they could cycle men into the line of fire whereas we would be forced to remain in plain sight as we reloaded. Luckily it seemed that our escape had gone unnoticed due to all the smoke and we were allowed to catch our breaths for almost two minutes. If my mental counting was correct we would only have to sit tight for two more minutes before the host could advance and the shaman could break the outer wall down. We were not that lucky, a man ran past our hiding spot and saw us. His eyes widened and he called out a warning just as he was shot in the chest. He stumbled out of sight but the wound was fatal. It had completely demolished his lung. A group of men arrived to answer his call and the battle started. The Ithlaki maintained strict firing discipline, firing and crouching to reload to allow the next man to shoot over his head. Even so we lost three of them in short order but managed to kill almost ten of theirs. They had to move into position and then get ready to fire whereas the Ithlaki was already in position when they enemy showed themselves. The defenders tired of the game and charged inside. Several fell as the Ithlaki fired but then the melee began. I was trapped in the back, which might have been as well since I was unarmoured and their bayoneted muskets outranged my sword. Two of the Ithlaki fell and Red stepped forward into the front line. Then it happened. I felt the timer spell trigger. I could almost see the the power flowing down the conduits and through the runes. The containment field around the shield breaker would power up first and then the shield breaker would detonate. The spell would feed on the power from the storage spell and the containment field would focus the unleashed power into the shield, hopefully boring a hole through it. Then the explosive rounds would fire into the generator through the hole, hopefully destroying the generator. If they were enough, which I was sure that they were not, then the rest of the power in the storage spell and the powerstone on my choker would be dumped into the final spell and the containment spell around that would funnel all of the heat into the shield. Ironically enough it was the shield that protected the generator that would ultimately aid in its destruction. It would keep the inferno inside, focused on the enchanted stone and putting further strain on the generator. It took longer than I had thought, and I was getting worried even as I stabbed a man in the face over Red's shoulder. Perhaps the power channels were too thin and the power flowed too slowly? Perhaps the generator was simply too strong? Despair filled me and I resolved to die well. I pushed past Red and the remaining Ithlaki and lashed out with my sword. I did not care much about injuries and I slew two of the defenders with swift strikes. I was much more nimble with my sword than they were using their muskets as clubs and the narrow alley favoured my shorter weapon. I shouldered the bleeding corpses aside and charged the next two. One went down with the point of my sword in his belly and I swayed aside from the thrust of the others' bayonet. I cut his exposed shoulder and he lost control of his weapon as his fingers weakened. Completely open I prepared to thrust through his throat when the world went completely white. A moment later a thunderous boom reached my ears and gravel and larger rocks fell around us. Red dashed in front of me and raised her shield and I heard several heavy impacts against it. She stumbled back into me and we nearly fell in a tangle. A powerful magical blast passed through me and darkness fell.

## Chapter 23

I could not have been out long, the magical blast had just put me down briefly for Red had just barely scrambled to my side. She pushed my hair out of my face as I came to. Shards of broken rock dug into my back and she helped me to my feet. Her face was jubilant.

"You did it! The shield is down and the tower has fallen!" Her words petered out in coughs from the heavy cloud of stone dust that permeated the air. The silence from outside was telling, only the cries and shots from the walls reached us but the sounds was muffled by the dust. The blast must have cleared the space around the tower and the defenders would be kept busy by the host that must be rapidly approaching. The two still living Ithlaki pushed to their feet and joined Red and me as we ran out to inspect the battle and if possible help the host somehow. I used some of the power I had stolen to clear the air in a space around us and the destruction was appalling. Fallen masonry was everywhere, scattered around a shallow crater that still glowed with molten rock where the generator had been. The heat haze above it distorted the image of the main keep behind it. The defenders on the walls was firing at will and Clansmen must be dying outside. I racked my brain for some way to help them but my weapons was out of ammo and I was still naked. There was little just the four of us could do. A presence entered the range of my magesense rapidly and I spun in its direction. It was above us and a shadow emerged from the cloud of dust. It landed lightly next to the fount.

Grasax had joined the fight. The power radiating from him nearly blinded my magesense and I had to do the magical equivalent of squinting to see him. How could he contain so much power without burning away? It was incredible. He walked closer and emerged from the cloud. He looked odd, my magesense told me that he was incredibly powerful and very alive. My eyes told me that he was dead. His body was dry and shrivelled and his eyes were lidded and shrunken. He wore a simple blue robe that clung to his skeletal form and a thin fringe of hair spilled from his head above his ears and down to his shoulders. His body was dead, but his heart still beat slowly and his brain was rife with activity. He carried an unadorned staff covered in runes and with a crystal headpiece. I immediately recognised it for it was materialised magic like the crystal everything back home was made of. His dead eyes looked at us and despite his motionless face I could feel his disdain wash over us. He did not move, not even a twitch to aid him in his spell casting. I barely saw the runes form before I was thrown through the air. I landed hard on my shoulder and felt it be flayed open as I glided over the gravel. I struck a fallen piece of masonry and came to a painful stop. One of the Ithlaki tumbled to a stop next to me with blood pumping out of his severed arm. He was not dead and despite the grievous wound he sat up and tried to push to his feet. He seemed to not have understood that his arm was missing for he fell awkwardly as he tried to use it to rise. I saw no sign of Red or of the other Ithlaki and fear for the beautiful redhead settled in my belly. I sat up and shook the dizziness from my head. Grasax had already dismissed us as a threat and was striding toward the font. A powerful shield protected his dead body from the torrent of magic spilling to the sky even as he pulled more of it into himself. My eyes widened. He was already so full of power that no more should have been able to enter him. He raised his staff and the headpiece flared brightly. The cooling rock melted and flowed, starting to rise into the familiar shape of the generator. Even before the rock was fully formed I saw the runes appear in the surface. I marvelled at his control and seemingly effortless enchanting. He used no reference books, no visible pre-prepared gems or scrolls. It was as if he remade the enchantment from memory. The shaman had not yet managed to convince the earth to split the wall and I was not sure how long it would take Grasax to rebuild the generator. Already a ring of molten stone had started to form as if he intended to reform the tower as well. The fallen masonry shuddered and started to move toward him as if pulled by invisible strings. He needed the stone to feed the spell he was constructing. We could not defeat a being this powerful, even with the host among us. Even so I refused to give up and I struggled to my feet. The one armed Ithlaki had finally lost consciousness and I pulled a pistol from his belt. I checked the frizzen and praised the Elements that it was still unspent. I cocked the weapon and took careful aim. The power coursing through the air from Grasax made every hair on my body stand on end and my skin stung as I walked closer. A spear came hurtling through the air and glanced off his shield. He did not even flinch, just kept rebuilding the shield generator. I followed the path the spear had taken and saw Red. My heart soared at the sight of her, despite the blood pouring down her arm. She drew her axe and charged Grasax. The remaining Ithlaki attacked with her and his longer legs made him overtake my friend swiftly. He raised his sword and struck ineffectually at Grasax's shield and the liche finally reacted. He turned around without his work on the generator slowing down. The Ithlaki rose into the air as Grasax lifted his hand. He struggled uselessly against the invisible bonds that bound him and I thought I saw a flicker of a malicious smirk on the monsters grey lips. The skeletal claw clenched and the warrior burst apart as if crushed by an invisible hand. His head and torso crumpled and ribs poked through his skin. His belly burst and innards spilled forth to hang in pulsing ropes to the ground beneath his weakly twitching feet. Grasax unclenched his hand and the mangled corpse fell to the cobbles with a wet splash. Grasax lifted his hand again and Red rose into the air with howl of frustration and rage. Even as panic overcame me I felt a surge of pride that her scream was completely devoid of fear. I fired the pistol and the shot flattened next to his temple in a flash of magical sparks. This time Grasax did flinch and Red fell to the ground. She landed awkwardly and she cried out in pain as her ankle twisted and she collapsed. The runes formed in the molten rock immediately smoothed out as Grasax lost his focus and the molten rock resumed its natural flattened shape. A snarl twisted his dead face and he turned to me and I saw death staring into my soul. He drew on my soul, even though he was not touching me and I felt my already diminished power start to drain. I was still too far for him to rip my soul out entirely but I was weakening rapidly. I danced back to get out of his reach and he followed up with a fireball at my chest. I threw myself to the side and rolled into a crouch and came up next to the armless Ithlaki. I noted a bubble of blood on his lips inflate and then burst. He was still alive. Without hesitation I reached down and clamped my fingers on his wound and ripped the soul from his body. I drank him down as his body burned before me and I leaped clear of the flames. Infused with his power I was more than half my usual strength. I brushed my fingers over the hilt of my large pistol and started to pour power into one of the empty casings. I pulled heavily on the magic field around me and poured on the power. Grasax launched a ray of green power arcing toward me and I split my stream in two. The vast majority of my stream went into the shield and the ray struck it full on. I stumbled back and angled the shield to glance the ray off of it. It struck the stone cobbles and it flash-boiled into steam. He levelled his staff at me and the crystal flared and I knew I would die. I would not be able to block or deflect an attack channelled through his staff. At least he was no longer working on the generator and the molten rock were slowly spreading into a pool. I hoped that the shaman would be able to take advantage of the distraction Red and I had paid for with our lives. The ground leaped beneath our feet and threw us both to the ground. A great groan of tortured stone was followed by a deep rumble and the crack of shattering earth. The ground shook violently and a deep crack spread from beneath the wall and opened the courtyard. The stone fell into the crack as it widened and the wall collapsed with a deafening roar. Men who were too slow to get away fell into the crack and their screams cut off abruptly. Grasax was thrown into the fount of magic and the ensuing reaction when the raw magic spilled across his shield blinded me. His shield collapsed with a loud crack and his undead body burst into flames. The earth stopped shaking and the roar of the earth was replaced with the roar of the Clansmen outside. Grasax came flying out of the fount, completely immolated in magical flames. He landed lightly and the flames sucked into his body and winked out. His robe and flesh was charred and burned but he did not seem to even notice. His shield was still down! I drew my sword and charged him but Red was quicker. She sent her axe hurtling toward his face but he deftly knocked it aside with his staff, stepped back and lunged. Red was completely unprotected with her axe out of line and her shield dropped somewhere along her tumble. She started to twist aside. The walking corpse was surprisingly fast and neither of us truly understood his strength. The butt end of his staff struck Red in the belly, and then kept moving. It burst out of her back and time seemed to slow. I roared a denial and charged the liche. I could see her soul start to stream through the staff and into the liche. I dove into him and he fell to the cobbles beneath me. I could hear the wet sucking sound as the staff was ripped out of my friend. My own sword had found a home in the chest of the mage and I started to pull on his soul. It did not flow as easily as the others I had claimed and I assumed it must be because his body was not alive. Something else held it in place in his body. I was thrust into the air and pushed off the Mage and he rose to his feet as if pulled by invisible strings. Men scrambled over the rubble in the breach in the wall and swept aside the few defenders that had managed to set up a thin protective line. I saw the Chief of the Ithlaki leading from the front. The breach was packed with Clansmen that levelled their muskets at the liche. Red had collapsed behind shattered masonry but I lay in the open. I raised a shield to protect myself and I saw a much more powerful one erupt from the liche’s decrepit form. In desperation I pulled my large revolver and fired the single shield breaker I had managed to recharge. The shot shattered on his shield and the familiar arcs of actinic lightning spread to envelop it, probing for weaknesses and disrupting the spell form. His shield failed and the Clansmen fired. Most of the shots went wide, several striking my shield and the backlash almost knocked me out. A dozen or so shots struck Grasax and threw him off his feet. A cheer went up from the Clansmen, victory was ours! I was not as easily fooled. I had stabbed him through the heart and he had barely seemed to notice. The dead man did his rising trick again and the cheer died down. Only a few men at the edges had not noticed as they fought the increasing stream of defenders. Grasax grinned, showing blackened and rotted remnants of teeth, and levelled his staff at the men. The Ithlaki Chief roared and charged straight at the liche. The crystal flared and a massive wall of force erupted from him and travelled swiftly toward the charging warriors. It shaved a thin layer of stone from the ground as it went in a spray of shrapnel and it struck the men with massive force. It was as if they had been struck by a tram on the Skyway. They flattened and burst apart and their torn remains was flung back into their fellows before they joined the tumble. Dozens died along with their Chief and the breach was swept clear. I was stunned by the sight. I had never seen such swift slaughter, nor such massive feats of magic. I could not tear my eyes from the mangled corpses scattered about. How could we defeat this creature? He should not be able to channel this amount of power without his body burning.

"Kyra!"

The cry was weak, but the silence that had fallen allowed me to hear it. Red was lying not far away, clutching the wound on her belly. I was sure that she was trying to keep her guts on the proper side of her skin. She watched me with an expression of fear and pain and the sight broke my heart. I brought her into this, and now she would die for it. Even without the shield we could not win. Not against a monster of this power. More men poured into the breach but the blast had allowed the defenders to rally and they met with the invaders in the breach. Grasax observed for a moment before he turned back to the shield generator. The rock started to flow back into the structure and the runes reemerged in the viscous surface. There was only one way for us to even have a hope of winning. Grasax was drawing heavily on the fount to replenish the power he expended. We needed to match his strength or we would surely be lost. I forced myself to my feet but my right leg would not obey me. A large splinter of rock was embedded in my thigh but I ignored it. Every limping step I took sent a searing pain through my leg as the splinter moved and cut me open further. Somehow I still held my sword. I pulled any magic that escaped Grasax into my store but even at my full strength I was like a candle next to his bonfire. I was sure that Grasax was aware of my shambling advance but he did not care. I was not a threat to him. I had no more tricks up my sleeve to bring his shield down a third time. When I was a few steps from him he tired of me and without looking flung a tongue of flame at me with his free hand. I started to dodge to the side and twisted my face away but I was too slow. The flames burned my neck, shoulder and the side of my head and I screamed in pain as my skin blackened and blistered. I fell on my belly and he stopped the attack. The hair on the right side of my head was burning but I had no strength to put it out. I disregarded my physical body in favour of my soul that I kept feeding on the magic. I pushed to my feet and activated the shield cutting enchantment on my sword. I swung wildly at his back, my old instructors in the Guard would have whipped me for my poor form. He noted the enchantment and swayed to the side rather than let me disrupt his shield. It was what I had counted on and I pulled on my blood magic and sent the last of my strength into my good left leg. He had not expected the leap and I soared past him... And directly into the fount. I pulled on the magic and energy poured into me. In an instant I was filled by more than I could hold and my body felt ready to disintegrate. My feet were burning with raw magic. I had to use this power or I would burn to cinders. I stabilised my fall with ropes of force and spun myself around to face the liche and hung hovering in the wild torrent of magical flames. His dead face was expressionless but I could feel his astonishment at my recklessness. I took inspiration from the Skylands that was after all in a similar situation. It was suspended in a geyser of magic, balancing on a shield. I funnelled power into shield beneath my feet and the relief was instantaneous. Magic still flowed violently around my body but it was no longer directly burning me. I started to rise, surfing the torrent of power. It was still more than I could bear and I could feel my veins burning with their power. They must be glowing through my skin and my eyes must be blazing with an inner light of their own. I threw out my hand and cast a ray of power at Grasax and he stumbled back as it struck his shield. He drank the power around him but it dried up quickly. I was consuming the power from the fount and poured it into the attack. With my other hand I incinerated the back lines of the defenders but I was still too full. My skin dried out and started to crack. Light and flames spilled out of the cracks. I had already given up hope for myself, but if I could take Grasax down with me it would be worth it. Perhaps the shaman could heal Red after. Grasax responded with a powerful beam of his own but my shield was too strong. I met his beam with one of my own and I howled with jubilant laughter as his was pressed back. The place where the beams joined shone brilliantly and magical sparks rained onto the cobbles where they burned dark scorch marks into the stones. I poured on the power, I needed to get rid of it or I would explode. My sanity was fraying at the edges along with my body but I did not care. All that mattered was that this undead abomination finally died. I increased the flow and pushed the join of our beams closer to him. My fingers sizzled and popped as the fat and muscles burned and melted. Bone showed through the gaps. With an effort of will the power coursing through my hand into the beam doubled and the beams were pushed into his shield. It popped with a crack and his arm and shoulder flashed into steam as the power struck him. He flew through the air and tumbled across the ground. My left arm melted and disintegrated up to the elbow but the pain was distant. My mind was fragmenting in the storm of power. Something struck my shield at waist height and I was pushed out of the fount. A loud scream pierced my insanity and I recognised that voice. Red. I looked down and saw her tumble away from me. She had managed to get to her feet and dive tackle me out of the fount. Her entire front was charred and her leathers burned but she was still moving. Coils of her guts had slipped from her belly in her leap.

"Anjali!"

It was the first time I spoke her true name. I was still too full of power and I was still pulling from the fount. I absorbed the flames still consuming her armour. She twisted her face toward me and her mouth worked wordlessly. I scrambled toward her, feeling ready to burst of power and fear. She could not form the words properly. The power coursing through me made my magesense keen and I saw through her entire body in a flash. She was broken, badly. The burns on her body was superficial but painful. It was the gut wound that was the most dangerous. With a thought I cauterised the major vessels and she screamed in agony. My voice joined hers in empathetic pain but luckily she passed out of the pain. I was not sure if my hasty triage would save her life. I could hear Grasax start to move behind me and with a thought my power sent me flying toward him. He had dropped his staff in his tumble but his remaining hand brandished an ornate dagger. The power of the fount still poured into me and over his shoulder I saw magic assaulting the warriors behind him. My fragmented mind had kept up the assault even as I helped Red, redirecting the power that threatened to consume me. Grasax no longer glowed with power in my magesense, robbed of the power of the fount he had expended much of his prodigious personal power. I grinned and launched streamers of magic at him from my hand and my stump. The twin rays, one brilliant green and one a fiery orange, coiled around one another in a deadly spiral to strike him in the chest. He threw up a shield to absorb them but it was a losing battle. In moments he would be exhausted. Impossibly his power grew and his shield strengthened. Where was he getting his power? I saw no influx from the empty field around him, all of the available power went into me. My skin cracked and shrivelled on my arm and shoulders as the power coursed through me. The gem on the pommel of his dagger flared brilliantly. A warrior in the battle behind him burst into blue flames as his soul was ripped from his body and surged into Grasax. The unfortunate man was followed by another, and then a third. He was devouring his own followers! He must have bound their souls to his own and now he was claiming their power in a last ditch effort to stay alive. His dead face had set into a determined expression but his concern was palpable. Dead, rotted teeth shattered in his mouth when he clenched his dry jaws. I pushed forward, taking one shaky step after the other. I sheathed my arm in a shield breaking spell and punched a hole in his shield. Combined with the power still arcing from me into his shield I finally broke through. His shield collapsed and I launched myself onto him. I landed on top of him and punched him in the jaw. Souls were streaming into him rapidly and he started to fight back but my shield protected me. I would not last long with this amount of power coursing through me, I was astonished that I had not yet disintegrated completely. I sheathed my remaining hand in a spell and punched it through his dry ribcage and curled my broken fingers around his dark heart. It slowly writhed against my numb dessicated paw. Through it I could sense the source of his power. I pulled on it heavily and he pulled back. It turned into a tug of war, will against will to claim the power of the other. I was slowly, ever so slowly winning. We stopped attacking each others bodies and went straight for the souls. The world faded before my eyes and I found myself in a vast darkness. A form before me shone with a harsh blue light. Grasax. I was sure he saw me similarly and we crashed together. Again and again we met and each time one of us stole power from the other. Back in the real world I was sure that we were both burning, and his dead body was much better equipped to handle it. Where we were, I was winning. After a long time of back and forth I finally caught him. We were almost equally matched by then and I was sure that he must have killed most, if not all, of his followers to gain that kind of strength. I encased his soul in a shield and pulled power from him. I filled the shield with my own power that burned his essence away in caustic bursts. I was getting continually refreshed by the fount and he was not. I drew power from him and poured it back inside the shield confining him as caustic magic that further damaged his spirit. He started to dwindle rapidly. I could still feel no fear from him, only a mild concern and a growing desperation. I shrank the shield around his spirit and the inferno compressed and intensified and burned him even faster. He dwindled down to nothing and I released the power. What was left of him was a shell, an empty husk. No, not empty. It was just powerless. As soon as I released it it slunk away and vanished from my spectral sight. The edges of me was bleeding away into the darkness, large pieces shearing off and disintegrating. I let go. I was ready to rest. Something called to me, disturbing my drifting mind. It was a low, keening sound but it carried no words. I kept expanding, dissipating into the void but the tone was insistent. More of a desire to make it stop than anything I obeyed it, maybe if I did what it wanted it would leave me in peace. With a tremendous effort I cut off the flow of power into me and ejected that which I already stored. It only accelerated my disintegration process so I did not mind relinquishing it. The presence screamed and I realised that I was hurting it. I shielded myself, and then raised another shield around that. Then with a big puff of power I expelled it into the space between the shields, funnelling it upwards through a chimney in the outer shield. My awareness faded as the power left me and the voice finally silenced.

## Chapter 24

Awareness returned in a storm of sensations. I could see women in the kitchen baking bread for the next meal and the cook stirring a large pot of stew hanging above a crackling fire. Two men were hauling manure from the privies out to the fields being tilled outside the walls by Clansmen. Dun Traelak was swarming with people. Most were working on cleaning up the courtyard or shoring up the breach in the wall. The large crack that had caused it to fall had narrowed and I assumed that the shaman had convinced the earth to repair itself. In one room Iolan was having words with Red's father, I could not hear what they were saying but the expressions on their face told me that their exchange was heated. The young man gesticulated wildly as he almost shouted. A woman dozed on a stool outside the room I was resting in and a warm body was snuggled up next to mine. Red slept peacefully, her breath warm on my ear. Without opening my eyes I studied her. She appeared to be fine, except that her soul was weak and she bore a multitude of new scars. A large ugly mess of skin showed where Grasax had impaled her on his staff and the organs beneath was bruised and had shifted from their original place. Memories of my battle with the liche returned and I gasped at the intensity of them. I relived the battle and my awareness fragmented and surged out in all directions. My magesense was much more acute and covered a much wider distance than it had and everything that happened in the castle and a fair bit outside bombarded me. It was too much, I could not take it all in at once but I could not shut it out. My mind spun and I retched. My mind was empty and only frothy bile spilled from my lips as my body convulsed. When I moved the cracks in my skin opened but they did not bleed, instead raw power gushed out of the glowing rifts and I panicked. Breath rushed in and out of my lungs in fearful gasps. My eyes were opened wide but what I saw was only a small fraction of what I sensed and the two sensory images overlapped and spun. I clamped my eyes shut but it hardly helped. I heaved again and my stomached cramped painfully around nothing. Something shook my body and a noise intruded upon the silence. It took a long while before I understood that it was a voice. I did not understand words and I wanted it to stop. I cried out and flailed with my arm and more raw power spilled from my broken body. I contained too much power and it spilled out of me. New power slowly trickled in to replace it but I was weakening rapidly. I could smell smoke and the voice changed as it cried out in surprise and pain. The words slowly started to make sense.

"Kyra! Stop! You are hurting yourself. Focus on my voice. Come back from where ever you are. Come back! Please!"

I listened to the words, drawing my awareness inside myself, systematically shutting out parts of the keep. The sense was still there but I shifted my focus. It was like ignoring a barely heard conversation on the other edge of the room. Piece by piece the barrage of perceptions shrunk to a more manageable level and my body relaxed. I breathed heavily for long minutes as the voice soothed me and I finally opened my eyes. Red's face hovered inches above mine and her face was full of concern.

"You're back."

I opened my mouth but only a wordless gurgle escaped me. My mouth was utterly dry and I started to cough into her face. Her face vanished from my view but I could still see her clearly with my mind. She reached across me and picked up a cup from a small table next to the bed and her fingers cradled my neck as she helped me drink. The tepid water burned my dry mouth and it caught in my throat.

"Slowly, " she cautioned, "we have barely been able to get you to drink at all. You are dehydrated. Small sips."

I swirled the water in my mouth until the pain passed and we worked for several minutes until I had drained the cup. I was exhausted from the exertion of both blocking my magesense and forcing my tortured body to accept the liquid. I wrapped my arms around her to pull her close but she seemed insubstantial as my left arm passed through her without resistance. What? Was I dreaming? Was she just a mirage? No, my right hand clutched at her back, the tips of my fingers digging into her soft skin. I raised my left arm and saw the stump just beneath my elbow. It was blackened and cracked but was not bleeding. I stared dumbly at it. I was a cripple now.

"No, don't cry! We will figure this out. Together. Just calm down."

Despite her own words her cheeks were wet with tears. She leaned down and pressed a hard, desperate kiss on my lips. It hurt, a lot, but I warmed on the inside and relaxed as I responded. I was not foreign to pain and would gladly weather it for her touch. I had a more pressing need though and I had to push her away. I winced as my stump touched her skin and I ripped my arm away. My right would suffice. I saw when I put it on her shoulder that the tips of my fingers were a ruin. The nails had melted off and the bone was showing through the thin covering of skin that remained. It did not look infected but I wondered if it would ever heal. It might be possible with blood magic but my body was too ravaged to afford the expenditure right now.

"Privies."

It was difficult to force the word out but the pressure in my bladder would not be denied. Red helped me to my feet and despite her own weakness she put my arm over her shoulder and steadied me. Every movement twisted the cracks in my skin and raw power seeped out. It must have burned her but she did not make a sound of discomfort. It was only a few steps to the privy but I was sweating heavily when she lowered me onto the seat. She refused to leave me for privacy but I did not mind. I wanted her close by. With that taken care of the ordeal of returning took a while but I was back in the bed soon enough. I was covered in sweat and droplets flashed into steam as they dripped into a wound. My body had channelled so much power that it had started to come undone and the wounds refused to heal. I looked down on my body and hardly recognised it. My veins shone through my pale skin as they coursed with power and rips and tears studded my skin and blazed with magical spill. How could I contain this much power? Compared to Grasax I still held practically nothing but it was many times more than I had been able to hold previously, despite my leaking. It was the battle, I suddenly understood. Using magic was like running, your abilities got stronger with exercise. The power I had channelled had expanded my store and channelling ability but my physical form was unable to hold it. I was living on borrowed time. I had been close to becoming an Archon, a Mage who absorbed so much power that their bodies disintegrated and became a being of pure magic. With that amount of power you could contain yourself for a time but the power would fade and the Archon would dissipate. I think that my body was on a terminal path, the constant leaking would widen the cracks and eventually they would be too large to contain my soul. They were not the only damage of course, my arm was missing and my remaining hand was burned as was my feet. The rest of me was a practically a single bruise from all the tossing about Grasax had inflicted on me. My blood magic had worked as I slept as my body desperately worked to repair itself and I was painfully thin. My hip bones protruded sharply and you could easily count my ribs. My breasts were empty sacks that looked like empty water skins with nipples. I looked horrible. I had never considered myself vain but I knew I had been attractive. No longer. A tear dripped from the corner of my eye as I fully grasped the damage done to me. I had not expected to survive the fight with Grasax and had expended my body, but now here I was. Broken and crippled. Even with the vast store of power inside me I could do nothing to help me. As soon as I channelled any of it the cracks in my body would widen and hurt me further. It was effectively locked in my body. Red sat on the bed next to me, watching me with concern written plainly on her face. I stared into her beautiful green eyes and tried to smile. At least she appeared to be fine, even though she was scarred and pale. She would be fine even after I died. Briefly I considered ending myself by expelling some power, it should be enough to rupture my body. It would be a mercy to die swiftly in a rush of power rather than a slow decline to the same fate. But I discarded the idea when I saw the look in her eyes. As long as there were life in my body there were hope. I was broken, but there may be some way to fix it. Back home Mages that hurt themselves like this was often put to death for safety reasons for when they finally burned the power within was released in a torrent of Wild Magic and my people knew nothing that could reverse the process. But Grasax had contained much more power than this without any ill effects. Of course, he had already been dead. Was that the key? Would undeath solve my problem? I did not fancy being a walking corpse, I think I would rather die properly. Red was looking at me strangely.

"What?"

"Your eyes... They glow violet."

I turned my face away from her in shame. Not even my eyes had been spared. She reached out and firmly brought me back to face her.

"Don't you ever look away from me in shame. They are beautiful. You are beautiful. And they match your hair now." A small smile curled her lip. Remembering the blast of flame that had struck me I brushed the side of my head and my ruined fingertips could still make out the burns on my scalp. I found the line where my hair begun again. I had lost a few inches above my ear and my hair now barely brushed my shoulders. Somehow my ear had been left mostly intact, the fire must have been put out quickly but the burns were still oozing. I reached out and clasped her hand but I could not muster the strength for a wince as my melted fingertips brushed her palm. I closed my eyes and fell back into blessed oblivion.

I woke up some time later, alone in the bed. Fear overcame me. Where was Red? Was she alright? The magnitude of my magesense assaulted me and I struggled to block it out. It was faster this time but it took several long minutes. When I had regained my senses I carefully stretched out again in search of my friend. I found her nearby, sitting in the privy and I relaxed. She returned a short while later and I let my eyes roam over her body. She was still naked and despite her scars she were as beautiful as the first time I had seen her. Not even the fact that she had knocked me the fuck out shortly thereafter marred the memory. Each of her scars was a medal of honour, a proof of achievements. When she got closer I could see the glow of my eyes reflected in her own.

"Do we have a mirror?"

"Are you sure?"

I nodded. I already knew what I looked like, my new and improved magesense had revealed every hurt on my body but it was time to see with my own eyes. Red rummaged around and shortly returned with a round hand held mirror. I steeled myself and raised it to my face. I was a mess. My face was mostly intact apart from a few scratches and bruises and the fine latticework of veins around my temples and jaw shone through my skin with an inner violet light but it was my eyes that captured my attention. They had indeed turned violet, a lighter shade than my purple hair but that was not the most astonishing feature. They were glowing with an inner light. Not a brilliant shine but more of a dull glow. I had only seen such in Mages that was using their powers but I was just lying here. I almost giggled when an image formed in my mind. When I wore my helmet my eyes would glow from the dark slits but my giggle turned into melancholy as I remembered that I no longer had my armour. It had been destroyed when the generator exploded since I had used the power in my choker to fuel the spell. Though now I held enough power to materialise it directly, if I could figure out how to use this vast store of power inside without burning. It would take focus and concentration since I no longer had a template stored in the crystal.

"Are you hungry? You haven't eaten for weeks."

Weeks?

"How long have been out?"

"Nearly two weeks. The shaman worked for days to patch you up. I've never heard of anyone ever requiring several of them working together and then live."

"Tell me what happened after."

Not much had happened after the fight with Grasax ended. She started her story shortly before I leaped into the fount. I had blazed with power even as it consumed me and she had realised that I would die if I stayed directly in the fount. She had forced her mangled body to comply and had expended the last of her strength to tackle me out of it. Somehow it had not worked fully for the power kept pouring into me but I had at least been out of its caustic flows. I had leaped on top of Grasax and then we had both gotten still. The defenders had all died and crumbled, including the slaves who had not been fighting. Many of those the Outcasts had stolen from our camp had died as well but some had not yet been bound to the undead Mage and had survived. The Clansmen had surged inside, led by Iolan and her father but none dared intervene. They had all been able to sense our struggle even though we just lay there. Then I had collapsed to the side and Grasax was still. The shaman hurried to incinerate his corpse and only the dagger he had brandished remained in the ashes. With the castle cleansed of the Outcasts the Clans had taken up residence and Iolan, who was now the Chief of Clan Ithlak after the untimely demise of his father in the breach, and her father had been debating which Clan would claim Dun Traelak. Bizhjerai had the better claim, since it was they who had been the leaders of the fight but Iolan argued that it should belong to Clan Ithlak since they had sustained almost all of the losses. Iolan's father had demanded the honour of the vanguard, and he had paid for it with his life. The Bizhjerai would have composed the second wave but the defenders had been slain by their own master before the charge. Red lapsed into silence and I could tell that she had omitted some vital detail.

"What are you not telling me, Red?"

She clamped her lips shut.

"Tell me. You don't need to coddle me."

"Iolan will surrender his claim to Dun Traelak if I agree to marry him."

My heart sank. It was too good of an offer to refuse.

"I won't do it! I refuse! Let them have the castle, I don't care!"

I reached out and pulled her close with my one good arm.

"This castle is too important to let slip for something like this."

She pulled out of my one-armed embrace, her face full of shock and hurt.

"Would you have me marry that insufferable twit?"

"Not if you don't want to."

"And I don't!"

"But this fortress will elevate any Clan that holds it. It is very defensible and that fount of magic out there is valuable beyond belief."

"I can't believe you are suggesting this!"

"Calm down. To answer your earlier question, yes I am starving. Let's get some food here and then we can discuss this rationally."

I could tell that she was pissed and she stiffly climbed out of the bed and poked her head through the door and spoke shortly with the woman waiting outside. With my mind I followed her down to the kitchen and watched her return with a cloth covered tray. Red sat silently fuming, refusing to look at me. I did not prod her even though I found her to be overreacting. She accepted the tray from the woman when she knocked lightly on the door and then deposited it in my lap. I pulled the cloth aside and was met with the enticing scent of grilled meat and freshly baked bread with a thick layer of butter on it. My mouth watered and my belly screamed for sustenance. I reached for the knife but drew up short when my stump failed to reach the food. This was going to take some getting used to. Normally I could have used magic to cut the food and levitate it into my mouth but my leaking magical wounds dissuaded me. Despite her anger Red understood my predicament and reached for the knife and started cutting the meat with precise, angry movements. I reached for the bread with my intact hand as she worked and bit off a large piece. I moaned in pleasure at the taste but I hardly chewed it and swallowed it down almost immediately. My hunger could be denied no longer. My dry throat caught on the bread as it constricted and tried to force it down and I choked on it. The coughs wracked my body and power spilled from my wounds like luminescent blood that made my skin blister. Bread sprayed from my mouth as my lungs worked but the pain blinded me. After an eternity my large swallow went down to my belly and I croaked out a request for water. Red had saved the cup from being overturned by my fits and she put it against my lips. Her angry expression had been replaced by one of concern and she discreetly batted out a flame where the bed cloth had caught fire from my leaking power. I took a smaller bite of the bread and deliberately chewed it into a mush. I could not afford to gobble it down swiftly and then choke on it. Red resumed cutting the meat but she kept watching me surreptitiously from the corner of her eye. I finished the bread and drew a deep breath.

"Are you ready to talk about it?"

"Yes."

"We must consider all alternatives but ultimately it is your decision, alright?"

"Fair enough. But I don't like the thought of marrying Iolan."

"Neither do I, trust me on that one."

"Why did you say that the fount of magic outside is important? It just dangerous."

"Quite the contrary, if used properly it can fuel a number of things."

"Really? Magic isn't that useful outside of battle. Sure you can light fires and dry your hair and such but we don't need it."

I arched an eyebrow.

"Really? Have you not seen my armour, or my weapons?"

Her eyes widened at the implication, but she asked me to make sure she understood my meaning.

"We can use the magic to create weapons such as yours."

I nodded. "Indeed, with the correct knowledge a fount of power is incredibly powerful. The Skylands is built on the technological applications of magic. Tell me, what is the most limiting factor of your lives?"

Her response was immediate. "The other Clans. They raid and steal our food and goods."

"No, the raids are merely a symptom."

"Symptom?"

"Yes, the reason for the raids is that the Clans lack food. You steal from each other because you can't feed everyone, and you can't feed everyone because you rely on your herds instead of agriculture."

"But we can't tend to crops because the other Clans would then know precisely from were to steal it."

"Yes, and you can't defend areas that large. But now you can. Dun Traelak will allow you to protect your stores and the magic fount will allow you let the magic work for you. More people can tend to the fields instead of making clothes and tools."

"And then we can sell the excess grain in exchange for the things we can't make ourselves."

I nodded. "Precisely. Possessing this stronghold is just not a place to hide from raids. It will shift the entire economy of the Clans if used correctly. The fields outside can feed your entire Clan and possibly several of the others. Whoever control the fortress will control the local grain market and by extension gain influence over the Clans. Your people will no longer struggle to feed everyone."

"But we've never gone hungry, unless we have recently been raided."

"Yes, but then you don't have many children. The Clan will grow if you have a surplus of food. Is that not worth a marriage?"

She glared at me but was silent. She could see my point but she was not happy about it. Neither was I. I really did not want her to marry Iolan, but the benefits to the Clan were too great to ignore.

"We could fight them. They lost many warriors in the assault, we could take them out entirely."

"Would you send men to die and wipe out an entire Clan just to get out of a marriage? Destroy a Clan that is your ally?"

"Fuck it all."

Despite her harsh words she picked up a morsel of meat and raised it to my lips and I accepted it. It tasted wonderful and I immediately opened my mouth for another bite. Her fingers lingered on my lips and I extended my tongue and licked the grease off the tips.

"I don't want you to marry Iolan, I lo..." I cut off my words. Even though we had shared several kisses now we had not spoken about it at all and I was suddenly uncertain. Her fingers hovered near my lips and the reflection of my glowing eyes had been joined by an inner fire in her green orbs. She threw herself on top of me and kissed me, deeply. The weight of her opened my magical wounds and liquid fire spilled out. A groan of pain escaped me and she immediately pulled back.

"I'm so sorry, I did not mean to hurt you."

"Don't stop. It is worth the pain."

Her face softened and a slow smile spread across her lips as she slowly bent down again. I meant what I had said. The sensation of her wet lips on my own was worth every jolt of searing pain her touch induced. Her own skin blistered wherever she touched my wounds but she did not seem to care. After a long while she pulled back and continued feeding me.

"Do you see now why it is paramount that Clan Ithlak does not possess Dun Traelak?"

"Yes, " her voice was reluctant, "but there may be another solution than marrying Iolan."

"I'd love to hear it."

"I don't have one right now. First we focus on you getting better."

I did not tell her that I probably wouldn't. It was just a matter of time before I died of my wounds. Perhaps it was better that she married Iolan. Our time together was finite.

"First and foremost we must gain control of the castle. Then I must return home."

"What?!"

"I can't use magic anymore. Even if I could my knowledge about magical fabrication is limited. I may be able to set up some simple constructions but we need a Skylander who knows these things. Without the knowledge it would take years, maybe decades to figure it out on our own." Decades I did not have. When I died the Bizhjerai would be on their own, magic wise. "And I know just who that would be." Of course, I was thinking about Kendall and I felt sure that he would jump on the chance to build something like this. I could bring him here along with mom and Marissa. They would have a nice life among the Bizhjerai, safe here in Dun Traelak. Greg would have been happy that his daughter would be free of the Skylands.

"What do you mean you can't use magic? Even I can see that you are brimming with power now. Being in that fount changed you somehow."

"It did, but these wounds I have concern me. I keep leaking power. I have seen this before in Mages that absorbed or channelled too much power. Every time I use magic the wounds will get worse and it could kill me."

I had gotten dangerously close to revealing that I was dying, but I was not ready for her to hear it yet.

"Will you heal?"

"Not on my own, no."

Her brow furrowed as a thought entered her mind.

"But I saw Grasax use as much, if not more, power than you did and he suffered no ill effects."

"He was already dead, Red."

"But why did his body not burn like yours did?"

That was an excellent question, and one that surprised me that I had not had myself. Again her instinctual grasp on magic astounded me.

"Good question. Maybe he had some knowledge to avoid that fate."

"We found a library after the battle. Maybe there is some clues there."

A small surge of hope settled in my belly but I squashed it ruthlessly. Hope was for fools who denied reality. Hope is the first step on the path to disappointment "Maybe. But I am still to weak to study it."

As I said it I noted her own drooping eyelids and she had grown paler as we spoke. Her own wounds had been extensive and the healing she had gone through must have drained her reserves severely. "Come here. Let us rest. We can talk more later."

She put the last piece of meat in my mouth before she put the tray aside and snuggled up next to me. The jostling made my wounds ooze once more and she shifted around until she managed to avoid contact with them. Then she rested her head on my shoulder and drifted off to sleep quickly. She must indeed have been exhausted. I was too but my mind churned with possibilities. If Grasax had known the secret to survive with that much power contained, then maybe he had written it down. I had a dark feeling that it was the undeath that had allowed him to survive.

## Chapter 25

A week passed slowly as we recuperated. Red got stronger faster than I did but I had some good progress. I ate almost constantly, quickly putting on weight. My muscles had not suffered much, only my store of fat had been almost completely exhausted and I soon started to move around the room on my own. My magical wounds stabilised with my movements, tearing and healing into more flexible configurations. They did not seem to grow unless I used magic. I had tried channelling just a trickle of power but had immediately felt them tear open but at least now I could move without leaking. I could not wear clothes for my wounds burned straight through them but since I did not leave the chambers privacy was not a problem. Red's father had visited me a few days after I first woke up and thanked me for helping the Clans defeat Grasax and offered me whatever I wished in return. I almost asked him to refuse Iolan's request of marrying Red but stopped myself at the last possible instant. Since we still had not discussed our feelings I did not want to drag other people into it. I am not sure what views the Bizhjerai had about same-sex relationships. Back home no one thought twice about it except for a small minority but I had only seen straight couples since coming Outside. I'd had several female lovers in the past but nothing that lasted long. Not that I'd had male lovers for any extended duration of time either. Red had had the woman who waited on us, Anna, bring us books from the library and we spent much time lying next to one another in the bed, reading. I had talked Red through the process of creating a light spell so we could read even long into the night. I was sure that she had recovered enough to join her Clansmen in the work on the fortress but for some reason she remained with me. I was not going to complain. I watched the progress on the repairs with my extended magesense as I practised to gradually expand my focus without getting overwhelmed. Even though I was constantly aware what was happening within my range I was getting quite good at not focusing on it. The trick to not getting overwhelmed was to focus on only a part of it, usually the space immediately around me but I found that I could shift my 'sight' to other portions. I was currently studying the fount on the courtyard and what I saw confounded me. It was much smaller than it had been. It was still a respectable flow but nowhere near the swift torrent it had been. Had the battle drained it of its power? I could sense two ley lines crossing, which was what fed the fount its power. The ley lines are like rivers, while magic is everywhere the density varied and blew like winds. When magic was consumed somewhere the remaining magic flowed into the void to replenish it as if to equalise the pressure. For some unknown reason the magic formed these ley lines and flowed across the landscape like rivers and whenever they crossed they amplified and fed each other. Had there been some sort of pool here before to increase the magical pressure beneath the fount? That would explain why it was lesser now. I shifted my perception beneath the ground where the ley lines were but could not see any trace of a pool. I gave up and sent my magesense toward the breach. The Clans did not know enough about masonry to repair the wall but the wood and earthworks would hold for now. Iolan prowled the castle and at least once a day he stood outside our door, demanding to see Red but she stubbornly refused him. We had had endless talks about alternatives to his proposition but we had both drawn up short.

"What if we offer him the arsenal instead? The weapons would make Clan Ithlak powerful, but it would hardly threaten us in here. Especially if we can build weapons like yours."

After the battle a second armoury had been found in the basement of the main keep and Clan Bizhjerai now possessed more muskets and powder than they had people to use them. There were even a few dozen rifles down there which were much more accurate and had longer range than the muskets though they were slower to reload. The bore had to be cleaned thoroughly between shots or the black powder residue would muck up the rifling and the tighter fit of the shots made it much more difficult to ram home. Rifled muskets were not efficient in mass combat, but for skirmishing they were excellent.

"Maybe, do you think that he is stupid enough to realise that the fortress is much more valuable?"

"Possibly. I did not understand the value until you explained how the fount could be used."

"Then we should propose it. We can replace the weapons in time if I can get my friend out here."

"Can't you make them?"

"No. I just use them. I can probably set up some rudimentary manufacturing process for simpler weapons like muskets or pistols but my weapons are far more advanced and I simply don't know how to build them."

Power kept leaking out of me at a steady rate. The energy escaping me dissipating into the weak magic field surrounding me before my body could reabsorb it. Days passed and my veins stopped glowing first, shortly thereafter followed by the glow in my eyes. My wounds faded to my normal vision but my magesense told me that they were still glowing brightly as they bled power into the air. I was hoping that when I returned to my normal power level the leakage would stop but that hope proved a futile one. I kept bleeding power and it was now clear to me that I would only have days left. I forced Red to take me down to the library and she fashioned a short skirt and a halter top for me out of old sheets. With the magical wounds covering my body burning straight through clothing it was the maximum coverage I was going to get. Not that there were much of me to cover any more. I had been putting on weight from my inactivity and almost constant eating but my empty breasts had just barely started to plump almost imperceptibly. I walked on my own down the stairs but Red refused to leave me alone and hovered around my shoulders constantly on alert to catch me if I should fall. Physically I felt fine, I was just very thin and I lacked the one arm. The library proved very organised, Grasax had been an orderly man despite his dishevelled appearance. I went straight for the section labelled 'Power storage' and perused the titles. I gathered several tomes to leaf through at a later time and then on a whim picked one about containing and gathering power from the magical field. I was on my way out with my prizes when my eyes fell on the spine of a book almost by accident. I froze when I read the title. It was just one word. 'Archons.' I licked my lips nervously before I snatched it up and put in the top of the pile that I clamped to my chest with my stump. Red waited by the door, her eyes never leaving me as I selected the books. Among the tomes I had chosen were several novice books that I was going to force her to read. Her intuitive grasp on magic was simply too great to squander.

"Let me carry those for you."

"I'm not a fucking cripple, Red."

She glanced pointedly at my stump.

"Fuck off!"

I stormed past her, stubbornly clutching the books to my chest. After a couple of stairs I was sweating and panting, I was still weak and had lost much of my endurance. I was sure that it would return when I restored my body's supply of energy but I had very small reserves as it was.

"Fine, have it your way!" I thrust the books at her and she accepted the burden with a smug smile. Luckily for her she offered no comment. On a sudden urge I made an about face and started descending the stairs again.

"Where are you going? Our room is up there?"

Our room. Our. The words sent a flare of warmth through me and my annoyance faded.

"I had an idea. I need to see the fount."

She knew me well enough by now to be suspicious and she glared at me through narrowed eyes as she easily kept pace with me.

"Don't do anything stupid."

"I won't know if it is stupid until after I do it. But I think it will work."

"Will what work?"

"You won't like it if I tell you, so I won't."

"How is that supposed to calm me down?!"

"It wasn't, " I teased with a grin. She rolled her eyes and huffed. For the first time in over a week I felt the sunlight directly on my skin and I closed my eyes and tilted my head skyward for a moment to enjoy the warmth. The magic field was denser here where we were closer to the fount but not by much. Even as I enjoyed the feeling of the sun on my face I inspected the fount with my magesense. It was indeed much smaller than it had been but whatever remained would serve my purpose.

"Anjali. Bàs Marbhadair. It is good to see you out and about again. We have found some magical items in the storehouses that we would like your help in identifying, if you are willing."

The man was of Clan Bizhjerai, though I did not recognise him. He was tall and broad shouldered and his muscles were well defined and long. He had the body of an archer and he displayed his arms eminently with the sleeveless vest he wore.

"Bàs Marbhadair?"

I realised that he was addressing me, and that I was seemingly ignoring him. I had completely forgotten to use my eyes to watch him, instead relying entirely on my magesense. I opened my eyes and looked at him. What was that he was calling me? The words were utterly foreign to me. I decided to play along for now and question Red about it later.

"Yes, certainly. Show me the items."

I could try out my theory with the fount after I helped these men. I was not entirely sure what kind of state I would be after my experiment. The man led us a short walk to the side of the courtyard and a smattering of 'Anjali' and 'Bàs Marbhadair' greeted us when the Clansmen saw us. I noted that several members of Clan Ithlak eyed us with barely veiled hostility. Apparently this alliance of ours had started to evaporate quickly now that the common enemy had been defeated. The man showed me a staff and a wand, both covered by runes. The staff was crowned by a crystal of materialised magic and a similar crystal was set into the base of the wand. Both crystals shone brightly with stored power. I inspected the runes on the staff and recognised several of the spells enchanted into the smooth wood. There were several telekinetic spells, presumably to levitate objects. There were another to focus a jet of flame and there were another complex spell that was open at one end. I did not understand it fully but it felt as if the slot was for putting a spell in. I assumed that the staff would use the spell somehow. The enchantments had clearly defined entry points but I dared not activate them in fear of opening my wounds further even with the tiny trickle that would be required. Instead I handed the staff to Red and pointed out the entry points.

"Point the staff at that pile of rock over there." I indicated a neat pile of the remnants of the shield tower. "Activate this enchantment." I tapped a set of runes with my broken finger.

Red focused a moment and the runes blazed into light. In my magesense the air seemingly solidified even though my eyes saw nothing. The pile of rock shuddered and I motioned for Red to raise the staff. The stones obediently followed the motion and rose into the air.

"The staff use the magic in the gem there to cast a spell. The light will dim as the magic is consumed and you activate this enchantment, " I pointed at the runes close to the headpiece, "to recharge it. The closer to the fount you put the staff the faster it will recharge. Did you find many of these?"

"Yes, several dozen. Same with these sticks."

"Wands," I corrected him. I picked one up and gave it a cursory glance. It was similarly enchanted but the spells it produced would be far less powerful, but much more precise. I told them as much and encouraged them to experiment, just make sure to not point it at another human being and keep their distance to the objects they aimed at before they knew what a certain spell would do.

"I see no enchantment on here that would be dangerous unless you aim them directly at a person. These would help you immensely with the cleanup and repair."

The man bowed. "Thank you for your counsel, Bàs Marbhadair."

I returned the bow with a deep nod before I left them to their experiments and walked toward the fount. Red fell into step beside me.

"Bàs Marbhadair?"

"It is from an ancient language. It translates roughly to Death's Killer. The men have taken to call you that after you killed the liche."

I chuckled at that. It was a fitting name.

"Do you find that funny?"
