"Sort of. Back home they call me Dragonbane and your people call me Bàs Marbhadair. I am starting to rack up the titles. Are they calling you anything new after the battle."

"They tried calling me 'Red Huntress'."

"Tried?"

"I wouldn't let them. I did nothing more extraordinary than the Ithlaki who joined us. I did not deserve a title."

"You survived," my voice was low but firm.

"More by luck than anything else." I did not agree, she had saved my life even as her own guts spilled out into the light of day and I had sensed the remnants of an infection in her abdominal cavity from all the dust that had stuck to her slick organs during their brief expedition from their home. Her voice told me that she did not want to speak about it further so I dropped the subject.

"What are you planning?"

I did not answer. I feared that she would have stopped me if I had told her. I walked as close as I dared to the fount, which put me very close. I felt the magic wash across me and started to seep into my body. I stood there for long minutes as the power slowly filled me up but there were no discomfort. I pulled hesitatingly on the power, drawing it inside more powerfully but still no ill effects appeared. I gained confidence as minutes trickled past. Well, here goes nothing. I reached out with my hand and pulled as powerfully as I could on the magic before my newfound courage failed me. Power surged into my ravaged body. My head swam with the influx as my magesense expanded. I wanted more and I strained to pull harder. My ruined fingertips started to heat up and I reluctantly lessened my pull. I steadily drank it down and I ignored Red's gasp when the veins in my arm started to glow once more. The glow spread up my arm and across my chest but I kept pulling. My legs shook from the ecstasy and my wounds flared one by one as the glow reached them and starting leaking power in increasing flows. The seepage was as nothing compared to what I pulled in. After almost twenty minutes I felt full and reluctantly stopped pulling power even as the ecstasy turned painful. I turned to face Red with a triumphant smile.

"Your eyes!"

"They're glowing again, aren't they?"

She nodded slowly. "Are you sure that was wise?"

I must have bought myself a few days at least before I bled out completely and as long as I was near the fount I would be able to replenish my soul indefinitely.

"Yes, let's talk inside."

I led her in silence back to our room where I lay down on the charred bed. My body was exhausted from the short trek, especially the last part ascending the steps, but my mind was spry and full of power.

"Alright. Talk." I could not tell from the tone of her voice if she was concerned or angry. Possibly both. I drew a deep breath, it was time to be honest.

"Red, I'm dying."

"What? No!"

She surged forward and reached for me but I held up my hands to stop her, even though I wanted nothing more than feel her arms around me.

"These wounds, they are bleeding power."

"I know. But you are getting better."

"No, I am not. As long as these wounds are open they bleed power and eventually my soul will leak out of me."

Her eyes widened suddenly. "That is why you drank of the fount."

"Yes. As long as I replenish my magic my soul will remain in my body, but if I get too weak..."

"So you are not in any immediate danger?"

"No. But I will not be able to use magic. My body can't handle that strain."

"But you just pulled power into yourself? Isn't that the same thing?"

"Almost. It is just a matter of where the magical pressure lies."

I launched into a long explanation of relative pressures and structural integrity. Magic and physics follow very similar laws, the difference was that magical pressure was partly controlled by will. When I drank power I created an artificial low pressure inside my soul and the surrounding magic poured in. The structure of my soul reinforced itself to withstand the sudden relative increase in pressure on the outside. When I pushed magic out I did the same but in reverse and created an artificial pressure on the inside to push it out. When that happened the structure of the soul did not have the same internal support and would shatter.

"Think of it like a ruptured water skin. You hold it beneath the surface of a vessel containing water. In this analogy water is magic and the skin is my soul. The skin is empty and you pinch its sides and pull to make it expand. Water is sucked into the skin through the hole. Then imagine you constrict the bag violently and it bursts. It is nearly impossible to cause it to burst while filling, but easy once it is full. Are you with me?"

She nodded slowly, tapping her lower lip with a graceful finger.

"So as long as there is a source of power for you to drink from you won't suddenly die?"

I nodded, happy with her quick reasoning. Then my heart fell when the implication finally sank home. I would be locked to the immediate vicinity of Dun Traelak for the rest of my life. I would not be able to survive without the fount for any extended period of time. Certainly not long enough to get back home. Even if I did I was unsure if I would be able to acquire enough power to sustain myself back home, especially being unable to actually use it to earn power. The only reason for my success as a mercenary had been my weapons and armour and they took much magic to maintain. Without them I would most likely not be effective enough to earn enough money to buy enough magic to survive. I closed my eyes and rested my head on the wall. Red sensed my sudden shift in mood.

"What? What did you just realise?"

When I told her her face filled with compassion but she forced a cheerful expression to hide it.

"Then you simply have to stay here with me!"

I finally let her crawl into my arms and I endured her shifting to avoid my blazing wounds. The pain was not as severe as it had been when the wounds were fresh but they still ached when they were charged like this. There were a way I could travel, I realised. I could take the souls of others to sustain myself. It was essentially the same as drinking from the fount. I would need to completely devour the soul of a moderately powerful person every few days at least but I did not want to murder people to survive. Not any more. A few short weeks ago I would have done it without a second thought, killing some poor sod who would not be missed or perhaps feeding while on the job but I was not that person any more. Red had changed me. I pressed a lingering kiss on her forehead.

"Red."

"Yeah?"

"Bring me the two books at the top of the stacks, will you?"

"Of course."

She returned with the two books, one of them was the book about Archons. I handed her the other, one of the books for novices.

"This is for you. You can learn a lot from it."

To my surprise she did not complain. Instead she accepted the book and settled back into the pillows next to me. I watched her read for a while. She was so beautiful when her eyes roved across the pages. Her reading skill had improved rapidly from all the reading she had done recently and she flipped pages every few minutes. I glanced at the text she was reading, it was pretty basic stuff and I knew she already knew these things. She would soon come to a place where she would be learning in earnest. I opened my own book and dove into the pages. I dearly hoped that there would be some information within that could help me.

The book was interesting, but very complex. Several times it told about concepts it assumed the reader already knew and I had to send Red down to the library for reference books. I had never been a magical savant and most of these concepts were completely foreign to me. Apparently my people were very ignorant about Archons and the practice of putting them to death before they could complete the transition was very pessimistic. Wounds such as these had been somewhat common centuries ago when almost everyone was a Mage and a society that spanned the entire world was completely fuelled by magic. The book referenced many contraptions that I did not understood and during the third day of studying it I had had Red bring me a book of history. Grasax had an extensive collection that stretched all the way back to the years just after the Apocalypse. Apparently humanity had been using a force called electricity to power their society before the Apocalypse. They generated the power through several means, some as simple as burning wood and other combustibles to boil water. The same concept was used in the Pioneer in the steam engines that both provided steam for the envelope to provide lift as well as power the cylinders that turned the propellers. Of course, the propeller axis could be turned by telekinetic spells but it was inefficient since the power requirement of a telekinetic spell grew exponentially to the velocity. It was much more efficient to use an expansion engine to turn the propellers. The ancient humans had instead of turning propellers turned some sort of contraption made of copper and iron to generate their electricity through a concept they called 'electromagnetism'. I had no idea what that meant and it did not seem relevant to the concept of Archons so I chose not to study it. Humanity had discovered magic during some sort of large scale experiment in a place called Saern. They had been searching for something completely different but the discovery of magic had been much more important. They had learned to pull the ley lines out of the ground and harness the power. Almost anything that could be achieved with electricity could be achieved with magic but the electricity required intricate machinery to command while magic obeyed the pure will of humans. Magic was as useful as electricity and yet much more versatile. In the span of decades the use of electricity was abandoned. Apparently the means by which they produced it had adverse effects on the climate and it had been their biggest fear for decades and magic did not appear to have any such problems. Many powerful Mages grouped together, joining in the belief that magic was for everyone. They joined their power and ripped open many of the largest crossings of ley lines in an attempt to saturate the magic field for use by the common man. Humanity prospered for a short few years but the economy was built around scarcity. With an overabundance of magic scarcity was removed almost completely and the economy collapsed. War ensued and the magic field grew denser and denser for each year that passed despite the wars that did their best to consume it all. When the magic concentration grew high enough Wild Magic started manifesting. The world ripped apart and cities fell almost over night. Millions, if not billions died in the ensuing Apocalypse. I tore my eyes from the page. The Skylands must be hovering above one of the Geysers the Mages of old had ripped open. But what had caused the magic field to weaken enough for people to survive the Wild Magic? The book didn't say. While very interesting, the book had not taught me much about the subject of Archons and I put it aside reluctantly. I needed to focus on the task at hand. My power dwindled and when my veins and eyes stopped glowing again I went out and drank of the fount once more under Red's watchful gaze. I threw myself into studying the book about Archons. It was a fate I desperately wanted to avoid. I found a promising section about magic wounds and armed with newfound knowledge the runes started to make sense to me. I contained my careful hope from Red. I did not want to give her false hope in case I was wrong. The rune structures were complex and I understood far from most of it but the surrounding theory did not strike me as odd. The date for the Pioneer's return to the Skylands came and went but I had no possibility of joining it. Red cradled me for hours as I cried that night. Even though I had no desire to see my home again the Pioneer had been my final link to mom, Marissa and Kendall. I feared I would never see them again. Even though I had come to terms with that possibility when I left, knowing that the last chance had passed struck me hard. I tried to distract myself from my sorrow by studying but I could not focus my mind. Instead I tried distracting myself with physical exercise but my exertions only lead to my wounds ripping open further. Not even that simple pleasure was allowed to me. Anything more strenuous than a slow walk seemed to rip and tear. Frustration and fear gradually filled me up until something within snapped and I decided to do something stupid. It was do or die. I waited until Red dozed off for the night before I disentangled myself from her. She protested in her sleep and clutched at the warmth I had left behind beneath the covers. Despite the mild days the nights were cold out on the plains. I sat down by the small table and put my back to Red, even though it would be too dark for her to see me. I opened the book on Archons and flipped to the page I had studied repeatedly for the last week and I risked a small trickle of magic to light a candle. I made sure to shield Red from the light so that I wouldn't wake her up. I dipped one of Grasax' pens in an inkwell and put my stump firmly against the table to brace it. One of the glowing wounds ran down my left bicep and I stared at it for a long moment as I gathered my courage. Then I reached up with the pen and put the tip against the skin right beside the wound. My skin twitched at the touch and tracing the rune proved exceedingly difficult with all the tremors of the skin. It wasn't as perfect as I had hoped it would be and the lines were jagged and curled but it would suffice. It would just be temporary after all. The candle burned low as I copied the intricate runes but before dawn I had made several complete circles around the wounds. It was quite a pretty mark, a sort of thorny spiralling pattern that ebbed and flowed around the rent in my skin. At a distance the individual runes were hardly even visible. I considered waking Red and ask her to activate the runes but I was fairly certain that she would refuse, or at least demand a lengthy explanation. When had I become the reckless one? I decided that proving the concept would help me convince her to aid me in containing the rest of my wounds. I put my finger to the edge of the temporary ward and channelled power. My wounds flared and opened a tiny bit further as the runes flared into bluish life. The runes burned themselves into my skin with a sizzle of coiling fat and a smell of burning skin and a coil of smoke and I cried out in surprised pain. Red surged from the bed in a storm of bedcloth and she brandished a dagger in her hand as she cast about for a threat. Her eyes fixed on me lying where I had fallen off the chair onto the flare and she dropped the dagger and stormed to my side.

"Kyra! What happened? Are you alright?"

The pain was already abating, though the runes still burned into my skin.

"Yeah, I'm fine," I lied. It may not have been a lie, I was just not sure that I was indeed fine. Red noticed the glowing runes on my arm.

"What did you do?"

"I healed the wound. I think." I glanced down at the wound. The runes had clamped the wound tightly shut and magical stitches kept it close but magical light still spilled between them. I focused my magesense on it and saw no leakage of power. The ward patched the hole in my soul and kept the magic inside. When the ward was turned into an actual enchantment it would still draw it's power from my soul but it would be a much smaller pull than the natural seepage. I turned a triumphant grin to my friend.

"It worked! The wound is not leaking!"

"You were not even sure it would work?!" Her voice was incredulous.

"Well no, to be honest. But I copied it entirely from the tome. I was mostly confident that it would work."

"Mostly?" she choked out.

"Yeah. Nothing is ever certain."

I pulled her in for a fierce hug. There were some hope after all that I would not be confined to Dun Traelak, and even better that I was not truly dying. We just needed to enchant all of the wounds.

"Why are the runes burning you?"

"I couldn't draw the runes properly with a pen. They are leaking power. It's just a ward, it'll fade. I'm gonna need your help to make the proper enchantments."

"Of course I'll help if I can, but not tonight. You need to rest, how long have you been working?"

I looked away sheepishly. "All night."

"Bed. Now." She punctuated her word by pointing sternly. Ordinarily I would be more than happy to be ordered into bed by a beautiful redhead but I was too excited to sleep right then. I was proven totally wrong as soon as my head touched the pillow.

## Chapter 26

I slept peacefully and deeply and woke up slowly with my nose full of the scent of Red's hair. And an undertone of charred bedspreads that I was rapidly becoming accustomed to. I glanced down at my arm. The wound I had sealed with the ward had opened once more and the runes was still burned into my flesh. The ink was completely gone. In order to make the effect permanent and protect me from leakage we would need to tattoo the runes in and normal ink would not suffice. We needed ink capable of channelling the power safely and precisely, ink like the one in the stylus that went with my grimoire. The ink contained within would not be enough though. We would have to make more, luckily we had a seemingly endless source of power nearby we could use but I would have to teach Red how to cast the spells. It was not a spell I was overly familiar with but the old lectures Kendall had given me on the subject in conjunction with the tomes we had available it should not prove to be too troublesome. I could not wait any longer and I gently prodded my friend awake. She sat up and stretched and I found myself mesmerised by her rippling body. The way she arched her back made her breasts protrude enticingly. After the battle her breasts were bigger than my own and I found myself oddly envious. I sucked a line of drool back into my mouth before she noticed.

"Wake up, beautiful, we have work to do."

"What?"

"Aren't you eloquent today?"

She glared at me through sleepy eyes.

"You are in an unusually good mood this early."

"I'm feeling hopeful!"

That earned me a smile on her pretty face.

"Very well, let me just make sure we get some breakfast. What time is it?"

I shrugged. I honestly had no idea but the sun was plainly visible above the horizon. I focused my magesense and noted the woman outside our door. Anna was back at her post. I wondered how she endured the boredom of waiting outside our door all day. For the first time I noticed her hands working relentlessly and I focused further to bring whatever was in her hand into focus. She was doing something with a long strand of cord and two bone needles. 'Knitting', Red had called it earlier. It amazed me what her people did with their hands. Back home such a process would be automated by a spell but the Bizhjerai did not know how to how to construct spells that advanced. To be honest it was not that difficult but for them it was. Red poked her head through the door and I followed Anna down the stairs with my magesense.

"C'mere, let me show you something."

I sat down by the table and Red joined me. I pulled out a sheaf of parchment and dipped a quill in the inkwell. My burnt fingers made it difficult to hold the quill properly but I did not need to write the runes out perfectly, I merely needed to show them to Red so that she could copy. I drew the runes much larger than they would be for clarity and Red watched my work with keen attention. Anna returned with a large tray piled high with food but since I only had one hand now I could not work and eat at the same time. My hunger would not be denied and I judged that I had already written out enough runes for Red to get started so I handed her the quill to practice copying the runes. The tray was laden with bread that was spread thickly with butter and piled with cold cuts from last nights roast buffalo and I crammed a large bite into my mouth. It was difficult manoeuvring the large sandwich with only one hand but I managed to balance the rear end of the bread on my stump for stability. The food was delightful, even after all these weeks I had not gotten used to the food having this much flavour. I forgot all about Red and her work as I ate and I washed down the sandwich with half a pitcher of buffalo cream. The fatty liquid slid down my throat in a viscous white torrent. I let out a loud belch of contentment and Red glanced at me through the corner of her eye.

"Y'know, a lady would apologise after a burp like that."

"Please," I scoffed, "I ain't no lady. If you had any idea about the thoughts going on up here." I tapped my temple with my stump for emphasis. Red turned fully from her work and regarded me with an amused expression.

"Oh really? Please, do tell."

I snapped my fingers and pointed at the parchment before her. "Focus, student!"

She resumed her work with a chuckle as I helped myself to a second large sandwich. My thin belly was already distended by what I had already consumed but I needed to eat to regain my weight and possibly have energy to spare to heal my hand and the burns that still studded my body. Primarily the burn on the side of my head that left my pillow a mess each morning. I had never been a still sleeper and my tossing and turning at night ripped the wound open into an oozing mess. I could not understand how Red could endure sleeping next to me with my oozing burns and scalding magical wounds but she refused to let go of me even in her sleep. I sensed someone approaching up the stairs and focused my mind in the direction. It was Red's father, along with two of his Huscarls and he was clutching a cloth wrapped bundle in his arms. He held it away from his body as if he wanted to touch it as little as possible and his guards looked worried indeed.

"It pains me to say this, Red."

She started at the sound of my voice, she had been completely absorbed in her work.

"What?"

Was that a worried tone in her voice?

"Better get dressed."

She rolled her eyes but smiled at my teasing.

"You are incorrigible. Why the sudden need for propriety?" She glanced pointedly at my own nakedness.

"Your father is approaching, and he has brought guards."

"I did not think you such a prude."

"Normally no, but do you really think this is something to see?" I lifted my sagging breast. It still sorely lacked the padding it required to fill out the skin.

"Yes." She looked at the wobbling flesh as I let it go and licked her lips exaggeratedly.

"Now who is incorrigible?" I was already stepping into the little skirt she had made for me and pulled it up to my hips so that it hung over my protruding hip bones. "Help me into this?"

This lack of hand was making it difficult indeed to get into the halter. We were dressed when her father knocked on the door and Red was ready to open it immediately. Her father hardly spared his daughter a glance as he barged in.

"Bàs Marbhadair, I need your help."

"Please, not you too, Chief. Call me Kyra."

He handed me the bundle he carried. I accepted it and knew instantly what was contained within. A dark presence stared at me from within the drab cloth but even so I wanted to see it with my own eyes. I put the bundle on the table and fumbled to unwrap it with just one hand. Red came close to help me but I waved her away with my stump.

"No. I don't want you to touch it."

"Said no man ever."

I glared at her even though her quip would have been amusing in any other situation. She had not yet understood the gravity of what was going on. I braced the bundle with my stump and flipped it open. It was indeed Grasax' dagger but unlike the last time I'd seen it the large crystal that was serving as a pommel glowed dully with an inner light. The presence gazing out at me was still weak, barely conscious and it grasped weakly at my power. In my wounded state I was unable to defend myself and it started drawing it from body. My wounds flared with power and pain suffused my skin.

"Get out! It's Grasax, he is in the dagger!"

"What!"

"Just go, he is feeding from me and I can't stop him. Go!"

The Chief made an about face and strode hurriedly from the room, followed by his Huscarls. Red stayed stubbornly behind and her father reached for her arm as he strode past her.

"Not Red, I will need her help."

My voice brooked no argument and he left. It amazed me that he trusted me with his daughter when I was visibly distressed. I had fought the liche in his full power without flinching, but both of us was diminished even though I now held much more power now. The problem lay in that I was completely severed from it. I sent my magesense into the dagger and dove into the complex enchantment. I found his mind deep within the crystal, nestled safely in an intricate latticework of runes. He was virtually untouchable in there. I swept the parchments, books and quills from the table and flipped the dagger onto the surface using the cloth. I dared not touch the dagger with my bare skin. I gritted my teeth against the pain and picked up the quill. Desperation lent my hand a steadiness I did not feel as I started scrabbling runes onto the table. I kept to the basics, working on a simple containment circle. There was no time for anything fancy, not at the rate he was draining me. The gem increased its glow as it stole power from me. It was the same kind of leeching aura that the Reavers surrounded themselves with.

"Red, get here and help out."

Her eyes were wide but she stepped closer without a hint of fear.

"What do I do?"

"Flame, burn the runes into the tabletop. We need broader channels."

Her face scrunched up in concentration until a focused jet of flame erupted from her index finger. The jet narrowed and brightened as she focused it and then she applied it to the runes I had inscribed. The charred furrows in the wood she left behind would not be precise, without clearly defined edges and they would bleed power but we needed to get a circle up as quickly as possible. We could do it properly later. I was not sure what Grasax could accomplish with the power he was stealing from inside the dagger but I was sure that I did not want to find out. I finished the first circle and immediately started on another one, a shield spell that would keep magic from seeping inside. I finished before Red could finish with the inner circle and I stepped back to give her space to work. I could tell from the sweat on her face that the effort of focusing her power and fighting the leeching aura was taxing her strength but there was little we could do about it. I focused on shutting my soul in an attempt to limit the flow of power but I was only marginally effective. Grasax must have idly absorbed the power that flowed past his dagger until he became strong enough for his aura to activate and then he had started stealing power from passersby. Would he be strong enough to break out of the dagger eventually? Possibly possessing a new body? I watched with trepidation as Red finished the outer circle and I resumed my place next to her.

"What now?"

"Charge the enchantments, but don't let them ignite. Let me know when they are on the verge."

She nodded and put one hand each on the runes and my magesense showed me the flow of power. After long minutes she nodded. I reached for the dagger but let my hands hover a few inches above it. The pull on my soul increased tenfold and I almost retched. I started pulling back, with everything I had. An invisible tug of war ensued and long minutes trickled past. Sweat dripped into my eye but I dared not shake it away in fear that the moment may momentarily disorient me. Slowly, ever so slowly, I started gaining ground against the invisible foe and then with a sudden rush the power rushed into me. I overpowered the revenant and devoured its power. The glow in the gem winked out and I ripped my hand back.

"Now!"

The two enchantments blazed into life, rising into the air to their proper three dimensional positions and the two shields were in place. The dark presence in the back of my mind had vanished with the power in the gem. He did not have enough magic to maintain his mind. I could not sense it through the containment field but I was sure that it was still there, inert from lack of power. The inside of the shield was almost devoid of magic, only what little had seeped in as Red activated the spells remained but I was sure that it was even now being absorbed into the dagger. I sat down on the floor hard, panting for breath. Red sat down on a chair, her legs shaking.

"The fuck just happened?"

"Grasax. He still lives. His mind is enshrined in an enchantment and he was gathering power. I don't know what could have happened if he grows strong enough."

Her beautiful eyes widened and she threw the dagger a worried look.

"Will this hold him?"

"For now, but probably not forever. We will need to construct a proper prison for him but for that we need to contain my wounds. There are several books on lichdom down in the library, quite a few of them penned by Grasax himself, but if I was him I would not have committed any of my own weaknesses to paper. Or I would have at least destroyed those books afterwards. But we should be safe for now."

Red rested her head on the table. Her inexperienced soul must be close to exhaustion from the exertion. What would have been a trivial task for me had drained her. With practice she would be able to do this in her sleep but that point was weeks, if not months, from now. I pushed shakily to my feet.

"Are you ready to make some ink? We better get started as soon as possibly. I won't be able to rest peacefully until that thing is properly locked away."

"No, but let's get going anyway. I feel the same as you. What do we need to do?"

"First step is rather simple. It is all outlined thoroughly in this book," I bent down and rummaged through the mess on the floor, "here. You have already read about all of the concepts but I think this is the first applied example for you." I flipped through the pages until I found the spell and handed the open book to my friend.

"Read this, I'm gonna tell Anna to fetch us some water."

"Good idea." She rose from the chair and settled down in the light of the window in the corner. It was small and only let in a small amount of light, as was common with windows in castles designed for defence. I noted that it took her as far from the dagger as she could without actually leaving the room. I stuck my head outside for a moment and my eyes confirmed what my magesense had already told me. Anna was nowhere to be seen, Red's father must have brought her with him when he left. I expanded my magesense and saw them hovering in the stairwell. I walked closer and shouted down the stairs.

"It's alright, he is contained! Can we get some water up in here, Anna?"

"Sure thing, Bàs Marbhadair."

"And some more buffalo cream, if you please."

I could already sense her moving farther away with hurried steps, obviously more than willing to put more distance between herself and the dreaded liche. Red's father approached warily and I awaited him at the top of the stairs.

"What happened? Is it safe?"

I started to explain as we walked back to the room I shared with his daughter but he stopped me while we was still a dozen paces from the door. I noticed suddenly that his Huscarls remained by the stairs, well outside of earshot.

"You know that I love my daughter."

"Yes?"

I had no idea where this was coming from.

"Then you must understand that I trust you when I leave you in her care. After all, you are not a part of the Clan and she will one day inherit the leadership after I die. If something happens to her..."

Was he threatening me?

"Yes, and I appreciate it. I like your daughter a lot." I did not let the true magnitude of my feelings for Red show in my voice as I looked up into his eyes.

"She likes you too. A lot."

"She's told you that?"

"No, she has not. She never speaks to me about such things, not since her mother..." his voice trailed of, clearly unwilling to voice such painful memories.

"Then how do you know?" I winced at the question. Of course he knew his own daughter well enough to read her like an open book. I suddenly realised that I did not even know his name. Red always called him just 'father' and everyone else called him 'Chief'.

"In all her life she has never let anyone call her by a pet name. None. Not even me, her mother or her brother. She has always been proud that she was named after a great hero. No one has been allowed to call her anything else. No one but you."

A surge of affection for my redheaded friend filled my belly and clutched at my heart. I found no words to respond and when he remained silent I nodded and turned to walk back to the door.

"Kyra."

I looked over my shoulder. "Are you going to tell me that if I ever hurt your daughter you will hunt me down and hurt me just as much?"

"Do I have to?" I turned back to face him and stared into his eyes earnestly.

"No."

He met my literally glowing gaze without flinching and nodded. We had an understanding. I rejoined my friend in our shared room but in my magesense I saw the Chief remain outside, staring at the spot where my back had vanished for long minutes before he left. Red glanced up as I entered and flashed me an excited smile.

"This is really fascinating! To imagine that you can make the magic do things for you without supervision. Imagine all the work you can accomplish over time!"

I laughed. "Yeah, my home was built on the principle. Do you have any questions?"

She did. Lots of them. She was still firing them off at me when Anna returned with a large pitcher of water and a smaller filled with buffalo cream. I poured the water into a basin and dipped a cloth in it and started cleaning myself off. I felt dirty all over after the brief contact with Grasax' mind and Red took my place as I drank a large cup of the cream. She never stopped asking questions as she cleaned up and many of them gave me pause before I could formulate an answer. Again she surprised me with her insightful enquiries and I found myself reevaluating several of the methods used in the spellwork she had studied. I had thought that Mages and engineers in the Skylands would have optimised the procedures but I realised that they were as hidebound by tradition and 'this is how we have always done it' than anyone could be. For a people that had been deeply steeped in magic for centuries they had not yet perfected the art. Eventually her barrage of questions abated.

"Are you ready to try it out?"

She pursed her lips, seriously considering her knowledge.

"I think so."

I picked up a stick from the stack of firewood next to the fireplace.

"Show me. Build the spell here on the floor."

She raised an eyebrow in surprise.

"Right here? Shouldn't we do this at the fount?"

"First rule of spellworking," I told her with a grin, "always prove your concept with minimal power first. If you make a mistake in the design and pour in the power it can be quite... Unpredictable."

"Is that why you prefer to launch spells in combat with the precast ones in your guns? I don't think I've ever seen you do anything properly complex in the midst of battle."

"Partly, but also because of the self-consuming nature of spells. Shooting the physical substrate will result in less burnout during the travel time since a shot is much faster than any spell you can cast. But it is also that because a complex spell will take time to cast and you are rarely undisturbed for that long during combat."

"But can't you shield yourself to buy the time?"

Combat magics was one of my specialities and I could answer without hesitation.

"Yes, but that would force you to remain stationary. Even if you are safe within a shield the enemy will also be free to think up any sort of fuckery, or they could simply react accordingly. Also, every impact on the shield will drain you of power and the backlash may distract you enough to make a mistake and then the effects will yet again be unpredictable. You can only channel a certain rate of power and that must be split between the shield and whatever spell you are casting, there is simply too many variables to take into account during a fight."

She was silent for a moment as she poured herself a mug of cream.

"What if you prepare several spells, or parts of them, in advance and just stitch them together on the fly?"

I did not follow. "What do you mean?"

"Suppose you write a scroll for an explosive spell, and one to launch it on another scroll. Then all you need to cast in combat is the connection between them, charge them up and release them. That could be done in a moment and then you could fight on with your sword as you charge it up. Perhaps you could even prepare a connection scroll and just slot the other spells into it?"

She drained the mug as I stared at her. That was completely insane what she had just suggested. It was also ingenious. She noticed my stare.

"What?"

"Red, you are a fucking genius!"

She scoffed. "You don't know how I fuck."

I was taken by surprise by her sudden joke and my response sputtered on my lips.

"You are so adorable when you get flustered. So you think it could work?"

"Damn straight I think. I have been fighting for most of my life and the thought never even crossed my mind. Are you sure that you are not an expert Mage masquerading as a Clanswoman?"

"You are too kind, I am just speaking the idea as it comes to me."

"It's brilliant. We need to test your theory, but first back to the task at hand. Show me what you got."

"But you've already seen what I got?" She made a gesture that indicated her body and I rolled my eyes. Was she flirting with me?

"Fair enough, get naked and then show me the spell."

"Get your mind out of the mud, Bàs Marbhadair. I am a lady."

I snorted but chose to not rise to the bait. Instead I pointed sternly at the floor and sat down on the bed to watch her. She knelt down, leaned forward, and focused her power to char the stick I threw to her in the same way I had done back in the armoury. Did she strike that pose on purpose? It did show of the curve of her hips rather nicely. She started to draw the runes with confident motions. Despite her confidence she drew each curve meticulously and she paused often to consult the book. I helped myself to another mug of the viscous cream and sipped the drink as I watched her work. She drew the spell flawlessly until just before she finished.

"That's not right." I pointed at the odd swirl at the end of the rune channel.

"It is not by the books, but I think this will work better."

"Unpredictable effects, remember?"

"Yeah, I remember but it feels right. Just trust me, you can spank me later if it doesn't work."

The idea of spanking her was enticing but I was fairly certain that it was just a figure of speech and not an actual promise. I waved my stump for her to continue. Contrary to her words she started double checking her work, and then did it again.

"Alright, I'm ready."

"Well then, fire it up!"

She placed her hands on the spell and focused her power. It came out hesitantly at first but as the power flowed along the runes, igniting them as it went she gained confidence and the small trickle turned into a rushing river of magic. The runes ignited fully in a bright blue light and rose into the air to assume their final form.

"Keep going, let's see what happens next."

"But the spell is supposed to keep going on it's own?"

"Only if connected to a source of power. It must feed on something after all. For now you will be that source."

She did not answer, instead she just kept pouring power into the spell. I could tell that she was tiring rapidly. Her store of power was not overly large yet and she had been of only average strength to begin with. I was already planning out a training regimen for her to build up her strength. After almost ten minutes a tiny speck of matter appeared in the centre of the spell and when Red noticed she was so astonished that she lost her focus. The spell fizzled and dissipated as it consumed itself and the tiny crystal fell to the floor with an almost imperceptible clatter. She picked it up using the nails of her fingers and peered at it where it rested in her palm.

"It worked!"

"'Course it did. You did well."

"Despite my little improvisation."

"Or perhaps because of it. The important thing is that it works. Do you think you are ready to cast it for real outside?"

"No, not now. Let's have lunch first."

"Excellent suggestion. I'll ask Anna to bring it up."

"Why don't we eat out in the courtyard? Would be nice to feel the sun on my skin."

"I don't mind. Some fresh air would be good."

I told Anna to bring us something to eat and meet us out in the courtyard with it. Red was glaring at the dagger on the table.

"What about that thing?"

"Better leave it where it is for now. I dare not move it, we would have to move the entire table with it or we would break the shielding and I don't think we will get it through the door without tilting it."

"I don't like having it in here."

"Me either, but we don't have a choice for now. Ready to go?"

"Yeah, lead the way."

We descended the stairs in a companionable silence and we sighed in unison when the sun warmed our skin. We found a relatively secluded spot and sat on the ground with our backs to the wall of the keep. Anna found us shortly thereafter with a basket of food and I wasted no time before I helped myself to a mug of buffalo cream to drink while she unpacked the rest of the basket. She set up a meal similar to what I'd had for breakfast, a sandwich of cold cuts and a salad. I was not too keen on the vegetables and started in on the meat and bread. Why eat plants when you could eat proper food? Especially considering that I had grown up eating only the stale fungus of my homeland. The courtyard was still bustling with activity but this time most of the Clanspeople working with the repairs and cleanup brandished the staffs and wands they had found in the stores. I saw a woman levitating blocks of stone toward the breach where a man received them with his own staff and set them in the breach. A young woman was on her knees there where she used a wand to carefully seal the rocks together. It would appear that the Clans were rapidly learning about stonework. Several large piles of stone was the only visible remnants of the stone tower. I wondered if Grasax had written down that particular enchantment, it would be quite difficult if not impossible to replace the shield without it. Maybe if we imported an engineer from the Skylands that had worked on the Great Barrier to help us we could do it. We finished our meal and as usual I had stuffed more down my gullet than I would have thought would fit and my belly swelled visibly, especially in contrast with my protruding hip bones. I cradled my belly with my remaining hand.

"Do you think it will be a boy or a girl?"

Red smiled before she answered.

"Considering the father it will probably look like a buffalo."

"You say that as if it is a bad thing. The buffalo are delicious."

She gasped and made a face of mock consternation.

"You're gonna eat your baby? You monster!"

I neglected telling her that eating babies were not unheard of at home. I was fairly sure that people did not kill children for food but if there were a dead baby nearby then I was convinced that someone with sufficient funds would be amenable to buy the corpse for dinner.

"I might not be able to help myself, it is just so tasty!"

"You still haven't gotten used to our kind of food?"

"If you ever get the chance to taste our fungus you will understand."

"That bad, huh?"

"Yeah. Mom could work wonders with it and made it palatable but after tasting this... No, there is no comparison."

"Tell me about her?"

"Who?"

"Your mother."

"Why do you want to know?"

"I dunno, you mention her sometimes but you never speak about her. I'd like to know what she's like, how like her you are."

"Hardly at all. I take after my father, except in looks. Mom is a gentle soul."

"As are you."

"Are you kidding?" I could not hide my disbelief. Me? Gentle? I had murdered so many people. I pushed the memory of a dead child aside. "Dragonbane. Bàs Marbhadair. Gentle?"

"Those may be respectable titles, but they do not define you. Not to me. You are the woman who joined the fight to protect your captors when you had no cause to do so."

"How can you say that when you know what I have done?"

"Because you did what you had to do to survive. Your home sounds like an awful place, I would have done the same if I had even been able to survive."

I was getting uncomfortable at the unexpected turn of our conversation so I changed the subject. "Are you ready to cast the spell?"

She watched me with a wistful expression when I shut her out. "Yeah, as ready as I'll ever be without a proper nights rest."

"Let's get to it then."

Red stood up and offered her hand to help me up. I grasped her wrist and she pulled me to my feet. We walked across the courtyard to the fount that was given a wide berth by the workers. Murmurs of 'Anjali' and 'Bàs Marbhadair' greeted us as we passed them. Red stopped a ways from the fount and stood in thought.

"What's the problem?" I asked her.

"How do I get close enough to the fount to draw the spell without, y'know?" She gestured at me and I realised she meant my glowing eyes and veins.

"As long as you don't pull the power into yourself this can't happen."

"Then what about the burning?"

She meant the fact that the fount's mere touch was caustic in nature.

"You need to shield yourself."

"I don't know how to do that."

That put a damper on our plans. There was nothing to it though than to power through and I started explaining how shields worked.

"Everyone has a natural shield at all times, it is infused in all of the cells in you body and it is what keeps your soul firmly entrenched in your body. It protects your mind from some influences and it is what animates your body. It is powered by your own magic at all times but it is so firmly set in your form that it does not take much power to maintain it. What we do when shielding ourselves physically is that we expand this shield and change its aspect. You push it out of your body." I frowned, realising that I did not make much sense. "It would help if I could show you but I dare not, not with all these wounds. It is not like a spell, there are no runes involved. Try to cast it with willpower alone."

"You can do that? I thought the runes were essential for magic."

"Do you use a rune when you dry your hair? Or light a fire?"

"Well no," she admitted.

"This is the same. Imagine the shield like I described it. When you do it this way it won't be very efficient but for now we just need you do understand the process. Give it a try."

A look of intense concentration appeared on her face and she stuck the tip of her tongue out of the side of her mouth as she frowned into empty space. I watched her with both my eyes and my magesense for long minutes. Her skin shimmered with power and something that might have been a shield wobbled out of her skin before it retracted. She looked at me with wide eyes.

"Did you see that? Was that right?"

"It was a good start. Do it again but try to push it further. I want you encased in an egg like shield about an arms length from your body."

She tried again and I waited patiently. Raising your first shield was mostly a process of trial and error but in the end it was not difficult. The runes were not necessary for any spell casting, they only helped focus the mind to set the flows and any complex spell was too complex to hold in the mind entirely. That was why we used runes and wrote them out. Once written the intent, the will if you like, was already set. After that it was a question of mere power. A shield was not a spell per se, it was more of an extension of the natural shield and there were no runes for it. You could create a shield with runes, but that was not an extension of your own shield. It was slower to cast and were usually not mobile, unless the runes were affixed to your person like those I'd had on my armour and it was slower to cast if you had not prepared them in advance. It was also more difficult to modify on the fly since you had to change the rune patterns while the spell was active. Unless you built in conditionals? My mind suddenly surged with possibilities. How complex conditionals could you craft? Could you make an seemingly intelligent spell? I digress. A runed shield had one important advantage and that was that it lacked the backlash side effect of the natural shield since it was not a part of you. Breaking the personal shield of a mage could knock them senseless or even kill them outright if it drained all of their power away. I almost missed when her shield bloomed out of her body, I was so ensconced in my own thoughts but her exultant cry snapped me out of it. I smiled broadly at her.

"Well done!"

"I did it!"

She looked around in amazement, watching her shield from the inside. Then realisation struck her.

"I can see it! I can see magic!"

"Yes, you will always be able to see your own magic. You are not seeing it as much as your brain paints it out for you to make sense of it. Without more training you won't be able to see one of my shields for instance but this is a good start. You may even figure it out on your own in time now that you can see your own magic. Now make it hard."

"What?"

I waved my stump through her shield but felt no resistance.

"I want you to keep me out of it."

She focused and her shield changed imperceptibly.

"Now?"

I poked my stump through it. "Nope, try again."

We kept going for a quarter of an hour before my stump struck something solid. "Excellent. Now you need to make it deflect the magic. Walk closer to the fount, slowly, and stop when you get uncomfortable. Make the shield reject the magic before you go closer."

I could tell that she was nervous but she did as I told her. I could see the magic of the fount pouring through her shield and she stopped. I waited for long minutes and stopped counting in my head when five minutes had passed. She would get there in time. She figured it out more quickly than she had figured out how to make it solid. Now that she understood more about shielding changing it would become easier for each time she did it. It would be trickier once she started making complex shields but that would come later. One mistake all beginners made was when they shielded their first magical attack. I had made the mistake back in the day when I was in training for the Guard. I had seen the fireball approaching and I had made my shield reject the magic. I had not factored in the heat and it had passed through my shield and scorched my eyebrows off. Kendall had teased me relentlessly until they grew back out. Red stepped closer to the fount and the magic flowed around her shield without hurting her.

"Careful. Don't overextend, you don't want to be in there if your shield fails."

I let her train for a few more minutes before I made her step out of the fount.

"Nicely done. I want you to keep shielding yourself at all times from now on. It will be good practice, both in shielding and to increase your channelling ability and personal storage capacity. If you drop your shield I will throw something at you."

She stuck her out her tongue at me but did not drop her shield.

"Be glad that you are shielded or I would have punished you for that," I smiled to take the sting out of my words. "You will need to be able to maintain the shield at all times without conscious effort or else it will be useless in a fight. Can't have you dropping it at minor distractions."

Before I finished speaking my fist lanced out at her face and her eyes widened in surprise. Her shield vanished and my fingers closed around her throat and I pulled her toward me and she stumbled, off balance. I smiled into her face inches before mine.

"Case in point."

"Kyra! Your wounds!" I let her go and glanced down at my body. My swift motion had torn a few of them open and they bled power. I had not even registered the pain of them opening. I was becoming way too used to being in pain.

"Yeah, it's fine. Why are you not shielding yourself?"

She did have the decency to look sheepish and her shield reappeared. She was getting rather quick at that. It had taken me much longer to learn to raise a shield that quickly.

"Shall we get started on the spell?"

I shook my head.

"No, not now. I want you at peak performance, and more used to shielding yourself. It seems easy now but remember that you have to maintain the shield and draw the runes at the same time and you need to have it pulled close to your fingers or you won't be able to hold the stylus. Besides, after the battle with Grasax you are already drained. We will do it tomorrow and spend the afternoon practising your shielding."

"You call that a battle? We were just drawing runes."

"Yes." Something in my eyes must have conveyed my sincerity for she did not object. I led her away from the fount and we headed toward the remaining armoury. I wanted some sort of weapon to use on her shield or I would destroy my remaining hand against its hard surface.

## Chapter 27

The next morning we stood by the fount again. Red had performed admirably during our training last afternoon and by the end of it we were both exhausted. She had forced me to let one of the Clansmen take the rod I had used to bash her shield from me when I tore my wounds for the third time and I had not protested too much. I was still not ready for heavy exertions and during dinner I had stubbornly eaten more than I should have. I was sick and tired of feeling weak and useless and desperately wanted to regain my strength. Even the little exercise I had gotten before my friend forced me to rest had felt good. We had both been exhausted and gone to bed early. Red had practised drawing the spell twice more and I was now confident that she would be able to copy it perfectly, even while shielding her body. What I was uncertain of was if she would be able to do it while her shield was being assaulted by the power coursing from the fount. I had cautioned her to take breaks if she felt weak and possibly drawing power from the fount to reinforce her shield. Now she stood staring at it, taking deep breaths to steel herself. The shield bloomed from her body, initially maintaining her shape before it bloated and formed the egg shape around her. Slowly the right side of it shrank down around her arm to hover inches above her skin. Her stylus bent when the shield contracted around it and she frowned at it until the stylus passed through. This was a very complex shield for a beginner. It had to keep magic out, as well as shield her from the small events of Wild Magic that constantly churned inside the concentrated power. As if that was not enough, she also had to maintain the irregular shape around her arm but yet again my beautiful friend astounded me with her quick intuition. Kendall would love talking to her, I could practically hear them already going on and on about esoteric aspects of magic. I was more interested in practical applications. Red walked into the fount and knelt on the scarred ground and she immediately started drawing out the runes. I watched like a mother hen, circling and never letting my magesense stray from her or the shapes she drew. It took almost an hour for she was so meticulous and once or twice her shield wavered and her hand slipped. I called out corrections to her runes once when she did not notice that her distraction had caused her to misalign the pattern. When she was finished she looked up at me and I realised that I had forgotten to tell her what to do now.

"Connect it to the fount."

She stared blankly at me. Fuck. I had not taught her the power gathering spell. It was like a net of runes spread over the fount that would absorb the power.

"Get out of there, I'll draw it out for you. It is nowhere near as complex as what you just made."

She extracted herself from the storm of magic and dropped her shield. I immediately let my hand whip out and smack her on the ass with an audible clap. She squeaked in surprise and jumped in outrage and glared at me. Despite her apparent shock there was a slumbering smoulder in her eye when she looked at me through narrowed eyes. So my girl liked it rough, did she? I filed that little nugget of information away for later. We had brought a piece of parchment and a pen with us and I quickly sketched out the spell. It was one I was infinitely familiar with since I used it a lot back home when I gathered magic from the field contained in my apartment. Red perused the scroll for a short few moments before she returned into the fount. She did not even flinch when the power enveloped her shield and within five minutes she had drawn the runes around the fount. The fount itself was not large, maybe a foot and a half in diameter but she had to shift around it without smudging the runes she had already drawn. She dared not lean across it, for good reason. I don't think she would have been able to maintain the shield in a full assault from the torrent. As she worked I noted something incredible. She had changed her shield to let in a small amount of the magic around her and even as she focused on drawing the runes she was absorbing the power trickling in and putting it in her shield. I had not taught her that. I had not even mentioned that it was possible to make the shield semi-permeable to magic. Her control after such a short time amazed me and a heat gathered between my legs at the sight. What can I say? Power turns me on and while she lacked the brute strength that I had, even back before the fight with Grasax, her control was astounding compared to her very limited experience. She finished the spell and without me prompting she connected it to the outer circle of runes. Then she channelled her personal powers into it and it blazed into being, igniting the outer spell as the power coursed through the rune channels. She stepped backwards away from the spellwork as it ignited and rose into the air. A small dome of brightly glowing runes hovered around the fount.

"Excellent work, Red. Now we wait."

Her shield dropped and I pinched her arm.

"Ow!"

"Shield up!"

"Fine." The shield returned around her and I tapped it with my knuckles.

"Good. That was impressive work. What gave you the idea of making the shield permeable to magic, I did not teach you that."

"No, but you did mention absorbing power from the fount to reinforce my shield, but how could I do that while keeping it out? Had to let some of it in."

"Solid reasoning. Let's see if we can teach you to see magic while we wait for the spell. Do you remember what I told you about what is called 'magesense'?"

She nodded.

"That comes after you learn to see magic. You don't really see it with your eyes, but you see it with your magesense but it is much easier to view it as if you do. You start with something familiar, like normal vision, and overlay the magical concepts. After that we can move on with seeing without your eyes, using only your magic."

"You can identify spells without looking?"

"Sort of. The acuity of your magesense is logarithmically proportional to the power you are currently holding."

Her brow furrowed in confusion.

"Loga-what?"

"Logarithmically. It is a declining mathematical formula to describe a sloping curve. It doesn't really matter. Look at it like this: the range of your magesense expands as you hold more power, but each inch you sense that is farther from you requires more power than the inch before it."

"So you need to double your strength to increase one inch?"

"At one point yes, beyond that it requires even more than double strength. The range increase rapidly at first and then slower."

"How far can you sense?"

"Before this," I gestured at my glowing eyes and veins, "about a hundred yards but it was not strong enough for details and walls and such obscured my sight. Now I can 'see' well beyond the walls with great clarity."

"Does it consume power to use it?"

"No, it is just there. I don't know how that works, maybe it is the mind expanding and not really using magic to see?"

"Alright. Where do we start?"

"Inside, I think. I am getting hungry."

"When aren't you?" She asked with a roll of her eyes. Did she just call me fat?

Red learned to see magic with the alacrity I was starting to expect from her and we moved on to actually use her power. She still needed to focus hard to perform any kind of magic and it was a slow process. We needed the magic to flow freely and effortlessly if she was going to use it for anything more complex than drying her hair and lighting fires. We worked through the day and each time she dropped her shield I threw something at her, or pinched her if I was within reach. If glares could murder I would be a pile of ash right now. It was still difficult for her to channel magic quickly when night started to fall and she was covered in a fine sheen of perspiration. Despite her exertions her eyes were still bright and alert and she wolfed down the dinner Anna brought us. I had spent the day basically just eating and watching my friend work. After supper we decided to go check on the spells on the fount. I had kept close watch on them with my magesense and I already knew that there were a small store of ink within a crystal shell ready for harvest. It might not be enough to seal all of my wounds but we would be able to prove the concept. The problem was getting the crystal container of ink out of the spell. Merely reaching in would disrupt the hovering runes and the effects could be unpredictable as the rune structure shifted. Since the spells were bound directly to the fount it would be nearly impossible to drain them of their power since they replenished faster than we could drain them. I started explaining the problem to Red but I quickly noted that she was not listening. She was staring at the spell construct with wide eyes and then it hit me. It was the first time she saw a complex spell structure. I admired the rapturous expression on her face, her childlike glee made her radiant. I was loathe to interrupt her fascination but we had a mission to accomplish and I snapped my fingers in her direction. Or at least I would have but my mangled fingertips refused to make the sound. Instead only a horrible rasping of bone and sinew on skin erupted and I winced at the sound. I had started to tentatively use blood magic to heal the appendage but I still lacked the physical reserves to do much. It seemed to help a little and I was confident that in time I could restore the fingers. The severed left hand was an entirely different matter. Enough of my fingers remained that I could use them as a template to restore the rest, but my left hand was completely missing. Maybe I could use the right hand as a template and then mirror it? I discarded the idea almost immediately. If that was possible the Fleshgrafters back home would do it all the time and severed limbs was one of the few physical wounds they could not heal. Of course, most people back home could not afford even rudimentary healing. If you are good at something never do it for free if people are willing to pay for it. It was the creed that ruled the Skylands, and the creed that had made me a mercenary. I would have been completely content remaining a member of the Guard if the pay had been equal to, or better, than being a merc. Most of the Guard remained because they had higher moral standard than I did. The Guard would not murder a child. Well, at least not without some sort of trial. Back to the task at hand. I could not snap my fingers to get Red's attention but fortunately for me she had dropped her shield once more in her fascination and I reached out and grabbed a lock of brilliantly red hair. I tugged it playfully and she jerked out of her awestruck stare. Before I could say anything her shield bloomed out of her and pushed my hand away from her body. Just to be a pain in her ass I did not let go of her hair and she yelped in surprised pain when her shield pushed my hand far enough away to pull her hair along. I let go before the hair was ripped from her scalp and grinned evilly at her.

"Mind your surroundings. A shield will protect you, but it can also hurt you if you do not think first."

"Ever the teacher, aren't you?"

"Only since I met you, " I said with a warm smile. She returned the gesture.

"Thank you. I had never imagined all the things you can do with magic."

"Don't mention it. I enjoy watching you learn. If you keep this up you will surpass me in no time and I will need to find another tutor for you."

"Your friend Kendall?"

"If possible, that would be ideal."

Her warm smile turned into a teasing one.

"You are not afraid to push me into the arms of a male tutor?" The way she emphasised the word 'male' made it clear what her meaning was. A warm feeling spread through my belly at the implication that I might not want to do just that and that she was completely on board with that.

"Not even a little bit."

She put on an expression of mock surprise. "You trust me that much?"

"Not at all, you little minx. Kendall prefer men."

"Oh."

I could not help but to laugh at her surprised expression. "So you two never…" Her question trailed off and her face coloured as she realised the intimacy of the question. I was far beyond feeling offended at mere questions and did not mind. I was not ashamed about my history with Kendall.

"Yes, once. That was when he realised that he preferred men."

"Oh, shit. That must have been embarrassing."

"For me? Or him?"

"Uhm, both?"

I laughed. "Yeah. I am not sure who was more embarrassed. Anyway, here is the problem with harvesting the crystal."

I started explaining and she tapped her lower lip as she considered the problem. "Any suggestions?" I wanted to hear her thoughts before I voiced my own.

"No. None. I have no idea how to solve this."

"We, and by that I mean 'you' need to alter the spell at ignition-time."

"Ignition-time?"

"That is what we call the time of a spells life cycle when it is active, post-ignition. It is possible to alter them, but it requires you to make the change perfectly. Since the spell is active each and every modification you do will instantly take effect. If you only apply the change partially..."

"The effects will be unpredictable, yeah you have been saying that a lot lately."

"When this much power is involved, the magnitude of the unpredictable events will that much greater, so be careful."

"How do I do this?"

"Imagine the change you want, imagine it perfectly and completely in your mind and then force your will on the spell. I suggest you focus on a small piece of the spell at a time and change it in small increments. As small an increment as possible that will keep the entire thing stable. Are you with me?"

"Yeah, I think so. What kind of change should I do first?"

"I suggest modifying the power feedback loop to the power gathering spell. It feeds itself with part of the magic it gathers. Disrupt it and the rest will starve itself out."

"Is that what you called, what was it? Single point of failure?"

"Precisely. Normally you would want to avoid that but for this application it wasn't necessary. No one would tamper with it and the spells were simple enough that the spells would not malfunction. The pattern actually helps us now since it will be easier to take the thing apart. Make your shield as powerful as you can, just in case."

Red nodded and I could see her shield thickening and changing to block magic and physical objects. She took a step into the fount and added a layer to her shield that would protect her from heat. Good girl. She knelt by the flowing dome of runes and focused. I narrowed my magesense to the area she was working on. It was a simple rune channel that emerged from the power gathering spell and looped back inside. Red reached out and the channel split apart. The output end writhed madly as raw power erupted and the focused jet scorched her shield. Sparks flew and blinded us both as her shield reacted to repel the force. Small events of Wild Magic erupted. One exploded with a bright light and a loud noise and several of the curious onlookers jumped in surprise. Another event manifested as a small luminescent bug that flew away on shimmering wings but as soon as it left the dense magical field of the fount it dissipated in a violent display of magical flames. A third event transmuted the very air into a combustible gas the burst into flame with a loud whoosh. Red stumbled back and landed on her ass, but she refused to drop her shield. I surged forward to snatch her out of the fount and almost broke my fingers on her shield when I reached for her arm. The fount stung my skin and I pulled the power within myself. I had bled quite a bit since the last time I fed from it and the chaos subsided a bit as I consumed it. Red scrambled backwards on all fours and I hurried to join her. With the power severed from the spells they fizzled out as they consumed themselves and the crystal container of ink fell from its levitating position. It fell right into the hole that was the fount and vanished from sight. We both stared dumbly at where it had disappeared. How the fuck could we have been so stupid to forget that it was hovering above a hole in the ground that stretched to the centre of the earth for all that we knew? We shared a startled look when the power from the fount diminished significantly. The crystal must be blocking the hole. With a loud whistle the container returned, propelled by the increased pressure of magic. It flew into the air as new power flowed around us.

"Catch it! Don't let it break!"

Red surged to her feet, raising her hands as if aiming to catch a ball.

"With magic! It'll break your hands!"

Her arms dropped to her sides immediately and she frowned at the container that had started to come back down. It hurtled straight at her face with bone breaking speed. She had dropped her shield. If she failed to catch it it would crush her face, possibly killing her. I took a few short steps and launched my thin body in a dive tackle.

"Ooph!" In another circumstance I would have laughed at the stupid sound she made when my shoulder knocked the wind out of her and I cradled my stump behind her head to shield it from the hard ground. In my magesense I saw the container slow dramatically but my tackle had broken her focus. Just as Red landed on the ground with me on top of her the container struck the stone cobbles, but it held. The back of her head bounced on my stump. I rolled off of her to let her regain her breath.

"Sorry about the tackle, but I wasn't sure if you would be able to catch it in time. We haven't practised telekinesis all that much."

She waved me off, still struggling to breathe. I left her to recover on her own and retrieved the container. It was a fist-sized dodecahedron filled with a luminescent fluid and the facet on top had an intricate rune carved into it. I returned to my still supine friend and offered my stump to help her up. Her fingers closed without hesitation around my mangled limb and I pulled her to my feet. I winced at the pain when my wounds tore from the movement and I handed her the container.

"Are you ready to ink me up?"

"We'd better get Uralnor for that."

I scrunched up my brow in confusion. "Uralnor?"

"He is the best Clansman with a needle. He is much better than I."

"Does he know magic?"

"Not even a little. But I can sketch out the runes in normal ink and he can fill them out. He will do a much better job than I."

Her reasoning was sound so I complied.

"Fair enough. Go get him and I'll set things up in our room."

Red nodded and left and I began the short trek up the stairs. I put the container on the table and risked the tiny amount of power required to activate the rune. Blazing agony shot from all of my wounds and it faded slowly. I was breathing hard and sweating profusely when I regained my sight but the top of the container had already dissolved and let the magical ink breathe air for the first time. I pulled out the sketches of the runes we would need and piled the stack of papers next to the inkwell before I went to the shallow basin and the pitcher of water to clean the sweat off. I was quaffing down a large mug of buffalo cream when Red joined me in the room with a man in tow. He was an older man, for a Clansman anyway, at around fifty. His hair had gone steely gray and his face was heavily lined but he still carried and axe on his belt along with a long dagger, almost a short sword. He took in my almost naked body in a single disinterested glance before he bowed his head.

"Bàs Marbhadair, Anjali tell me you want some ink?"

"That is correct, Uralnor. She told me that you are the best inker Clan Bizhjerai have."

He bowed at Red. "She is too kind. I do my best."

"He is really good, I can think of no one better," Red interjected. I noted the leather bundle in his hand.

"You brought your tools, excellent. Are you ready to get started?"

"Don't we need to sketch the runes first?"

"I already have the ones branded into my flesh, let's start with that and do the rest in the morning."

"Show me," Uralnor said with obvious interest. I raised my arm to show him the burn scars in my skin. He hummed and hawed and pulled my skin with his thumbs to see how the scarring deformed.

"The scarring will make it difficult, but I can work with this. I need light," he added the last part over his shoulder to Anjali and within a few moments a light spell came into being above his head. Uralnor looked at her fondly.

"You always did learn quickly, Anjali. Your father will be proud."

"Thank you." 

Uralnor unrolled his leather bundle and revealed a set of delicate tools. He withdrew a small vial of ink and a needle but I held up my remaining hand to stop him.

"I need you to use that ink," I indicated the glowing container. Uralnor frowned at it but did not comment, instead replacing his own small vial in the bundle. He withdrew another with an amber liquid inside and held it out to me.

"You better drink this, it will numb you to the pain of the needle."

I was tempted but after a moments consideration declined his offer. I was afraid that it would dull my mind and in my current state I was not sure how that would affect my magic. If I became too relaxed I may explode as the wounds opened fully. He shrugged and put the vial back.

"Suit yourself. It is going to hurt."

"These wounds already hurt. A little more pain will hardly make a difference."

The wound was on the inside of my bicep and we struggled for a bit to find a way where I could sit comfortably and at the same time give him the posture to work.

"This will probably be easier if you lie down on your back. The bed perhaps?"

"Fair enough." I lay on my back on the bed and Red sat cross legged next to me. She gripped my hand as Uralnor sat down. She carefully guided the light to illuminate the wound without blinding him. For once I did not rebuke her for dropping her shield. He spread a thick layer of ink over a rune, just enough that the design below was visible through the faint glow and then he put the needle to my skin. A small delicate hammer occupied his other hand and he started gently tapping the broad end of the needle. I hardly felt the bite, the pain from the wound completely overshadowed the pain of his implements. I am not sure how long it took but the fine lines of power was intricate and the edges had to be perfectly aligned for maximum efficiency. Red's eyes never strayed from the slowly emerging pattern but I was quickly getting bored. My nose was filled with the scent of ink and blood and the charred smoke of the bedspreads smouldering where when my wounds shifted to intact areas. Despite the pain in my body my eyelids were getting heavy and before I knew it I dozed off.

I was awakened when Red shook my shoulder. Uralnor leaned back and stretched his back and shoulders.

"It's done, Kyra. Are you ready to try it out?"

I sat up and inspected Uralnor's work. It was perfect and completely covered the scarring. The ink was glowing a dull blue that matched my blazing veins.

"Yeah. Activate it."

She reached out and pressed a finger to the edge of the pattern. I felt a shiver course up my arm and down my back from the contact. She looked into my eyes and then activated the enchantment. Power surged into the tattoo and the glow intensified as it activated. Magical stitching appeared and pulled the wound tightly shut and then my natural shield was reinforced, effectively patching my soul. Red withdrew her finger and the enchantment fed directly from my soul. With my magesense I noted with satisfaction that the wound had completely stopped leaking power and even as I watched the fierce glow of both the wound and the tattoo faded to a much weaker burn. I looked up at Uralnor.

"That is absolutely perfect! Do you think you have time to do another tomorrow?"

"Another? That was one of the most complex tattoos I've ever made! How many more do you want?"

I suddenly understood that he had not yet understood the significance of the ink, he thought it was merely decoration to obscure an ugly wound. He could not see the magic in the ink. To him it would have looked as if my wound had just darkened. I gestured at my body.

"All of these wounds need one."

His eyes opened wide.

"All of them?"

"Mhm. It is actually an enchantment that seal the wound. These wounds are magical in nature and my soul bleeds out through them. I need to patch them all up or else I will die."

"In that case I am here to help, Bàs Marbhadair. Anything you need. We owe you so much for getting rid of Grasax."

"Tomorrow then."

He nodded. "Tomorrow. Do you have the design written down somewhere so I can study more in preparation."

"Yes, certainly. The papers on the table, take them with you if you wish."

Uralnor gathered up the papers on his way out, leaving his tools behind. Red carefully brought the ink container and put it on the table. I could tell from the strain around her eyes that she was exhausted.

"We should rest too. It's been a long day."

I stood up and pulled the halter top over my head awkwardly, only having one hand was getting seriously tedious. When I was finally ready for bed Red had already stripped and bedded down and I hastened to join her. For the first time in a long time I fell asleep with a fair bit of hope.

## Chapter 28

The next day was incredibly boring for me as Uralnor worked hard. The inkwell was halfway empty, there had been much more waste than I had anticipated and I sent Red outside to recast the spell on the fount. I did not like letting her do it unsupervised but she convinced me to stay behind and let Uralnor work. She returned two hours later, reporting that a new crystal was growing in the fount. I spent an hour explaining to her how to sever the flow of power without that spurt of magical power she had triggered the last time as Uralnor worked on a wound on my belly. The inkwell ran dry as the sun set and Uralnor retreated for the night. The next day I watched Red harvest the ink without incident and Uralnor resumed his work.
