He was working on my legs now and my arm was free so I could read a book while he did. Each wound he sealed lessened the pain in my body and my head felt clearer than it had for a long time. This particular book had not made any sense the last time I perused it but now with a clearer head I managed to understand bits and pieces. Those pieces let me understand further bits of information and before long I scanned the pages rapidly. It was Grasax himself who had penned it and he proved to be quite the pedagogue. I was trying to figure out how to contain, or even better destroy, the dagger that housed his mind. Something intruded on my concentration and I blinked up at Uralnor before I realized that he had spoken.

"I'm sorry, say that again?"

He looked away nervously. Was he bashful?

"I need to lift your skirt to treat this wound fully."

I looked down and again lamented the lack of breasts that usually had made a direct line of sight impossible. The edge of my short skirt lay less than half an inch above the wound high on my inner thigh, Red had chosen the length of the skirt for just that reason.

"Yeah, sure, go ahead. I don't mind." I bent my leg and angled it to give him better access and he hesitantly reached out with two fingers and pinched the cloth to pull it up. He arranged the cloth carefully to preserve my modesty but the angle of my leg made that almost impossible. He stubbornly kept his eyes averted from my partly revealed crotch. I did not wear anything under the skirt. The only upside to my current condition was that the magic had burned the hair from my body and it had refused to grow back. The only thing puzzling me about that was that I retained the hair on my head but I assumed that it was the secondary natural shield around my brain had kept the worst of the magic from reaching my head. It must also be why none of the wounds I had attained during the battle with Grasax had appeared above my shoulders. Red watched Uralnor's discomfort with some amusement and I shifted my leg again. She mouthed the word 'slut' at me and I stuck my tongue out at her. My silent teasing turned into a grimace of pain as I felt the bite of the needle. A downside to the lessening of pain each enchantment brought was that the needle hurt more in comparison. I dove back into the book to distract myself. By the next day I only had one wound left and I could hardly wait until it was sealed. Finally being free of the pain would be marvellous but that longing was only second to actually using magic once more. I had not realised how dependent on magic I had been. I awoke well before dawn and could not remain in the bed even though a beautiful redhead clung to me in her sleep. I had too much anxious energy in my body and I had to burn it off. I gently disentangled myself from Red and for the first time since my injuries I engaged in physical exercise. I started leg bends, since they would put less of a strain on my remaining wound along my ribs, right beneath where the hem of my halter would be. When my legs were screaming I chanced to do some push ups and to my surprise it did not tear my wound at all. I kept going until my arms collapsed and I fell on my face on the floor. I rolled over and started doing crunches but that did tear my wound and I sat up, full of disappointment. With my magesense I noticed that Red had woken up but she had not moved, merely opened her eyes and watched me. Without giving away that I had noticed her being awake I put my hands against the floor behind me and rested my weight on them, pushing my shoulders back and thrusting my paltry chest out. Better give her something to look at, despite my figure still being quite pathetic. My magesense picked up on her increased heart rate and I felt my own heart start to beat faster. I liked the way her eyes roved over my body and at that moment I wanted nothing more than her to come and ravish me right there on the floor. I was just about to angle my leg to reveal my arousal and give her a come hither look when someone knocked on the door. Being so focused on Red I had not sensed Uralnor arriving. I bit back a curse and called out to him through the door.

"Just a moment. We're not decent." I stood up and slid into my skirt. I sensed with delight Red's reaction when her eyes found the drops of moisture between my legs and with my magesense I saw a similar mess between her own legs. It was quite apparent what we wanted, why didn't we just act on it? The thought disturbed me and I pushed it aside. Uralnor was waiting. Red dressed in a simple wrap around robe and her nipples tented the thin fabric. I snickered and pointed and she glanced down at herself. She shrugged sheepishly and opened the door for our guest.

"Anjali. Bàs Marbhadair. Ready to finish up?"

I nodded and assumed my place on the bed and Uralnor sat down on the stool beside it. He inspected the wound and his hesitant manner returned. I spoke before he opened his mouth.

"Let me guess, this halter is in the way?"

He nodded silently, not meeting my eyes. I stared right into Red's face as I reached up and pulled my halter up. My breasts were still more than half empty but I had put on enough weight for it to wobble to the side with pleasant jiggle and her eyes followed it obediently. The end result was not as flattering, flopping limply over my bicep but she did not appear to care. I basked in her admiration for a moment until I felt the familiar wetness of the ink on my skin. Uralnor had quickly memorised the complex pattern and was freehanding it by now. I steeled myself for the incoming pain and gasped when the needle hit home.

"Be still."

"I can't, I have to breathe."

"Well we can't have that. You need to be still or else I won't be able to do this properly. How about you hold your breath while I work, say thirty second intervals?"

I did not like that idea but I nodded. Better get this over with. I drew a deep breath and held it. I managed to remain still as he worked but before long my lungs screamed for air. He stopped tapping the needle and I drew several deep breaths before he started again. The frequent pauses made his work much slower than the other wounds and this particular one was long and jagged like a bolt of lightning. The circumference was one of the longest and that was the reason why we had left it for last. Before he was even a quarter through it my head was spinning from lack of breath and tears poured out of the corners of my eyes from the combination of lack of air and the pain. A hand found mine and I gripped it tightly. The world shrank to pain and short, desperate breaths. I could of course had called a break but I wanted him to finish as soon as possible. The torment stopped and after several seconds I realised that he was finished and I drew a breath. The world slowly came back into view as the stars that had been all I could see for the last eternity faded. Red put her finger on the enchantment and it ignited almost immediately. She had gotten used to activate them. The wound closed and I was finally whole again. Well not whole but at least patched up. More than a dozen tattoos graced my body. I sat up and put my breast back in the halter.

"Thank you, Uralnor. You have saved my life. Whatever you need, and if it is within my power you shall have it."

"The honour is mine, Bàs Marbhadair. You owe me nothing."

He started packing up his tools and I stood from the bed. I shared a look with Red and by the look on her face I was not certain who of us was more nervous.

"Well, here goes." I raised my hand and channelled a small bit of power. There was no pain, quite the opposite. Power coursed through me in a powerful torrent. The small amount of power I had meant to channel into a simple light spell caused the spell to flare brilliantly, blinding all three of us. I cut the power off instantly and blinked to regain my vision. I tried again with the same results. Then understanding hit me. I could channel much more than I used to be able to. What had been a small trickle for me was now much greater. To my magesense my soulstream looked about the same as it had before but power seemed to flow more freely. I channelled a minuscule amount of power, a small part of what I just had channelled and the light spell glowed with a gentle white light. Gaining confidence I slowly increased the flow. Exultation surged in me and runes exploded out of my hand and stump. Magic flowed in great arcs around me, bursting into visible light at my will. Small objects around the room floated into the air and fell into orbit around me. I turned in a full circle to watch the magic with my own eyes even though I saw it all with perfect clarity with my magesense. A maniacal laugh escaped my lips and Red joined me. Her magic did not flow as easily as mine but it surged out, joining it's dance with mine. Sparks flew where the power touched. Uralnor had backed into a corner, watching us with some concern but completely devoid of fear. I channelled more and more power and the magical fallout increased. The bed rocked when my power gripped it and Red squeaked in surprise. The sound startled me and I cut off the power. The magic faded and the floating objects fell to the floor in a loud clatter. More than one fragile thing shattered against the stone floor. I stared at Red and she smiled back in jubilation. With a single step I launched myself onto the bed and wrapped my arms around her. I pulled her tight and I felt her heart beat against my chest in tandem with my own. I pulled back and stared into her eyes. Tears were trickling down her cheeks and I realised that my own cheeks were wet. She was so fucking beautiful. Then I kissed her. She melted in my arms and returned the kiss passionately. Her fingers traced a sealed wound on my back and it did not burn her. I was safe once more, safe to touch her, to kiss her. Kiss her all over. She was getting close again and the feedback loop between us brought me to the same level. Her pleasure was my pleasure, and mine was hers. We both panted once, twice, three times and then we both orgasmed again together. It was not as glorious as our complete meld had been but it was a delectable end to a wonderful time. Red collapsed over me and we clung desperately to one another as we breathed hard to regain our breath. Red spoke first.

"What was that?"

"I don't know, but I loved it."

"Yes, I loved it too. I love you."

"And I you."

She chuckled into my shoulder.

"What's so amusing?"

"I never thought I would say those words to a woman, but it feels so natural."

I squeezed her hard. "Yeah, it does, doesn't it?"

I neglected to tell her that it was the first time I had said those words to someone who was not my family. And I did count Kendall among them. I had never been in love before, not truly. Red pulled back and gazed into my eyes.

"So I guess I did well?"

"As I said, best student ever."

She giggled. "I passed the test?"

It was my turn to arch my eyebrow. "Do you think that the test is over? This was just the first part. I'm thinking that it is at least a three-parter."

"Oh, it's on!" She dove forward to kiss me and I lost myself in my lover.

It was the best night ever.

## Chapter 30

The following weeks was the best week I could ever remember since dad was killed. I was no longer in constant pain, could use magic once more and had been adopted into a new family. But that was not the best part. Red and I banged almost constantly. We simply could not get enough of one another and we explored each others bodies completely with fingers, lips and tongue. Red had quickly gained confidence in having sex with a woman and the mere sight of her almost took my breath away. I was loathe to leave the bed each morning and more than often whoever woke first awakened the other with soft kisses or caresses that more often than not escalated. This morning had been no exception and Red was still basking in the afterglow in the bed while I tried to focus on the tome I had selected from the library. She had pushed me from the bed, claiming that I was too hot and she wanted to cool down. My magesense kept returning to her supple body sprawled in a tangle of sheets and the lingering sweat on her skin. I watched her stretch languidly and a fire ignited between my legs. I flipped the tome closed with a dull thud, giving in to the temptress in the bed. I stood and turned with a smile. That was when the stars fell. A large blazing light entered the range of my magesense and before I could react fully it grazed the top of the main keep and sent the walls shaking. A shadow flickered across the window as a second blazing meteor entered my range. Red sat up sharply in the bed and stared at me.

"What the fuck?"

I was too stunned to answer, it all happened so fast. What the fuck were those things? Then a roar reached my ear through the open window. I knew that roar. It still haunted my nightmares. I was moving before I really understood what was going on. I scrambled for clothing, armour, anything.

"Dragons!"

Red's jaw dropped for a moment before she bounced out of the bed and for once I barely noticed the expanse of naked skin. Screams of terror erupted from every part of the keep. In no time we were armoured with whatever scraps we had laying around and were hurtling down the steps. I blinked against the sudden brightness of the sun and scanned the courtyard. It was a picture of organised chaos. The Clans were rallying. Dragonkin raids were not as common as those of the Outcasts but they knew what to do. I cluster of men drew my attention and I focused my magesense on them. They were hauling on pieces of fallen masonry from the roof that had been broken. Beneath the stone lay a man and the others worked to free him. It was no use, his pelvis and legs had already been crushed and he was dead. I jogged toward to them to order the men to arms. We could deal with the corpse later. I shouldered my way through them, all the while keeping tabs on the circling dragons. Their magical brilliance blinded my magesense and I could not make out their physical forms. They looked like circling stars but I could hear the beat of their wings and their occasional roars. Where they fighting each other? Or preparing to swoop down on the keep? Where were their kin, the wyverns and Drakonids? I froze when I laid eyes on the dead man. It was one of the young men I had danced with during the feast of my adoption into Clan Bizhjerai. He had had a pretty smile, I remembered.

"He's dead. Leave him for later."

I forced myself to turn my back on the poor man. I realised that I had never caught his name, and now I probably never would. The warriors reluctantly followed me and Red fell in by my side. A group of Clansmen met us and handed weapons and bandoliers of ammunition to my group. Several grabbed the heavy spears the Outcasts had used to fight the beast I had lured to the wall. I doubted that they could actually harm a dragon but these men had more experience fighting Dragonkin that I had. I had only fought the one after all. The dragons seemed content circling above us and then they collided with a meaty thwack. Hope filled me for they appeared to fight each other. Perhaps they were not here for us after all. Their circling brought them steadily farther away but as one of them swooped over me a warm rain fell on my face. A drop struck my lips and the rich taste of blood filled my mouth.

"It's bleeding!" I am not sure who had called out and for some reason the others cheered. A group of them ran to the stables. I turned to Red.

"Why are they cheering?" Red laughed with an excited look in her eyes.

"They are not attacking, they are fighting! Probably over mating rights."

"So?"

"Don't you get it? Dragons fight to the death!" She saw my confused expression and she continued. "Dragon meat is very expensive, we need to claim the loser so we can sell it in the cities. Even the bones is a precious commodity among mages."

I nodded slowly. The bones of a creature that heavily steeped in magic would make a fine substrate for magic items. Perhaps not as good a substrate as actual materialised magic but that art seemed lost out here. A group of warriors led a trio of horses toward me and I noticed that Red's father had joined us. Red swung into the saddle as her father accepted the bridle of one of the others. The warrior offered the reins of the third horse to me and I just watched them in consternation. I could not ride. Red somehow made her horse dance sideways toward me and she offered me her hand. She pulled me up behind her. I'd rather not have ridden, preferring my own two legs, but I did not want to miss out on this hunt. The dragons were rapidly vanishing in the distance as their fight brought them farther away and the hastily gathered party galloped through the gates and onto the plains. The newly tilled fields rushed past us but those who tended them had sought refuge in the keep. A herd of buffalo cowered in a close group, warily glancing to the sky. A single brave herdsman crouched nearby, arrow nocked on his bow. It was almost laughable to think that a dragon would even notice the tiny shaft but his courage was commendable. I raised my voice to be heard over the thundering of the hooves.

"Why aren't they fighting with magic?"

Red turned her head and looked at me like I was an idiot.

"Dragons can't use magic."

"But they are blazing with it?"

"Yes, they can channel it to humans who can use it for them, but on their own they are just large beasts."

That explained the Mages on the back of the dragon that had attacked the Skylands. We kept riding and several of the warriors let out loud whoops of joy at our headlong rush. The wind whistled in my ears and almost drowned out the sound of the hooves as it whipped my hair around. Red's great mane of wavy red filled my vision and filled my nose with the sweet scent of her. The speed, the sound, the smell and the motions of the beast beneath me spoke to me. It resonated within me and I lost myself in the sensations. I tightened my arms around my lover's slender waist and pressed myself along her back. The supple leather she wore bled the heat of her body into mine and the sensation of the thin blouse I wore against my breasts were delectable. I slid my fingers under the opening in her sleeveless vest and caressed her stomach. I could feel her shiver through our contact and I leaned in and kissed her neck in that spot I had found to be oh so sensitive. I don't know what came over me but I could not help myself. I slid my fingers lower, beneath the hem of her trousers and found the wetness my magesense had already told me about. Her lips parted in a gasp whose sound was stolen by the rush of the wind but I could feel the vibrations from her throat through our closely pressed bodies. With each galloping step of the horse we both lifted slightly from the back of the beast and during one such moment I slipped two fingers inside her. She was ready and waiting and she angled her hips to not crush my hand when she fell back down. Even so my fingers were pushed all the way inside with a swift thrust and Red almost lost her grip on the reins. I licked and nibbled up her neck and jaw and I caught her ear between my teeth and bit it gently, careful not to rip it off with the jolting of the horse. Again I mourned the loss of my other hand or I would have put it to work on her breasts. Instead I used the stump to cling to her waist or I might have been thrown off the horse. I was panting with the excitement of it all, almost as hard as Red was. Each step of the horse brought my own pulsing sex down on the back of the horse, hard, with a jolt of pleasure. Without stirrups and saddle it was almost impossible for me to parry and I was jostled helplessly. For once, I did not mind. Red's head rolled back to rest on my shoulder and the reins fell from her convulsing fingers but the horse followed the others without direction. It tossed its head and looked back at us when the reins slackened but when she saw us still there she turned her attention back forward. The loss of control of the animal scared me, and the fear pushed my excitement even higher. I was getting close, the feel of Red gushing around my fingers almost enough to bring me over the edge on its own and the beasts loping gait almost finished the job. I smothered Red with my entire hand and the hard nub pressed into the heel of my palm as I ground my hand across it. Red tightened around my fingers when she came and the long moan that I barely heard over the rush of wind sent me hurtling over the edge. I sank my teeth into her shoulder, right where it joined her slender neck, in my passion but she did not seem to mind. Her hand rose and grabbed the hair at the nape of my neck, pressing my face and teeth deeper. I did not draw blood, but it was close. She tightened and relaxed rhythmically around my fingers. I kept playing with her idly as she came back down and an aftershock ripped through her. We were at the back of the group and I was almost certain that our little adventure had gone unnoticed but I could not be sure. The distant roar of the dragon made her jerk and sit back up and scramble for the reins. Her shifted posture made her fall down hard on my hand and I winced in pain as my fingers bent unnaturally. She stood in the stirrups and grabbed my wrist and pulled it out of her trousers. Instead of letting me reclaim it she brought my slick fingers to her mouth. She did not lick them delicately like I had expected, instead she shoved three of them in her mouth all the way and sucked hard. Her soft tongue swirled between them, tasting herself. My eyes crossed with the sensation. Shit, I was getting turned on again. She kept licking my fingers well after they were clean, or rather not that clean but covered with a completely different bodily fluid. She let my fingers slip from her mouth and I wrapped the arm around her. I ground myself against her back, well on the way to getting off again. The roar of one of the dragons snapped me out of it and I realised that our gallop had slowed into a more sedate canter. The horses could not keep it up for long. They were breathing hard and covered in lather already. I glanced around to see if any of the warriors were watching us but everyones eyes were riveted to the battling dragons. They had started circling again and we had gained on them. I could not make out any details at this range but their motions struck me as sluggish. I had no idea how long dragon fights usually lasted but something hinted that they were closing in to the finale. The dragons slammed together and bit and clawed as they started plummeting to the ground. Before they hurtled too close to the ground they broke apart and started rising again on heavy beats of their wings. The one now to the left of us was rising much more slowly. The sun glinted red off its scales as it laboured to climb. The Chief waved his musket in a pattern above his head and our caravan turned in a wide loop on his command. The other dragon had reached a height almost twice that of its adversary and as I watched it tucked its wings to its back and it started to plummet with a roar. Even I could see that this was the end. The other dragon had only one possible escape, down. It banked its wings and started to fall to the side but the higher dragon adjusted its dive. It struck the other dragon from above, slamming it violently downward. Its neck and tail curled upward as its midsection was wrenched downward and it cried it pain. It looked as if it had broken its back but it flailed wildly with its hind legs. The top dragon bit down onto the join of long neck and shoulder and raked its claws along the back of the lower dragon. When they broke off the lower dragon kept plummeting and struck the plains before us. The other dragon beat its wings heavily and it roared in victory. It shot through the air above us in the direction the duelling pair had come from and as it passed I caught a flicker of slate gray. My stomach lurched and I was suddenly back on the Skylands, lying on my back beneath a large belly that looked exactly like the one that surged past. It was one of Savistlin's brood, but it was much smaller than she had been. The dragon threw us a baleful gaze but dismissed us with a snort. And then it was gone. How could a creature that large fly that fast? It was incredible. The warriors howled in excitement and kicked their tired mounts into a gallop. Red joined the cry and followed our kin. I clung on for dear life but I felt numb. The sight of the creature brought back bad memories and again I saw Greg melt into a crisp puddle before my eyes. The look in his eyes as he stared at me atop the dragon as he charged. The way his hair flashed into flame and his skin charred and melted. How his eyes burst and dripped down the bared bone of his cheeks. His screams of agony as his flesh dripped from his frame in the intense heat of the fireball. At that moment I felt alone, well and truly alone, even though I was surrounded by my new family and held the woman I loved in my arms. The dragon on the ground was still moving. It struggled to its feet as we approached, cradling one of its forelegs to its chest and limping awkwardly completely devoid of the deadly grace I had seen back home. It saw us and turned its head to face us and I saw that one of its eyes was a bloody mess. The other stared at us with pain-maddened light blazing from its good eye. It spread its wings and hissed at us as we spread out in a circle around it. Our horses danced, pranced and whinnied in panic at the proximity of the large predator but the dragon watched us warily, refraining to attack. It turned its head around, trying to watch all of us at the same time. Large loops of guts hung from long rents in its belly and deep gouges all over its back sent torrents of blood running down its flanks to fall in a heavy rain from its belly. One of its wings was tattered, rendering it incapable of flight. Despite its horrible wounds it was beautiful. The large red scales glinted in the sunlight and it moved with deadly intent even though we had it cornered and scared. I had no understanding of the healing capabilities of dragons but the despair in its eye told me that it was dying. The Clansmen dismounted, every fourth man gathering the reins and leading the scared horses aside. Keeping a wary eye on the dragon the men with spears stalked forward while the rest aimed their muskets. Shots rang out and bloody craters appeared on the already bloody flanks. The blood was almost invisible against the deep red of the scales and the new wounds looked insignificant among the rest of the damage. Red raised my rifle and fired. I had taught her to use the weapon since I could not use it with only one hand. She was not a good shot yet but the large target at this range... Even a child could not miss. The shot sank deep, just behind where the tattered wing joined the body and sank beneath the join. The round detonated and ripped the wing completely off. The dragon roared and lurched forward toward my friend. She stared at it in slackjawed surprise that it could move that quickly despite its wounds. I kicked her legs from under her and she fell heavily on her back just as the dragons teeth snapped shut where her torso had been. Each fang was longer than my hand and would have mangled her body beyond recognition. I found myself staring straight into the remaining eye and it burned with hate. Red fired again from her prone position and blew its chest wide open. Men surged forward, prodding with their heavy spears and the dragon retreated. It lashed out again and snapped one of the heavy shafts in its mighty jaws. The dragon roared but it had lost much of its power and it came out more like a terrified mewl. Organs slid out of the cavernous wound in its chest and a salvo of shots struck its other flank. It turned sluggishly and the men on its blind side fired again. The dragon stumbled and fell, its weight shaking the ground. The men cheered but I was sickened. This was torture, cruel even. The dragon struggled to regain its feet but it was too weak. It lay twitching pathetically. I could not take it any more. Even though one of its kind had killed my friend and countless others back home this creature was in pain. It was dying. No reason to prolong its suffering. I strode forward and the men raised their musket to avoid hitting me. Red grabbed my shoulder to pull me back but I shrugged her off. In the corner of my eye I saw Iolan still aiming his musket at the dragon along with his Huscarls. They apparently did not care if they shot me by accident. With my magesense I saw Iolan shift his sights slightly so that his weapon aimed squarely at me. I raised my shield and strengthened the side that faced him. Without letting my gaze leave the wounded dragon I watched him with my magesense. I saw his finger curl around the trigger. Do it. Do it, asshole. Give me a reason to kill you. It would solve so many problems. Just give me the easy way out. Behind me Red frowned at the unexpected direction I had strengthened my shield, alone among the Clansmen to be able to see my magic. Her eyes flicked to Iolan and her body tensed but I waved her back without looking. Her lips curled in a sly grin and she remained where she was. Sadly Iolan did not take the shot and he finally raised his musket. His Huscarls emulated him a moment later. I snorted at his cowardice. He may have been able to claim the inaccuracy of the musket made him shoot me but I would not have cared. I would have burned him to a crisp before he could raise any words in his defence. I walked up to the dragon and looked down into its eye. Its slitted pupil focused on me and my heart bled for the pain I saw there. It had given up, finally broken both inside and out. It accepted its death and watched me pleadingly. I realised that it was no mere beast. This was an intelligent creature. I drew my large revolver and thumbed the selector. The cylinder spun to an explosive round and I cocked the hammer with my thumb. I raised the muzzle to point directly into the eye. I hesitated, mourning the pain of this creature. It blinked slowly, a translucent membrane sliding down over the eye a flicker of a moment before the eyelid rose from below to cover the orb. It felt as if it was nodding at me. 'Do it,' it seemed to tell me, 'end the pain.' The eye slid open again and a large tear dripped out of the corner of the eye. I could see myself reflected in the shiny surface and the gaping maw of the muzzle of my revolver. I refused to look away. It deserved to not die alone. Behind me Red was whispering with her father and after a short, but animated, discussion the Chief approached Iolan who was watching the proceedings.

"Chief Iolan of Clan Ithlak, in honour of our alliance Clan Bizhjerai offer you the first pick of the prize."

Iolan's sullen expression turned into one of greed at the offer. He opened his mouth to accept when the Chief continued.

He must have realised that Red would not marry him, not as long as I was around, and that he would not get a better deal than this. I had a feeling that Iolan would not give up his plans so easily. The men approached the fallen beast with drawn hatchets and daggers and started carving it open further but my attention was drawn by something happening inside the beast. The corpse was ablaze with magic that left the corpse in great torrents and I drank some of it in hungrily but it was far more than I could contain. Much of the magic did not evaporate into the magic field though, instead it was drawn into the hind quarters of the dragon. The body was still mostly alive, even though the creature itself was dead and I could sense the shifting organs. Something was happening and I focused my magesense on the area. Magic surged into a concentrated point of tissue. I could tell that it was not a part of the original dragon, it was something else entirely. No, not something else. Something new. It drank the magic and shot tendrils through the corpse and devoured it from within. What it ate was a mere fraction of the flesh and organs relative to the sheer size of the massive beast but the rapidity in which it did was astonishing. Not even blood magic could force flesh to meld that quickly. I snatched the axe from Red's belt as she passed me but one look at my face stopped her question short. Touching the head of the axe with my stump I spelled the blade to easier part flesh and I struck again, this time just barely breaking the scales apart. I struck again and the flesh beneath parted much more easily than the scales but the dense muscles resisted much more than human flesh did. Iolan pranced around, pointing at pieces of organs as they were hauled out of the cavernous belly, claiming the choicest bits for his Clan. The egg pulled gently on my soul and I had fed it a continuous stream of magic all the way here. It was the same kind of aura that the Reavers and the dragons had, but not as aggressive. I gave Red the egg and I walked into the fount. It was easy now to shield myself with my increased strength and channelling abilities, almost laughably so. The magical flames curling round the edges of my shield and reacted violently with it. Taking my cue from Red I made the shield semi permeable to magic and drank of the fount. I sat down cross legged and started drawing runes around the fount with a focused jet of flame from my hand. I did not melt the runes into the stones, instead I settled with simply charring the stones themselves into the pattern. The spell was familiar to me by now after having taught it to Red recently and the power gathering spell flowed naturally from my hand. Remembering Iolan's covetous looks at the egg I wrote a shield spell around it, one that would repel physical force. I was certain that Iolan was not trained in magic, since hardly any of the Clansmen were. Maybe one of the shaman could convince the elements to break it but it would alert me long before they managed to break it down. I turned without rising and reached out my stump toward Red. I sighed and switched arms and she placed the egg in my hand. I almost dropped it since it was hard to balance the large round thing in the palm of my hand and Red snatched it back. She came closer and held it out and I took it, pressing my stump onto one side and my palm to the other. I balanced it on a spell of telekinesis where the fount would be when I removed my personal shield and I activated the inner enchantment and stepped back. The power gathering spell channelled power into the shield and the fount erupted, destroying my telekinesis. The egg fell for a moment, threatening to vanish down the hole like the ink container had but the levitating spell I had drawn out caught it as it ignited and held the egg firmly in the fount. The flames licked and caressed the scaled surface but did not burn it. The egg absorbed the power almost as fast as it surged forth. Most of the energy not caught by the gathering spell, which was most of it, vanished into the gore drenched shell. The shield manifested as a small dome around the whole thing and I kicked it to make sure it was sound. It hurt my toes but did not budge. The shield contained the overflow energy, concentrating the magic field inside. When the concentration became too strenuous to contain the shield would increase in size to reduce the pressure. It was similar to the shield that had surrounded Dun Traelak before when Grasax was still in control. Wordlessly I offered my stump to Red and she grasped it as she would my hand. I led her inside for a hot bath. The tub was already full of water when we arrived and I made a mental note to thank Anna for her foresight. She had gotten quite good at anticipating our needs after all the time she had spent serving us. With a thought my clothes came undone and I shrugged out of my blouse and stepped out of my boots and trousers. Sometimes it scared me that I did things with magic without even thinking about it these days. Back before I became this glowing monstrosity magic had always taken intent and focus but now I used it as easy as breathing. I climbed into the warm water and it started boiling around my skin. The heat dispersed swiftly enough to not scald me too badly but I welcomed the pain. Red hastened out of her own bloodspattered clothes and despite the small size of the tub she joined me. She had to press her body close to mine and fold her legs between mine to fit under the surface but I did not mind. Her presence was comforting. The death of the dragon had disturbed me more than I thought it would. I thought it would have been easy to slay their kind after our fight on the Skylands, but the look in the red dragons eye had shaken me to my core. Red clutched me close where she lay on top of me in the hot water and rested her cheek on my shoulder. She shared my misery silently, stoically, not understanding the reasons but accepting the burden as her own. I kissed the top of her head and returned the embrace. The water was cold when we finally retreated to the bed for a restless night of sleep.

## Chapter 31

My melancholy stuck with me for days, and Red sympathised with me when I tried to haltingly explain my feelings. She had my back, no matter what. Iolan had returned late that first night and he and his men had left with their haul at the break of dawn. I was glad to have him out of our hair but I had a feeling that that was not the last we had heard from him. I visited the egg several times every day and it kept drinking of the turbulent power erupting from the earth. The dome expanded slowly as it filled up faster that the egg could consume it. I shook myself out of my sadness eventually and Red rejoiced at my first tentative smile, the first one in several days. It was strange, back home I could go weeks, sometimes months without smiling but since meeting her it felt as if I seldom stopped smiling, until that encounter with the dragon. I threw myself into improving the keep and repairing it. I had learned much from studying Grasax' library and how to work stone and metal with magic. It was similar to how it was done back home but instead of feeding the spells pure magic so that it could construct the matter from energy you fed it both magic and matter through a few supplementary spells. The entire process cost much less magic than producing the matter from nothing and the slight overflow from the fount was sufficient for my current needs. I started adding plumbing to Dun Traelak and I showed an excited Red how we could just turn a knob on the newly grown stone faucet on the wall in our room to receive warm and cold water. Baths became much more common after that and I expanded the tub to make it more comfortable for the both of us. The breach in the wall was nearly repaired, the magic staffs and wands the Bizhjerai had found speeding up the repairs tremendously. I searched the library for clues to reconstruct the shield tower or destroy the dagger that contained the liche but I had to settle for a more permanent prison for him. I burned the runes into the very stone of the cellar and connected a significant portion of the fount to power them externally. I resolved to check the prison often, just in case, but the dagger no longer darkened our room with its presence. Red continued her studies and our days settled into a pleasant rhythm. The days started in highly enjoyable calisthenics followed by a common bath and then magical studies. Lunch out in the chilling air of autumn in the courtyard followed by physical exercise as we sparred. I got used to the off-balance of my body with my severed arm and adopted a shield that could be strapped to the stump. My biggest issue was coming to terms with the fact that I could no longer use a revolver in my off hand, or my rifle. I gifted the small revolver and the rifle to Red and taught her how to maintain and recharge them. Before long Red started with her own construction work on the keep, tentatively repairing the roofing that had been destroyed by the dragons. I watched her work proudly. I doubted I could have done it better myself. Weeks dragged on and I started to worry that the egg would not hatch. It had absorbed a tremendous amount of magic by now and blazed in my magesense. How could it contain that much without burning? Of course the adult dragons had held much, much more than this. Our quiet life was interrupted one day when a group of Bizhjerai warriors arrived in a rush from one of the roving bands herding the buffalo across the plains. Red and I burst into the main chamber after word reached us and we walked into chaos. The assembled Clansmen all spoke over each other and the Chief raised his hands for silence but no one paid him any heed. I tugged on the sleeve of a nearby warrior and he glanced over his shoulder at me. He did a double take when he registered who I was. He inclined his head in respect. What was his name? I racked my memory and finally dredged it up.

"What is going on, Urien?"

He grinned excitedly at me.

"They found another one!"

"Another what?"

"Skylander!"

I stared at him, dumbfounded. A creeping suspicion stole over me and I shouldered my way through the throng. The Skylander was kneeling on the floor, bound like I had been but with the manacles locking hands behind back. The shock of green had confirmed my suspicion.

"Alissa!" I surged forward and threw my arm around my friend. She was thin and haggard and her face was covered in bruises and one of her eyes was swelled shut. She leaned her head into my neck and her shoulders shook with silent sobs. I pulled back and inspected her for further wounds.

"Kyra? What happened to you?"

I glanced down at my stump. "Got into a fight. You should see the other guy. I am so glad to finally see you alive. I feared that the bear had killed you."

"No, I ran. I've never run that fast in my life and when I realised that it did not follow me anymore I was lost. I thought it killed you or I would have searched harder for you."

"Sshh, don't worry about it. You are here now, we are both safe." I hugged her again and realised that the room had gone silent. Red was glaring at me through narrowed eyes.

"What happened to you, Kyra? You are glowing."

I sighed. "I almost Archoned."

Alissa's eyes widened and she recoiled. Her rejection hurt, but I understood her reaction.

"It's fine, Alissa. My wounds are sealed. I'm not gonna blow up on you."

I turned to face the Chief.

"This is my friend, Alissa. She is the one I arrived here with, the one lost in the woods. I can vouch for her good behaviour."

A warrior stepped up alongside me angrily.

"She almost killed Traystan!"

"He attacked me first," my green haired friend piped up.

"If Bàs Marbhadair vouches for her, we can trust her. You would have defended yourself in her position, Arvald. Unleash her."

The man grumbled but obeyed his Chief and Alissa rubbed her wrists as the manacles was removed.

"Are you hungry, Alissa? I'll have food and water brought to our rooms. Come, tell me everything that happened."

I led her up to the room I shared with Red, my lover following us closely. I ordered Alissa to bathe while we waited for Anna to return with the food. Alissa stripped out of her soiled and torn clothing, the same clothes she had worn when we first set out, and I saw how dreadfully thin she were. She had been a lithe woman to begin with and had had little to spare. She sat down in the tub with a contented sigh.

"What happened to you, Alissa? Tell me everything."

"There is not much to tell. After the bear attacked us I ran. I was lost in the woods and I roamed alone. I barely survived on berries and the small furry creatures we saw so often."

"Squirrels."

"What?"

"They are called squirrels."

"Alright. I ate squirrels and small birds to survive. I saw the Pioneer pass over me but I was too far away to make it to the landing and they left me behind. I had given up hope when I reached the plains but I dared not leave the sanctuary of the forest. I knew I would die out there in the winter so I eventually ventured outside. That's when these people found me. Who are these people? I did not think anyone lived out here."

I smiled at her ignorance, remembered the short while since I had been just as ignorant.

"These are the Bizhjerai. Look, I've been adopted into the Clan." I showed her the Mark on my shoulder that was bared by the vest I wore. "The Clans roam the plains, tending their buffalo. Red, tell Alissa about your people."

Red sat with her back to the wall, ramrod straight and with narrowed eyes. Why was she so pissy? She was silent for a long while until she spat out a short summary of her people. I glared at her antagonistic tone.

"Red, a word."

I retreated to the far corner as Alissa dunked her head under the surface, taking advantage of the lull in the conversation to wash her greasy hair. Red joined me without a word and looked at me with her eyebrow defiantly arched.

"The fuck is your problem?"

"She is," she said with a pointed glance at Alissa, "I don't trust her."

"Why not? I vouched for her, don't you trust me?"

"I do, you know that. But you said yourself that you did not know her that well. You have hardly spoken of her at all and then she shows up and you rush to her side, throwing your arms around her and and and..." She trailed off, sputtering. I felt my eyes widen. So that was what this was all about. Amusement replaced my irritation in a flash.

"Are you jealous, love?"

"So what if I am?" her tone was defencive. "I don't like her!"

I stepped closer to my lover and she held her ground.

"She is just a friend," I reached up to cradle her face with my palm. Despite herself she leaned into it, rubbing her cheek across my scarred fingers. "I love you, Red. Not Alissa. You are my one and only, never doubt that. Now and forever."

Her expression softened. "I love you too. Now and forever," her tone was petulant and perhaps a little embarrassed. I slid my hand behind her head and pulled her in for a swift kiss. I flashed her a smile and rejoined Alissa. Her brown eyes travelled from me to Red and back and a slow smile spread over her face.

"You certainly did better for yourself that I did." Alissa commented and I smiled at Red.

"I certainly did. I found everything I ever wanted out here. Who would have thought that?"

Alissa laughed. "Yeah. What about your mom or your daughter?"

The old pain of missing them resurged from my belly and my face fell.

"I don't know. I hope I can bring them here. Do you think either of us will ever see the Skylands again?"

She shook her head slowly. "I don't know. I am sure that if any of the others survived their reports will bring more here. There is too much resources here to leave alone. Did you see any of the others? Why did you not rejoin the Pioneer? Was it because of her?"

"We found Raynard. And partly. It is a long story."

"You found Raynard? Did he make it back?"

I grimaced. "No."

"Dead?"

"Yeah."

"How did he die?"

I was silent for a long moment, reluctant to admit what I did even though I did not regret it. Red reached out and squeezed my hand. I drew a deep breath and let it out in a rush.

"I killed him."

Alissa's eyes widened. "What?!"

"As I said, it is a long story. I'll tell it over supper." I had already sensed Anna approaching with a basket full of steaming meat. I am sure Alissa would enjoy this as much as I. Alissa climbed out of the tub and dried herself off with magic. I made sure to avert my gaze for Reds' sake and my redhead had the decency to look sheepish when she noticed.

"That smell! Marvellous!"

"You are going to love this Alissa. Have you been cooking with magic this whole time?"

She nodded, not understanding the nuance behind my question.

"The Outsiders cook over burning wood. It flavours the meat wonderfully. I don't think I will ever get sick of it."

We ate in silence for several minutes, punctuated by Alissa's squeals of delight. Even Red was touched by her obvious enthusiasm. The poor woman must have been starving she wolfed the down so fast. When she slowed down enough to talk she pointed sternly at me.

"You, talk."

I drew a deep breath, gathered my thoughts and started speaking. It was quite the tale and it took more than an hour to tell. Alissa's eyes grew wider and wider and she clasped her hand over her mouth when I retold the story about the fight with Grasax. I fell silent at the point where I passed out and to her credit Red told the rest from her perspective.

"That was quite a story. Life is never boring for you, is it Kyra?"

"There is more."

"Seriously?"

"Yeah. We fought another dragon just a short while ago."

"A dragon?! And you survived? I guess you truly have earned the name Dragonbane."

I chuckled at that. "This one was already wounded and dying. We just finished it off."

My mood darkened at the unpleasant memories and Red saved me, telling the tale in my stead.

"And that is how we ended up with a dragon egg out in the courtyard."

"Well damn. And I thought my tale would be popular back home but this eclipses everything."

"Don't feel too bad. If not for one thing I would have preferred your experience."

Her brow furrowed in confusion. "What is that?"

I looked pointedly at Red. "Her." My lover beamed at my honest proclamation.

"Meeting her has made it all worth it. Even this." I raised my stump for emphasis. The conversation died down after that and I could see Alissa swaying in her seat. Her eyes threatened to close.

"You should get some rest, Alissa. We can talk more tomorrow. I'll have Anna lead you to a room, there is space enough here. I am so happy that you are alright."

"Me too. That you are I mean. I am so happy for you two. You deserve to be happy, Kyra."

She left with Anna and Red hugged me from behind where I still sat on the chair.

"I am glad that your friend is still alive. Forgive me for my attitude tonight."

I caressed the arm across my chest.

"There is nothing to forgive, love. It is actually quite flattering that you get jealous. It is adorable. Just don't let it go out of hand. Remember that I won't look twice at another woman as long as I have you."

"What about men?" I could tell that she was teasing me. Two could play at that game.

"Good question. They do have a certain anatomical part that you lack."

"What?! My mouth is not good enough for you?"

"I don't know, is it? It was quite some time since I felt it's touch." That was a lie, just this morning she had reduced me to a quivering mess right on that bed over there.

She growled into my ear and licked the lobe.

"Better jolt your memory then!" She pushed me off the chair and I threw myself onto the bed, full of anticipation. As usual, she did not disappoint.

## Chapter 32

It was a week later, a week were Alissa roamed Dun Traelak and making friends among the Bizhjerai. Her easygoing nature and willingness to work hard along their sides soon caused them to lower their guard and include her in the work on the keep and fields and she was more than happy to help out wherever she was needed. Her skillful application of magic where it was needed proved effective at increasing productivity. Her constructions were small but applied at key positions. She spent much of her time maintaining the spells since the overflow from the egg did not leave much to bind to her constructs. I was awakened in the dark of night, not knowing what had prodded me from my rest. I cuddled down in the sheets once more and pulled Red into my arms. She roused sleepily and happily accepted my embrace, moulding her body along mine. Her breasts pressed into my ribs comfortably and her soft hair caressed my shoulder and side. I inhaled her scent and started drifting off once more when a motion in my magesense caught my attention. My focus narrowed like a diving falcon on the motion. It was the egg. It was not moving, but something inside did. I sprang from the bed as if fired from a cannon and Red nearly tumbled from the bed as she was flung from my side. She protested loudly from the tangle of sheets but I was already out the door. I had not bothered to dress at all and sprinted naked down the halls of Dun Traelak. Was the egg hatching? I burst onto the courtyard, guided through the dark by my magesense. I stopped by the fount, faintly aware of Red following me down the keep at a more sedate pace. At least she had had the presence of mind to garb herself against the chill night air. Winter hung heavy in the air and the grass was turning yellow in the fields. The first meagre harvest of the newly tilled fields had been just a few days ago, the seeds sown too late in the season to grow fully but the grain supplied had been substantial nevertheless. The Bizhjerai would not go hungry this winter. I raised my shield and ploughed into the fount, severing the power feedback loop with a flick of my wrist. I cared not a whit about the events of Wild Magic that struck my shield, completely disregarding the random events. I snatched the egg from the fount with my power and cradled it to my chest. I bore it to safety before I sat down on the stones, egg in my lap. It was quivering violently as the little dragon inside moved. It bucked sharply to the side as it struck the inside of its prison. Should I help it? Should I crack the egg on the stones to release it? I calmed myself with an effort of will. The dragon would be able to break out on its own, releasing it early might injure it. Red approached and wrapped a robe around my shoulders.

"Kyra, whats going on?"

"It's hatching!"

She sat down next to me and placed her palm on the warm egg. She felt the motion inside and her face was painted with an expression of awe. We watched the egg for tens of minutes, entranced by the motions inside. The magic radiating from it blinded our magesense from peering inside but we could feel the motions through the shell. It cracked with an audible crunch and the struggles within intensified. Another powerful strike from inside and a piece of the shell folded outward, held in place by a thin membrane on the inside. A tiny reptilian snout poked out, crowned by a protruding tooth. The snout vanished inside and was replaced by a torrent of amniotic fluid that slimed down my leg. I could not wait any longer. I stuck my finger inside and tiny needlesharp teeth closed around my finger. I cursed in surprised pain and pulled my finger free but the little creature held fast. The head followed my finger as I pulled hard and the egg opened wider. It let go of my finger and I heard it draw its first breath of life. The tiny sucking sound was the most beautiful thing I had ever heard, apart from Red's voice crying out in orgasm. Tiny paws reached out by its long sinuous neck and scratched at the egg. Red stabbed out with her knife and my stomach clenched in surprised panic. The fuck is she doing? Why would she kill this tiny innocent life? I started pushing the egg away from my traitorous lover but the edge of the knife lodged in one of the cracks. With a twist of her wrist she opened the egg further and more of the warm slime trickled out. The dragon baby gained traction from the weakened shell and broke it open. It struggled out of the confines of its birth and slithered wetly into my lap. I discarded the egg and embraced the tiny thing. To be honest, it was not that tiny. Its body was about the length of my arm, not counting the tail and head. I marvelled at how it could have fit in the egg, it must have been tight by the end. It raised its head to eye level but its eyes were still closed. It smelled my face, drawing air into its slitted nose. Then a forked tongue darted out and licked my face. It stood on my legs with its hind legs, its forelegs on my chest and wings hanging limply down its back as it smelled me once more. Then it opened its eyes and looked into mine. At the same time magic surged out of it, scanning its surroundings and something clicked close within me. A presence in the back of my mind nestled comfortably. He reached his head forward, for he was a he I suddenly knew, and bumped my nose with his own and something snapped within me. Tears came unbidden to my eyes and ran freely down my cheeks. He tilted his head and licked one of my tears from my face and nuzzled my jaw. It jumped from my arms, his slick body slipping from my arms and he leaped onto Red. He gave my bewildered lover the same treatment but she did not seem as affected as I was. He leaped to the ground and started happily munching on the remains of his egg and lapping at the amniotic fluid on the stones. Without taking my eyes from his magnificence I spoke.

"Do you feel that?"

"Feel what?" she asked me in a reverent whisper.

"His presence. He sits in the back of my mind. He is so happy to be eating."

How I knew it I did not know. I just knew.

"No. I feel nothing of the sort. What happened?"

"I think I'm bound to him. Perhaps because he saw me first, or because I claimed his egg. I don't know. But I do know that I am his mother now." I looked at my friend and lover. "We have a son."

Red opened and closed her mouth several times before she spoke. "How do you know it is a boy? I see nothing between its legs."

"I don't know how. I just know."

In no time the little beast had devoured its shell and I could sense his fatigue. It had been taxing escaping the shell and now with his belly full he wanted nothing but sleep. He crawled into my lap and tucked his snout beneath his tail and fell promptly asleep, safe in his mothers arms. Red grabbed me by the shoulders, her face plain with worry.

"We better get you two back inside," her voice was soft but firm. I did not protest as she led me back to our chamber. The dragon did not rouse as we walked, not even when Red turned the faucet of the tub. I was soiled with the fluids from the egg, and so was the dragon. What should we call him?

"Kyra? Are you alright?"

I looked up dreamily at Red. "Yes, more than alright. Isn't he magnificent?"

She looked at the dragon and a small smile tugged at her lips but worry won out over her wonder. Despite the weeks of incubation she had obviously not thought this far ahead. Or maybe she had not expected the strength of my reaction. To be honest, neither had I. But then again, none of us had had children before. The emotions coursing through me were akin the those I'd had when I adopted Marissa, albeit more sudden. I could not wait to show my son to her.

"Yes, he is. Now get in the tub, I refuse to share a bed with you otherwise."

That roused me into action. The dragon woke up and protested when I set him on floor and shrugged out of the still open robe. He watched with interest when I climbed into the tub and he rose on his hind legs to peer at the warm water. He just barely reached the surface with his snout and his tongue flicked out. He let out a gleeful little roar and extended his wings and with a leap and a flap he splashed into the water with me. He sank to the bottom like a stone and I groped to save him with panic in my heart. I needn't have bothered for he surface on his own, standing on the bottom on his hind legs as he used his wings to remain floating. His eyes grew heavy from the heat as he basked in the warmth. Red giggled at his obvious expression of contentment and before I knew it my lover joined us in the warm water. Her face was slathered with amniotic fluid from where he had licked her face and she cleaned off before the water became too soiled. The dragon turned to her and drifted close to Red and rested his head on her shoulder, nestling his long neck between her full breasts. His claws alighted on the tender flesh and dug in but she did not seem to mind. She stroked his back as a radiant smile spread across her face. She looked at me with shining eyes.

"I can feel it now! It is not like you described, but he is definitely in here!" She tapped her temple with a slender finger. "He is beautiful."

She looked down at the winged lizard with wonder and I basked in the sight.

"Our son." I did not realise that I had spoken the words aloud until Red returned my gaze.

"Our son," she agreed and I had never been happier. The dragon fell asleep there, head nuzzling Red and his tail curled around my ankle and we watched him for hours, neither of us tiring of the sight. Eventually the water grew cold and a great yawn made Red's jaw crack. We exited the tub and helped our son out onto the floor. He wobbled sleepily for a moment before he dashed into the corner, smelling, searching like a dog. Perhaps there was a rat in the wall he had caught the sent of. Magic bloomed out of me and Red when we dried ourselves off and the little dragon spun around, peering at us with interest. A small surge of magic flowed into me and judging by Red's widening eyes she felt it to.

"Is he feeding us magic?"

"I think so." She turned to the dragon. "No need for that little one, we have enough to spare."

The trickle of magic lessened but did not stop as he peered at us suspiciously as if we did not know better. Red yawned again and climbed into bed and I joined her promptly. The dragon leaped onto the bed and curled up at our feet. I did not have the heart to push him off and before I knew it I drifted into a peaceful sleep next to the woman I loved and our newly hatched boy.

"What should we call him?"

Red looked at me, and then she turned to consider the dragon who was toying with a knot of leather, chewing it with his sharp little teeth. He was only a few days old and had become the favourite inhabitant of Dun Traelak. In the memory of the Clan no dragon had been hatched outside of of their own roosts and having a dragon ally would bolster the power the Clan Bizhjerai even further than the heights Dun Traelak had already accomplished.

"Malkareth." Red's voice carried a tone of proclamation and the little dragon released his toy and looked up at her.

"He seems to like it. Where did you get the name?"

Red chuckled. "Sometimes I forget that you know nothing of this world. Malkareth was one of the first dragons, or at least one of oldest in memory. He was the patriarch of the Red Flight. This Malkareth must be a direct descendant from him."

"What happened to the original Malkareth?"

"He was slain by the Gray Queen Arborous, Savistlins' mother."

"She still alive?"

Red nodded. "Yeah. She must be centuries old by now. Possibly thousands."

That surprised me. The tomes of history in Grasax' library, our library now, that told of the time before the Apocalypse made no mention of dragons and that was only centuries ago. I supposed that they may well have existed back then but the books did not describe something that was taken for granted. According to the annals of the Skylands it was formed during the Apocalypse six hundred years ago. Malkareth ran toward me and leaped easily onto my lap. I reached out my fingers to scratch the scales on his head but he dodged my hand and snatched a piece of meat from my breakfast plate and retreated with his prize. He watched us warily as he hastened to devour the morsel, fearful that I would reclaim the food from him. I laughed and let him have it. He had done little but eat and sleep since he hatched and every spare moment he had spent exploring our chambers. I had never seen anything as exhausted as he had been after the few times we had let him leave the room. He got excited by everything, licking and sniffing everyone. He did not appear to fear anything and curious about everything. He had nuzzled up to random Clansmen and had become a favourite among the women. They found him adorable and kept sneaking him bits of food to eat that he was more than happy to devour. He had already grown noticeably. Nothing had excited him more than the first time he laid eyes on the fount. He had charged into the dangerous magic before I could stop him and stuck his head into the hole in the ground. My fear had swiftly abated when the magic flowed into him without harming him and he had taken a long nap in the warmth of magic. In fact, that was when he had started growing come to think of it. He appeared to feed as much off magic as he did off meat. To test my theory I let raw power flow from my skin and my sealed wounds flared. Malkareth roused immediately, staring at me for a moment before he came hurtling back toward me with the scrap of meat dangling from the corner of his lipless maw. He leaped into my lap once more and basked in the power.

"Malkareth." Red spoke the word and the little dragon looked at her, the entirety of his attention focused on her.

"Malkareth it is," I agreed. It felt good to give him a name. I stroked his back and his wings quivered with pleasure and his tail whipped lazily through the air. Red stood up and closed the window we had opened to air the room out. Winter was swiftly approaching and the room chilled quickly. The Clan had started to trickle to the keep for the winter but there was still room to spare. Some of them had opted to not live in the castle proper, instead erecting their winter dwellings outside the walls. If someone invaded they would be able to retreat behind the walls in short order but come winter this place would be packed. I did not mind, I rather looked forward to meeting the rest of my adopted family. We finished our breakfast and prepared to get to work. Red had her magical studies and I wanted to get started with the shield tower, but first I needed to head down to the cellar to inspect Grasax' prison. With the influx of people the potential damage the liche could cause if he broke free increased and I wanted to make doubly certain that he was contained. Malkareth leaped onto my leg and used his claws to climb my clothes to find a perch on my shoulders. He had gained weight since his hatching but I could still carry him comfortably. I laughed.

"Looks like little Mal will be hanging out with me today." The dragon let out a small roar of assent. "Are you sure you don't want to hang out up here with Mama Red, little guy?"

He looked from me to Red and then back again before rustling his head in what I took for a no. His understanding of proceedings amazed me. Red kissed me and then pecked Mal on his muzzle and he responded with a lick across her lips.

"Have fun, little man."

I left Red in our room and descended the stairs to the cellar. The runes around the door looked fine but I deactivated them and entered the room beyond. The dagger lay on a plain stone table carved with runes. It contained no magic that I could sense but even so I tried to drain it. I had left an opening in the spells containing him for just this purpose. It could only be opened from the outside but it was still a weakness in the protection but I had deemed it better than to be forced to dispel the whole arrangement each time I wanted to drain the magic from the dagger. Malkareth snarled at the dagger and would not let his eyes stray from it but despite his show of defiance I could feel him trembling as he cowered against my neck.

"It's okay, baby, the evil dead man can't hurt you. He is contained in the spells." Mal hissed again but relaxed slightly. We left the room behind, activating the runes on the door on our way out and I took an unplanned detour to the kitchen. A roast was cooking slowly on a spit above the fire in one of the ovens, slowly cooking for supper. Malkareth leaped from my shoulders to alight on the floor where he crouched low like a stalking mountain cat Red had told me about. Wings tucked close to his body and head held low he advanced on the roast. The women working the kitchens watched him with amusement as he hunted his prey. I swiped a piece of cheese when no one was looking and nibbled on it, not that I was that hungry but I still had not tired of the tastes of the Outside. With a growl Malkareth pounced on his prey and a flick of his wings brought him in range of the roast. He clung to it with claws and teeth and ripped a mouthful from the roast. The women laughed at him even as they kept kneading the dough they were working on. His tail swung low and brushed the flames and he yelped in surprised pain. He shot from the oven and raced toward me, mewling pathetically. I knelt down and stroked his head as he rubbed against me, complaining sadly.

"That's what you get you greedy little bastard," I told him fondly. He did not appear damaged, only slightly singed and he quite obviously overplayed his pain to garner affection. I was more than ready to fuss over him and made little cooing sounds of comfort. He went still and his eyes went wide, slitted pupils dilating as he saw something behind me. My magesense told me that it was this mornings hunters that returned with their quarry. They had felled a deer and brought it back for butchering. Entrails looped out of the gutted animal the two men carried between them, the remnants of their field dressing. Malkareth rushed toward them and leaped to snag the dripping meat. It snapped and he gulped it down, leaping to take another bite. The hunters' eyes gleamed with amusement at his antics when they put the carcass on a table and produced their tools to quarter it. Malkareth whined when the cadaver vanished from his sight and he tried to climb the table but the carved stone offered no purchase for his claws. He settled down on his hind legs, tail curled neatly around his paws as he looked up at the hunters with pleading eyes. One of the hunters, a young man named Ravil, took pity on my son and cut off a piece of hind leg for him, skin and fur still attached. He held it between two fingers and showed it to Malkareth and the little dragon stared intently at it. Ravil dropped the piece and Malkareth snatched it from the air. It vanished down his gullet faster than I could blink and he was back to pleading as if he had never been gifted the morsel. I enjoyed watching him torment the hunters with his adorableness but I had work to do.

"You guys okay watching him for a bit?"

"Of course, Bàs Marbhadair. We adore the little fellow, he is safe in our hands."

"We named him Malkareth this morning," I told them with a smile I could not suppress. Nor did I want to. Ravil knelt on the floor and scratched Malkareth below his chin. The dragon enjoyed the scratching for a moment before he became more interested in licking the blood off the young mans fingers.

"A powerful name for a powerful little dragon." His voice was at odds with his words, using the odd voice I had heard women use when they spoke to puppies or their very young children. I turned reluctantly to leave and added over my shoulder, "Don't feed him so much that he gets sick. He has no idea when to stop eating." I remembered all too clearly the mess he had made when he overate last. The soup of acid and partly digested meat had smelled awfully and Red had had to stop him lapping it all up and making himself sick again. I'd rather avoid that in the future. I left him in the kitchen staffs' capable hands and moved over to the fount. It was time to start containing the power it spewed forth instead of letting it disperse into the general magic field. I raised the usually shield around myself and got to work drawing out the two spells required. The spells was familiar to me and I even made some improvisations that I hoped would increase their efficiency. Before I could finish the pitter patter of claws on stone drew the attention of my magesense and I smiled at the little dragons headlong rush across the courtyard. It annoyed me that he was alone, the hunters were supposed to look after him. Even as I finished the inner spell I scanned the keep and saw the two hunters sprinting down the corridors, searching in vain for Malkareth. Their panicked faces quelled my annoyance. The little pest must have slipped away when they relaxed but a moment. Malkareth had proved to be a little trickster, hiding objects and disrupting work with his need for constant attention. He lay down nearby and watched me work with keen interest, somehow sensing that he ought not to disturb me. I finished the spells and activated them and the expanding magic containing shield activated when the power gathering spell fed it power. The runes rose into their now familiar dome. Malkareth watched them rise with fascination and cautiously approached to sniff them. His tongue darted out to taste the closest rune and a jolt of power licked out and stung him. It did not appear to harm him but he stared at it with a perplexed expression. How I could tell that it was perlexion written on his reptilian face was beyond me. Perhaps his emotions filtered into mine through the connection in the back of my head. I stood up and he climbed up my body to resume his perch on my shoulders.

"C'mon little guy, we have plumbing to create." He cawed in assent and I brought my son along to work.

## Chapter 33

Winter came uneventfully, apart from that Malkareth grew rapidly and was soon too big to ride my shoulders. He was of a size with the large dogs the hunters used to flush out prey, easily weighing in on a hundred and thirty pounds, if not more since his musculature seemed to be denser than the hounds. How he would ever be able to fly was beyond me with that weight and if I had not seen dragons many times his weight fly I would never have believed it possible. His wingspan was more than twice the length of his body and he had to keep them folded whenever inside. It was getting difficult to keep him fed and the meat supplies was dwindling swifter than we had anticipated. At this rate we would have to start slaughtering the lethargic buffalo huddling outside in the cold waiting for spring. No one complained though for the entire Clan was proud to count a dragon among its members. The plumbing Red, Alissa and I installed in the keep was highly appreciated, allowing everyone within the confines of the keep to stay clean and healthy during the winter months. Especially the toilets, which had been a foreign concept to the Bizhjerai before my arrival, was regarded warmly since it saved both time and discomfort and spared them the treks out into the cold to the old latrines. I resumed my study of liches, searching for a way to finally destroy Grasax and eliminate the looming threat his dagger posed. I was tucked into our bed beneath warm blankets with my nose in a tome on the day Malkareth turned three months old. We had celebrated with roasted haunch of venison for breakfast and even treated him to a sweet pastry. He had not been overly fond of it, preferring the meat. In the end Red had taken pity on the sweet cake and eaten it with relish. It was gone down her gullet before I could even snatch a taste. She did have the decency to look sheepish at that. My love did have a sweet tooth. She was outside, sparring with the warriors to burn off some excess energy despite my efforts to wear her out this morning. I had woken her up with my tongue on her most sensitive place and she had been enthusiastic to say the least.

"Mother, where is Other Mother?"

I yelped in surprise and nearly tumbled from the bed. Malkareth stood beside the bed, watching me seriously. The words had not been spoken, instead they seemed to pour into my mind. I stared at him in surprise and awe. His first words had been extremely eloquent. I had not expected him to even be able to speak, much less make so much sense straight away. He watched my shocked expression with concern.

"Mother, are you alright? What is wrong?"

I pulled my stump from my mouth and swallowed. "Nothing, everything is fine, dear. I was just surprised. When did you learn to speak?"

"I don't understand, I have always spoken to you."

"Not like this. Not with words."

He tilted his head to his side, pondering my words.

"I think I understand. You can hear me more clearly now?"

"Yes, I can. And it makes me so happy to finally hear your voice."

"I am pleased. Where is Other Mother?"

"Uhm. She is out in the courtyard, sparring with the warriors."

"What is 'sparring'?"

"That is when you practice fighting."

"Why must she practice? Are we expecting trouble? I will rip them apart myself!"

The sudden anger in his voice took me by surprise.

"No. No, Malkareth, we are not expecting trouble, currently. Your mother's are warriors by trade and we need to keep our skills honed. If we don't use them regularly we may get hurt if trouble comes."

"I understand, Mother." He peered at me for a moment before continuing. "I have never seen you 'spar'."

I looked away, feeling guilty that I had neglected my skills for so long. "I know. I have been spending time in these books instead. I really should go outside and join them, shouldn't I?"

"I don't know. Should I? If you fight, I will as well."

"I don't know how dragons fight. Do you want to learn?"

"Yes. I want to be able to protect you."

The thought of him fighting to protect us brought me nearly to tears. I did not want him to lead the life I had. I wanted him to be free and happy, living the careless life of the hunt and eventually a mate of his own. Eventually I would have to introduce him to his own flight for that to be possible and the thought cut my heart like a knife. I would lose him then.

"Why do you cry, Mother?"

I wiped the tears away with my stump. "Nothing you need to concern yourself with sweetling, you will understand when you are older."

Oh how I had hated when my mother told me that when I was a child, and here I was using the same tactics with my own baby. Malkareth did not appear to mind, he accepted my word for what it was.

"Do you want to go watch Red train?"

He nodded his sharp face, the human gesture looked odd on his reptilian body.

"Let's go, I'll join you." I discarded the tome I had been reading, despite the relevant chapter I had found and I led my son down the stairs in search of his other mother as he called her. We emerged onto the courtyard that was more than half covered by the slowly expanding shield. We crossed it, the only change we felt was the suddenly much denser magic field. Malkareth preened and drank deeply of the magic. There seemed to be no limit to his capacity of storing magic and his power dwarfed even mine by now. Oddly enough his veins or eyes did not glow like mine did. Must have been something to do with his dragon physiology being more adept at storing the power. We found Red amidst the group of warriors, sparring with a taller blond woman with a scar down her cheek. She was one of the newly arrived Clansmen from one of the more remote bands and I had never spoken to her. She was very skilled with the spear she brandished with two hands and she used it to trip Red as she pressed her attack. Red fell on her ass and raised her shield to cover herself as she scrambled backwards to buy herself space to regain her footing. Before the blond woman could lash out at her disadvantaged opponent a flash of red dashed past me with a roar. He snarled at the blond woman who fell back in panic at the sight of the enraged dragon.

"Mal, no!"

"Mother! Are you alright?"

The fighting stopped immediately, some of the warriors relaxing and leaning on their spears while some of the newcomers hesitantly lowered their spears in defence of their female companion. Not all of Clan Bizhjerai had gotten used to what they still considered a dangerous beast. Red had dropped her shield and stared at Malkareth with slack jawed surprise. She saw me and surged to her feet.

"He spoke to me, Kyra! With words! He spoke!"
