I beamed at my lover. "I know, Red. He spoke to me upstairs just minutes ago. Our baby has said his first words!"

She laughed in disbelief. Neither of us had expected this.

"Mother?"

Malkareth was still snarling at the blond woman but he had calmed down significantly at our lack of outrage. Red answered him.

"Yes, Malkareth. I am fine. We were just practising, I was never in any danger. Apologise to Maria."

The dragon stalked closer to Maria, sniffing her chest before his tongue dipped into the cleft between her breasts exposed by the leather vest she wore. I stifled a giggle. We had not taught him any human propriety, not expecting him to be able to comprehend it. We had known he was intelligent, but not to this extent. Maria's pale face reddened in indignation but she dared not move.

"Apologies, Maria. I thought you meant harm to Mother."

I noted that he did not call Red his 'Other Mother' while in her presence. He must have done that to avoid confusing me. It warmed my heart that he considered us both his mothers given that he was not bound to Red in the same way he was to me. She only felt him when he wanted her to while he was ever present in the back of my mind. Red approached me, tears of pride streaming down her tears. She was so beautiful that I could not help myself. I gathered her into my arms and kissed her, long and hard. She was panting when I pulled back for a breath. To be honest, I was panting a fair bit myself. Red knelt down when our boy lurched toward us and she wrapped her arms round his neck and he looped his head around her neck. It was long enough to just reach around and he rubbed the top of his head against her cheek.

"I am so proud of you, son. Each day you surprise us. When will we know the full extent of what, and who, you are?"

"I don't know, Mother. Even I don't know the full extent of it yet."

His self awareness impressed me, but I had a more pressing need on my mind. Or rather, in my loins. The kiss had started a fire within me that could only be quenched in one way and my magesense told me that Red was in a similar predicament.

"Will you be alright out here with the warriors for a bit, Malkareth? Your mothers need to celebrate in an, uh, 'grown up' manner."

His reptilian eyes twinkled with amusement. "Yes, Mothers. I will watch this 'sparring'. The concept intrigues me."

I grabbed Red by the hand and started to pull her toward the gate of the keep.

"You are going to mate, aren't you?"

I froze in surprise. Red and I had been careful to enjoy each other only when he was either asleep or elsewhere occupied. He was still too young to be introduced to that particular wonder of adulthood. Yet again I had underestimated him. Red started to answer in a dismissing manner but I decided that honesty was better. Our child was too perceptive to be fooled by a half-assed lie. "Yes, Malkareth. We are. In a while your mother will not be able to walk properly."

His eyes narrowed with merriment and his tongue lolled out the side of his mouth in a gesture that I had learned was his way of laughing.

"Which of my mothers are you referring to?"

Red and I answered in unison, "Both!" We broke out in girlish giggles at that and I could not wait a moment later. I could already taste her wetness on my tongue and I could not bare to be devoid the sweet nectar a moment longer. I grabbed her hand and pulled her along.

Much later the ecstasy of my latest orgasm slowly faded in ripples and Red smiled up at me from between my legs. She climbed up my body and gave me a messy kiss as she traced her fingers along the long wound under my breast. I moaned into her wet mouth from the pleasure. All of my magical wounds had turned out to be major erogenous zones for me, something that Red took great amusement in abusing, not only restricted to our bedroom activities. Sometimes she would stroke the small wound on the back of my hand as I was reading, or speaking to a Clansman. It was quite embarrassing to be reduced to a mewling mess from a single touch in front of other people but so far I had been able to maintain my composure. Red plopped down beside me, breathing hard. I reached down between her legs to return the favour but she recoiled from my touch.

"No more, please. It is sooo sensitive."

I could not imagine any higher praise. I felt the same, a pleasant ache radiating from my nethers and my body was completely satisfied. So far it had been a good day. I rose from the bed to fetch us some water. There had been a fair bit of sweating involved, not to mention all the other fluids that had been expelled from our bodies. I stumbled as I stood up and had to brace myself against the wall. Red giggled.

"I guess that means we fulfilled our promise to Malkareth."

I answered her comment with a smile as I walked bow-legged to the table and the waiting pitcher of water.

"Yeah. I can't believe that he is talking. Or how intelligent he is."

I poured two mugs of water and cursed my lack of hand that prevented me from carrying both back to bed. The second mug rose on its own and floated toward the bed. Red had become quite proficient with telekinesis lately.

"I know, right? I am so proud of him."

"You and me both, love."

I passed the window on the way back to bed and I looked to out watch the training warriors for a moment. They had advanced to mounted practice and the row of horses advanced in intricate patterns across the courtyard before they broke into a charge. Spears sank into straw filled targets. Some of the horses seemed spooked and danced to the side, making their riders miss their marks. Malkareth was among them, mimicking their movements as if he was a charger himself. I chuckled at his playful antics and returned to the bed and pulled Red into the crook of my severed arm. I took a long pull of water before I nestled down into the soiled bed. A nap would be nice.

## Chapter 34

Spring was breaking the cold grip of winter and Malkareth had grown to rival the size of the stallions bred for war. He could not longer fit comfortably in the halls of the keep so he had moved, to my great despair, into the stables where he had made a comfortable nest for himself. The horses had grown used to him, even though he eyed them hungrily from time to time. He appeared to like horses almost as much as he did humans and I had no fear that he would harm any of them. It pained me to not have him in our chambers any more but it did have the upside of letting me and Red enjoy each other more frequently. He watched the sparring of the warriors each day and seemed resolved to learn to fight with us when trouble inevitably came knocking on our door. He had taken his first tentative wing beats just yesterday, making a short glide across the courtyard. He had not stopped talking about it for hours with youthful exuberance, but his first flight filled me with both motherly pride and fear. When he learned to fly properly I feared I would lose him. That he would fly away and not return. Red tried to assure me that that would not happen, he would not leave his mothers behind but I could not shake the feeling. I found myself wanting to make excuses to him why he should not try to learn to fly but I knew that was selfish. He was a dragon, a king of the skies. He belonged up there. I was trying to study the tome about liches once more, determined to finish the fight with Grasax I had started more than half a year ago but my gaze kept being drawn out the window where the warriors sparred. My son lay perched near the fount, drinking of its power as the horses careened around the courtyard. The shield tower was slowly growing from the immense spell I had drawn with the aid of Alissa, Red and the few Bizhjerai we had started teaching magic. They were still novices but when given templates for a spell they could copy them easily enough. Marie was one of them and she showed a great deal of promise even though she still showed a clear preference for physical combat over magical. She would come around and probably become a hybrid warrior like myself. I had started sparring again at Mal's insistence. He was worried that I would be damaged if it came to a fight. I had not yet told him of my sordid past and he still held me in childlike awe. I feared that once he learned of the things I had done he would despise me. The thought of a child dying beneath the heel of my boot resurfaced and the old familiar pain made my breath hitch. I blinked the tears away and wiped them from my cheeks before Red could notice. I knew she would rush to comfort me and that would break me. I could cry later, deep in the night when she slept. I did not want to worry her. I glanced at my beautiful lover but she was engrossed in a tome of magic and had not noticed my brief outburst. I looked out the window again and Malkareth was gone, vanished. Fear bubbled up and chased away my old guilt over the dead girl. Where was he? Had he flown away? Had someone taken him? I knew the thought that someone would be able abduct the large dragon from within the security of the keep without a sound was ludicrous but my maternal instincts chased all logic from my mind. I raced closer to the windows and searched the courtyard with growing panic. The row of riders charged their targets and I found my son. He was in the row, charging along with the horses. On his back sat a rider, blond hair streaming in the wind from their passage. Marie. She had come a long way since her first less than pleasant encounter with my son. She had feared the dragon for weeks after that but had eventually overcome the fear when she realised how civilised he was. It hurt me that he let another person ride him, not even Red or I had ridden him before but the sting of pain was washed away from the excited joy that streamed into the back of my head. He charged in unison with the horses that treated him like one of their own kind, albeit scaled and winged. Marie's spear struck her target perfectly and Malkareth spun around more gracefully than his equine friends.

"Red, come and watch this."

"What is it?" She spoke even as she approached the window.

"Marie is riding Malkareth."

"Sounds kinky."

I stared at her, aghast. "That is our son you are talking about!"

"I know. Sorry." I could tell that she wasn't, she just apologised to mollify me. I chose to let it slide. She watched Malkareth careen around the courtyard with Marie astride his back and Red laughed with delight. She did not seem even slightly hurt that he let another person ride him before any of us was allowed that privilege. Not that we had asked him though. The very thought struck me as strange. He was our son, not a mount.

"I think I am going to sleep in the stables with him tonight."

Red gave me a weary glare.

"Kyra. We have talked about this."

We had. Numerous times.

"I know, but he needs his mother from time to time."

"What he needs is space to figure out who he really is. He can't do that if you loom over his shoulders all the time."

The thought of me looming over the massive dragon was preposterous, but I knew she did not mean it literally. Malkareth still cowered before our fury when he misbehaved but we could never stay mad at him for long. He was our baby.

"So you keep saying, but I am his mother!" Even to my own ears the argument made no sense.

"I am his mother too. And I say leave him be."

Reluctantly I responded, "Yes, dear." She heard the sullen tone of my voice and let out a resigned sigh.

"If you stay here for the night I will make it worth your while," she followed her words by suggestively licking her red lips. Even though she was bribing me with sex to leave our son alone I could sense her crotch moistening at the thought. Motherhood had not quenched either of our libidos, something I was immensely grateful for. He had matured incredibly quickly, already being the mental equivalent of a very intelligent teenager. I feared that meant that the time when we lost him and he set out on his own was swiftly approaching and it broke my heart. Tears sprang unbidden to my eyes and I turned my face back to the window to hide them from Red. It was a futile gesture, her magesense was almost as acute as my own at this short range. She stepped in behind the chair I sat on and embraced me from behind. She pressed her soft lips onto the top of my head as the tears trickled down my face.

"I know what you are thinking, my love, and stop that right now. He won't leave us for a long while, and even then it will not be forever. He loves us. He will not leave us behind."

"You can't know that."

"I can," her voice completely full of certainty, "he is my son too, remember?"

I nodded, not trusting my voice.

"Come, eat with me. Then we will go see him, will that make you feel better?"

Her previous anger was replaced with concern. We had started fighting after Malkareth started growing, but we never stayed mad long and we were closer for it. We both knew that our anger stemmed from anxiety over our odd family situation. The whole Clan loved our dragon but none more than me or Red. I still remembered his first breath as if it was just moments ago and the wave of love that had swept over me. Red dragged me to the table where Anna had set up our lunch just minutes ago. She still brought food to feed Malkareth even though he had been to big to enter the keep for almost a month. Not that the meagre portion she brought him would fill him any longer. He could devour half a buffalo on his own now, though he no longer ate constantly. He ate only every other day, spending the rest of the time sleeping or training with the warriors or watching me or the other Mages in training work their magic. Despite my inner turmoil I ate with my usual gusto, moaning in pleasure at the tastes I had by now tasted a hundred times or more. Red ate sparingly, having had breakfast just recently but I was always up for eating. I crammed my craw with everything Anna brought us, too much. I waddled over to the bed and lay down, suddenly sleepy. Red joined me on the bed, idly caressing my distended belly. I was hoping her caress would turn into something more, but was unsure if I would be able to act on it without puking up my large meal. She patted my belly fondly.

"Why do you always do this? I know you feel ill after eating that much."

I did, but it was worth it.

"It is just so good. I can't help myself."

"You still haven't gotten used to our cooking?"

"Nope. Never will. I am going to get fat if I keep this up. Will you still love me when I am too big to walk on my own?"

She chuckled at the thought and her hand slid upward to cup my breast. I had regained the weight I had lost and was back to my normal body, something that pleased Red immensely. If anything I might be a little plumper than I had been back home. She squeezed my full breast.

"As long as the fat goes to all right places I wont mind. Even if it doesn't I will still love you. There will just be more of my Kyra to love."

She buried her face into the side of my other breast and nuzzled it with her nose. I could not help but laugh at her cheesy pronouncement. She always knew how to cheer me up. I reached down with my arm that encircled her and landed my hand on her ass with an audible slap. She shuddered and her eyelids grew hooded. She shook her head to clear it.

"Not now, Kyra. Later. Let's go see our son?"

That was probably the only suggestion that could pull my head out of the pleasant thoughts of enjoying her supple body.

"Yes, let's."

In short order we were dressed and down in the courtyard, watching our son helping Marie off his back using his foreleg as a stepladder. The blond woman stroked his neck with affection before she rejoined her brethren. Malkareth had already sensed our approach and bounded toward us. He pushed his face against mine and his tongue slobbered all over my face. Before I could recover Red was treated to the same messy treatment.

"Mothers! Did you see? I was a horse!"

We both laughed at his exuberance. "You are so much more than a horse, my son."

"I know, I can fly!"

"You can? When did you learn?" Red's tone was surprised and Malkareth lowered his gaze sheepishly.

"Well not at the moment. But I have wings. I should be able to fly. I want to learn!"

My heart twisted and my earlier fears returned with a vengeance. Our boy was growing up so fast.

"I have already glided across the courtyard countless times, I am sure that I can fly if I really try, but..." his mental voice trailed off.

"But what? What is the matter, son?"

"I am scared, Mothers. What if I fail? What if I crash?"

I put my hand on his muzzle, his warm breath rushing between my fingers as I soothed him. His large eyes closed and he leaned into my touch, still finding comfort in the touch of his mother.

"You will not fail, son. We believe in you. Try, fly!" Red encouraged him.

I did not agree with Red. I wanted him to stay here, with us. But I knew I could not hold him back forever. His fearful eyes cut into my soul. All he wanted was to fly, but he was scared. He was still a child. What kind of mother would I be to deny him his greatest wish.

"I will fly with you, if you let me."

Relief practically shone through his slitted pupils and relief flooded through the bond we shared.

"Thank you, Mother. It means a lot to me. Saddle up!"

"Now?!"

He winked at me, his earlier fear forgotten in the reassuring presence of his mom. "No time like the present!"

I glanced at Red, expecting support in dissuading him. She mouthed the word 'Go!' and jerked her head in his direction. I grumbled under my breath but moved closer to the red dragon. Red grabbed my stump, spun me around and planted a lingering kiss on my lips.

"Ugh." He was so like a human teenage boy that our kiss ended with us chuckling into each others mouths. Red pushed me toward the dragon and he offered his foreleg like he had with Marie. I climbed onto his back and sat with my legs dangling on either side of his long neck. Without a backwards glance he set off toward the gate in the wall. I was almost pitched off his back from his lurching gait but my heels soon found purchase in the join of his wings when I folded them for stability and my hands grasped the sides of his neck. I found my balance and unlike my experience on horses I found this rather pleasant. The feel of his muscles bunching and relaxing against my thighs was reassuring. I was completely safe astride the massive dragon. He was much smaller than his mother had been when she died but he already dwarfed the horses he had befriended. We rode a fair way from the keep but even from this distance I saw the distinctive flare of red from the hair of a person watching us from the top of the wall. I waved at her but I did not know if she saw. Malkareth halted, suddenly brimming with nervous energy. I patted the side of his neck.

"You can do this son. Don't hesitate, don't think. Just fly," and then I added "and also don't drop me!"

He took me by my words, quite literally and he rose on his hind legs. They bunched up beneath him and then with a powerful spring we surged into the air. My belly sank into my pelvis from the force of his thrust and his leap brought us much higher into the air than I had expected. We slowed, and then started to fall. His wings snapped open and he beat them once but our fall only slowed marginally. Fear and uncertainty poured into my mind from our connection and he beat his wings once more. One more swift wing beat and they caught the air properly. We rose a little higher and he swiftly gained confidence. We rushed through the air, the wind making my eyes water and whipped my hair into a snarl instantly. I raised my shield to protect me from the air but the greater wind resistance nearly ripped me from my perch. I collapsed the shield but kept it like a visor in front of my face to keep the wind out of my eyes. With only a few quick breaths the air inside grew stale and I focused on altering the shield to keep the wind from my eyes but still let air in to breathe without letting the wind steal the breath from my lungs. A few minutes later I had accomplished my task and then the reality of the situation struck me. He was flying. I looked down and my head spun. He was flying very high. Dun Traelak had already vanished behind us.

"I am flying, Mother! I am doing it!"

His exhilaration infected me and despite the lurch in my belly I whooped and cheered for him. I'm sure my voice was stolen by the wind but his contentment with my inarticulate praise shone from the bundle of emotions in the back of my head.

"You can speak to me in here. You don't have to use words."

I opened my mouth to reply but then closed it shut. I focused my thoughts at him.

"Like this? Can you hear all of my thoughts?"

The thought horrified me that he had been able to hear my every thought since his hatching. His steady wing beats faltered.

"No need to scream at me. And no, I can't hear your every thought. Just the ones directly focused at me. When you focus that hard it splits my brain."

"Sorry."

"It's fine, you did not know. Just think at me and I will hear it clearly."

"At any range?"

"I'm not sure. I have never been far enough from you that it has not worked."

"Try with Red, she should be far away enough to test your limits."

His response was wistful. "I don't have the same connection to Other Mother like I have with you."

"Why is that?"

"I don't know. Possibly because you were the first I encountered?"

"I have seen other dragons that I presume have this kind of bond with several people, can't you connect with her?"

"If I can I don't know how. If I could I would have."

I could not wait to tell Red. She had never mentioned it but I knew it pained her to not have the same kind of bond with our son. This news would give her hope for the future.

"Are you ready to try a dive, Mother?"

Before I could respond he turned upside down and dropped like a stone. I was pressed into him from the change in direction and was in no danger of falling off. He roared in excitement and my own paltry voice joined his mighty roar. Our headlong dive planed out and our velocity increased to staggering levels. We hurtled along the ground, scattering a herd of buffalo as we shot past them. Malkareth was too excited to even give a thought of taking one of them and he beat his wings to regain altitude. Dun Traelak approached rapidly in the distance and despite my excitement I was more than ready to return to the ground. Better do this in small increments. Tomorrow we could take a longer flight. Malkareth had no such plans though and we shot past Dun Traelak in a flash and soared toward the mountaintops behind the fortress. The air grew chill as we ascended and I risked extending my shield a few inches and heated the air inside. Malkareth dove into a valley and his claws dragged through the surface of the river within before he climbed to the skies again. The view took my breath away. It was beautiful. The snowcapped mountains framed a tranquil valley filled with green trees and verdant grasslands, divided in two by a river fed by many estuaries. I had a sudden vision of a small cottage up here where I lived with Red, mom and Marissa and possibly Kendall while our dragon son roamed the skies, hunting the wildlife that must thrive in the forests. Perhaps that could become reality some day.

"Let's return to the keep. Red must be getting worried by now."

"But Mother!"

"No buts, young dragon. Do as your mother commands!"

"Yes, Mother."

He banked his wing and I was again pressed into his back as he turned us around in a wide loop. Dun Traelak appeared before us and before I knew it he shot down toward it. Was he planning on landing in the courtyard? Oh, no you don't! The space was too constricted for a safe landing, or at least I assumed so. I'd rather he try his first landing farther out on the plains like he had done with his takeoff. Before I could voice my concern we were already upon the keep. He flew a tight circle around it and then dropped toward the courtyard. He angled his wings hard and I was almost pitched over his shoulder but thankfully his hind quarters sank toward the ground as we lost speed and I was instead pressed into his neck. His hind paws made harsh contact and he was slammed forward. His thinner forelimbs were too weak to absorb the momentum and he was thrown to the ground, his chin following but a moment later.

"Mal!"

He roared in surprised pain as we slid across the courtyard, straight over the fount. Luckily the runes I had drawn where etched in the stone and was not disturbed but the budding foundations of the shield tower was not so lucky and the still fragile stone shattered across his chest. Frightened Clansmen scattered before us and luckily everyone got out of our way. He roared again as we started to slow but his shoulder ploughed through one of the support beams of the overhang of the stables and part of the building collapsed behind and over him. Splinters of wood shot through the air, one cutting through my temple and blood started to immediately trickle down the side of my face. We ploughed into the wall and came to a full stop. I took a few quivering breaths before I realised that Malkareth was not moving and his neck was bent at a sharp angle against the stone. I slipped off his back.

"Mal! Oh, dear spirits no! Mal!" I rushed toward his large head, panic gripping my heart tight. He could not be dead, not my child. This wasn't happening! He had been so happy to finally fly! The one eye facing me was closed and I fell to my knees next to him. I was too panicked for tears. I threw my arms around his massive head and pressed my forehead to his. His eye snapped open and I was launched backward when he climbed to his feet. I rolled with my fall and ended up on my feet. Thank you, old mercenary training. Relief flooded me at the sight of him standing.

"Mal! Are you alright?"

"I am fine, Mother. I just misjudged our velocity. I will not make that mistake again."

His eyes focused behind me and in my magesense I saw Red come sprinting toward us. Fear was writ all over her face but she relaxed when she saw us both standing.

"Mother!" He shouted mentally at Red, "I flew. Did you see? I flew!" He bounced over to her and Red leaped and wrapped her arms around his neck, hanging with her toes dangling several feet off the ground.

"I saw, you were very graceful. Majestic."

He preened at her compliments. I wanted to tell Red to not compliment him right now, she should not reinforce his reckless behaviour but I was so relieved that he survived the horrific landing that I let it slide.

"The view up there was amazing, Red. You just have to see it."

"I'll take you there right now, Mother. It was amazing!"

I leaned closer to Red and spoke into her ear.

"I found the perfect location for that cottage we have been talking about."

Her face lit up at the thought. "Show me!"

Malkareth watched us both and hung his head.

"I don't think I can carry you both at the same time. I need to grow more."

I patted his neck consolingly. "That's fine, son. You can show Red tomorrow."

Both of them aaawed in disappointment.

"Tomorrow? Let's go now!"

I chuckled at his excitement, he was so like a child with a new toy. Refusing to stop playing with it for even a second.

"I think that is enough flying for one day."

"Please, Mother. I can do it. I want to show Mother the valley we found."

I looked sternly at him. "Are you sure? Remember just now when you almost died?"

He snorted steam through his slitted nostrils. "I was not even close to dying. The crash just rattled me a bit. I am strong enough for another flight. What do you say, Mother?"

He directed the question at Red, knowing her to be the more lenient parent. Why did I always get stuck with the role of the naysayer? Red saw my expression but decided to ignore it and promptly climbed our son. She pointed imperiously upward.

"To the sky, my child! Bring me that horizon!"

With a roar of glee Malkareth did not bother to walk out of the keep, instead launching himself into the air once more. His take off went much smoother than his first and his wings caught the wind on the first powerful beat. I was left in the wind and swirling dust of his passing. Despite my immense pride at his accomplishment I was left with a hollow feeling. I was sure that this was the first step to our losing him. Now that he had gotten a taste for freedom he would not give it up. It was a bittersweet mix of pride and sadness and I suddenly understood what mom must have gone through when I boarded the Pioneer. I watched the dragon carrying my lover shrink into the distance until they vanished and then I returned to our rooms. I resolved to distract myself from my melancholy with study. They would be back soon enough. I dearly hoped so.

They did indeed make it back alright though Malkareth was tired after his exertions. Red on the other hand was very excited and her enthusiasm extended into the bedchamber. Sometimes I thought I had gotten complacent in my new life but then she pulled me to bed and blew my mind as she had so many times before.

She quickly became adept at magical construction and she had just a few days previously shown me a little bug she had constructed out of pure magic. It flew around the room on gossamer wings and inspected our surroundings. It seemed particularly interested in rooting out magical sources, namely my sealed wounds. It may be useful in the future to sniff out minor crossings of ley lines that could be opened up into founts. The procedure for ripping such a crossing open was detailed quite extensively in one tome I had found in the library, penned by Grasax in his youth when he was still a mortal. I was concocting a plan to use Red's marvellous bug spell to find a nearby crossing to open up for Malkareth. Even though I was loathe to give him more reasons to spend time away from the keep and away from my presence he was consuming much of the power from the fount, more than we could spare with our current plans for the keep and the shield tower. I had suggested to Red to give the bugs the ability to absorb power from the magic field they flew around to make them completely autonomous and not rely on being recharged every now and again, that way they could scout out further. She was adorable where she sat by the table with her nose in her book, scribbling drafts for the spell. She had an ink stain on her nose where she had scratched herself without thinking. I could not help myself and disturbed her in her work to kiss her. Her lips curled into a smile into my mouth.

"What was that for?"

To my great pleasure her breathing had quickened. Even after all this time I could reduce her to a quivering mass of need with a single kiss. I still got it.

"Nothing. You. Love. Choose one. Or both."

She puckered her lips and I was more than happy to oblige her.

"How's it going with the spell? Can I help?"

She looked down at the runes on the parchment before her and tapped a blank area. I studied the structures around it. It appeared to be the connection between the power gathering dome and the storage spell powering the bug. She had even included a magic containing shield to prevent energy leakage. It was all rather neat.

"How do I make sure that the actual spellbeast is not overloaded with power if it happens into a denser field? I need to be able to vary the absorption rate proportional to the density of the field."

That was an insightful point. Normally you bound spells to a constant flow of power but these bugs would traverse the field spatially and would encounter many different levels of densities. They may even have to cross completely dry areas. I thought for a moment.

"I would suggest making the storage spell larger to act as a buffer and have a continual conditional that chokes the input channel in proportion to how charged it is. Let the power gathering spell feed itself but allow an output from the store to serve as backup. If the gathering spell fails it will run dry eventually since it can't manifest spontaneously."

"Yes, I had already considered that. But that would leave the storage spell underutilised since the inflow would diminish as it filled up."

I nodded. "True, but would it be sufficient?"

"Probably. But not efficient."

"What about measuring the power contained in the storage spell? Choke the input completely when it fills up."

"You can do that?"

I shrugged. "Yeah. It's not trivial, it's all about knowing the capacity of the spell and calculating the magical pressure threshold for the breakpoint. I am sure I read it in one of these books recently, let me find it for you." I rummaged around the large pile of books in the corner. Somehow books tended to stay in our chambers instead of returning to the library. I found the book I searched for and flipped through the pages. There it was. I plonked the book down in front of my gorgeous redhead and pointed at the headline of the chapter.

"Automation of regulation of flow of magic based on internal power levels. It sounds more pretentious than it is."

She patted my hand over the book. "Thanks, love. I'll look into it. Then there is the matter of momentum."

"Momentum?"

"These bugs are made purely of magic and they weigh practically nothing. That makes their flight erratic, I think that some inertia would help them manoeuvre."

That was easily remedied. "Make their bodies from materialised magic. That would give them some mass and it could double as a power store."

"That's genius!"

"That is why you love me."

She smiled up at me. "Not the only reason."

"Oh," I leaned my face closer, relishing the effect my hot breath on her face had on her body, "tell me more of these reasons why you love me."

I was fishing for compliments, but I did not care. I loved when she gushed over me, just like she did when I did the same to her. Instead of answering she reached around my bent waist and pinched my ass. I let out an exaggerated squeak and widened my eyes. The violet light spilling from them reflected in her green orbs, joining the fire already roiling in them.

"Are you sure that was wise? Keep that up and I may keep you from your work. For hours." My voice had dropped to husky whisper, I was more than ready. Just say the word. She pinched me again and I sprang on her with an animalistic growl. She tumbled from the chair and we fell in a tangle. I darted my head down, smattering kisses all over her face as she laughed but her attempts to swat me aside was only half hearted. I kept attacking her and forced my thigh in between hers and rubbed it against her. Her attempts to free herself turned into clutching me close. She gripped me with desperate need, her work entirely forgotten. My magesense was shrinking to encompass only her but I noticed something circling above the keep. I dismissed it from my thoughts, my magesense would soon be unable to sense them at all and then I could focus entirely on much more pressing matters. The creatures kept pace with my shrinking senses and as they grew closer it was plain to me that they were no mere birds. I pulled away from Red and focused. She protested wordlessly and craned her neck to kiss my jaw.

"Something is going on. Do you sense them yet?"

Her range was far shorter than mine even though it expanded slowly each day that passed. She shook her head, not really comprehending my words and only wishing I would return to kissing her. I wanted the very same but these two things worried me. They did not blaze with magical power, but they contained far more than the average human. Possibly twice as much or maybe even more. More details grew clearer as they descended in languid circles. They were humanoid, except for the large wings on their backs. I rushed to the window and looked outside, trying to get a visual on the things. I could not get a clear view but the sunlight flashed red when they struck the light breaking through the cloud cover in the proper angles. There was no doubt in my mind that they were preparing to land in the courtyard but the Clansmen below had not yet spotted them.

"What are those things?"

Red had sensed them too and was starting to calm down, though her heart beat rapidly for completely different reasons. She was getting ready to fight.

"I don't know, but we better get down there, warn our people."

She nodded and burst from the room at a run, me hot on her heels. Despite being much shorter than me she ran faster when she really poured it on, unless I used my blood magic to power my strides. I would leave her in the dust in a short sprint but anything longer than a hundred yards would leave me a useless, breathless pile on the ground while she was ready to fight. I burst out onto the courtyard hot on her heels.

"Bizhjerai! To arms!"

To their credit they did not halt in surprise or stare or any other stupid reactions. Instead they dropped whatever they were doing and rushed to the armoury. Most of them were already armed with various sharp or blunt implements but the call to battle required firearms. Within moments men and women emerged from the keep, hastily trying to load muskets and pistols even as they walked to make way for the others. We only had a meagre amount of weapons, the small supply that Clan Ithlak had not claimed after the battle. We had not yet managed to set up any manufacturing process for weapons yet. The fount was completely dedicated to growing the shield tower, the plumbing and Malkareth's feeding. I hoped that Red's bugs would find other sources of power to funnel to the keep to supplement the diminished stream of magic. The warriors milled about the courtyard, confused at the lack of enemy. That was when the creatures dropped to the stones. They landed lightly with a snap of wings that had become familiar to me after all the flights I had taken with Malkareth during the two months since he learned to fly properly. The creatures straightened out from their crouched landing and folded their wings to their backs. They were indeed similar to humans. One was a male and the other a female. The wings were attached to their shoulders and large, overdeveloped muscles decorated their shoulders and chest. The man looked grossly disproportionate but most of the females bulging musculature was hidden beneath her breasts. It only served to make her already substantial bust seem even bigger. I pushed aside a stab of envy. I routinely disliked any woman with larger tits than my own, which in itself was a rare occasion. Especially since I had joined the Bizhjerai whose women generally featured a slimmer build than the women on the Skylands. Weapons were raised into line at the sudden appearance of the two figures but none dared fire. The creatures did not seem hostile and they stood calmly watching the muzzles pointed at them with their arms idly by their sides. The red scales that covered them was the same shade that adorned my son and fear gripped my belly in a cold fist. These must be servants of the red dragonflight, Malkareth's kin. Had they come here to take him away from us? I would not allow it! Not as long as breath flowed through my lungs. The female pushed her white hair from her face and spoke.

"Where is the dragon?"

I shouldered through the ranks of tense warriors, hand resting on the hilt of my revolver. I'd kill them both if they even hinted at taking my boy away from me. I'd blow their heads apart and then go take a nap and sleep like a baby. Fuck these monsters.

"Why do you care?"

Two pair of yellow eyes, so similar to my sons', turned calmly my way. Their eyes widened at the sight of my glowing eyes and veins. Yeah, two can play the monster card, bitch. Red was right by my side, clutching her axe in her right hand and a rifled pistol in the second. I had crafted that weapon for her, painstakingly carving the rifles in the formerly smooth bore with my magic and moulding the special tight fitting balls to go along with it. When had she had time to load it?

"Where is the dragon?"

"Answer my question!"

"We asked first. Where is the dragon?"

Her statement struck me as utterly childish, even spoken with the voice of a mature woman. The male bristled, showing fangs and and elongated tongue. The Bizhjerai adjusted their aim and the men calmed down reluctantly.

"You came into our home. We will ask the questions. Besides..." I let my voice trail off menacingly and gestured with my arm, indicating the row of muskets and spears. The woman inclined her head gracefully, conceding the point.

"Who are you?"

"We are of the Red Flight. We have come for the progeny."

"No."

Her voice widened in surprise.

"He belongs with his kind."

"He already is."

A graceful line of scales a darker shade of red than the rest of her that emulated an eyebrow rose.

"You keep him prisoner here and call yourself Dragonkind?" She shook her head and muttered under her breath. Despite the softness of the word I could hear it easily through the deafening silence. 'Humans,' she had said with derision. These two were far less bestial than those who had attacked the Skylands, looking more like humans turned dragon than the other way around.

"He is not a prisoner! He is here of his own free will!" I almost added, "We love him!" but bit the words back.

"Is he now? Never before has a dragon willingly served humanity. We have always peacefully coexisted, each benefiting from the relationship."

Peacefully my ass. I had not forgotten Greg's death.

"Doesn't really matter. He's not here."

"Then we will wait."

A ruckus from the back drew my attention and in my magesense I saw the ranks of the warriors parting before the Chief.

"What is going on here?"

"These assholes are here to take Malkareth away." His face contorted. He adored his unexpected grandchild. One night when he had bounced the baby dragon on his knee and drunk too much fermented milk he had admitted that he had given up the thoughts of grandchildren when his daughter chose me. Until Malkareth hatched.

"No. I will not allow it."

I felt Red's hand on my severed arm and I recoiled at the expression on her face. It was not defiant, or even angry. It was pensive. She leaned close.

"Maybe we should hear them out. Let Malkareth speak to them. Perhaps they can teach him about being a dragon." I ripped my stump from her fingers, shocked to the core that she would even suggest such a thing. What if he decided to leave with them? What if we would never see him again? I blinked furious tears from my eyes and turned my back on her heartbroken expression. She had read my emotions clearly from my expression, and my reaction hurt her. Well good. Her words had hurt me and sent my heart thumping in a panic. The two dragon people where whispering to one another in hushed tones, clearly surprised by something. Their attention snapped back to me.

"Malkareth? Was that the name you just used?"

"Yes, that is his name."

"Malkareth lives?"

The question struck me as odd, they had came here presumably because they had seen him on one of his long forays into the wild. Of course he lived.

"Of course he does."

"The return of the Great One. This is a glorious day indeed, we thought him lost forever. We must meet him!"

The pieces finally clicked home. They believed him to be the original Malkareth, the patriarch of the Red Flight. I came to a decision.

"Kill them."

Hammers cocked on a dozen muzzles and the female dragon womans eyes widened. She threw up her arm.

"Wait!" Red cried out the denial in the same moment and she grabbed my arm again.

"The fuck are you doing, Kyra?!"

I shrugged her off and ignored her. The warriors glanced at each other, unsure what to do about the conflicting orders. I was Bàs Marbhadair, Hero of the Clan and lover to the Chief's daughter but she was the actual daughter in question. And the Chief remained silent. They opted to do nothing. The dragon woman spoke quickly, trying to defuse the situation.

"If you kill us you bring the wrath of the entire flight down upon you! We merely wish to speak to Malkareth. Greater Dragons is the highest in our society, if he does not wish to return with us he will remain here. He is immortal and the short time of your lifespans will be nothing to him. If he wishes to remain here until your death that is of no concern to us as long as he knows where his kin are. He must be guided by his own kind."

I did not believe her. She was here to take my boy. Realising I had lost I whirled and left the courtyard, clomping up the stairs. I seethed alone in a chair by the table for more than an hour before I sensed Red approaching. She radiated fury. She entered the room and leaned against the door with crossed arms.

"What the fuck?" Her tone was tense. I had never seen her this angry before.

"They have come to take Mal, Red. I won't allow it."

"It is not your decision to make," he enunciated each word, biting it off like it hurt her tongue.

"What?" Sometimes my eloquence surprised even myself.

Red stalked over and sat down across from me. I did not dare look her in the eye but her furious face was clear as day in my magesense.

"It is his. Mal is growing up. You can't control him like this anymore. You have no right."

"But he is my baby!"

Her eyes flared.

"Cut it out with this selfish bullshit! He must live his own life! You can't make decisions like this for him!"

"He does not know what is best for him." Even to my own ears my argument was weak. Red scoffed.

"You underestimate him. You always have. You still think of him like that tiny creature that crawled into your lap from the egg. He is a grown dragon now. Let him be a dragon!"

"But they will take him away from us!" My sudden yell startled her but she only raised a beautiful eyebrow and glared at me. I was forced to look away.

"And what if they do? If they try to take him against his will, I will summon the Clans and burn their home to the ground. But if he wants it we must let him go, Kyra."

"I can't."

"You must. There comes a point when every parent must let go of their child. Do you think Father was happy when I chose you?"

That shocked me to my core. "He wasn't?"

"Of course not, how thick are you? Really? He wanted me to find a man, preferably a Chief, and grow fat with a horde of children. Instead I chose a woman, forsaking both ambition and family. A foolish woman, it now strikes me." Her words hurt. Deeply.

"But you know what?"

I shook my head, unable to speak.

"He changed his mind. When he saw how happy you made me he changed. Just like that. Because that is what matters. That your child is happy. That they do what they want, not what you want! Can't you see that?"

She made sense, but logic did not stand a chance against my emotions.

"I don't know what I am doing, Red. Anything that threatens him, it chases all rational thought from my mind."

"I know. That is why I am so angry with you. You don't think anymore, you just feel. When I first met you I was struck by how rational you were, no matter the situation. What happened to you?"

I shook my head. "Motherhood?"

"Don't you think your own mother went through this exact thing when you left the Skylands?"

Realisation struck me. She must've. And yet she let me go with nary a tear. Every time I went into battle she must have felt this heart wrenching fear and pain. How could I put her through that without a second thought? I owed her so much. A sob shook my body and the floodgates opened. I collapsed over the table as the sobs ripped out of me in heart wrenching heaves. Red watched me coldly, arms still crossed over her chest. A long while later my sobs petered out and I lifted my head from my arm and looked up at her. Her face was blurry to my eyesight but detailed in my magesense. It made for a confusing disconnect between my senses.

"The thought of him leaving. It hurts. You are right, in everything. I see that now. Oh, my poor mother. I must return to her, tell her I love her and tell her how sorry I am for everything I put her through. I must go. Malkareth can carry me home, I think." Red's angry expression turned into one of horror as I rambled on.

"You are so right, Red and I am sorry. For everything." Tears where streaming silently down my face as my mouth babbled on uselessly.

"It just hurts, the thought of losing him. There is only one thing I fear more."

The silence stretched until Red broke it with a whispered question.

"What?"

I reached my remaining hand across the table to her. "Losing you."

My heart sank when she did not answer and left my hand lying on the table. I had already lost her. My paranoia about our child had pushed her away. After a long moment she reached out and put her hand in mine and gave it a reassuring squeeze as her face softened.

"You drive me crazy when it comes to Malkareth, Kyra, and you are not rational right now. I love you, never doubt that, and I won't leave your side. But you have to listen to me and not do anything hasty. You must let Mal live his life as he wishes. Promise me that."

Relief flooded through me and fresh tears sprang to my mind. I had thought I was completely dry. I nodded, agreeing to her demands. I knew I was being overprotective but I resolved to keep my thoughts to myself and respect Mal's wishes. If he wanted to leave I had to let him. He would be miserable if I forced him to remain against his will and he would inevitably grow to resent me. That thought hurt more than the thought of losing him. At least knowing he was happy, even if he was not by my side would have to be enough.

"You are right, Red. I love you. Now and forever. I don't know what I would do without you."

"Now and forever," she responded gently.

She let go of my hand and rounded the table. She knelt on the floor and embraced me. Her touch unmade me and it was a long time until my thoughts made sense again. Red left me and rummaged around among the assortment of pitchers on the table. She returned with a mug of fermented buffalo milk.

"Here, drink this. It will steady your nerves."

I gulped down the pungent milk in a single long pull. She pulled me by the hand to the bed and pushed me onto it and lay down beside me. She kissed my jaw tenderly and nuzzled my neck.

"Now about this idea of returning to the Skylands to see your mother. If it is really what you want to do I will help you but we must think about this rationally. We must plan. First of all, can Malkareth carry you there? You said it took weeks for your Skyship to bring you to our shores? Can you even approach without getting attacked? Last time a dragon visited people died. You may not be given time to identify yourself."

Damn, she made way to much sense.

"We will ashk hiem." Why did I slur my words like that? My eyelids grew heavy and lethargy spread through me like a wildfire.

"Did yhou druoh?" Sleep claimed me.

## Chapter 35

I awoke after nightfall. Red was back at work on her spells by the table.

"Did you drug me?"

"Mhm. I got the sleep potion from the shaman before I came up here. You were hysterical, Kyra. Out of your mind. Forgive me."

I waved her apology aside. "You have nothing to apologise for. I am the one that owe you an apology. More than one. I don't know why you put up with my shit."

Without looking over her shoulder at me she answered. "Mostly because your ass is as close to perfection as anything can be."

I could still feel the tension between us but she was cracking jokes. We would be okay, in time.

"You are right, Red. About everything. Henceforth I will follow your lead." 

Her red tresses whistled through the air as she spun around in her chair, her anger resurfacing.

"No! That is not what I meant! We are in this together. Both of us! I ask you to rein in your hysteria, not to force me to make all decisions!"

I looked away. "Yes, dear."

"Look at me, Kyra." I forced myself to meet her steely gaze. "Swear to me that you will not turn into a meek yay-sayer."

"I swear." I tried to convey my sincerity through my glowing eyes and I must have succeeded for the fire of her fury died away.

"Good. Now help me with this bullshit spell before I lose my mind."

I leaped to assist her, eager to make up for my earlier idiocy. We worked together for an hour before I felt her relax next to me. She grabbed my hand and lifted it to her lips and kissed the back of it.

"Relax, Kyra. You don't have to tread lightly around me. I thought we were past that. You pissed me off, I yelled at you and you understood. We are okay now. Seriously, calm down."

Damn, when would I stop crying? It seemed it was all I had done recently. She reached up and brushed the tear away with her thumb.

"No more tears, love. Just, no more. I can't stand seeing you this frazzled. You were always my rock, my anchor. Let me bear some of this burden for you." I leaned my forehead on her shoulder.

"Thank you. I love you so much it hurts sometimes."

"Malkareth returned two hours ago."

Her unexpected pronouncement startled me and I nearly jumped out of my seat. I scanned the keep with my magesense and found him in his nest in the stables. The two dragonkin where with him, staring at him. I was sure that they were communicating silently, mind to mind. I wanted to go down there and chase them away but I forced myself to remain. He had to make his own informed opinion. If he asked me for my own I would give it, no holds barred, but I would not try to influence him in any undue way. I meant my oath to Red. She saw my internal struggle and her lips curled in satisfaction at the outcome. She shook her head.

"I can't decide if you are the worst or best mother ever. Probably both."

I could not help but laugh at that, an edge of hysteria to my cackle. Red joined in and the tension between us evaporated. I wanted to gather her into my arms and never let go. Meeting her was the best thing that had ever happened to me. Red gasped and her face paled. I was instantly on alert.

"What? Red, what's wrong?"

"I got it!"

"What?"

"The spell!"

She turned promptly from me and hunched over the parchment, furiously drawing the runes with precise motions. Despite her excitement the rune structure was perfect. She filled in the blank spaces on the parchment and leaned back with an air of contentment. I checked the runes and could find no fault. There were even some structures that I would never have thought of. I squeezed her thigh.

"And so the student becomes the master."

"Please, you flatter." I could tell that despite her protest she was pleased with my praise.

"No, seriously. Your solution is so elegant. I would just have used the inefficient solution I proposed earlier and called it a day."

"But it would have worked fine."

"Yes, but this is perfect. I mean it, I can find no flaw in this. We need to get you a better teacher."

"I have seen you do extraordinary things. You defeated Grasax!"

I nodded. "Fighting is what I am best at. It is all that I am good for. I destroy, and I destroy completely. You are a true builder."

"Fighting is not what you do best."

The heat in her eyes gave me an idea what she was thinking about but I wanted her to say it. A small smile toyed with my lips.

"Oh, yeah? Name one thing I do better than fighting?"

She leaned close and the things she whispered in my ear was incredibly indecent indeed. Despite my inner turmoil heat flashed between my legs. She stood up and pulled me toward the bed.

"Don't you want to try the spell?"

"It can wait. I have more pressing needs that require your expertise."

Even though I knew she was doing this mainly to make me feel better and distract me from our son speaking to the Dragonkin I was more than happy to oblige. I would never get enough of her.

## Chapter 36

I screamed with excitement, howling my pleasure to the heavens. Malkareth extended his wings and arrested our plummet with a lurch and we shot past the growing grass. Even as we flew in our aerobatics he chattered incessantly in my mind about all the things he had learned so far from Serena and Marius, the two Dragonkin. It turned out that they had once been human but had been gifted with the features of dragons in return for their long service. Both was more than a century old. They had taught him to bind more humans to his mind and to share in his magic and I will never forget the look on Red's face when the bond sank deep into her mind. She had been moved beyond words and had not stopped trembling for hours. Mostly the two Dragonkin had taught him about dragons and their culture and how they coexisted with their human allies. The dragons offered magic that they gathered while flying across the continent and the humans provided a home, hearth and a secure source of food. No disease would claim any bound by a dragon and the power they provided was immense. They were like mobile founts, but even greater. Wherever they went they soaked the magic up and with their swift flight they accrued power incredibly quickly. Mal had outright laughed at their suggestion that he joined their roost, to my great relief. He admitted to harbouring a wish to visit some day, but not yet. He swore that he would return, and I believed him. It was difficult not to when his every emotion was laid bare through our bond. Being true to my word to Red I had kept my own thoughts and emotions regarding the matter shielded from him so as not to influence him. Red had sensed my action and rewarded me handsomely that night in the bedchamber. Even just remembering that night made my loins ache with the memory of the morning after.

"Mother, please. That is disgusting."

Oops. I had let my thoughts spill over. I scanned the horizon, letting the chill lingering in the spring air cool my suddenly flushed skin. Something caught my attention in the far skies. A dark blot against the white clouds in distance.

"Mal, head north. There is something there."

He did not offer any comment but our course shifted immediately. Half an hour later the thing had grown significantly and I had a sinking feeling that I knew what it was. Just minutes later I ordered Mal to take us back home. I had seen enough and had to report back to the Clan. Malkareth had barely alighted on the courtyard when I was off his back and storming through the keep. I found Red with her father in what had been the throne room when Grasax lived here. It was good that they were both here, they should both hear this. Red looked up at my sudden entrance and smiled in welcome. Her smile slid off her face when she saw my stony expression.

"What's wrong? Is Mal..." Her voice trailed off, she feared even speaking the question.

"He is fine. We were out on a flight and there is a Skyship by the coast."

"Skyship?" Red's father was not as used to the terminology of my home as Red was and she answered in my stead.

"Skylanders."

I nodded. "They appear to be building an outpost on the coast, where the Elwyer Forest is thinnest."

"An outpost?"

"Resources. We don't have anything natural on the Skylands. They have come to claim our resources. Stone, wood, meat, anything and everything."

"You told me of the Pioneer, it would not be large enough to bring many. We could surprise them and wipe them out."

I shook my head. "It wasn't the Pioneer. This one was much larger, there are many of my people on the ground already and they outgun us. If we attack them I don't know if we would win. Even if we did, there is plenty more where they came from. Two and a half million people live on the Skylands."

"Then what do you propose?"

"Parlay. There is no doubt in my mind that war is coming. Skylanders do not pay for what they can take. But before they know our strength or the lay of the land we may be able to stall for time, gather allies."

Red's father had been silent up to that point but now he interjected.

"Are you sure about this, Kyra? Do you think your people come here with ill intent?"

"They are not my people any more, remember? And yes, I believe so. Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow or even next year but war is coming. And we are the first obstacle between them and the rest of the world."

"Surely they are not powerful enough to threaten the whole world?"

"No, of course not. But they are powerful enough to crush us before the rest of the world even notices, and what else matters after that? We can't fight them alone, even if we rally all of the Clans. We may be able to hold them until they are reinforced from the Skylands but after that? All bets are off."

Red proposed the unthinkable. "Can we flee? Simply move elsewhere and let someone else take the brunt of the initial onslaught?"

Her father shook his head. "Probably not. The other Clans would surely notice and many would join us if they believe the threat. The Cities would see a great horde of barbarians on the warpath and come to oppose us. We would waste our time and lives fighting people who are not truly our enemy."

"Can we rely on the Cities for aid?"

Again he shook his bushy head.

"No. Not unless they are threatened directly."

"Let's save the plans of war for later. First we need to make contact with these Skylanders and unveil their intentions. Can you take us to their outpost, Kyra?"

I nodded.

"How long will it take us to get there?"

"Two, maybe three days if we bring someone who know the way. I can describe the route roughly."

An hour later fifty Bizhjerai warriors was mounted on the courtyard. Since I had not yet learned to ride Malkareth had offered to be my mount. He quivered with excitement to meet my former people, despite the fact that we would run all the way instead of flying. Serena and Marius had adamantly intended to join us, unwilling to let the red dragon out of their sight but I talked them down. Seeing Dragonkin with us would not endear the Skylanders to us. I feared the sight of Mal would be enough to antagonise them but when they recognised me I hoped they would assume that he was my slave. I was the Dragonbane after all. The days passed in a rush, especially the third day that Mal and I spent scouting the forest as the Bizhjerai slowly made progress. The Skyship was still hovering above the encampment and we flew as close as I dared. We stayed much higher than the Skyship and I hoped that anyone down below that looked up would mistake us for a very large bird. I stared in wonder at what I saw. A thick ray of magic poured from the horizon, supported at regular intervals with floating stations that gathered and refocused the ray of power. The Skyship received the power and projected it down over the settlement and contained it with an ever expanding shield. It was the same kind of enchantment as the shield tower that finally had finished growing just days ago. The enchantment was slowly constructing itself up its walls and soon the shield would be restored. Below the Skyship a settlement was quite literally growing out of the ground. Magic coalesced into structures and several manufacturies was well on the way. I assumed they were for common tools and utilities and dearly hoped it was not ammunition factories. The ground swarmed with soldiers, Guard and special forces both along with a generous dollop of ununiformed mercenaries. What surprised me the most, stunned me even, was the great ray of magic. Where did they get all that power from? When I left magic had been scarce, most of they geyser being consumed by keeping the city afloat thousands of yards above the ocean. The rest had been consumed by the manufactories. They must have shut down a significant part of the city to afford diverting this much. People would be starving as a consequence. I urged Mal away before we dropped onto the plains. He set off at a loping gait to catch up the the Bizhjerai. We had found no clearings large enough for him to land in, so running was the only way to go. We easily caught up with the horses. Where they were encumbered by the foliage, being careful not to snag a leg on a root or vine or step into an unexpected pit and have a lame horse Malkareth lumbered straight through the forest. The foliage was no obstacle to his massive momentum and he was far too agile to get trapped by any mere hole in the ground. Our headlong charge calmed down when we reached the tail of the line of warriors and Red fell back to join us.

"Nothing new. They are still building their settlement."

"Any sign of warriors?"

"Everywhere. We need to announce ourselves plainly or we risk startling them."

I was beyond nervous. I was not sure if I was ready to face my former kin already. Reuniting with Alissa had been an unexpected joy, but these people were true Skylanders. She had lived here for half a year in the wilderness. I was glad that we had thought to invite her along. If the Skylanders found two of their own already cooperating the odds that they would not just kill us out of hand was much lower.

"Relax, Mother. I will not let anything happen to you."

"It is not myself I am worried about."

"Who are you worried about? Other Mother? I will protect her too."

"No. Yes, I am worried about her. But mostly I am afraid of what the presence of these Skylanders means."

"But they are your people?"

"They are my people in the same way that the Red Flight is your kin."

"I understand. They are not to be trusted until proven trustworthy."

Pride over his sound reasoning threatened to burst my heart. It gladdened me that he did not trust Serena and Marius just because they looked like him. Before I was ready we crested a low rise before we entered the area cleared of trees surrounding the settlement. We were spotted almost immediately and shouts of warning rose to the skies. Soldiers poured out from between the semi-constructed buildings and formed a massive block before us. The Chief raised his hands, showing them empty of weapons and the Bizhjerai warriors emulated him. We rode slowly down toward the soldiers and their commander obviously did not view us as a threat. The Bizhjerai halted thirty paces from the front ranks and Red, her father and I along with Mal rode forward to meet the commander who stood unflinchingly a few steps in front of his host. I could see him pale visibly at the sight of the dragon and some of his men lowered their weapons to point at him but none dared fire. The dragon was friendly, but who knew what would happen if they fired. Everyone knew a few shots would not take drown a dragon, even one of such modest size as Malkareth still were. None wished to provoke him. We halted in front of the commander and before I could dismount a voice rang out over the low murmur from the soldiers.

"Kyra? Is that you? Get out of my fucking way! It's the Dragonbane, don't you see? She is alive! Kyra!" From my elevated position I could see the source of the shout. Cries of 'Dragonbane!' and 'Zorantis' spread through the crowd as the tall, armoured figure shouldered his way through the ranks. He was armoured like all of the special forces but bore no weapons. Instead a long staff was clutched in his hand, crowned by a blazing crystal. I did not believe my ears. I knew that voice. I slid from Mal's neck, ignoring his silent inquiry and rushed toward the tall figure. I threw myself in his arms as he finally emerged from between two men in the front ranks and he pulled me tight against his armoured chest.

"Kendall, what are you doing out here? You are not a warrior!"

"I came here to find you, or figure out what happened to you." He pushed me away and let his eyes roam over my body. I squirmed under his intense inspection. There was no way he was going to miss my glowing eyes and veins or my missing arm. "What did happen to you?"

I waved my stump. "Later. It's a long story. How are you? And mom? Marissa?"

"I'm well, so are they. But they are worried about you. When the Pioneer returned without you... We refused to believe you dead even though many of the others of the First Expedition was confirmed killed. You know only three returned?"

"No, I did not know that."

He looked into my eyes meaningfully.

"Raynard did not return. It is unknown if he yet lives."

I returned his look. "He does not."

He was silent for a long moment. "Good."

I glanced at Red and her father and saw her watching me warily. The commander of the soldiers followed her gaze and bowed respectfully. He recognised me despite my new glowing features. I looked back at Red with a question in my eyes and I wished she could read my thoughts.

"Think it, and I will relay your thoughts to Other Mother."

"Red, this is Kendall, he has news of my family. Can you and your father handle this for now?"

"Yes, go, but we may need you later."

I grabbed Kendall and pulled him further from the row of soldiers that had already started to disperse. A small guard remained to match the Bizhjerai warriors. I whirled and again hugged Kendall. I was so happy that there was a friendly face among my former kin.

"Kendall, what has happened back home? I'll tell you my story after."

"A lot has happened, and at the same time very little. The Pioneer returned and the three survivors' report spread through the Skylands in no time. They spoke of verdant forests and fields and primitive people who lived there."

"They are not primitive!" I protested but he talked over me.

"The only dangers were in a few dangerous plants, but only if you ingested them, and a few dangerous animals. And the people, of course. A few of the mercenaries where slain by the natives, the rest died of exposure. A few even lived with the natives for a while. The decision came down swiftly from the upper management. We were to establish a colony to claim the resources. The promise of land to anyone willing to relocate almost ended crime overnight and the whole Skylands united. Everyone who aided the colonisation efforts were promised rewards but we did not have much power. Construction on the Hand of Glory," he indicated the vast Skyship above, "started almost immediately. The Pioneer was sent out to scout in other directions and they found another Geyser. Not as large as the Great Geyser but still substantial and the magic scarcity vanished. Prices dropped and the crime stopped completely." Well that explained this surge of power. With the capabilities of mass production that had been idle for years due to the lack of power now re-purposed to work for colonisation the progress would be swift. The heavily overpopulated Skylands would soon belch forth a torrent of settlers and they would be armed to the teeth. Poorly trained, apart from the Guard and special forces but better armed than anything the Clans could bring to bear. This was worse than I thought.

"I signed up out of curiosity, and perhaps to move here. But deep inside I hoped to find you alive and well. At least I found you alive."

A smile broke through my maudlin thoughts.

"I am well, Kendall. I found the woman of my dreams, and I have a son!"

A smile twitched his lips. "The redhead? I saw the look you gave her. What's her name?"

"Anjali. Though I call her Red."

He snorted at that. "Of course you do. Wait, what? What was that part about a son?"

"Well, more of an adopted son."

"You seem to have developed a tendency to adopt strays."

He did have a point.

"What's his name, how old is he?"

"Malkareth, and he is nearly nine months old now."

"A little baby? Aaw, I can't wait to meet him!"

I suppressed a smile.

"You already have." Now I did laugh at his confusion. I pointed at Malkareth and he felt my attention shift to him and he lumbered over. Kendall's eyes threatened to bug out of their sockets.

"The dragon?!" He choked out.

"Yes. Mother hatched my egg and cared for me."

"It speaks?!" Kendall's voice was a hilarious squeak.

"Of course I speak. What else did you expect? Are you this Kendall Mother have so often spoken about?"

Kendall gathered his wits with laudable aplomb. "I am. Pleased to meet you Mal, may I call you Mal?"

"Everyone else does. Pleased to meet you too, Kendall. Mother speaks highly of you." He placed his claw in Kendall's proffered hand and they exchanged a bizarre shake.

"I never thought I would shake the paw of a dragon. Life is full of surprises. Now Kyra, you have some explaining to do."

I gave him the abridged version of my story and his expression grew ever more shocked. He was silent for a long minute after I finished.

"That is quite the tale there, Kyra." His face fell when a thought occurred to him. "You aren't coming home, are you? You have finally found the life you've always craved."

I shook my head slowly. "I am Bizhjerai now, Kendall. I stopped being a Skylander a long time ago."

"Skylander," he said as if tasting the word, "I like it."

"You should come with, we could use your skills in preparation for the coming war. And Red needs a better teacher than me."

"War?"

"Please, Kendall, think! You were always the smart one between the two of us. Do you really think the Skylanders can come and claim resources unopposed? Eventually they will attack the Clans and they will not be able to stand against them, not for long. Then the Cities will come to face you when they feel threatened enough?"

"Cities?"

"I have never been there, but Red tells me there are many cities further inland. They have magic and weapons, not as good as ours but in far vaster quantities."

His silence was telling.

"The Skylands may win, or fight to a standstill but to what end? The loss of life will be massive, on both sides."

He ran his fingers through his blond hair.

"You are right. But what can we do?"

"I don't know yet, we are here to establish some good will. If we can trade and help each other for now we may stall the war for some time, but it will come. We must buy ourselves time to plan. We can't win without the Cities, or the dragon flights but neither will help unless we can convince them of the threat. Make a show of force, convince the Skylanders that peace is more beneficial than war. Make the cost of war higher than the cost of trade."

"I don't know, Kyra. There are many people coming from the Skylands. They need to live somewhere, and there is no place to return to."

"Please, Kendall. You know I would not ask this of you if the situation was not dire."

"Yes, I know. I trust you, Kyra, but I don't have much influence."

"Then come with us. You skills in construction will be invaluable. We need to arm the Clans."

A sudden thought entered my mind. If it came to open conflict, there may not be a chance to bring mom and Marissa here. But they would be safer back in the Skylands if war broke out. The desire to bring them here to a good life warred with the desire to keep them safe.

"I know that look, Kyra. They are safe where they are. But I think they would risk everything to come here. Especially Marissa, she has been speaking of you almost non stop since you left. Always 'Do you think mom is happy?' or 'Do you think she has forgotten us?'"

"I have not forgotten!" My voice was hot with passion.

"I know, calm down. Not for one moment did she believe you dead," he affected a girlish voice, "'Nothing can kill mom. She stared down a dragon!'"

I could not help but smile at his impression of the eleven year old. More like twelve by now, I realised with a jolt. Oh how I missed the cheerful little brave girl.

"Is it possible to bring them here? If fighting erupts we may be able to sequester them in the mountains, or in the Cities."

"The artificial ley line we have constructed doubles as a Skyway. That is how we were brought over. It takes just a few days one way. The Hand is almost all weapons and the shield generator. It has very little space for cargo."

That gave us some hope that the Skylanders could not bring materiel here en masse, but Kendall dashed those hopes almost immediately.

"They are constructing cargo ships even as we speak. They'll be slow but can carry much. But the bulk must be manufactured on site. That won't be a large problem with the ley line powering us."

It bothered me that he referred the Skylanders as 'us' but he had just been dumped a lot of knowledge. It would take a while for him to adjust his thought patterns, if he ever would. He thought for a minute before he spoke again.

"Here is what we will do. I will request to make a short trip back to the Skylands and I will ask Marissa and your mother what they think. If they wish it, I will bring them here and somehow get them to you. How will we find you?"

"Bring them south across the plains. I will fly with Mal and look for you each day. We will find you and guide you the rest of the way to Dun Traelak." I paused. "Will you come with them?"

"If I am able. I will persuade the Commander that an ambassador to the natives is in order."

"But you said you don't have much influence?"

He squeezed my shoulder. "But I have famous friends, one that happens to bang the daughter of the most powerful Chief." He winked at me.

"Mother, Other Mother is asking for you."

Kendall gave no indication that he had heard my son and I assumed he had been left out of the conversation.

"Red is calling for me. I need to join her."

I was loathe to leave my friend so soon after our unexpected reunion but we had pressing matters to attend to. I gave him a crushing hug and turned to leave but he stopped me with a word.

"Before I forget, I have a gift for you." He reached into a pouch on his belt and produced a choker identical to the one I had lost in the fight for Dun Traelak.

"I made this for you, based on the new Valkyrie armour."

"You carried this all the time in the slim hope of finding me?"

"Yes. You are too stubborn to die."

I stood on my tip toes and kissed his cheek. "Thank you, Kendall."

"Don't mention it. I see you lost your rifle?"

"I gave it to Red. I can't use it anymore." I brandished my arm, severed beneath the elbow. He watched the stump with saddened eyes but nodded in agreement. He had that look in his eyes that he always had when he had an idea.

"It may take a few weeks before I return from the Skylands, if I am able to score a seat on the next trip. If we don't meet again before you have to return to your people, look for us on the plains to the south. Stay alive, Kyra."

"Stay alive, Kendall."

I turned from him before I lost my composure and let Malkareth lead me to where Red and the Chief sat by a small folding table someone had brought for them. I put the choker Kendall had gifted me on and I realised how much I had missed its constricting presence.

## Chapter 37

The negotiations had been easy, especially after I joined them. The commander mentioned that he had seen my mad climb onto the dragon and he seemed to have a crush on me. The Skylanders were not interested in fighting, or encroaching on Clan territory. They lay claim to the abandoned Elweyr Forest and a strip of the plains that the Clans did not use anyway. The commander readily agreed to trade, making arrangements for a market out on the plains by the edge of the forest in a few weeks time. He was much more interested in shoring up the beachhead they had established than anything else and we left the Skylanders somewhat calmer than we had arrived. The three of us, Red, her father, and I, still believed that war was inevitable but it may yet be years into the future. I knew better. My woman and her father underestimated the sheer speed with which Skylanders built and the number of people that would soon arrive. It would not take long for them to spread through the Elweyr forest, cutting it down for their lodgings. They would soon be encroaching upon our territory. Lands we needed for our herds. If they stopped us from herding the buffalo they would start to starve and with their dwindling numbers so would we.
