One side or the other would be forced to defend itself sooner or later and after the first shot was fired in anger... A few days later we were back in Dun Traelak and I lay in my bed with my love at my side but sleep refused to give me respite. Red woke up and saw me staring at the ceiling.

"What is wrong, love?"

"I am worried about the future."

"Me too. But it does not help to lose sleep over it. Get some rest, we can make plans in the morning. We still have time."

"Yeah, but how long?"

"Doesn't matter. We will do what we can."

"And if that is not enough?"

"We will make sure that it is. Even if we can't win, even if we die I will die a happy woman."

I clutched her tight.

"You are fine with being killed by Skylanders?"

"I would be happier if it did not end up that way, but if it comes to that. Yes, I would. For without them I never would have met you."

"You would have married Iolan and had a gaggle of children at your feet."

"You have already given me a child. A better son than any mother could hope for."

A massive son with sharp claws and teeth.

"Yeah. I feel the same. You are the love of my life, Red. You make it all worth it, but we are not going to die. Either of us."

The conviction in my voice surprised even me.

"How can you be so sure?"

"Because if it becomes plain that we will lose, I will knock you the fuck out, sling you over Mal's back and fly far away."

She pulled away, suddenly frosty.

"You would abandon our people to their deaths?"

I recoiled, aghast.

"Of course not. If it came to that then all of our people would already be dead! I won't leave even a single Bizhjerai behind to die if I can help it."

She returned to my arms, mollified.

"What about the other Clans?"

"Fuck the other Clans. There is only one Clan dear to my heart, and it has the most beautiful woman amongst their number."

She chuckled. "I never thought your ego was that large," she teased me with affection and I pinched her ass in retaliation. She gasped into my breast.

"You know I mean you. I am just a glowing freak, but you, you are a true beauty. And I love you so much."

"You are not a glowing freak. Well you are, but you are my glowing freak and in my eyes you are the most beautiful woman our Clan ever has had the fortune of having. Beautiful both inside and out." She reached up and pecked me on the nose.

"Now rest."

Despite my earlier fears, I did.

## Chapter 38

I stared at the page in the book, like I had for the last several minutes. This was it. I had finally found it! After all these months of searching, I had found the key to finally putting Grasax to rest. Excitement filled me with a rush that left me breathing hard. My thoughts churned. I reread the page, and then read it twice more. It would not be difficult. The concept was simple, but the weakness was well disguised. In order to let his mind enter the enchantment a channel had to be opened, one that could not be closed from within. The difficulty lay in ousting him from the outside, something that would have to be done in real time. I would have to connect myself to the enchantment, rip what remained of his soul from inside and toss him to disperse into the magic field all the while not getting trapped myself. It would put myself at risk, or whoever performed the ritual. It would have to be me. I was the most powerful magic user the Clan had. Kendall was more disciplined and more adept at casting spells but for this raw power would be much more important, especially against a foe that could steal your power for his own. Besides, Kendall would not arrive for weeks if at all. I was alone in the chamber I shared with Red, she was outside sparring with the warriors. For once I was glad for her absence for she would have talked me out of doing this right away. She would make me recheck my work and then insisting on being present. I loved her too much to risk her. Besides, her presence would distract me. No time like the present. I gathered the tome and rushed down to the cellar, all the while searching the keep with my magesense. I ducked into an empty room to avoid Anna who were approaching. I felt guilty for avoiding her since she walked with obvious intent in her steps, presumably searching for me with a message. I let her turn a corner before I resumed my trek. I avoided contact with anyone, which may have been foolish. If I failed Grasax would be free but if I told anyone they would undoubtedly rat me out to Red. The Clan was well familiar with my reckless streak and knew that Red would handsomely reward anyone who stopped me from doing, according to her, stupid things. Opportunistic bastards. The thought was fond though. I appreciated their concern, I really did, but sometimes it really got in my path. I deactivated the runes sealing the cellar the liche had been contained inside for so many months. After a short internal debate I sent my thoughts out to my son.

"Mal. I am going to try some magic I found in a tome. I am down in the cellars. If you don't hear from me in twenty minutes, send Red down here."

"Will it be dangerous?" His voice contained a note of concern.

"No. But it may backlash and trap me in the magic. Your mother can release me easily enough," I lied. I felt bad lying to my son, but that was a mother's prerogative.

"Do you need my magic?"

I considered his offer. "If you sense me dwindling, I would appreciate a boost."

"Yes, Mother. I will watch over you." I felt much calmer with him watching my back with his prodigious magical reserves at the ready. I opened the book and rested it on a field of telekinesis beside the table that was covered in runes. I would need to disable them, clear the table and inscribe new runes before Grasax gathered enough power to wake up fully. I took a deep breath and got to work. I severed the input channel from the fount and the spells containing the dagger faded from view and collapsed in on themselves. With a flex of my mind I shaved the top layer from the table in a rain of stone chips and erased the rune structure. There was no going back now. I hastily started inscribing the runes that would open the channel using a wand that focused the jet of flame. I copied the runes as fast as I could, but I could not afford to rush things. I kept a wary eye, and part of my magesense, on the dagger and the power levels within. The pull was weak at first but it grew rapidly as he soaked in the power that leaked into the room from the severed input from the fount. Shit. I should have warded the room first and severed the input further out. Power was swiftly pouring into the dagger, much swifter than I had planned for. Sweat beaded on my forehead as I increased the speed of my drawing. Even before I was halfway there I could feel the dark presence in the dagger stir and send tendrils of awareness toward me. The intent behind the darkness was still sluggish, not yet truly awake. My hand brushed one of the dark tentacles and it latched onto me like a viper. Power surged out of me and two more tendrils whipped out to grasp my soul. Fuck. Fuckity fuck, fuck. Cold gripped my hand and I nearly lost the grip on the short wand I used as stylus. I lanced out with my power, severing the tendrils but more shot out as he stole even more power. I slammed a barrier down in front of the severed rune channel from the fount and sparks flew from the contact. The backlash of the violent interaction made my head spin and I lost focus. My hand spasmed and burned a long furrow across the surface of the table, destroying part of the runes I had already carved.

"Mal! I need your power!"

Strength flooded me and I poured the influx into the barrier. My vision cleared and I erected a dome over the dagger, pushing the tendrils back from me. The assault lessened for a moment as the dark presence was rebuffed but then his assault redoubled as the tendrils lashed out across the dome.

"Mother!"

I had no energy to spare responding. It took all my focus to maintain the two shields and draw the rest of the runes out at once. I shaved off the damaged part of the structure and started over. Before I was finished hands pounded on the door.

"Kyra! Open up!"

I could not respond, only a mewling noise escaped my lips when I tried. Oh, this had backfired spectacularly and it was all my fault. I had been too excited to put an end to the undead liche that I had not thought it through.

"Stand back from the door, I am about to blast it down."

I felt her power flow and then the door rattled its hinges. I had activated the containment spell after I entered, just in case Grasax got loose. It would stall him for a few minutes at least, but it would also keep Red out.

"Kyra! Anjali, join me!" Alissa. I felt them work in concert as I drew the last rune. If they broke down the door I would be knocked senseless from the release of magic. The room was too small for me to hide from the explosion and I was still unable to make coherent sounds. I strained to maintain the shields. If I was distracted for even a moment and my shields failed Grasax would be loosed. There was only one thing I could do to salvage the situation. I slammed my hand on the activation rune and channelled my power. The room vanished around me, along with my body. Once more I floated in the darkness where I had defeated Grasax last, and there before me was the spectre of the man himself. He had stolen quite a bit of power. Dark ropes of power lashed out from him and I threw up a shield in desperation. The darkness coiled around it and writhed, searching for a weakness even as it constricted the shield to break it. I launched a stream of brilliant fire and the spectre dissolved. I blinked in surprise. No way it was that easy. I was correct. The darkness surged together and he reformed. He was immortal in here. It was impossible to defeat him here. Even if I did he would merely return to dormancy. There was only one way this could end. I fought my instincts and released the shield. The darkness recoiled from me in surprise, suddenly wary at my lack of defence. It was quite obvious that I had dispelled the shield willingly and I cursed. I should have pretended to be defeated, now he was suspicious that I had a trick up my sleeve. Not that I had sleeves in here, I did not even have arms. Or a body. Before he could figure out what I was up to I launched myself at the darkness, wrapping myself around it. It was an odd concept. I was surrounded in the darkness, completely enveloped but even so I tried to wrap myself around it. It was like turning myself inside out. I spread out and my edges started thinning, fraying. Power flowed into me. Malkareth. He was feeding me his power. My edges regained their solidity as I expanded but the darkness merely retreated. That would not do. He attacked again, tearing at me with claws of purest black. I let him rake my soul, allowing the darkness inside. He coiled within me in a perversion of intimacy. The tendrils sank deep, almost down to my core. He reached through my magic, sinking phantom claws into my very soul. I grabbed his claws and pulled him inside. I wanted more of him inside me. All of him. I pulled him deeper and with a silent clap of thunder all was bright white. Where there had been darkness surrounding me, only white remained. Only I remained. Grasax roiled inside me, lodging deep in my soul like a cancer. Power encircled me, trying to trap me. The enchantment! The dagger tried to claim me in its prison, like it had held Grasax. A low droning voice intruded on the silence. It beckoned me and I flowed toward it without moving. Grasax uncoiled within the brightness that was me, his darkness spreading through me like ink through water. He consumed me from within, growing ever stronger. Something snapped and I fell back inside my body.

"Kyra! Oh, dear spirits no, Kyra!"

My eyes opened and my vision was framed by Red and Alissa kneeling above me. I lay on my back on the cold stone floor. Their relief was plainly written on their faces. I sat up, but it was not me controlling my body any more. It was as if I was watching another through my own eyes. Grasax. He had wrested control of my body from me, even as he was consuming my soul. The only thing that sustained me was my son, pouring his power into me in a fading trickle. I screamed in silent denial. This wasn't happening. My friends had not yet realised that it was not me behind my actions and Red threw herself into my arms. Grasax hesitantly returned her embrace but gained confidence swiftly. A wicked smile curled my lips as he clutched her close. Then he started ripping the soul from her body. She was still healthy and undamaged and her soul was rooted firmly in her body, so he could not claim it in an instant. He drew it out of her, slowly at first but in ever increasing magnitude as it weakened. She gasped into my ear.

"Kyra?"

"Not anymore." My voice was dark and cruel. Red started struggling but his grip was too powerful. Alissa grabbed my arm and started heaving to release Red. I gibbered on the inside, fighting his leeching influence on me, cheering Alissa on and screaming in defiance and horror. He ignored both Alissa and me, focusing on stealing the life of my love. Red's struggle weakened and something snapped inside me. I roared and blazed with power as Mal poured the last of his strength into me in a great surge. I felt his presence fade from the back of my mind. Horror stunned me. I had not been bereft of his presence since he had crawled into my lap directly after his hatching. He had given his life to help me. I had been a fool! I thought I could destroy the liche on my own and now my son had paid with his life with my love soon to follow. There was no doubt in my mind that Alissa would be next, and then every man, woman and child of Clan Bizhjerai. Grasax would have no mercy on the people who had bested him once. Screaming with vengeance I lashed out at him from inside, striking at my own body in desperation. My fingers weakened and my death grip on Red slackened. She rolled to the side and the pull on her soul lessened into a small trickle. Her head rolled to look at me and a silent cry of triumph erupted from my core. Bolstered by the victory I redoubled my efforts. My power was waning fast, but so was Grasax'. One by one I gripped the dark tendrils controlling my body, pulling them into myself to join the darkness at my core. Each tendril I crushed back into him released a part of my body back into my control. I scrambled back from my friends to put distance between us. Alissa grabbed Red under her arms and pulled her away from me, watching me warily. I ripped the last of Grasax' influence from my body, weakening quickly. With him barely contained within my soul I pushed him out. He resisted with all of his might but the jolt of power my son had sacrificed himself to gift me was greater than what he had managed to steal. Slowly, ever so slowly I pushed him out of me. I excised him like pus from a cyst, slowly at first but then with a great burst. A cloud of darkness burst from my mouth and nose and even my eyes. The cloud dispersed quickly, fading away with a wail. A final silent scream of denial and he was gone. The silence in the room was only broken by my panting breath. Alissa watched me with wide eyes, still clutching my love. Red! I crawled over the stone floor, too weak to rise. Power still surged into the room from the severed channel and I drew on it deeply, replenishing my power now that Grasax' devouring presence was gone. Alissa put Red gently on the floor and stood before her in a protective stance with her knife drawn.

"Alissa, it is I. Grasax is gone!"

"How do I know that?"

"Remember what we spoke about after we disembarked from the Pioneer? How I told you my father died? That he was killed by the government when he could not work any longer? Grasax could not know that."

Her suspicious glare did not waver.

"How do I know he has not claimed your memories?"

I applauded her diligence, even as she stood in my way. I did not have time for this though, or rather Red had no time for this. I had absorbed enough power to stand and I struggled to my feet. With a wave of my hand Alissa was pushed up against the wall, her own magic striking the shield even as she hurtled across the room. The backlash from her strike staggered me, but the shield held. I rushed to Red, kneeling by her side. She was unconscious, and deathly pale but her breasts still rose and sank with breath. Her power was low, almost exhausted. Her soul was bleeding from the lack of ablative energy. I pulled on the channel and poured the power into her. I did not form it into a purpose, just sprinkled the power on her bared soul and it drank it down like a sponge. I kept pouring power into her until she was patched up and her eyes opened.

"Drink, Red. Drink the power."

She started pulling power on her own with a groan and I relinquished the control of the channel. I released Alissa and she charged me. I was too drained to stop her. She could kill me if she wished. I deserved it after my mistake. It had cost me my son and almost my love. She drew short when she saw Red's open eyes, knife still poised ready to strike.

"Kyra?" Despite her stance her voice contained a tiny trickle of hope. I nodded as tears trickled from my eyes.

"Thank the spirits!" She dropped her knife and threw her arms around me. "Will she be alright?"

"For now. Help me bring her to the fount. She needs more magic to heal."

Instead of grabbing Red's feet Alissa used her power to levitate my lover beside us as we walked to the courtyard. People were about their errands as if nothing had happened, and to the best of their knowledge nothing had. A few cast worried glances our way when they noted Red's levitated form but none accosted us with questions. In the corner of my eyes I saw a great red body lie motionless, as if sleeping. A pained cry was wrenched from my mouth and I fell to my knees at the sight of his dead body. He had given his all without hesitation to save me from my own hubris. I was stunned, numb. I wanted to crawl to him, embrace him. Stroke his scales and tell him that everything would be fine. But it wasn't fine, and never would be again. My life had ended with his and I was even deader than Grasax had been. That was when my magesense noticed the faint movement of his chest. Hope replaced the loss in an instant. He yet lived! He must have passed out before he could give me everything. The panic and hope of a mother rushed through my veins and I surged to my feet and easily overtook Red and Alissa. I dove into the fount, pulling the power inside as fast as I could. My veins blazed into their glow and my wounds lit up from inside. I threw out my arm and a crackling ray of power arced toward my son. It struck his scales with tremendous force and his body slid a few inches across the stones. The power soaked into his drained body like it had Reds. I increased the flow, feeling the agony of my wounds as the patches on my souls were strained to bursting. I did not care. I would give my life for his ten times over if I had to. His heart started beating more powerfully and within minutes his great eyes opened. His eye found mine and the relief within when he saw me almost unmade me. His presence bloomed in the back of my mind and I fell to my knees, unable to maintain my focus. He struggled to his feet and approached. Most of the fount bent toward him as he sucked it inside, only a trickle remained for Red to consume. It was more than enough for her relatively weak soul. Compared to Malkareth's bonfire she was but a candle, and I was little more than a torch. Red sat up, rapidly reinvigorating. She had not been hurt physically and as her power returned to normal levels she was practically restored completely. I stood by the outskirts of the fount, stroking the flank of my son as he lay down to feast on magic. Red pushed to her feet and stalked toward me, her face unreadable. I spread my arms to embrace her. The world tilted, my cheek stinging and ear ringing. She had slapped me! Her fist thundered into my ribs and the air left my lungs in a rush. I fell on all fours, resting awkwardly on my stump and struggled to breathe. Her boot slammed into my side, rolling me over onto my back. I rolled with the force of her kick, cradling my cracked ribs. I lay there panting, recovering. She towered over me, staring down. The sun framed her, casting her face in shadow and making her hair shine a brilliant red. Even when radiating fury she was the most beautiful sight I had ever seen. I eventually struggled to my feet and she raised her hand to punch me in the face. I did nothing to protect myself. I deserved whatever she chose to give me, and more. I had been beyond foolish. Her fist connected with my jaw and nearly dislocated it but I remained standing albeit hunched over and twisted to the side. I straightened my back and met her furious eyes. I refused to wipe the blood trickling down my chin from my split lip.

"What the fuck!" She screamed and hammered my chest. "How could you be that stupid! You scared me half to death!" She struck me again, staggering me. "I can't take this, Kyra. No more. No, fucking more. I'm done." She took several deep breaths. "We will discuss this later. In private."

I nodded numbly. Red turned to our son.

"Are you okay?"

"Yes, Mothers. I am fine. I just need to replenish my magic and I will be good as new. Mother, don't be angry at Mother. She destroyed the liche. I helped her." A note of pride coloured his last thought. Red smiled at him.

"You did well, son. I am proud of you. Her, not so much. Rest now."

"I will, Mother." A yawn stretched his jaws until it cracked and showed his double row of teeth. He was asleep even before his jaws clacked close but even then the magic kept pouring into him. Red turned to me.

"You. Come. Now."

I followed her meekly, knowing that the worst was yet to come. When we were alone in our room she remained by the door, refusing to look at me. The silence stretched on. I could not bear it any more and drew a breath to explain myself.

"Don't. I don't want to hear it. I have heard it all before. 'I just wanted to keep you safe, Red' and 'I could not bear to see you hurt on my account' and all that bullshit. Never again, Kyra, do you hear me? Never again. You include me in matters that involves us, especially concerning our son!"

I opened my mouth.

"No! You don't get to speak. Not now. I know you mean well, but did you even pause to consider what it would do to me to find your corpse down there knowing that I could have been there for you. Helped you? Well? Did you?" Her voice rose to an angry scream on her last words.

I looked away. I hadn't thought of that. I knew what it would have done to me if our roles had been reversed. It would have destroyed me. Completely and utterly. I realised how selfish my decision had been. If I only had explained to her what I would do I may have been able to persuade her to stay away. Why did I always rush into things without thinking? She sneered at my expression.

"It is clear that you did not even pause to consider me. You are a selfish cunt, Kyra. You don't respect me. I am not worthy of helping you. The great Bàs Marbhadair, always saving the world on her own." Her tone turned to one of mockery on the last sentence, dripping with scorn.

"No! That is not..."

"Shut the fuck up!" Her scream cut me off.

"I can't even fucking look at you right now. I need some air." She turned and ripped the door she had leaned on open. She paused and spat the words over her shoulder. "Don't you dare watch me with your magesense. I don't want your presence near me." She stalked out and slammed the door behind her. I sank numbly down onto the edge of the bed. I felt like shit. Like a piece of shit. I was a piece of shit. It was not that I had not included her in the ritual, it was that I had not even asked for her opinion. She was correct in all that she had said. Everything but one thing. I did respect her. More than anyone and she was worthy of helping me. I just loved her too much to risk her. I could not bear the thought of something happening to her. I would rather risk failure and death than letting her come to harm. I resisted the urge to track her with my magesense. I would respect her wishes, even though she had no way of knowing if I obeyed her command or not. The hours that followed was torment. Her angry words had hurt me, but only because I knew I had deserved them. Evening came and went and the hours dragged by miserably. I cried until I had no tears left, and then some more. Midnight struck and I stripped down and crawled into bed but sleep would not come despite my exhaustion. I tossed and turned in torment. Only an hour or two remained until dawn when the door slowly opened. Red entered and sat down on the bed, her back to me. She reeked of wine. She had never been one to drown her sorrows in drink. My actions had truly driven her to her wits end. I dared not speak but I knew she was well aware that I was awake. Her magesense, even drunk, would tell her that my eyes were open. Even without her magesense my eyes glowed brightly in the dark and would have tipped her off. Her words were slurred when she finally spoke in a low, weary voice.

"I know why you did it, and I know that you love me. But I can't keep this up any longer, Kyra. We have had this discussion before and you have promised not to do it. Each time you promise and each time you break it so don't even bother promising it again. Your actions belie your words. How can I trust you now?"

There were no words that could convey my feelings, my intentions. There was nothing I could say to repair between us what my actions had broken. I would have to show her. Truly show her. I reached out and put my hand on her arm and I surged out of my body. I did not merely reach out, I left my body completely and entered hers. In her drunken state her defences were weak and I slid around them delicately to avoid hurting her. Our emotional distress weakened our barriers and we joined into one being. Despite her anger she let me in and I bared my heart to her. My every thought, every emotion mingled with hers. She watched the events of the day play out in an instant from my perspective, from my reasoning to going behind her back to how the threat of her life had awakened the power to defeat the liche. Her soul was filled with hurt pride, fury, sadness, but most of all fear. Fear of losing me. I watched from her eyes as her memories played out. How she had been sparring with the warriors when Malkareth had suddenly surged to his feet, screaming into her mind that I was in danger. How her throat had seized in panic and how she had sprinted down to the cellar. How the door had blocked her and her panicked gasps as she battered the door down to find me lying on the floor. I had been dead. I wasn't breathing, my heart wasn't beating. My normally glowing veins were dark and cold and my eyes did not shine as they stared sightlessly at the ceiling. She had almost died then. Her own heart had stopped beating for several seconds and her world had collapsed around her. Then the glow had returned to my eyes and I had woken up and her relief had been unbearable only to have me try to kill her. Then everything was a mess until she woke up by the fount. I relived our fight before she stormed out. Her night has been as miserable as mine, if not worse, and my heart bled for her. Our souls separated slightly, enough to retain individuality but still conjoined emotionally. I found our bodies crushed together on the bed and I inhaled the scent of her hair that covered my face.

"I will never put you through this again, Red. I swear." My sincerity flowed through the bond between us and she listened guardedly. "I will include you in everything from now on and let you decide. I can't protect you from everything. I know that. You are a grown woman. You were wrong about one thing though. I do respect you. More than anyone. And that is why I can't bear the thought of my actions leading to you coming to harm but I see now that that is just as wrong as keeping you in the dark. We are in this together, if you take me back. Together, completely. If you die, I die. If you live, I live. If you hurt, I hurt. Now and forever. Your choice."

She was silent for long minutes and my heart sank. I had pushed her once too many.

"I told you before, Kyra, that I love you. Now and forever. And I meant that. I still do. But this have to stop."

"I know." My emotions flowed into her in a gentle flow and hers into mine. I felt her accepting my words, but not forgiving me. Beneath the acceptance lay a hard surface. She meant what she said. I had pushed her to the brink, dancing on the edge of a knife. Beyond was the point of no return. Her love crushed into me. Her fear was rooted in the thought of losing me. Of losing our son. I clutched her close, pushing the depth of my love into her soul. I would do anything for her. Anything she wished. I'd kill everyone in the whole world if she wanted me to. I would kill myself at her whim. I would even let her risk her life for me if she wished it. Resolve to be a better woman for her settled firmly into me, snaking its way into the very roots of my soul. Through our connection she could feel the change within me, and the sorrow it caused me. I meant it. Even though it would unmake me I would let her make choices that could lead to her death. I would fight her, I would try to dissuade her but in the end the decision was hers and I was a fool to have tried to take that right from her.

She watched the play of emotions inside me and then, like the sun breaking through the cover of clouds after a storm, she changed. A river of pure, unrestrained love poured from her to me.

"You finally understand."

"I do."

No words felt adequate. Her love was balm on my torment but I refused to let it go. I grasped it firmly, clutching it close. Using it to fuse the resolve to the bones of my soul. Red reached up and kissed the fresh tears that dripped down my cheeks. I could not hide the stream of revulsion at her foul, wine-soaked breath. She could not suppress a giggle.

"Do you see what you do to me, Kyra? You have driven me to drink."

"I am sorry."

She shut me up with a finger across my lips. "No more apologies. I feel the change in you, and you know where I stand. You won't get another chance. Now let us put this behind us and hope that it will never be brought up again. What do you say?"

I nodded. I was more than happy to move on, though I would not ever let go of this shame. It would help me to be the woman she deserved to be with.

"So Grasax is finally dead?"

I nodded, not trusting my voice just yet.

"Good. Then at least something good came out of this. Now I need to sleep, I am exhausted."

She dozed off almost immediately, falling into a wine induced sleep. Even though we may have resolved our issues for now, sleep would not relieve me of my pain that night.

## Chapter 39

The following week was miserable. Red behaved as if nothing had happened, but I could feel the tension between us. My actions had stretched the bond between us to the breaking point, and it would ache as it contracted back to its usual tightness. It was impossible to fault her behaviour, but it was there in the tiny hesitation before she touched me, in the pause before her lips found mine and when she sat next to me she was a little bit farther than she used to be. It broke my heart every day to know that I had caused this rift between us. Even the knowledge that the dangerous liche was dead did little to make me feel better and I found myself spending time away from the keep with my son. We ranged far and wide each day. I made the excuse that we scouted for sources of power but in truth I needed to occupy myself. If I didn't I would just follow Red around like a lovesick puppy and I knew that would only infuriate her. As expected, Mal and I found no sources of power, but one day on a long voyage east of Dun Traelak we encountered dragons in the distance. Gray dragons. Savistlin's flight. We turned around immediately. The Grays and the Reds had been feuding for two hundred years and we had no chance of defeating a fully grown Greater Dragon. Mal was far from fully grown. It astonished me how swiftly he grew. Within a year he would be fully grown, according to Serena the Dragonkin. Marius thought it would take longer and that he showed promise to grow to a stature to rival even the great Malkareth of old. According to them the old dragon had towered over all others, save for the behemoth patriarch of the black dragon flight. The Blacks were the largest of the dragons, but could hold the least magic. The Blues lived in the ocean, down in the deeps and rarely encountered. The Green dragons were wingless and dwelt in the jungles to the south. The Reds were the most powerful magical wise and the Grays were the most versatile. My thoughts were shattered by my son's roar and he rolled to his back and we fell. I glanced up, now down, as I was pressed into his back. Had he seen something? There! A family of elk had braved the plains. It was foolish of them to do it during the day, but dragons were not common enough for the large wildlife to watch the skies. The elk babies scattered but the patriarch of the group was simply too heavy to accelerate his body quickly enough. Wings snapped and we lurched around. Malkareth brought the creature to the ground with his hind legs, crushing the pelvis of the magnificent beast. A snap of his jaws and the elk went slack. I slid to the ground, leaving my son to feed. Judging by the size of the elk Mal would not be able to fly for some time with the weight in his belly. He would need to digest it first. Luckily he was not like other reptiles who could take weeks to digest their prey. I resigned myself to staying here for the night. It was already getting late. Mal ripped and tore the elk apart but despite his evident relish he saved me a generous portion of meat. I thanked him and started searching for wood to cook the meat. I was loathe to cook it with magic. I far preferred the taste of grilled meat. Out on the plains there were precious little wood to be had and I made do with grass. I cooked the meat with a combination of magic and the burning grass. It was not as good as a properly grilled meal but it was far better than anything I had eaten before leaving the Skylands. Mal grew drowsy after his meal, like he always did, and his great snores comforted me. I was secretly glad that he had killed the elk. It would give me an excuse to stay from the keep longer. I watched my sleeping son, marvelling at how he towered above me, even lying down. I still clearly remembered how he had stood in my lap, resting his paws on my shoulders as he licked my face that first night. He had been so tiny, so curious. Something in my magesense tickled my memory, and when I realised what it was my blood went cold. I focused on the part of him just behind his head in his neck. It was tiny, so small that I had not noticed it before. My magesense zoomed in on the irregularity. It was a rune, but a rune unlike any I had ever seen. It was so tiny that it would have been impossible to draw it physically. I looked closer. Even smaller runes surrounded it. My magesense flew across his body. He was covered in them, but the majority was concentrated around his head, around his soul. A portion of them looked familiar and I racked my memory. Where had I seen these runes before? With a lurch the memory sprang back. Grasax' dagger! Knowing where I had seen them my memories unfolded and the rune structures started making sense, piece by piece. The enchantment on the dagger was very familiar to me by now after months of study. Malkareth was similar, the runes forming a sphere of containment around his soul. I dug through the enchantment, slipping between the cracks in the runes. There was his soul, enshrined in the protective runes. Realisation struck me and I suddenly understood what the dragons were. They were not alive. No, that is not true. They were alive, very much so, but not in the same way as humans. Humans and beasts formed naturally in the womb, their souls springing into being as the magic field condensed in the burgeoning body. The dragons were created. Their minds were a spell, but not a structured spell like those I was familiar with. Instead of a set of formal runes that defined the behaviour of the spell the dragon soul was more a series of abstract concepts powered by magic. Someone had imagined them and willed them into being by raw power. Such creations were inherently unstable and unable to sustain themselves. That is where the surrounding enchantment entered the equation. It contained the artificial soul, stabilising it and making it practically immortal as long as magic was supplied to fuel them. It was almost like the bugs Red had worked on but on a much, much grander scale. Without a biological brain the entity inside had little direction, little volition. It simply was. Blood magic had wrought their bodies and the spellbeast possessed the body. No, possession was not the correct term. I had been possessed by Grasax, an intruder temporarily taking control of the form of another. This was more like habitation. The containment enchantment snaked throughout the dragons body, allowing the soul to reach out and control it. Someone had created the dragons, but for what purpose? The answer was obvious. To gather magic. It made sense. The way the dragons could absorb power in tremendous amounts but not use it for themselves. I should probably have leaped off instead of this sudden dismount. I tumbled through the air, thrown about in the turbulence left by his passing. I fell out of his slipstream, still tumbling wildly. I angled my wings to straighten my fall but were already too close to the ground. I maxed out the thrusters, skimming only yards above the ground. I shifted the wings imperceptibly, angling them down to increase the catch of the wind. The thrusters, now pointed more steeply at the ground stopped hurtling me forward, instead working to keep me aloft as my speed swiftly decreased. I alighted in the tall grass surprisingly softly and was left staring around me. That was easier than expected. I imagined it would be even easier from a higher altitude, giving me more time to adjust and prepare for landing. Malkareth flew in a large loop to turn and landed next to me. Red slipped off his back and embraced me.

"You did it! Was it hard?"

"No, quite the contrary. Shall we try again, or do you want to try your spell first?"

"You should rest a moment, let me run a trial."

She produced a gem from her pocket and it sprang to life in her palm as she activated it. A body formed around the gem, made entirely of magic and tiny wings unfurled. Mal watched it with interest. The little wings blurred as they beat and the bug wobbled into the air. It looked like a glowing bumblebee as it weaved through the air. It landed on Mal and started pulsing. After a minute it returned to land in Red's palm and it shrank back into the gem. Her eyes widened.

"It worked! I could see Mal as the source of power. It showed me what it had found!"

I stroked her back, congratulating her. It was a clever spell. I just wondered what good it would do only being showed the source. Not knowing where it was in relation to yourself would make it nearly impossible to find. I did not want to piss on her parade so I held my tongue. We climbed back onto Mal and we were soon high in the sky. Not as high as we usually flew, but far enough for me have ample time to adjust on the way down.

"Here I go again!" I told them both mentally. The mental equivalence of a kiss entered my mind. Instead of activating the wings right away as I had the last time I climbed to my feet on his rippling back. The muscles playing beneath his scales made for uncertain footing and the wind nearly ripped me from my perch but with some focus I could stand quite easily. I strode the few steps to his hind quarters and leaped off. The wind whipped me, but without the large windcatch of the wings I did not tumble. I plummeted through his slipstream and gained velocity. I spread the wings, not to their full length and angled them along my body. My headlong plummet turned into a steep dive and I gradually expanded the wings. My fall ended in a leisurely glide that ended by angling the wings to pivot my legs down below me and I fired the thrusters to absorb the last of my momentum. I barely felt the landing, it was easy as stepping off a stair. Mal joined me a moment later. Red slid off his back but instead of hurling herself into my waiting arms she scanned the skies. I was a little miffed, to be honest, that she ignored me but something in her face made me hold my tongue. Within a minute I noticed tiny specks of magic entered the range of my magesense. Her bugs. She had released them from the air and now they were finding their way back to her. Astonishing that she had given them the ability to locate her even though she had changed position since they last registered her. They landed in her extended palm and deactivated. Now she embraced me. It would appear that we both had achieved success that day.

## Chapter 41

I walked between the tents. It was like a dream come true, Skylander and Clansmen mingled freely. Bartering. Goods changed hands, and smiles were everywhere. Everywhere but on my face. The weeks had passed smoothly and Red and I were closer than ever. Our near-end-of-relationship fight and subsequent reunion had cemented our love. Each day I had ranged north with Mal, searching for Kendall, mom, and Marissa but they day where I had expected to find them had come and gone. Anxiety filled me. I feared the worst. I watched a Bizhjerai woman offer handmade garments to a Skylander who dangled a beautiful necklace from his fingers. It was no mere bauble, magic swirled around the gems and I could sense the runes engraved on the fittings. The Skylander accepted the knitted scarf, relinquishing his magic item to immediately rub his cheek against the soft wool. I remembered my first touch of wool. It had been glorious, and so different from the cloth produced from magic. Magical cloth seemed to be in high demand with the Clans. Leather was useful, but far from truly comfortable and it was very non-stretchy. I saw several Clanswomen wearing the snug trousers popular on the Skylands. It was nearly impossible to make leather supple enough to hug their hips and thighs like that. Only the finest doe-skin, scraped thin and tanned for weeks would fit like that. I saw an old scarred Ithlaki man trade horses for crystal tools and even a lone Reaver perusing the enchanted runeblades. I shuddered at the sight of the man. He had deactivated his aura and none of the Clansmen looked at him twice. Reavers were Clanless, but honourable ones. Their methods were gruesome, but they were respected. None wanted them as enemies. I turned a corner around a tent that offered no goods, only food in exchange for coin, and my belly rumbled at the smell. It was a stew, a glorious stew. The Skylanders had immediately embraced the style of cooking of the Clans, savouring the meat in particular. The Clans were not as interested in the fungus that the Skylanders had brought, but they respected its filling nature. It had not taken long before the meat and the fungus had married in a stew and the two sources of food had blended perfectly. The bland fungus absorbed the flavour of the stew and gave it a much needed thickness, broken by the rich flavour of the tender meat. I hoped that the two cultures could blend as perfectly, without the war I still was certain would come. But for the first time, I had hope. A tiny voice shrieked wordlessly behind me and I spun toward the sound, my hand falling to the grip of my revolver. What I saw stunned me senseless and brought me to my knees. A little girl, coming at me full tilt.

"Mom!" Marissa launched herself at me, folding into my arms as if she belonged there. And she did. I clutched her tight, tears stinging my eyes. "You're glowing! Just like Uncle Kenny said!" I snorted at Kendall being called 'Kenny'. His mother had called him that as a child, and he had always hated it. I stood up, bringing Marissa with me.

"I have missed you so much, little one."

"I missed you too, mommy." Mommy. The word brought the tears out in earnest. Just a few steps away stood Kendall, and beside her my mother. The world shrank to encompass just the three of us. Mom stared at me, both hands clamped over her mouth. Her eyes roved over me, my glowing eyes, veins. Over my scarred head and missing arm. She rushed toward me.

"Oh, my poor baby! My little girl! What have they done to you?"

I shifted Marissa to my hip, holding her in place with my arm and threw my severed arm around my mother. She cried and pawed at my back, crushing me against her breast. The world felt much safer there, cradled against her. Oh how I had missed her. Despite being a grown woman of almost thirty, her embrace returned me to the small child I had once been.

"I am fine, mom. More than fine, now that you are all here. I feared I would never see you again!"

"We feared the same, yet here you are. But you are damaged. My poor little girl." Her eyes hardened. "I assume that whoever did this to you are no longer breathing?"

"He stopped long before he did this." Her brow furrowed in confusion. Had her face always been this lined? She appeared to have aged decades since I saw her last. "Long story, I'll tell you later. Come, there are some people I want you to meet."

Still carrying Marissa I lead mom along. Kendall followed us silently, a happy smile on his face. Mom would not stop asking questions, nor did I want her to.

"Tell us what you've been through since leaving! Kendall have refused to mention anything, saying he wanted you to tell us yourself. The man is insufferable, almost as stubborn as you!"

I chuckled. "It is a long story, first I have a surprise to show you. I have a son, mom. You are a grandmother!"

Her face paled, but then her face settled into a sceptical expression. She eyed my waist and breasts. My armour was form fitting enough that it revealed that my waist was too thin to have borne a child and my hips were not wide from childbirth. Neither was my breasts swollen with milk but still the firm orbs of youth. I had not been gone long enough to meet a man, procreate and then give birth. Even if I'd fucked a guy as soon as I made landfall I would only have given birth a month or two ago.

"Is that... A dragon?" Marissa had spotted Malkareth, dozing on the grass outside of the large market camp.

"Yes." I sealed my lips shut as we approached. Mal noted our approach, even though his eyes were closed. Mother was hesitant to approach but when she sensed no wariness from me she gathered her courage and followed. I spoke to my son.

"Malkareth, this is my daughter Marissa, and my mother."

The dragon opened his eyes and lifted his great head from the ground. He looked first at Marissa in my arms, and then at mom.

"Sister. Grandmother. It is such a pleasure to finally meet you."

Marissa squealed in delight at the voice in her head and squirmed to get out of my arms. I let her go and she rushed up to the dragon, caressing his scales without any hesitation. Mom paled.

"Grandmother?"

I turned to her. "This is my son, Malkareth. I hatched his egg months ago and adopted him." I firmed my voice to overrule her protest. "He is my son."

Mom took one look at my face and swallowed. "Yes, I see he is." She turned to the dragon and stretched out a trembling hand toward the dragon.

"Well met, grandson." He sniffed her hand and then his forked tongue lashed out, wrapping several times around her arm. Despite herself my mom smiled. She would come to accept Mal as her family in time. Marissa finished her inspection of his forepaw and stepped purposefully toward his head. He lowered it down to peer at her. Her hair blew with the force of his breath.

"Brother. You are very pretty."

He chuckled. "Sister. It must run in the family."

"May I ride you?"

I approved that she had asked him directly, and not me. He is his own, not my pet. Mom had other ideas.

"Certainly not..."

I cut her off. "Of course she can, but it is up to Mal."

"I would be honoured to carry my sister to the heavens."

Marissa giggled. "Do you always talk like that?"

"Yes. It is the way of my kind." Marissa started climbing the dragon but I sensed someone else approaching our little congregation.

"Wait. There is one more person I want you to meet." I pulled Red into a one-armed embrace. "My wife."

"Wife?!"

"Yes, mother. Anjali and I are married." I gazed down into the shorter woman's eyes. "I love her."

Mom's face softened. "Then I will as well," she drew Red into an embrace. "Welcome to the family, Anjali. What an exotic name. It certainly fits your beauty. My daughter always did have a discerning eye."

Red's face turned the same shade of her hair. Marissa slid down to the ground and looked up seriously at Red.

"Does that mean that you are my mother too, now?"

Red fell to her knees and looked into the girl's eyes. "If you want me to, I would be honoured to be your mother. Kyra has spoken much about you, and about how much she missed you."

Marissa smiled brightly. "You talk like him," she pointed at Mal. "I like you. You can be my mother too." And with that, Red was a part of her family. Red remained on her knees, a stunned expression on her face as Marissa climbed her new brother. She kicked her heels into his neck as if he were a horse.

"Up and away, bro-bro!" Malkareth roared and leaped to the sky, swiftly shrinking onto the distance.

I pulled Red to her feet and had to steady her as her knees threatened to fold under her weight.

"What's wrong, love?"

"Nothing. Everything is just perfect. The look in her eye. She accepted me as her mother, just like that. It was humbling."

I kissed the top of her head. "She trusts me. She has known me for many years now and if I love you, she will to. And I do love you, more than you can ever imagine." I kissed her hair again. Mom watched our exchange with misty eyes. Tears flowed freely down her lined cheeks.

"Mom, what's wrong?"

"Just.. It's... You are finally happy. It warms my heart to see you find someone you love, and a place to truly call your home."

I left Red behind and gathered mom into my arms as she finally broke down. It was not tears of sadness, but tears of joy. And my own joined hers. My family was finally gathered in one place, and I wished dearly that it would never be otherwise. Through my magesense I could see Red and Kendall make awkward small talk, two strangers knowing that they better get to know each other. Two strangers, suddenly thrust into familial bonds. As I let my mom work though her emotions and stroked her back consolingly with my one remaining hand I saw them relax. Their discussion became lively and I just knew that they were speaking about magic. They would be fine, they had a major common interest and I knew that Kendall soon would be tutoring her. I would make sure he did. It pained me that I would lose time with her in favour of him. Some of my most cherished memories was me teaching her magic but I could not teach her anything more. I had taught her all I knew and she needed a new teacher. She would take to magical construction, Kendall's forte, like a fish to water. She would never be like me, a master of death and destruction. I realised that we were perfect for each other. I would tear down the old, paving the way for the future that she would construct. Mom stopped crying and stepped back, dabbing at her eyes with her sleeves.

"Now, Kyra, tell me all about what have happened."

"Soon. I'd rather Marissa was present to hear it as well."

Kendall joined us with Red in tow.

"That would give us time."

"Time for what?"

His eyes twinkled. "I have brought a gift. A possible solution to your problem."

"He has been working tirelessly on it, almost all his time has been spent on it. His boyfriend has been much vexed by the lack of attention."

I was doubly surprised. What problem? And also, boyfriend? I glared at Kendall.

"Boyfriend? Why is the first I hear of this mysterious man from my mother?"

His cheeks turned pink.

"He is an officer in the special forces. I may have neglected that his deployment to the Outside may have played a part in my decision to enlist."

Men!

"Tell me everything about him! When can I meet him?"

"In due time. First, the gift."

"But you are the ambassador the Clans? I can't ask you to leave your man behind!"

He held up his hand to silence me. Red watched our interaction with a fond smile.

"Relax, Kyra. He is the commander of my honour guard now. He will join us, never fear. Focus now, I come bearing gifts."

A large pouch attached to his belt drew my attention as he stuck his hand inside. He withdrew a large object composed of magic crystal. It was a replica of a skeletal hand, jointed and completely articulated. It was covered in runes and channels. The ends of the radius and ulna bones were severed and the elbow joint was missing.

"Is that what I think it is?"

"It depends on what you think. You have never been particularly known for you intelligence."

Red bristled at his off the cuff insult.

"Kyra is the most intelligent woman I know!"

He held up his hand placatingly. "Relax, sister. I tease."

Red jerked, mouthing the word 'sister' silently with an awestruck expression. She had gained many new family members in a very short amount of time.

"Sit down, Kyra. This will take but a moment."

I sat down on the ground, mind spinning. I had never in my wildest dreamed of something like this. I numbly offered my severed arm. Kendall produced two crystal screws from his pouch as he inspected the stump.

"This will hurt. A lot. Are you still adept at Blood magic?"

I nodded, knowing what he would have to do. He looked up at my mom and Red. "You may want to look away. This could get messy."

Mom did, making excuses that she would fetch us something to eat and drink. Red sat down on my other side and took my hand. She kissed it. I set my jaw and nodded for Kendall to proceed. He produced a small wand from a holster in his belt and an invisible blade of force erupted from the tip. It stung when he slid it beneath the skin of my stump and agony blazed as he flayed the end. I nearly crushed Red's hand with my own but I managed to not scream. I summoned my magic, cauterising the end of my arm to stop the bleeding. My vision swam from pain. My resolve not to scream failed when he cut half an inch of flesh from my arm, exposing the bone. I could feel Red's desire to interrupt but she held her tongue. I pulled on my Blood magic, forcing the broken vessels to stop bleeding and they scabbed over before our eyes. Kendall folded the skin over the wound, cutting precise holes to let the ends of my bones peek through. My Blood magic sealed the skin over the wound almost immediately. I could feel it pulling on my reserves already, consuming fat to restore the wound. Red would be disappointed at my diminished hips and breasts but hopefully I would not thin down the skeletal waif I had been. Kendall held a screw to my radius and his eyes flicked up to meet mine.

"This will hurt even more."

I nodded, eager for him to get this over with. The sooner it ended, the sooner the pain would fade. His magic twirled the screw and it dug into bone. I felt nothing at first, only vibration through my bone but a searing agony shot through my arm when the screw bit into the marrow. My scream echoed in my own ears. The process repeated itself with my ulna and left me breathless. I found myself lying in Red's lap, panting. The pain settled into a sharp ache, but it was manageable.

"We will let your Blood magic help the screws settle before we proceed. But first, the final touch."

His touch was gentle and he constructed rune channels from my body into key runes on the flat sides of the screw. The runes activated, kept alive by a trickle from my soul. He showed me how to connect the prosthetic arm to the screws and left it with me to decide when to equip it. I was touched. He had thought this up for me, and constructed it at great expense. Or at least it would have been back before I left. I had no idea how costly magic was these days. The surplus must have crashed the market. I could not help but laugh when I thought about the rich, fat bastards who had lost their income with the surplus. Blood trickled through the join of skin and bone but I did not care. It would heal before long. Mom returned with a large basket and the smell of the glorious stew reached my nostrils. We settled down for a picnic and before we were done Mal and Marissa rejoined us. The little girl hugged the leg of her brother, not being able to reach his neck and then skipped to sit down next to me. Her dark hair was whipped into a single, thick snarl. She sat in front of Red, scarfing down food and incessantly chattering on about her flight with Mal. With some prodding from me Red started untangling the snarl of her hair and gained confidence when the girl smiled over her shoulder. Before long mom told Marissa gently to be silent and let me tell my story. Marissa quieted and looked at me expectantly as she shovelled stew into her little mouth. I took a sip of the wine mom had bought, wine from Clan Azwail if I was not mistaken. There were no wine on the Skylands, only booze distilled from fermented fungus. I started to tell my story.

## Chapter 42

A swarm of Red's little magical bumblebees wafted toward the skies from the courtyard. Kendall had solved the issue of reporting back the location of any source of power. The little bugs now recorded their motions, and since the point of origin was know the location could be extrapolated onto a map. The process took some thought and calculation but could be performed swiftly enough. The swarm spread out, swiftly vanishing from both sight and magesense. I flexed my new hand. There were no sensation in it, but the sheer enjoyment of once again manipulating physical objects had not faded. I had spent almost an hour juggling a mug with it. The runes blazed with power, fed by my soul. The lines coursed across the surface, emulating veins with strands of telekinesis. A thought brought the claws embedded in the tips out with a soft clink of crystals. They retracted with another thought. Kendall had added them, knowing that I would approve of the hidden weapons. The first night I tried sleeping with the arm still attached I had shredded the sheets and scored marks down Red's side, and now I removed it each night before bed. I would not risk further harm to her. The scars on her side would forever remind me of the damage that could be caused by a careless moment. She bore me no ill will, and had persuaded me of that fact repeatedly, and vigorously with her body. I focused on the fount. It was almost completely gone now, all of the power siphoned to the various manufacturing processes that had been erected over the last few months. Guns, rifles, pistols, swords and axes slowly grew into being. Kendall had taken Red under his wings and she blossomed under her tutelage. They had set to construction almost as soon as we returned from the market camp. The keep was slowly transforming into a true bastion. We needed more power, the fount was no longer enough, hence the swarm of bugs to scout for more. I had barely seen Red what with her working so closely with Kendall, and I was left mostly to my own devices. If I had not known that he was happy with Tristan, his boyfriend, I might have been jealous but as it was I instead started to feel lonely. I had not broached the subject with my wife, not wanting to become the clingy woman who held her back. Even Marissa trailed after them constantly, soaking in the knowledge that escaped them to reach her ears. Mother had ingratiated herself with the Bizhjerai women, taking up a key position as chamberlain in the fortress. The Bizhjerai women, still unused to living in a keep instead of roaming the plains, had been inefficient in their scheduling and chores but mom sorted that out swiftly enough. Mal had grown large, and I had taken it upon myself to train a crew to ride him into battle. The few Clanspeople that showed aptitude for magic had been bound to him. Not bound like Red and me, but a bond that would let him fuel their magics when they were close. Kendall had fashioned him a collar, similar to my choker. Instead of storing the power in a stone it used his own personal power. We had discovered that while he could not cast spells himself, he was more than able to activate pre-cast spells and he could now manifest a lightweight armour almost instantly. His reserves of power were great enough that it hardly mattered how much it cost him. We had even experimented with mounting a cannon on him, but it proved too unwieldy to aim and reload in flight that we had let it dissolve. Instead his crew were outfitted with rifles similar to my own. Red had returned my rifle and smaller revolver with the return of my hand and she had claimed a newly produced one from the factory. Each of the Riders, as they were called, wore a collar with armour and harness. They were twelve in all, four women and the rest men. Marie, the blond woman who had first ridden Malkareth, were their commander. I had intended to assume that mantle at first but it was decided that I was too valuable as a fighter to waste my time commanding. They did have a point. I was the most powerful magic user the Clan possessed, or any of the Clans for that matter, and my power would be best served as artillery. The Valkyrie armour was beyond Kendall's knowledge to reproduce so the other Riders wore the same kind of armour I had before but he spent much of his time attempting to reverse-engineer the Valkyrie. The Riders stood lined up behind me, ready for a drill. I turned to Red and curled my fingers around her gorget. I pulled her close for a kiss. There were so little time left for just the two of us now. Despite my hope from the market the preparations for war had begun in earnest. Riders had been sent to the Chiefs, attempting to forge alliances. There had been no sign of animosity in any of the limited contact the Clans had had with the Skylanders during these last six months since the market. Every other month a party from the Clans ventured to the now semi-permanent camp to trade on the edge of the Elweyr Forest. I reluctantly pulled back from Red and she leaned forward as if to prolong the kiss. Without saying goodbye I turned toward my son. We had to get going. He stood up from his prone position and magic swirled around him. His armour manifested in a flash and I climbed onto his back. The other Riders joined me, locking their harnesses to his with snap hooks. Serena and Marius, who had recently returned to their Flight with the promise of a short return, had helped us forge the armour in the style that the dragons used. I was surprised when Red fastened herself next to me. She smiled at my confused expression.

"I was thinking I'd join the drill today."

"What about your work with Kendall?"

"He is tutoring Marissa today. I will not be missed."

"Then I will be glad to have you." I leaned toward her for a kiss but we were distracted when our son leaped to the sky. We shot across the plain toward the northeast. Malkareth launched into his now familiar movements. The Riders strapped to his belly fired their rifles on Marie's mental command, relayed by Mal to the others. The rounds arced toward the ground, leaving visible arcs of power. The rounds were crystal and set with a simple lingering light spell. Tracers, Kendall had called them, and they allowed the shooters to assess their accuracy. Since we had no targets, each Rider had to observe and make the adjustments themselves. They racked the slides of their rifles and fired again. When their five shot magazines went dry Mal rolled onto his back and we on his back fired. Unable to beat his wings while on his back we started to plummet. The Riders exhausted their magazines swiftly and rolled back on even keel and I scrambled down his side and hooked myself secure on the harness. The grass hurtled past below. Power arced from him into the Riders, and from them into their chargers. Their magazines reloaded slowly, for none of them could yet channel much power at any one time. That would change with practice. I let out a stream of heat downward, scorching the grass in a long black furrow. I did not really require the practice, but the Riders needed to learn what to expect from me and each other. Red swung down beside me, joining her efforts to mine. Where I poured power into my spells, laying out swathes of destruction on the innocent grass her attacks were more subtle precision shots. Bolts of heat, force and of other nefarious purposes destroyed shrubs and bushes. We gained altitude and in the distance I saw a camp of one of the Clans. It was odd. Despite being almost noon the camp appeared deserted.

"Mal! Take us closer to the camp."

"Yes, Mother."

He banked his wings and we looped toward it. In a minute we hurtled past it. It was indeed deserted. I reached up and unsnapped my hook and fell to the ground. My Valkyrie wings set me down lightly in the camp. What I had not been able to see from the air became apparent. Blood stained the sides of the tents and the ground was a churned mess of footsteps. One of the fires was spread out, as if someone had fallen across it. There were no bodies, nor anything of worth remained. Mal touched down beside me, the Riders disembarking and fanning out through the camp. Each Rider covered another with their rifle while they advanced, leapfrogging through the camp. I had taught them that. Standard Guard procedure. The Riders returned and confirmed what my magesense had already informed me of.

"The camp is empty, Bàs Marbhadair."

"This is an Ithlaki camp," Marie informed me.

"Where are the people?`What happened here?"

Something shone in my magesense and my heart fell. I needed to confirm this with my own eyes. I walked through the camp, the Riders and Red following me warily. They could all sense the fury emanating from me in waves. I squatted by the object and fished it out of the grass where it had been hidden. The aggressors had made sure to clean up after themselves, but this detail had been missed. I rolled the crystal casing around my palm.

"Skylanders." I spat the word as if it burned my mouth. Gasps and words of outrage met my pronouncement. The war had begun.

Iolan arrived at Dun Traelak within the week, howling with fury. His people had been slaughtered, and he was out for blood. He pointed at me where I stood next to Red's father.

"Her people slaughtered mine. I demand blood!" Spittle flew from his lips with his words.

"And you shall have it, Iolan. In time," Red responded firmly.

"This atrocity can not go unanswered!" The young Chief was incensed.

"Winter is coming. We can't start a war until spring. You know that."

"The war has already started!"

"Iolan is right." The man stared at me in surprise. He had not expected agreement from me. "But so is Chief Bizhjerai. Patience is a virtue, now more than ever. We are not ready to face the Skylanders in open conflict. We do not even know if this was an act of war."

"They murdered innocent Ithlaki!"

"It may have been rogues, or a band of mercenaries. We do not know if the Skylands sanctioned the action." I tried to remain calm, but he was making it difficult.

"See how she defends her kin! We can't trust her!"

"Shut your mouth, Iolan. Kyra have proven herself time and again. She harbours no good will for her former people. She is Bizhjerai." I appreciated Red's support.

"Of course you would come in support of your whore! You are as corrupted as they are."

Her father snapped and his voice was a roar of fury.

"You forget yourself, Iolan. That is my daughter you are speaking to."

The Ithlaki paled, realising his overstep. "Do you expect me to just swallow the death of my people? Let the Skylanders prey on my kin? My lands?"

"Of course not. But we need to know what happened. We cannot rush into an ill-conceived war, especially if it is as Bàs Marbhadair say and the raid was the actions of rogues!"

The Chief turned to Kendall. "What does the ambassador say?"

My friend was silent for a long minute as he considered the situation. "I was not informed of any overt action against the Clans," he held up a hand to forestall Iolan's angry retort, "but I would not expect to be. I am of course officially required to blame the action on rogue mercenaries but in truth I know as little as you. I would not put it beyond my kin to think they could get away with a raid such as this."

"They took everything. Even the bodies? Why would they not let us burn the dead as is our custom?"

Kendall drew voice to speak and missed my shake of the head. Do not tell them, Kendall. Don't.

"The Skylands is completely devoid of meat. All we have is the fungus that grows in the caves."

I closed my eyes, but not before I saw Iolan recoil when he drew the inevitable conclusion. Even Red's father paled. Red herself did not react. I had already told her about the cannibalistic tendencies of Skylanders.

"Monstrous!"

I could not disagree. The thought that had once enticed me now filled me with revulsion.

"You must calm down, Iolan. There can be no victory now. We must gather our strength, build weapons. Arm ourselves. Even then we can't defeat the Skylanders. They have soldiers and weapons beyond your imagination back home. They will come in an unstoppable river if you provoke them. We need the Cities."

"The Cities?" he scoffed, "they will not come unless the enemy is at their doorstep. They care not a horses balls about us!"

He had a point, but what else could we do? Any victories won against the Skylanders already on our shores would be a temporary one. When the full war machine of the Skylands turned it's vengeful gaze upon us we would be swept away on it's fury.

"What about the dragons?" I shot a glance at Serena who had stood silently by, content with observing. "Will you come to our aid?"

"I can not speak for my Flight, but it is possible. I must speak with the Elders."

"Fuck the Elders, and fuck the dragons. Clan Ithlak will stand on its own, if you all are too cowardly to fight."

Iolan turned and stalked from the room, his Huscarls fell in line behind him. I watched him leave through my magesense, directly for the stables. Apparently our guest did not intend to stay for supper.

"Will he abstain from attacking the Skylanders?"

The Chief looked doubtful.

"Perhaps. Probably not. Fuck that pompous little prick, he will bring death on all of us!"

"What can we do, Father?"

I had a suggestion, one the Bizhjerai would not approve of but I had to voice it. "We can kill Iolan. Install a new Chief in his stead. A calmer one."

Red shook her head. "The whole Clan will be in uproar. Any Chief in opposition of retaliation will not have any hope of getting elected to succeed him, let alone living through the elections. Clan Ithlak must be howling for blood."

I saw only one recourse to postponing the war until spring. "Then we must move at once. We must destroy Clan Ithlak before they provoke the Skylanders into action."

"No," Red's father, my father in law, spoke the word. His voice was weary, but resolute. "Clan Ithlak is large, and powerful. We will need them as allies in the coming war. We can't spare their warriors, nor our own that would fall in such a futile battle."

I threw up my hands. "Then what the fuck are we to do?"

"Prepare. We need more weapons, and armour. Hope that the Skylanders focus on Clan Ithlak to buy us time. The Ithlaki can take the brunt of the fighting while we gather our strength. Clans Azwail and Irileth have already pledged support to Bizhjerai. With them I am sure that Clan Druknar will follow and they will in turn bring the Olnar with them. Even two of the Reaver bands has expressed interest in fighting these newcomers."

Red scoffed. "The Reavers will fight anyone."

"True. I don't care as long as they don't fight us."

"You speak the truth, Kyra. Ambassador Kendall, is there any chance that you can speak to the Skylanders to divine the truth behind this unprovoked attack?"

"Possibly. But I am not certain that they will allow me to return if I travel to Utopeia."

Utopeia was the name the Skylanders had taken to call their rapidly swelling outpost. I spoke up.

"We can't afford to lose Kendall. He is too important to our preparations."

"Agreed. We must assume that this was a wilfull attack and act accordingly, short of attacking ourselves. Pray that Iolan does not act rashly."

The meeting ended and Serena rushed to find Marius. They would return to their Flight and consult the Elders. This was a proper shitshow.

## Chapter 43

Thankfully the winter snow struck early and hard, and drove the plains into a forced tranquility. Clan Ithlak was locked into their winter holds and I hoped dearly that the chill would cool their tempers and lust for vengeance. Red's bugs returned with the locations of many minor crossings of ley lines and I spent a few days with Kendall poring through Grasax' library. He learned the procedure for opening a ley line crossing swiftly enough, the true issue lay in funnelling the power to Dun Traelak. Of course, we could raise manufacturies at each site, but it would be much more efficient to route all power through a central nexus. Taking inspiration from the artificial ley line that powered Utopeia, Kendall, Red and I worked to reproduce it. The receiving end took almost a month to design and grow above the shield tower, but it was finally finished. Malkareth flew us to the closest crossing and we ripped it open in less than a day. The fount that exploded from the earth was less than a tenth of the fount at the keep. But it was one tenth more power at our disposal. We sowed the seeds of the containment spells and the artificial ley line and left it to construct on its own. We would return the day after to inspect it and possibly review the process before we proceeded to the rest. The next day the enchantments showed promise, and the process was sound. A month later we had nearly a dozen supplementary founts spread out across the Bizhjerai lands, and several more swarms of scouting bugs ranging farther for more. We had more than doubled our power input but it was not enough. Weapons and armour spilled from the manufacturies but it was not nearly enough to arm even Clan Bizhjerai, let alone the other Clans. When the snow melted Clan Ithlak was bound to go on the offensive, and after that it was only a matter of time before open conflict ensued. Each fount took almost a week to connect to Dun Traelak, most of that time took no effort on our path though and we could work on other things while we waited. All we needed to do was to rip the crossing open and initialise the enchantment. It would construct itself in a pace determined by the power output and then all we needed to do was to return and align the extruder toward the receiver. Some of the farthest founts required relays on the way, like the ones reinforcing the long ley line arcing from the Skylands to Utopeia. Those founts took even longer to connect. I wondered if we could somehow disrupt they ley line from the Skylands. If we could rob Utopeia of power much of the impetus behind their military would fade. The same went for our war machine though. Our own lines of magical supply was as vulnerable. My only consolation about that was that since neither I nor Kendall knew how that could be achieved, short of destroying the relays or the founts themselves, neither would the Skylanders. Besides, they would have to find them first. That would not be too difficult once they lay eyes on Dun Traelak. All Skylanders could see magic, and they could simply follow the artificial ley lines and destroy the origin. After much consideration we decided to send Malkareth out to spread the Riders throughout the holds. We needed more magic users to counter the Mages of the Skylands and their magical contraptions. Training a Mage was slow work, but to bring them to level of proficiency of blowing things up was swift. Them growing in strength was the slow part and the Riders all had copies of a training regimen of my design that would push them to the brink if they followed it. I knew that many of them would burn out if they followed it, but time was not on our side. It pained my heart to know that Clansmen whose only desire was to help would die as an effect of the punishing pace set out by the training but it had to be done. We needed as many magic users as was possible come spring. The Riders were proficient enough in magic to start their training before moving on. We even sent Mal with an emissary to the closest of the Cities, still weeks away by horse, with a plea for aid but we were not hopeful. When the snows started melting we had enough supplementary founts to rival the power of Utopeia and Dun Traelak had grown almost twice in size to accommodate the manufacturies. Kendall had taken to the skill of melding magic with matter as a fish takes to water and most of our constructs were composed of granite instead of magic crystal. A second wall far beyond the first towered to the sky, twice as high and thick. Cannon ports studded its surface and Bizhjerai warriors trained daily in their use. I was saddened by the loss of innocence of the Bizhjerai and I wondered what the future held for my people. Gone were the days of peacefully roaming the plains, the occasional raid of a rival Clan the greatest threat. The age of industry had finally caught up with them and they would never be the same again. Along with industry, the attention of the Cities would follow. The goods produced by the Clans would be of interest to them. But it was better than the alternative. To be crushed under Skylander heels. The tools of war churned from Dun Traelak and caravans braved the melting snow and the spring floods to distribute them among the Clans. Clan Ithlak received the first shipment. We were convinced that they would make the first move against Utopeia and we wanted it to be as effective as it could. We received no word of thanks, but the caravan returned intact and without it's cargo. The Riders were finally outfitted with Valkyrie armour but the time it took to produce it was not cost effective to outfit any more of our warriors with it. Only a few chosen were gifted with the precious armour, mostly commanders and their messengers, those who needed to move swiftly across the battlefield and where horses where not suitable. The snows faded but the plains were sodden with water. The mud would not allow horses firm purchase. The weather did not prove our ally, and the sun burned the plains. In mere weeks the ground would be hard enough for war. By this time, most of us longed for it. Not for a lust for battle or glory but for an end to the wait. The waiting had us all on edge. I read the reports of Clansmen burning to death when they pushed their magic beyond their capabilities. One young woman of Clan Azwail erupted so violently that her entire village burned with her.
