I read each report with a heavy heart but that one unmade my resolve. I cried through the night while my wife stroked my back, making comforting sounds. The first shot in retaliation was fired some weeks after the spring celebration, the Buknalia. It was a festive occasion, wine and fermented milk flowed freely but the event was subdued. It was odd seeing the Bizhjerai and Azwaili guests dressed in traditional Clan garb among the manufactories. The impending conflict weighed heavily on the festivities and it was a much more subdued celebration than last years had been. I spent as much time as I could with my family, particularly Marissa. I had a feeling that I would be too occupied come summer to spend any time with her. She was a lovely girl, full of youthful optimism. The harried looks of the Clan did not seem to affect her and she greeted the world with a bright smile. Wherever she went the stressed people relaxed and she left a path of smiles in her wake. She was often seen with Malkareth, speaking silently as they played. It was odd seeing the massive beast playing with the little girl, and it warmed my heart to see my children get along so well. It was at such a time Red found me, gazing out a window at their play on the inner courtyard. She slipped her arm around my waist and rested her head on my shoulder as she watched our children. She had truly become Marissa's second mother. She had even begun teaching Marissa the way of the spear, against my will. I did not want Marissa's innocence marred with the art of war. Not yet. That would inevitably come soon enough. But Marissa so dearly wanted to be like her mothers, and it broke my heart. I could not deny her any wish, a smile from her crumbled my resolve and I agreed to let Red train her. I reached up and played with my wifes hair with my crystal hand. I brought a strand to my nose and inhaled her scent, like I had so many times before. It was there the news reached us. A breathless messenger found us and reported that Clan Ithlak had sent out a war party a week past. They had been encountered by Bizhjerai scouts far from their winter hold and the scouts had taken days to return. I swore and ran for the courtyard, asking Mal mentally to order the Riders to attend. Red was hot on my heels, Valkyrie armour more than half formed around us already. Malkareth stood ready, already armoured and waiting. The Riders appeared one by one, gliding on magical wings or sprinting between the buildings. We mounted up and off we went. By this time the Ithlaki warband may already have struck, depending on if they encountered any Skylanders. Utopeia had constructed farming outposts on the plains just prior to the snows. There were no doubt in my mind that it was one of these that the Ithlaki aimed to destroy.

We found their trail near their winter hold and it was easy to follow. Hours later we found them, but we were too late. The attack was already over and the Ithlaki were rounding up prisoners. The farming village was not large, it could not have held more than a couple of dozen people and most of them lay dead on the ground. Only a handful of Ithlaki had fallen. The attack had been entirely unexpected. Mal landed and ran the final stretch on foot. I leaped from his back, advancing ahead with my Valkyrie wings. I was already shouting when I landed.

"Iolan! What the fuck?" I already knew what the answer would be. His men were armed with our weapons and armour and they tensed when I stalked near. The young Chief sneered at my approach.

"Bàs Marbhadair! How good of you to join us. Unfortunately for you, the battle is already done. Victory is ours!" His warriors cheered. I wanted to strike him. Instead I clenched my fists and drew a deep breath.

"You call this a victory? These people were farmers, not warriors! It is like slaying babes in the cradle!"

"They were Skylanders. That alone makes them deserving of death, one far less swift as this." He stared at me meaningfully as he said the words. I would not let him provoke me into reckless action.

"They have not offended you, or hurt your people. They are innocent."

"There is no such thing as an innocent Skylander. Is there?" He aimed the last question at the kneeling man beside him. The Skylander paled and sputtered but were too scared to form words. I felt for the man. He must have been a poor worker back at his home, come to Utopeia for the promise of land to till and food for him and his family. And now it was all dashed to ruins by this impetuous fool. I nearly struck him then, but the damage was already done. There were nothing to gain from fighting him and his men now, except to alienate Clan Ithlak.

"Let these people go, Iolan. They are of no further threat to Clan Ithlak. Let them go as a sign of good faith, and I will speak to the Skylanders. This situation can still be salvaged. I will explain that it was a misunderstanding."

"But it was not. They attacked Clan Ithlak, now they will pay the price. These Skylanders are not so impressive, they hardly put up a fight."

The full scope of his idiocy was revealed to me. He thought all Skylanders were like this, weak and ripe for the plucking. He thought that his easy victory here was an indication that he could take on the Skylands on his own. "I will not let them go."

I squared my jaw. "You will."

He raised an eyebrow? "Or else? You will do what? You will do nothing! Like you always do." He turned his back on me, addressing his men. "The great Bàs Marbhadair, cowering behind the walls of Dun Traelak! She comes here to make idle threats while Clan Ithlak fight her battles. She brought these Skylanders here, let her deal with them!" He spun around and pulled a dagger. My hand fell to my revolver and I took a half step back. He reversed the dagger and offered me the grip.

"Prove where your loyalties lie, Bàs Marbhadair. Kill these weaklings."

I stared at him in incredulity. Did he really think that I would do this?

"Iolan, stop this madness!" Red had joined me and the Riders spread out on either side of me. Malkareth towered behind me, a deep growl coming from his chest like the roar of a distant waterfall. Iolan swallowed, suddenly nervous. But then his face set into a stony expression.

"Se how she shirks her duty, refusing to do the dirty work herself. Very well. Once more Clan Ithlak shall to what the Bizhjerai will not."

He pulled a pistol from his belt and aimed it at the head of the man cowering at his feet.

"No!"

Before I could launch myself at the man the weapon bucked in his hand and the man at his feet toppled sideways in a spray of blood, bones and brains. A woman further down the line screamed but she was silenced by the blade of one of the Ithlaki warriors. The slaughter unfolded before my eyes, the prisoners put to the sword by the once proud Ithlaki. Men who had fought valiantly by my side against Grasax and his cohorts now ruthlessly murdered defenceless farmers. It was over quickly, the last Skylander bleeding out onto the budding grass. There was no going back from this. The war would erupt in earnest. In the distance I saw a figure lowering a looking glass from his eyes and hastening away. A Skylander lookout, or possibly a survivor of the attack. We could still catch him if I sent Mal after him. The Skylanders wouldn't know what had happened. But they would know enough. They would eventually find the outpost and the slaughtered occupants and they would know. There had been enough death this day already. Suddenly weary to the bones I signalled for the Riders to mount up. The moved without their usual crisp alacrity, reluctantly withdrawing from the fight. I followed Red onto the back of our son.

"You will pay for this Iolan. Either by their hands," I nodded in the direction of Utopeia, "or by mine. One day you will pay."

"Take us home, son," I thought at Mal and he launched to the skies, leaving the site of the slaughter in the dust. My emotions trickled through my bond and into Red and she embraced me from behind. There was no going back now.

Red modified her bug spell so that they would be able to send a pulse of power to the nearest fount. From there it would piggy-back through the ley line to a receiving spell in Dun Traelak. I distributed a swarm of the bugs across the Elweyr Forest surrounding Utopeia. They would notify us if the Skylanders left in significant numbers. The Clans was already in the process of herding the buffalo out on the plains. We could not afford not to. They were the primary source of food for the Clans and we could not rely on the fields surrounding Dun Traelak to feed them all. The herds would be vulnerable to attack, each loss to the Skylanders would be keenly felt in the bellies of the Clans. Each herd was accompanied by contingent of heavily armed warriors, but we did not have enough men to spare to guard them all properly. We had to rely on our network of scout bugs and the Riders to reinforce any herd that was assaulted. I was sure that the first stages of the war would be one of resources. The Skylanders would have to bleed our herds and destroy our artificial ley lines. Only when we were weak of hunger and magic starvation would they strike at the heart of our might. Dun Traelak. We were at a severe disadvantage. Utopeia had lines of supply to the Skylands, entirely protected by the ocean. The Clans had only one means of striking at it: the Riders. We could not risk it. If we were lost then we had no way of swiftly reinforcing any defence of the herds. The ocean and forests were patrolled by more than just the Hand of Glory, several smaller Skyships watched the area. If the dragons would support us then perhaps we could do something about that. Or possibly the Cities, who according to Red possessed similar Skyships that were powered by steam and gunpowder.

I was playing hide and seek with Marissa, but my heart was not truly in it. The poor girl had not yet fully grasped the acuity of my magesense and there were no place in Dun Traelak she could hide that I could not find within minutes. I made a show of searching for her anyway. I would not spoil her fun by heading straight for her.

"Where could she be?" I cried out loud as I made a mock showing of peering between two buildings. A girlish giggle, partly muffled by the thin wooden wall of the stable, reached my ears. I could not help smiling at her enjoyment. I entered the stable and I could hear her gasp. With my magesense I saw her excited expression and she clamped both hands over her mouth to force herself to not make a sound. She was hiding on the hayloft and could see me plainly. I made sure to avert my eyes when she peeked around the bale she hid behind. I stalked silently toward one of the empty stalls.

"Ah-HAH!" I leaped around the corner and made a show of scratching my head. I could feel Red focusing on me from our chambers and her amusement and affection for us both trickled through. I grasped at the encouragement, one of the few happy aspects of bleak days. I blew a mental kiss through our bond. A shockwave slammed through the keep, setting my skin atingle. The signal!

"Marissa, come down from the loft. I must go!"

"But mooom..."

"No buts, young lady. The Skylanders are on the move!"

She gasped and before I knew it she slid down the ladder and embraced me tightly.

"I don't want you to go."

I knelt down and hugged her. "I know. But I must. Our people are in danger and only mommy can help."

"Will mom go with you?"

I could already sense Red rushing through the castle.

"Yes, I believe she will." I was awarded with a bright smile that belied the tears brimming in her large eyes.

"Then all will be well. Mom will take care of you."

I chuckled despite myself and mussed her hair.

"Riders! Mount up!" The mental call slammed into me from my son. The Riders were already congregating from where they had been. They had all felt the signal and knew what it meant.

"Now go! Find grandmother, stay with her until we return." Marissa dashed away and I sprinted out toward my son. He was already armoured and the Riders were snapped in. He shot to the sky and I caught up on a surge of my armour. I rarely went out without it fully manifested. I landed on his back and engaged my hook into his harness. Marie was right beside me, breathing hard. We shot out across the plains, bound for northeast. I smiled wryly at Marie.

"Do you think my son would approve of you riding another man than him?"

Her response was a the mental equivalence of sputtering.

"Please, I can sense the remnants of your previous activities seeping down your legs."

I did not mention that I had noticed her fucking a Bizhjerai warrior behind the kitchens even as I was playing with my daughter. Such sights were common for us gifted with acute senses. You learned to tune it out with time. The blond warrior blushed beneath her half-formed helmet.

"Who is he?"

"He is no one. Just one of the warriors that caught my fancy."

The tone of her thoughts told me that he was most definitely not 'just no one'. She fancied him. I had not recognised his face, he must have been one of those recently rotated to the keep from one of the roving bands.

"Kyra, leave the poor woman alone," Reds' thoughts were full of amused reproach.

"Yes, dear."

We flew in silence for a few minutes. "His name is Tanyi."

"Do you like him?"

"Yes. I have not known him long, but he is an honourable man."

"Good. I would not have expected less of you. I pray you find happiness together."

A slow smile lit up her youthful face. How odd that she would strike me as youthful since we were of an age. I felt so much older than my roughly thirty years.

"Oh, I think that we will."

I hoped they both survived the coming war. I hated the thought of young love snuffed short. I feared that we would not arrive in time, but my son was fast. What would take days by horse took a mere hour on the wings of a dragon and the battle was in full swing when we arrived. A hundred and fifty or so Skylanders were arrayed against the Clansmen. They were Azwaili, and they had the terrain at their advantage. They had retreated onto a hill and had erected a barrier made from carts and wagons. The Skylanders had no cover and the low ground, but they outnumbered their opponents by a small margin. These were not Guard or special forces. A disorganised mob of mercenaries faced us. They were too spread out for us to do much from the air.

"Mal! Go low, drop us behind them. We need to break their fire to let the Azwaili charge!"

Mal dropped suddenly toward the battle. On my command the Riders leaped from his back and fell upon the unsuspecting enemy. We struck the ground hard in a combat landing and shields erupted around us as we straightened up. Some of the mercenaries had sensed the flare of magic when our thrusters engaged and turned to face us. I raised my rifle, aimed down the sights and squeezed off a shot. A man fell, a bloody crater in his chest. The Riders chose their targets carefully, firing on those who turned to engage us. Each man that fell soon rose to fight his fellows. I had remembered how efficient a distraction the zombie rounds were and had made sure that the Riders carried several of them. Explosive rounds tore apart the areas where the Skylanders were too tightly packed. My magazine went empty and I dropped the rifle to fall to hang by the strap behind my back. I drew my revolvers and charged, trusting that the Riders would join me. Shots struck my shield but it was powered and projected by my armour and I suffered no backlash. My revolvers sang a thundering song of destruction, and mercenaries died. Their formation broke and the Azwaili warriors leaped their barriers. They swiftly formed a line and fired a volley and the lines of mercenaries broke down completely. Mercs did not fight as a unit. They did not have the training for it. On the Skylands you fought every man for himself, unless you were Guard or special forces. The Azwaili charged as one. That was when Mal entered the fray. His great speed took some time to turn around but he had finally entered his first battle. Worry for him warred with the rush of battle. I saw his momentous landing bowl over a cluster of mercs, crushing several underfoot. A swipe of his claws ripped two mercs apart and his great jaws crunched down over a woman. Her body burst apart in his mouth and he tossed the corpse disdainfully over his shoulder with a flick of his neck. It hurt me so to see my gentle, beautiful son stained so. I would much rather he spent his life prowling the sky, hunting what he would eat. Instead he was here, fighting in the war of humans. I holstered my empty revolvers and drew my sword. The battle was already mostly over, but there were still Skylanders left standing that needed killing. The Azwaili struck the survivors when I cut down the second mercenary to oppose me. There were no more foes for me to fight. A few survivors were fleeing, running as fast as they could for the hills. One fell, shot in the back by Marie. The rest were set upon by my son. I turned away from the slaughter, trusting him to finish the fight. I took stock of the situation. None of the Riders were wounded, their shields had protected them and I sensed no pain from my son. The Azwaili were not as lucky. They had been set upon a for a good while before we arrived. They had lost a dozen warriors and almost double that were wounded, but would live. Almost everyone bore scratches and minor wounds. Red ordered them to withdraw back into safer lands, to be replaced with a herd with fresh protectors. I knew she doomed some of those men who would replace these, but such was war. These warriors had done their part, for now. The Riders mounted up and we returned back to Dun Traelak to await a new alarm that was sure to follow soon. I was worried about what killing humans had done to my son, but he was excited. He speak about the battle, reliving the moments with the excitement of youth. I remembered that I had been like that once, as had Red. She was as silent as I was, except when she spoke praise in response to one of his exploits. I told him to be silent a moment while I addressed the Riders.

"Riders, attend me!"

I felt their focus land firmly upon my thoughts.

"You all performed admirably, just as we trained. I am proud of your all. Unfortunately there will be more events like this. Stay vigilant." On a whim I added. "We Ride."

A mental murmur of 'We Ride' followed my pronouncement. In a flash we were back home and I had barely dismounted when I was informed by a warrior that another signal had sounded almost as soon as we left. He told us of the location and off we went again. I was sure that we were too late this time, our other battle having taken too much time. I was correct, we found only corpses and the herd gone. We followed the trail of the herd and found them being herded back to Utopeia by a large contingent of Guard. The Riders were a support unit and even with Malkareth on our side we would not be able to defeat such a force. It rankled within me, but I gave the order to leave. The Skylands had already won this battle. Expectant faces turned to dismay when when they saw our expressions upon our return.

## Chapter 44

Such was the month that followed. No two days followed without at least one attack on the herds and at first we completely destroyed the attackers. The Skylanders were quick learners and they soon learned to keep a wary eye to the skies and retreat at the first sight of dragon. Without the support of ground troops it was futile to chase them. Instead we had to let the Skylanders leave to harass another herd. The Chief organised parties of skirmishers to patrol the plains bordering Utopeia to harass and bleed the raiding parties to lessen the burden the Riders had to carry. They were highly effective. The Clans knew the lay of the land, and they had horses. The Skylanders had no cavalry, only infantry. The patrols struck fast and hard and vanished just as quickly without fear of retribution. Each attack claimed dozens of Skylander lives at the cost of only a few Clansmen. Each death of our own was keenly felt while the Skylands had an endless supply of willing soldiers. It would take time to ferry them over from the Skylands though, and time was our ally. Each day the herds grazed unmolested the fatter the buffalo got and the more food they would bring to the warriors of the Clans. Clan Ithlak burned more farms, but were punished harshly for it. They overextended in their hubris, and paid dearly for it. Utopeia reacted to our harassing tactics by increasing the size of their raiding parties and included Mages with their forces. That turned out to work somewhat in our advantage, since large parties meant that they were less manoeuvrable and more predictable. It also packed them closer together so that the Riders could truly unleash the devastation held within our weapons. Malkareth excelled in breaking apart packed formations and our magic ripped men and women to shreds. I lost count on how many just the fourteen of us killed, the dozen Riders, Red, and I, but it must have been in the hundreds. None of us had yet suffered a single wound. The Valkyrie armour proved effective. It was only a matter of time before we faced the special forces, and I dreaded the day. Our hastily trained Mages proved effective at what they did when faced with common soldiers, but the Skylander Mages outclassed them completely and we lost many during the bloody summer. Almost all that we had trained during the winter were dead before even half the summer had passed, but those that survived had been forged in the crucible of war and were to be reckoned with. The Reavers who had joined us proved to me our most devastating weapon once they closed on the enemy. Their auras dissolved even the armour, weapon and clothes of the opponents, leaving them naked and defenceless to face the onslaught of their weapons and magic. I saw one surrounded by mercenaries from the back of Malkareth and the Reaver stole their gear and souls and single handedly killed more than a hundred of them. It was too much even for a Reaver and he Archoned before I could do anything to aid him. His furious spirit, held together by his stolen magic alone ravaged the remainder until he was spent and faded away. I knew that Grasax had created the Reavers centuries ago and resolved to find the secret behind their creation in his library. I was sure that such an impressive spell would be documented there. There were more Reaver Enclaves hidden out on the plains, and I sent out riders to find them to invite them to join us. They proved very useful indeed. We lost a score of herds before the summer ended, and the fighting died down with the coming of autumn. It would be a harsh winter. The Clans could not afford to lose that many beasts. The Skylanders had not gone unopposed. The Riders burned most of the harvests before they could be shipped to Utopeia. The Skylanders would have to rely on supplies from home, but the fungus farms were dimensioned to feed the Skylanders that had left even before they did. There would be food enough to allow them to make it through the winter. Only the transportation to Utopeia may prove a problem. At the very least, every shipment of food was not a shipment of materiel of war or soldiers. Red's bugs proved instrumental in our defence. They gave us enough warning to react to any excursions of the Skylanders, and she sent a swarm of them into the city itself to scout. Many died, burning when they struck shields or were plucked from the air by concerned Skylanders but many made it through. When winter fell and the plains grew dormant once more we were fed steady reports on the happenings in Utopeia. Manufacturies sprang up to replenish their weapons and ammunition now that food had to be shipped from the Skylands instead of the fuel of war. Almost a year had passed and there were no sign of the dragons. Serena and Marius had not returned and we resigned ourselves to the fact that we were on our own. The harvest of grain had been plentiful, too far from the border for the Skylanders to assault, but it would not be enough to feed everyone until spring. Kendall made attempts to cultivate the Skylander fungus using spores from the dried rations that remained from when he and his men had joined us. The fungus grew rapidly when supplied ample magic and the frequent harvests may be enough to bolster our stores to last the winter without rationing. How the other Holds would fare, I did not know. Clans Bizhjerai, Azwaili and Ithlak had suffered the worst at the hands of the Skylanders since their territories were the only ones that bordered directly with Utopiea. When the first snows began to fall caravans from the other Clans arrived with gifts of meat and wild berries and other edibles in recompense for us taking the brunt of the assaults. It did little to lift my mood. It had been a hard year, and many lives had been lost. But it was just the beginning. Things would get far worse before there were any hope that it would get better.

## Chapter 45

The few short months of autumn passed, and the chill in the wind spoke of early snows. That would keep the Skylanders in Utopeia, no doubt, but would slow the Riders to harass their settlements. Despite my reluctance to attack poor farmers in the freezing cold I had resigned myself to the necessity. My old, cold pragmatism was resurfacing and I did not like it. I steeled my heart and tried to embrace it. Red noticed the change in me and I could feel her heart breaking for me through our bond. I had come a long way from the troubled woman I had been, but I was regressing from the stress of warfare. She had opened me up to the joys of life and now I was starting to shut them away. It was temporary though, or at least that is what I told myself. After the war everything would return to normal or I would be dead and then it would no longer matter. The break in the fighting lulled the Clans into a sense of security and the mood of the keep lifted steadily. A first thin layer of snow fell. It barely stuck to the ground but it was enough for Marissa to play with. We built small snowmen together and the little witch actually stuffed snow down my shirt one morning. With a mock growl the fight was on. I chased her down the courtyard and filled her trousers with icy cold as she squealed with laughter. Then her treacherous brother joined the fight and to my great surprise he sided with his sister. I suppose he rooted for the underdog. His great paw pinned me to the ground, gently but firmly, and being unable to move my daughter packed my shirt with snow even as I cursed her out. We were both shivering and blue of lips when we retreated back to our chambers. Red looked up from the scroll she had been perusing and saw our dishevelled appearance. She let out a sigh of exasperation but she could not hide her amusement at our antics from me. Her love dripping through our bond warmed me even more than the water of the bath she forced us both into. I had extended the tub even further back when Malkareth still lived with us in our chamber, he so dearly loved to soak in the warm water. He had recently discovered warm springs in the mountains to the east and he spent many of his nights there, soaking in the warmth. I splashed water at Marissa in retaliation for her snowy attacks outside. She returned fire immediately and then the war was back in full swing. Red was disturbed by our play and stood by the edge of the tub, her arms crossed. She was not truly cross with us.

"Children. Behave!" I exchanged a glance with my daughter and an unspoken truce settled between us. Then we both reached for Red. She had no time to react, only a widening of her green eyes before we pitched her headfirst into the water, clothes and all. She flailed in the water and resurfaced sputtering. With wet snarls of hair across her face and wide eyes she looked like a drenched cat. I gathered her close and attacked her face with kisses. She relaxed against me and chuckled in defeat before she settled down into the tub, leaning back into me. I curled my arms around her, caressing her side with my crystal fingers. It was a perfect moment, a rarity in this troubled year. My wife, daughter and I enjoying a simple bath together. I realised that this is what life was all about. There was nothing more important than family, those you loved and who loved you back unconditionally. Our roles was suddenly clear in my mind. Marissa and Malkareth was the future. He was the power, the foundation this family stood on. Red was the builder who built our future, and Marissa showed promise to take up her mantle. I was the protector who would let them work in peace. I was a force of destruction, always had been and always would be, but that was not always a bad thing. For those opposing me, certainly it was, but for my family it was necessary. I would destroy anything that threatened what my family built, and for now that was the Skylanders. I would kill them all if it let my family live in peace and I would kill them all gladly. Calm resolve flooded me. I would bear the guilt of any atrocity willingly, happily even, if it safeguarded their future. Marissa was overcome by the heat, her small body warming up much swifter than mine and she climbed out of the tub to cool down. I was not entirely sure on which date she had been born but she must have passed into her thirteenth year by now and had started blossoming into a woman. Her body was no longer a wiry block any more, her hips had started to widen and her flat chest had started swelling slightly. If she kept developing at this rate she would turn into a curvy seductress before her eighteenth year. I longed to watch her grow up. She would find a boy and fall in love and have children. Or find a girl and fall in love and adopt children, like I had. It was still too early to tell where her preferences lay. I would do everything in my power to make sure that she survived and was free to live her life as she saw fit. I just hoped that she would not turn out like me, to become a destroyer. There were already too many like me in this world. It needed more Reds, or Kendalls. I remained in the tub for a long time, clutching my wife. She sensed my mood and she remained in my arms to comfort me. The odd acceptance that trickled from me to her puzzled her, I could sense it, but I did not wish to articulate my feelings just then. I just wanted to be in the moment, with my wife in my arms. It was two weeks later when the snows began in earnest and the Bizhjerai finally relaxed. It would be impossible to wage war on the plains in the thick cover of snow. We were awoken before dawn by the alarm of the sentries. The long blast of the horn awakened me immediately and I rushed to the window, followed by a sleepy Red. A dark shadow crept steadily closer over the thin snow cover and the air was dotted with larger shapes. My heart sank and settled firmly in my stomach. The Skylanders had braved the cold, and they had come for a winter siege.

## Chapter 46

There was nothing we could do as the enemy army approached. Only Clan Bizhjerai resided in Dun Traelak and it would appear that the full might of Utopeia had come to our doorstep. The snows would keep the other Clans in their Holds until spring, while the Skylanders would be supplied by Skyship from Utopeia. We had no hope of opposing them outside of our walls and shield, so we did the only thing we could. We reinforced the shield and watched the approaching army warily from within the relative safety of Dun Traelak. There must have been almost ten thousand people outside our walls, not counting the crews of the Skyships in the sky. The Hand of Glory had covered their advance, towing the artificial ley line behind it. The Skylander camp grew quickly into a small city of lodgings, even a wall protected them from any forays. The magic field projected by the Hand was not as powerful as ours, but it hardly mattered. There were no parley, no attempt at negotiation. The Skylanders had come to rip the heart out of the Clans. Without the weapons and ammunitions spilling forth from Dun Traelak the rest of the Clans would fall. It was only a matter of time. We had enough weapons in our stores by now to arm every man, woman and child of the Clans but the weapons were useless without people to wield them. Their camp completed within days and sheltered from the cold by the shield projected from the Hand the Skylanders settled down to wait. Would they attempt to starve us out? We had supplies to last most of the winter and once the snows melted the other Clans would come to relieve us. It would be a tough fight, but with their aid I was certain that we could drive them off, though we would have no hope to wipe them out completely. No, the true attack would come when our supplies dwindled and we were weak with hunger. Then they would try to break us and claim the Keep for their own, or destroy it and flee back to Utopeia. Without Dun Traelak fuelling the war the rest of the Clans could be dismantled almost at will. A tense game of patience started as the days passed. The Hand tested our shields at least once a day with a heavy bombardment of her cannons but she had no hope of breaching us. I watched the magical fireworks with a knot in my belly as the thunder of guns split the silence of winter. I watched the Skylander camp for hours every day, trying to catalogue their strengths and weaknesses. Most of the combatants seemed to be militia. Armed civilians with little training. They would pose little true threat to our trained warriors. It was the mercenaries, Guard and special forces that worried me. And the Skyships, never forget the Skyships. If our shield failed they would be able to punish the fortress from the air with virtual impunity. I convened with Red and Kendall and discussed it. Kendall immediately started working on anti-air cannons, but without a proper way of testing we could not truly now if it would work. Life returned to normal inside the keep and the laughter and apparent contentment of the Clans surprised me. It was astonishing what you could get used to. Again I contemplated taking my family on the back of my son and flee south to the Cities but I knew that none of them would follow me. Nor would they ever forgive me if I drugged them and stole them away in the night. No, we were in this for the long haul. Our food stores dwindled when the days grew warmer. Both sides of the siege grew desperate and the day for the final confrontation was rapidly approaching.

I was in the cellar, working with Kendall on a special kind of ammunition for our anti-air cannon when Red's thoughts intruded on my mind.

"Kyra! Skyships!"

"They're attacking?"

"No, from the south! Get up here!"

I got a sense of her general direction. She was behind the keep, in the narrow valley behind Dun Traelak. I had been worried that the Skylanders would attempt to ferry warriors there with their Skyships to assault us in the rear but they must have realised that the valley was too narrow to get enough men there swiftly enough to have an effect. I rushed to the surface and joined her. Sure enough, in the skies on the horizon several shadows were approaching. Thick smoke belched from smoke stacks on the sterns and told us that it was not Skylander ships. Skylanders did not fuel their engines with coal, but with magic. The Skyships from the south were all smaller than the Hand of Glory. The Clan rallied and formed up for battle as the Skyships touched down in the narrow valley. Great doors slid open in their sides and men and women in strange garb leaped to the ground. Long leather coats and skull caps adorned their forms and their boots were made of a glossy material unknown to me. They carried swords and pistols but they spared our assembled warriors a single glance before they set to unloading crates. A man I recognised emerged from the bowels of the ship. He was Bizhjerai! The emissary we had sent to the Cities more than a year ago. We had thought him lost on his travels. He rushed toward us, followed by a man in a particularly large hat. His blue eyes played over me, taking in my glowing stature and crystal hand and apparently assumed that I was in command. He reached out a hand and gave me rakish smile. I shook his hand like Bizhjerai warriors, forearm to forearm. His brow furrowed at the unexpected grasp but he swiftly rallied.

"Honoured Clan Bizhjerai! I am Commodore Raistlin, commander of the Fists of Heaven!"

"Kyra Zorantis. This is my wife, Anjali, daughter of the Chief of Clan Bizhjerai."

Raistlin showed no surprise at the introduction, he must have been briefed by the emissary.

"A true honour to stand in the presence of warriors of such high esteem. I have heard many stories about you, of your prowess in battle and ferocity in love both. I do so enjoy stories of love and death! I have come bearing gifts of food. When I was told of your plight against these 'Skylanders' my heart broke and I could not stand idly by."

"He means that he saw opportunity and took it. The man is a mercenary," the emissary clarified. What was his name? Hulor, if memory served.

"Alas, good Hulor speaks truth. I am but a humble sword for sale, but I hope that my gifts is well received. And pave the way for future relations, eh? Pray tell, what do you think of my ships? Glorious, are they not?"

I was stunned by the golden bullshit that spilled from this man’s lips but Red saved me from composing a reply.

"They are truly a wonder to gaze upon. Will you lend their support against our enemies, Commodore?"

"Ah, precisely the matter I wish to broach, but sadly my lips are parched from our journey. May I trouble you for wine and rest and then we will broach subject once more. Please, accept my wares as a gesture of good will."

The Commodore offered Red his arm and she took it and led him toward the keep.

"Your gift is well received. Let me take you to my father. I am sure that equitable terms could be conceived before this day ends."

I stared at my wife. How had she learned to speak like him this quickly? I did not trust these people, not yet, and I opted to remain to watch them. The southerners joked and laughed as they unloaded their ships and a small wall of crates swiftly stacked up. I waved for the Bizhjerai to carry them into the keep to replenish our stores. I took a crate for myself and opened it. Dried foods were stacked high. I recognised meat, but I could not tell from what manner of beast. The rest I had no clue what they were. Some round, hard pebbles the colour of mud, grain and long dry stalks composed the rest. It all looked edible. The southerners was a jovial lot, easily drawing the taciturn Bizhjerai into conversation. Smiles covered the faces of the warriors as they worked side by side with the mercenaries. I inspected the Skyships. There were only four of them, and they were smaller than the Hand of Glory. There were eight Skylander ships, not even counting the Hand. I hoped that these ships would be at least able to distract the Skylander ships if our shields failed. I looked to the sky behind me. One of the smaller of the Skylander ships had drifted closer to observe the new arrivals. The reports of our replenished stores would undoubtedly spur the Skylanders into action. Their greatest advantage was our impending hunger and now robbed of it they would have to either try to break us, or retreat. I was hoping for the latter.

It turned out that Commodore Raistlin was quite the entrepreneur back at his home. He owned several companies, several larger than the Fists of Heaven. One of his largest ventures were a trading company, and he was here with the Fists to aid us in exchange for exclusive trading rights if the war was won. When asked why he did not favour the Skylanders whose exotic goods would bring a greater profit he just laughed and claimed to appreciate the underdog. Besides, the Skylanders were the aggressors and had shown no indication of trade. They were conquerors. The snow was starting to melt rapidly during the heat of the day, but the chill that night brought froze the water into slick cover of ice. The Skylanders would have to make their move, attack or retreat, soon.

## Chapter 47

My premonition proved correct. The alarm went up in middle of the night. So it was to be a night time attack, when most of the defenders were asleep. I sprang from our bed, leaving the warmth of my wife behind. My Valkyrie armour started manifesting before I was out of our chambers, Red hot on my heels. Marissa had already been instructed to find mom and hide with the rest of the noncombatants in the cellars. I burst out onto the courtyard and stumbled. It was not the slick ice that betrayed my footing but rather the fact that one of our artificial ley lines had collapsed. The relay in the distance, bereft of its supporting magic, crashed slowly toward the ground. Another ley line vanished, followed by another. One by one the founts on the north side of the mountain range died. The Skylanders had prepared. They stole more than a third of our power input in the span of minutes. Say what you will about the Skylanders but they were very well synchronised. I could feel our shield weakening before the backup power store gems kicked in. It was almost too late. The Hand of Glory opened up with a full broadside, lighting the night up in flashes. The other, lesser ships joined their big sister. I could hear the whistle of the projectiles approaching and the impact shook the foundations of the Dun Traelak even though they crashed against the shields far above our heads. The night lit up as if it was the middle of a summer day. A mesmerising shower of sparks slipped through the weakened shield and trailed smoke and magic as they fell onto the stones. One warrior screamed as a bright spark struck his shoulder and burned clean through him, erupting from his thigh to melt the stone of the courtyard. First blood belonged to the Skylanders.

"Take cover! The shields will hold for a while yet!"

I put action to my words and manifested a shield of my own. I leaped to the top of the wall and from there glided to the outer wall. I wanted the Skylanders to see me. The vaunted Dragonbane, facing her former kin in defiance. Malkareth joined me, standing beneath the wall and resting his forelimbs on the top as he gazed out across the Skylander camp. I hoped that at least one Skylander heart clenched in fear at sight the Dragonbane and the Wings of Death as my son had been known amongst them standing unflinchingly before the bombardment. Red joined me moments later. All orders had been given, now we just had to wait. The shield recharged before the next volley, the diminished input augmented by our stored power. It was only a matter of time before they battered our shield down. The amount of power that had gone into the construction of the ships and their ammunition was staggering. It was enough to reduce the keep to rubble in a matter of hours. I spent the the rest of the night and whole day after on that wall, defying the thunder of guns. Our shields held up and when night fell my family retreated back to the keep. There were no point remaining there when it was too dark for the Skylanders to see us. Kendall found me on my way to bed.

"Kyra! I have dire news. If they keep this bombardment up then the shields will fail before noon tomorrow."

I spat out a curse. "And if they halt for the night?"

He shrugged. "At the current rate we recharge? Maybe to nightfall, maybe a couple of hours more."

"Fuck. Tomorrow we fight, then."

He nodded solemnly. "Tomorrow we fight."

"Inform the men, make sure that they are ready. How many did we lose today?"

"Just the one. The others learned from his death to take cover despite the shields."

I rubbed my hand across my eyes wearily. "What was his name?"

"I don't know."

"Find out. I won't have a man die whose name I don't know."

Kendall bowed, actually bowed, and murmured, "Bàs Marbhadair." He turned and left and I stared at his retreating back, shocked. I shook myself and pushed the door to our chambers open. Red was sitting on our bed, her face in her hands even as her Valkyrie armour dissipated. I set my own to dissolve and sat down heavily beside her.

"How bad is it?" Her voice was low, and weary. It had been a nerve wracking day.

"The shield will fade tomorrow, at noon or nightfall depending on if they keep up the bombardment through the night."

As if to mock my words the thunder of artillery rumbled through the keep and light flashed like lightning through our small window. "Better get some rest, Red. As much as we can with this fucking noise. It will be a long day tomorrow."

"No."

"No?"

"If this is the last night we have together, if the worst would happen tomorrow. If this is it, I would make the most out of it. I would have my wife one last time."

Our lovemaking was desperate, mournful and frenzied. The second bout was slower, more tender. I made sure to love every part of her body, within and without and she returned my affections. The thunder of guns roared through the night, but we did our best to overpower them with our love.

There was precious little sleep for us, or for any of the defending warriors. Through the night I had sensed a great many Clanspeople engaging in similar life affirming activities that I had been with my wife. I had observed tender moments between Kendall and his man, and Marie and hers. I harboured no guilt at my voyeurism. I needed to see that there were still tenderness in the world. Something worth fighting for. I was crossing the courtyard when a shot rang out. It was too close to be a Skylander. I spun around, drawing my revolver. A man lay sprawled on his stomach, one of Kendall's honour guard. Another of the guard stood behind him, smoking rifle still aimed at the body. His hands were trembling and his eyes were wide.

"What is the meaning of this!" I stalked closer, aiming my revolver at his chest.

"He was going to destroy the shield spell. He was still loyal to the Skylands." His voice quavered. "Is he dead?"

I focused my magesense on the body. He was not breathing. I nodded.

"Fuck! I did not mean to kill him, I sought only to wound."

I got all up in his face, pushing his rifle out of line with a brush of my arm.

"Are there any among you who share his sentiments? Answer me!"

"One or two, no more."

"Name them! Tell me!"

"Gaius. Merkhan."

"Where are they?"

He sealed his lips stubbornly shut and I pushed him onto the ground. He found himself staring into the wide bore of my revolver.

"Where?!" The gathering crowd started at my unexpected scream.

"Barracks. I saw them last in the barracks."

My finger tightened on the trigger, but his friend lay cooling on the ground behind me. That was proof enough of where his true loyalties lay. His suspicion at his friends gave them lesser credit. I had no time to divine the truth in the matter. The shields were of utmost importance. If they failed we would fight, but if they were destroyed from the inside... The resulting release of energies would kill hundreds and throw the rest in disarray. The nexus of power was too volatile to risk. I realised that we had a fatal flaw in the design. If the Skylander ships broke down the shield, and then fired on the tower... The result would be much the same. I stalked toward the barracks.

"Find Kendall," I barked at a nearby woman, "bring him to me. Hurry!"

The door to the barracks crumpled around the blow of my magic and sprung from shattered hinges and the honour guard inside scrambled to rise. My weapon spoke and Gaius' head burst apart. The other guards stared with open mouths as his body toppled to the floor in a rush of gore. Weapons, never far from hand, primed and rose hesitantly in my direction. Me revolver swivelled to point at Merkhan but their commander, Kendall's man, stepped in line.

"What is the meaning of this, Dragonbane!"

I had no time for this, even now Merkhan was edging discreetly toward the rear exit. My power exploded out of me, tumbling the men to the floor. Merkhan did not get out in time, my shot took him between the shoulders and his torso erupted in a fountain of blood and mangled organs. He tumbled headfirst into the wall with a sickening crunch and slid down the wall into an ungainly heap. A large smear of blood marked his passing.

"Anyone else harbouring plans of sabotage? Well? Anyone?"

Shocked silence streamed from the stunned soldiers. None dared rise from the floor. I spun and left them there. A group of Bizhjerai eyed me warily.

"Watch them! Don't let them get close to the tower."

Kendall came running. "What the fuck is going on?"

"Your men tried to sabotage the tower."

"What?!"

"They are dead now, the rest put under guard. We have greater concerns now."

I explained the weakness in our defences and his face paled. We rushed into the shield tower, personal shields protecting us from the turbulent energies within. We worked furiously for hours as the bombardment rained down outside. We rerouted the power to form new storage stones deep in the earth beneath our feet, working through our magesenses. The channels were inefficient and leaked power but speed was more important that efficiency at this point. We needed to move the large concentration of power to a more protected site. We took a risk and modified the spell in ignition-time. The channels would close if the stream of power became too swift. It would mean that the channels had ruptured with the destruction of the tower. Even as we worked I felt the shields weakening. I left Kendall to finish the work and burst out into the midday sun. I looked up, confirming with my eyes what my magesense had already told me. The shield cracked with each impact, the rifts slow in healing. Segments collapsed and shards rained down, evaporating before they struck anyone. A projectile soared through the opening before it could close and struck the side of the inner wall. Screams erupted when stone shards sprayed those nearby but there were only superficial wounds. The shields would not hold much longer. Just a few volleys later the shield collapsed and the enchantments in the tower burned out and flickered. We were unprotected. A roar reached us from the Skylander camp.

"Man the walls! Protect the keep! The Skylanders are coming!"

A horde or Bizhjerai emerged from their hiding places, sprinting toward the outer wall. I joined the mad rush and leaped to the top of the wall, my Valkyrie wings bringing me ahead of the throng. The Skylanders were rushing closer to take advantage. With them they brought cannons, mortars and large treaded vehicles. Thick crystal armour plated their sides and large cannons protruded from their fronts. The Bizhjerai manned the cannons along the wall, already loaded and primed to fire. The Skylanders approached maximum range, a distance drilled into the minds of each defender. With our elevated position we would outrange the Skylanders, and we were well protected behind the wall. For now. The Skyships were already drifting closer and lower to adjust their aim. Before long they would be in position to pummel our walls. Where the fuck were the Fists of Heaven? I searched the sky behind us. There! The southerner Skyships were rising, large propeller fans spinning up to propel them toward the Skylander ships. They may be strange people, but cowardly they were not. I just prayed that their distraction would be enough for us footsloggers to see off the ground assault. The armoured vehicles surged ahead of the Skylander army and the Bizhjerai gunners scrambled to adjust their aim. I had never seen these vehicles before, they must have been a new invention. The Bizhjerai fired and purple smoke belched forth with the sound of thunder. Hundreds of cannons fired along the length of the outer wall, most of the shots going wide. Some struck a vehicle and scored deep lines in the armour, but none penetrated. Some of the round balls skidded along the ground to plough into the Skylanders rushing closer behind. Blood sprayed as limbs were severed and men and women died. The fallen were crushed into the frozen earth by the boots of their companions. The Bizhjerai reloaded but the tanks were in range. They responded in kind. The wall shook with the impacts, but the hard granite absorbed the force in showers of shaved rock. It would take more than that to breach these walls. The Fists of Heaven blocked the sun when they passed overhead. The tanks stopped and pivoted to the side, shielding the Skylanders behind. Their turrets turned to face the wall and fired again. One of the tanks were blown apart by the Bizhjerai response, but the burning husk remained an obstacle. A tank fired and I reached out with my power, throwing the shot to the ground where it exploded harmlessly. Others with sufficient power joined me, lashing out at the incoming shots with their minds. The Skylanders did the same even as their compatriots assembled mortars and field guns in the cover of their tanks. They did not have enough of the armoured vehicles to shield their entire line and the Bizhjerai gunners soon learned to focus on the exposed areas. The mortars started firing to rain down death on top of the wall, and beyond. Our Mages protected us from most of it. Our own mortars behind the walls started firing blindly in high, arcing trajectories. The first shots fell well short of their mark and corrections were shouted down by spotters on the walls. The second volley proved much more deadly and the tanks could not shield the Skylanders from above. Airburst munitions sprayed shrapnel from above, turning the Skylander gunners into mangled meat. Despite the scale of the carnage the losses were relatively minor on both sides. Most of the Bizhjerai gunners were completely safe inside the walls, only those on the top being exposed and those were mostly protected by us magic users. But we were burning through our reserves swiftly. The dense magic field was already starting to evaporate with the loss of the containing shield, and the Skylander Mages were continuously recharged by the Hand. I saw several of Bizhjerai magic users along the length of the wall flagging and mortars struck, tearing men apart with each blast. Power surged into us, and the defence bolstered. Malkareth had alighted behind the wall and powered our Mages, but not even his prodigious reserves would hold forever. The artillery duel lasted hours, and hundreds died. Most of the dead were Skylanders, but the Bizhjerai lost many and each death weakened us considerably. The Fists of Heaven proved themselves time and time again, deftly engaging their more numerous counterparts. Their superior expertise in airborne combat proved effective and the inexperienced crews of their opponents brought the Skylander ships in each others way more often than not. The four Fists worked in tandem gracefully, as predators hunting in a pack. The massive ships moved with a slowness that belied their ferocity. Each massive volley of their guns were enough to topple buildings but the massive armour of the Fists barely noticed and the magical shields of the Skylanders absorbed the attacks in dazzling displays of pyrotechnics. Technology faced magic in a titanic duel in the skies. Even as I deflected incoming shots from the walls I watched the Fist separate one of the smaller Skyships from the others and circle it. The battle stilled as the combatants turned to the sky. The battle in the air slowed as the Fists prepared for the deathblow. It was as if the three ships hesitated, savouring the fear of their defenceless prey. The Skylander ship burned and smoked but still lived. Its fallen shields flickered into being just as the three Fists unleashed their full broadsides. Thunder struck and the weak shields collapsed. The iron balls tore through the envelope and the gondola. One of the engines shattered and the Skyship listed and drifted to the side. It lost altitude as the high winds grabbed it. Without the engine it was unable to parry against the wind that grabbed its fins and it was swiftly dragged from the battle. The Fists abandoned their mortally wounded prey and drifted to engage the remainder. Cheers erupted from the defenders of Dun Traelak and a cry of dismay reached us from the Skylanders. The murder of the Skyship did not go unanswered and the uncoordinated flotilla had positioned itself while the Fists focused on the one ship. The five remaining ships unloaded on the smallest of the Fists. Engines burst apart, shattered engines tumbling through the air along with the engine room crew. The innards of the ship thundered down on the Skylander army, many unable to get out of the way. Even in death the Fist wounded its murderers. The Hand of Glory spoke, and the Fist died, slowly dropping as steam streamed out of its ruptured envelope. The two remaining Fists roared in fury and grief. The whistles and sirens connected to their engines screamed a high pitched keening dirge in sorrow when they vented steam. They had lost their sister, and the hundred men and women of the crew awaited a crushing death. The ones that still lived, that is. Kendall's anti air cannons finally opened up in support of the remaining Fists, their distraction buying time for the Fists to rally. It brought the guns of the Skyships down on Dun Traelak, and the ground trembled before their fury. The Skylanders on the ground opened up once more, and the nerve wracking cannon duel resumed. With Malkareth bolstering our magic users we managed to defend the wall for hours and the Bizhjerai learned to time their attacks, ducking into cover when the telltale whistle of mortar rounds approached. Those who did not learn died messily, getting turned into so much meat in an instant. Everywhere I looked the land was covered in purple smoke, blood and debris. Dead Bizhjerai littered the keep, but not as many as I had feared. The Skylanders had fared far worse. I sensed Kendall, furiously at work inside the shield tower to repair the shield enchantment. Red was with him, and for now she was safe. The Skylander air ships picked apart his anti air guns with precision bombardment and their crews died fiery deaths. The distraction removed, they turned back to engage the Fists. The three remaining Fists had taken full advantage of the distraction and another of the Skylander ships were haltingly retreating from the battle. It was wounded, but far from dead. It would return in time but not today, or perhaps not even tomorrow. But it would be back. I walked up and down the wall, ducking into cover and bolstering the confidence of the defenders. Whenever the defenders courage flagged I was there, hurtling through the air on my Valkyrie wings. My shining presence and rousing words rallied them back to their guns, but we could not keep this up for long. The sun was setting already and it felt like both an eternity and the blink of an eye since the assault had started at midnight. A surge of magic caused me to spin around in time to see a startled Bizhjerai woman impaled on a crystal sword. Valkyries rained down on the wall, firing and stabbing wildly around themselves. They had crept close in the cover of the smoke and launched themselves onto the wall. The guns on that section of the wall grew silent after I saw a group of Valkyries drop into one of the hatches leading inside the wall. The Skylanders outside the walls surged forward, tanks shielding the column of soldiers. The guns further along the walls took advantage of their angle and fired into the sides of the column, killing men and women by the dozens. Their former opponents, now unopposed rallied and death rained upon our heads. I charged a Valkyrie engaged with one our our gunners and my blade cut through her shield and severed the wings from her back in a dazzling shower of magical embers. The gunner lashed out and kicked her in the chest and the Valkyrie tumbled over the shattered crenellation with a startled shriek. Her scream cut off suddenly when she struck the ground far below. Her friend levelled his rifle and shot me but my shield absorbed the impact. My revolver bucked in my crystal hand twice, the first shot obliterating his shield with with a shield breaker spell and the second punching through his crystal armour and struck him in the chest. He fell to his knees before the round exploded, sending his arms in opposite directions and his head to the sky. I leaped through the welter of gore that had been his torso to engage the Valkyrie behind him. Her enchanted blade cut effortlessly through the cannon, destroying it. The gunners lay dead at her feet. I could see the smile on her full lips through the opening in her helmet. Her blue eyes were wide and her full breasts, perfectly outlined by her armoured corset, heaved with swift breaths. She pointed her sword at me.

"Dragonbane! Betrayer!"

I responded with a snarl and surged toward her, propelled by my armour. I batted her sword to the side with my own and tackled her. I landed on top, her crystal wings shattering under our combined weight. She got her leg in between us and kicked me off. My wings flared and put me down on my feet. She rolled up gracefully into a combat stance, blade held warily in a low guard. I assumed a wrath guard, my sword held over my shoulder, ready to lash out at her side. The woman gasped and gurgled, a foot of steel protruding from her neck. She fell to her knee, revealing a Bizhjerai warrior giving me a grim smile. He put his foot on the back of the dying woman and kicked her off his blade. I nodded in thanks and the man turned in search of more foes. His head vanished in a spray of blood as a cannonball whistled past me. I blinked his blood out of my eyes and ducked behind the crenellations. The Skylanders were almost at the walls, carrying long ladders. We had to get these fucking Valkyries out of our hair or we would be swarmed with Skylanders in minutes. Rifle shots pinged against the stone all around me as the footsloggers came into range. Ducking below the cover of the crenellations I ran toward the hatch. Only a few Valkyries remained on the top of the wall, the rest either dead or down below. I left the Valkyries topside to be dealt with by the others and dropped through the hatch. I descended into chaos. The loud din of fighting deafened me. In the tight confines the superior armour of the Valkyries worked to their advantage, and their shield breaking swords cut through the crystal armour of the Bizhjerai. The Clansmen were not used to fighting in armour, despite the months of rigorous training, and they were forced back despite outnumbering the Skylanders ten to one. The Skylanders were not prepared for the presence of Bàs Marbhadair, though. My power exploded out of me, wounds glowing when the magic surged. I jabbed sharp spears of force through their shields, ensnaring them and encumbering their movements. The Bizhjerai drew back, puzzled at the sudden turn of events. Then they saw me. They redoubled their efforts with loud cheers and their own blades sank deep, coming away stained with blood. Valkyries died in droves, but not without cost. Even encumbered they were still dangerous, many of them magic users not without skill. Bizhjerai burned or came apart in surges of magic. I stabbed my sword through the back of a towering man even as I shot a woman through the side of the head. My thoughts descended into incoherency. The battle took me over completely until the Bizhjerai stood victorious. I was drenched in blood, the warm stickiness finding its way through the gaps in my armour. The sting of several wounds intruded on my thoughts. The Valkyrie armour was good, but far from impervious.

"Bizhjerai! To your guns. There are Skylanders at the walls that needs killing!"

I glanced out a nearby cannon port. A ladder was just outside and a body blocked my view. I aligned the point of my blade and pushed it between the gaps of the armour. A shriek of pain rewarded my effort and my sword was nearly wrenched from my hand as the woman tumbled backwards. I left the gunners behind and my armour threw me through the hatch and into more chaos. The Skylanders had scaled the walls and were pushing the Bizhjerai defenders back. They had not yet gained proper foothold, but the Bizhjerai were steadily pushed from the enemy beachheads. If the Skylanders from a pair of ladders converged... A Skylander crested the wall and his smooth bore shot destroyed the head of a blond Bizhjerai woman next to me. My revolver claimed his head in vengeance and I holstered the now empty weapon. These Skylanders were mercs mixed with militia, sent here to die and bleed us. The Guard and special forces would come to deliver the deathblow. I shouldered myself through the throng of Bizhjerai to the front line and I engaged the milita. They were untrained and scared but the sheer press of them pushed us back. The mercenaries, experienced in underhand tactics from the Undercity, hung back. They let the militia take the brunt of the attack and darted forward to strike when opportunity arose. They were the backbone of this assault. I leaped to the sky and my wings brought me hovering above the melee. I would be completely exposed from fire from outside the walls but I trusted my shields. My thrusters burned friend and foe alike, but that could not be helped. I charged a simple spell and launched it into the mass of Skylanders crowding the ladder. The explosion threw them in disarray and the Bizhjerai surged forward to put an end to them. Spears lashed out, hooking into the ladder and pushing it from the wall. The Skylanders ascending it cried out in fear when they fell to their deaths. The man on the top of stair snarled and grabbed two of the spears even as he fell to his premature death. One of the Bizhjerai surrendered his spear but the other was pulled from the wall to join the dead piling up against the wall. The action inspired me and I swung out to hover outside the walls. Nets of telekinesis slid out from me to grab the next ladder and I pulled. The ladder fell from the wall, bringing death to yet more Skylanders. Shots struck me from below and my shield collapsed. Before I could reinforce with my own personal shield a shot pierced my armour and embedded itself in my thigh. Pain blinded me and my wings flickered with the break of my focus. I fell toward the mob of Skylanders below. Even more shots struck my hastily erected personal shield and I nearly passed out of the backlash. In desperation I poured power into my wings and I hurtled blindly through the air. As luck would have it I soared over the wall and landed on my shoulder amongst the mortars on the other side. Many were destroyed, their mangled crews littering the stone of the outer courtyard. I rolled with my momentum and finally came to a halt. I gritted my teeth against the pain and forced the shot out of my leg with my power. Flames burst out of the hole when I cauterised it. I did not have time for further triage. The bleeding had lessened and I scrambled to my feet. I put weight on my leg. It hurt like a motherfucker but it would support me if I favoured my left leg. I soared back to the top of the wall. The gunners below had reloaded their cannons and fired point blank at the tightly packed mob of Skylanders below. Long bloody furrows were carved in their ranks and the cries of pain of those unfortunate enough to survive filled my ears. It was the sweetest of symphonies I had ever heard. The Skylanders was thrown into disarray and the assault on the wall faltered. Skylanders were cut or shot down and pitched over the wall. The piles of dead around the ladders were six men deep and the frozen ground thawed into a bloody mulch. Hundreds of Skylanders fell to the cannons, unable to get out of the way for they were so tightly packed. The survivors fled and a hope surged within me. The assault had cost hundreds of Skylander lives and their army was greatly diminished. Of course, it was just militia and mercenaries that had died. The true warriors were still fresh in their little city. A powerful surge of power from within Dun Traelak made me spin around and what I saw sent a flicker of hope hurtling toward the skies. Red and Kendall had repaired the shield enchantment and a fresh shield rained down toward the walls. It settled into place and the mortar rounds splashed harmlessly against it. The Bizhjerai roared with victory. The shield flashed and in its weakened state it broke apart. I looked up. The Fists were limping away, each wreathed in flames and the great armour was pitted and torn. They had been forced to flee. Skilled as they were, they had had no chance against the superior number of Skylander ships, especially with their sister having fallen. They had kept the Skyships at bay far longer than I could have asked of them. But their retreat let the Skyships focus on the walls.

"Get off the wall!"

I surged off the wall on ethereal wings, followed by the few other Bizhjerai Valkyries on the walls. The rest were not as fortunate. The Skyships fired again and the wall erupted in flame. Men and women vanished in the fire and the ground trembled. My ears were filled with a loud ringing sound. Gunners poured out of the inside of the walls, protected by the stone but the top of the wall where I had been moments ago were scoured clean of life. The stone glowed faintly from the heat in places. I guided the emerging warriors to safety, even as mortar shells fell on our heads. I deflected as many as I could, aided by the few Bizhjerai magic users that still had power to spare but many still struck home. The carnage cut deep into my soul and my previous hope vanished. The wall quaked beneath the horrific onslaught of the powerful guns of the Skyships, supplanted by the now unopposed barrage of the field guns. The wall would fall, and things would get truly messy. With a thunderous roar a large section of the wall collapsed and I was covered in a cloud of stone dust. I was protected from it within my shield by I could see nothing. With my magesense I saw the Bizhjerai mill around in confusion and I screamed to rally them and pointed them in the direction of the inner walls. The entire section between the walls would soon be flooded by Skylanders. That is when I saw the large group of warriors dashing toward the breach. At their head ran Red's father.

"Bàs Marbhadair! Get them out of here. We will hold the breach!"

It was a suicide mission. "No! Leave it! Fall back to the inner wall!"

He paused beside me, waving his warriors on.

"Kyra, if we don't hold the breach these men will have no chance of escaping alive."

He was right. "But you will all die! There is no way you can retreat from the breach!"

"We will die, yes, but many more will live to fight another day. My warriors all know this."

Fuck it all, he was right. I stared into his blue eyes, so alike those of his daughter despite their differing colours.

"I will lead these men to safety, then I will come back for you."

"No, Bàs Marbhadair. You are much too important to waste like this."

"You are the Chief!"

"I am an old man. You are the future, you and my daughter. Keep her safe. Let our sacrifice bolster the men in the days to come. Live. And fight!"

I nodded, blinking furious tears away. With a squeeze of my shoulder he rushed to join his men. Skylanders were already at the breach, trading fire with the Bizhjerai. Our time was short. These were not militia. Guardsmen faced us now. I rallied the Bizhjerai and ran for the inner gates, gathering more as we went along. The warriors jammed at the gates, several hundred people trying to crush through them at the same time. I screamed for order but I went unheeded. Red found me there and joined my efforts to untangle the mess by the gate. The breach would not hold for long, especially with the Skylanders crowding over the now unprotected wall to take them in the rear. A small group of Skylanders approached the throng by the gates. I spat out a curse and soared to intercept them. Red landed next to me and we both raised revolvers. The group of Skylanders scrambled to halt their charge when we suddenly dropped before them and our revolvers claimed most of them before they could react. The rest fell to our sword and axe. I turned to review the crowd by the gates and noted with relief that most had now passed into relative safety. I started for the gate but Red remained behind.

"Father! No!"

I winced. She had sensed her father at the breach, now cut off from us by the emerging Skylanders. She broke into a run toward the breach and I soared through the air, twisting to land before her. I caught her around the waist and pulled her toward the gates. She flailed and screamed, cursed and spat. She even fired the thrusters of the Valkyrie armour and tossed us both to the ground. She wrenched free and broke into a sprint. Still lying down I slid across the ground, thrusters spewing magical flames. I caught her foot and flipped her on her face. She struck hard and lay dazed. I cut the wings from her armour and slung her over my shoulder. My wounded thigh screamed under her weight as I hobbled back.

"Father!" Her anguished cry broke my heart, but she had lost all of the fight that remained in her. In my magesense I saw her father standing on a pile of rubble and corpses, surrounded by his few remaining Huscarls. He was swinging a large two handed axe with deadly precision but he bled from a dozen cuts. He slew Skylanders with each offensive swing of his axe but it was futile. There were no escape available and an endless supply of Skylanders to fight him. I knew his fight was over when a musket shot struck him in the belly but the tough old warrior refused to lie down and die. Even as blood gushed from his lips to mingle with his bushy red beard he grabbed a Skylander woman by the throat and hoisted her into the air. With a clench of his fingers he crushed her throat and heaved her into her friends. A sword scored his shoulder and he responded with a one handed swipe of his axe that took the top of the Guardsmans head off. One of his Huscarls died, shot through the head, and the Chief avenged him with a savage blow that split the Skylander from shoulder to groin. The axe lodged in the dead man and the Chief let it go, throwing himself bodily at the wary Skylanders. He bore three of them to the ground and even as countless blades found homes in his body his hands would not release the throat he clenched. His fingers refused to relax even when breath escaped his body for the last time and the woman he was choking joined him in death shortly with lolling tongue and face blue of lack of air. Red sat against the inner wall, frozen in shock as she sensed her father die. She drew a shuddering breath and released it with a whimper. I reached out and cupped her face but her eyes stared straight through me, hollow with shock.

"He gave his life to save us, so that we may see him avenged!" I saw no indication that my words had reached her. I shook her lightly. "Snap our of it, love. We have Skylanders to kill!" That seemed to reach her shocked mind and her beautiful eyes brimmed with vengeful fury mingled with grief. Her voice was a wet snarl when she spoke.

"Grief comes later. I would have Skylander blood first!"

"That's my girl! Come with me, and I shall see that you have enough to bathe in!"

I held out my crystal hand, and her gauntleted fingers grasped my wrist and I pulled her to her feet. Why were the Skyships silent? Why had they not pummelled the inner wall to rubble as they had the outer? Unable to bring their field guns over the wall, not until they commanded the gate, the Skyships would be their best hopes of breaching the inner wall for a second assault. And then there was the main keep. Dun Traelak was wounded, but we were far from dead. And like a wounded beast we would bleed our killers dry before surrendering. I suddenly realised that I had not sensed my son for hours. Worry slammed into me. Had he fallen and I had not even realised? No, not possible. Besides I could feel his faint presence in the back of my mind. He was far away, rapidly coming closer. Had he ranged out and harassed the rear of the Skylanders? Destroyed their supplies possibly? That was quick thinking of him. I soared to the top of the wall, followed by my wife. The Skyships were coming closer, but they were not firing on the keep. Why did they hold back? They should press their advantage. The Bizhjerai were exhausted while the majority of the Skylanders were still fresh. They had us pushed back into a corner. Why were they holding back? The Skyships fired their prow guns and I braced for impact, but the shots were not aimed at us. The glowing shots soared through the sky, up toward the mountains behind us. What the fuck where they doing? Hoping to trigger an avalanche to cut off our only route of escape through the valley? Possibly. Then my magesense lit up when a star entered my range, then another and a third followed my many lesser fireflies. A familiar roar shook the walls. Dragons. I spun around, wanting to see with my own eyes. The night sky was dotted with shadows, the stars blinking as flying forms blocked their light momentarily. I counted four Greater Dragons and a countless swarm of Dragonkin. The flying horde whistled past the keep and magic rained down on the Skylanders. Malkareth splintered off from the swarm and landed on the inner courtyard as he had so many times before.

"Mothers! I brought friends!"

"Riders! Mount up!"

I soared onto his back, and the surviving Riders did the same from various points of origin. Two of our numbers were no longer among us, and their loss pained us all. Red alighted next to me.

"No, Red. Not this time. With your father dead you must remain to lead the Bizhjerai. Lead them out there, support our new allies. But stay safe. Stay alive."

Her mouth set in a reluctant expression, but she knew I was right. We could not let our new allies finish this fight for us. We did not even know if they could. The elite of the Skylands were still out there. She slid to the ground.

"We Ride!"

Mal launched in the air and the fading voice of my wife reached me.

"Bizhjerai! Attend! The Red Flight has come to aid us, do we let them fight our battles for us?"

A roar of denial met her words and then we were too far away to hear the rest. Mal joined the swarm of dragons. The Greater Dragons focused on the Skyships and despite being dwarfed by the massive Skyships their nimbleness proved difficult to hit accurately. Whenever a shot came too close one of the Mages on their backs deflected the shot. Massive amounts of magic streamed from the riders and the shields on the ship were rapidly approaching their limits. The Riders were not as powerful channellers as the other dragons' riders, not yet, but our rifles proved efficient. The lesser effect, but greater accuracy proved pivotal. The Mages wrestled down the shield with brute strength and our accurate weapons destroyed vital systems. Destroying scrying crystals used for aiming silenced the guns and explosive rounds tore the engines apart. The ships were still flying but could not manoeuvre, nor could they fire without fear of striking their own. The lesser Dragonkin, the Drakonids and the wyverns, were all over the Skylanders.
