The Skylanders still had the numbers, but they no longer had the magical advantage and their training lay in concerted fighting. The Drakonids did not fight as a unit. They swooped over the battle, their speed and erratic flight patterns proved difficult to shoot down. The sheer number of fire aimed at the sky brought down hundreds of Dragonkin, but the survivors dropped to the ground to tear into the frightened Skylanders that were struggling to reload. Human Mages on wyverns poured fire and other deadly magic into the thinning ranks of Skylanders, but the enemy were rallying. Skylander Mages returned fire. The Hand of Glory still fuelled their Mages with the artificial ley line.

"Mal! Take us closer to the Hand."

He banked his wing and we swooped upwards, dodging and weaving as we flew against the current of dragon bodies. Beneath us the Bizhjerai were swarming out of Dun Traelak, forming long triple ranks before steadily advancing. The Dragonkin horde focused mainly on the rear and flanks where the weakness of the formation lay and the Bizhjerai would soon assault the front that was struggling to engage the enemy in their rear. The slaughter would be immense. But the Skylander Mages proved troublesome. They fried Drakonids from the sky and shielded the Skylanders around them, forming pockets of calm in the panicked night. The Hand loomed closer and grew to fill my entire view. We skimmed along her belly to loop around her stern and the ley line receiver there. One glance told me everything I needed to know. An incredibly powerful shield protected the receiver. It would be nearly impossible to break through it. It would be easier to fight our way to it from inside the ship. Malkareth sensed my thoughts.

"Mother! I have an idea."

"Speak."

"If we disable the ley line temporarily, the shield will weaken. If I lend you my power you can focus a blast to destroy it."

"How do we disable the ley line?" That was kind of the entire problem we faced. In other to disable the ley line we had to disable the ley line.

"I think I can drink the flow of power for a short while. It may be enough."

"Are you certain? I won't risk you!"

"I am not, but I promise that I will leave the flow of power if I feel threatened."

The situation was dire, and I gave him permission. The Riders had heard our short discussion and were ready to link their power to my spell. None of us could channel a spell powerful enough to blast even through a weakened shield of that magnitude but all together, boosted by Mal? Possibly. Mal looped around and aligned himself with the ley line and then he carefully dipped inside. He made sure to only dip his belly or the Riders would suffer. He pulled hard on the stream and the lance of power ahead of us flickered and died out. I threw out the runes of the spell I had chosen and the Riders poured their power into the structure. The air was heavy with it. Mal roared and poured the power he drank through us. It was so much, more than I had ever experienced even during my fight with Grasax. The spell flared into life, but I had constructed it to expand with power instead of being saturated. We hurtled toward the Hand and the shield had indeed weakened. We kept pouring power into the spell until the last moment where Mal pulled up to avoid collision with the massive ship. I released the spell with a scream. It was invisible but its passing rippled the air. It thundered into the shield. It buckled under the power and strained against the onslaught. It ripped and tore and then vanished. The remainder of the spell slammed into the receiver and broke it apart. Then the now unblocked ley line struck the ruined stern of the Skyship like a wave of water against a dam. With the rune channel broken the raw magic ripped through the ship, tearing it apart. It must have struck the storage gems inside for the resulting explosion ripped the ship apart. Debris rained down on the army below. Hopefully the Bizhjerai was outside of the rain of death. The ley line bled power across the land, but it was no longer tuned to be used by only the Skylanders. Dragons drank deep of the power, depriving the Skylander Mages of its comfort. Mal dove to join the battle below. The Bizhjerai fired, three ranks firing in volleys. Skylanders fell in droves by the front. The Greater Dragons landed in the mess of bodies, and magic spilled forth. The slaughter was immense, on both sides, but the Skylanders had the worst of it. One Mage after another Archoned in desperation. I leaped off Mal's back, angling for the closest Archon. A desperate Mage who no longer had anything to lose was incredibly dangerous. He sensed me hurtling toward him and his ethereal head pivoted in my direction. A ray of power sought to bisect me but with a flick of my wings I dodged it. I slammed a containment shield around him, compressing his power as much as I could. He raged within and I almost threw up from the backlash. His power was leaking rapidly without a body to hold it and his fragmenting mind was not disciplined enough to maintain the shield that could prolong his life for a short while. I stole the power that leaked out of his spirit-form and put it back into the spell. He expended his power mindlessly, swiftly, and he faded quickly. I dropped the spell, breathing hard. A Skylander thrust at me with her bayonet but I brushed it aside with my armoured forearm. The claws of my crystal fingers flicked out and I buried them under her chin, my hand sinking deep into her head. I curled my fingers inside the mushy contents of her skull and her face twitched when she died. I pulled my hand free before she fell. There were more Archons nearby, killing Dragonkin. My wings bore me over the field of slaughter, for it was no longer a battle. There were no clearly defined lines, no sides. It had devolved into a free for all melee on the blood soaked mud. The mix of forces prevented the dragon Mages from killing masses of enemies but the Greater dragons strode through the battle as their riders killed with precision. I consumed another Archon in the same way as the first. It would have been impossible to do so if not for my sealed wounds. They allowed me to absorb and channel power in a rate that was far beyond the normal. Another Archon faded on her own and the suddenly the Skylanders were running for the hills. I cut down those who fled too close to me, and I sensed hundreds die as they tried to survive the night. None of them did. You could not flee on foot over open plains when you were chased by airborne predators. Ten thousand Skylanders dead in less than a day. Never before had such a slaughter been inflicted on my former home. It was a tremendous blow on unprecedented magnitude, but the lives lost tonight was but a rounding error compared to the sheer numbers that remained. We would live for some time yet, but there were more Skylanders to replace the dead. There always was.

## Chapter 48

There were no celebration of the victory. It had been won at such a great cost. Each and every member of Clan Bizhjerai had lost someone they held dear. The cleanup after the battle took days, the Skylanders piled high into pyres and our own burned individually in ceremonies. The largest was that of the Chief, and the entire Clan gathered for it. It was sombre occasion, and no one protested when Red took up her father's mantle as leader of the Clan. The aid of the Dragonkin sped up the cleaning, without them we would be gathering the corpses for months. Three thousand Drakonids remained of the five thousand who had come to our aid, but the survivors did not mourn them. The Drakonids were bred to die in defence of the Flight, like the soldiers of an anthill. Even the dead wyverns, lesser dragons, were not mourned more than in passing. None of the Greater Dragons had been killed, but one had been wounded in the fight against an Archon and had lost most of her Mages. She returned home to her roost to recuperate. Humans who had followed the Dragons were a different manner. The dragons had their own burial ceremonies that ended with the Greater Dragons devouring the bodies of their fallen. So that they would forever carry a part of their former allies with them. The thought warmed me, in a morbid way. I hoped that one day my son would feast on my flesh, so that I would forever be with him in a sense. The Fists returned to their home, their ships too damaged to aid us further. Red granted them exclusive future trading rights in return, as was promised. She could not speak for the other Clans, but she would advocate for the rights to include them as well. Salvage of the fallen Skyships and repairs of Dun Traelak started almost immediately after the cleanup and as the snows melted completely the sorrow that had dampened the spirits of the Bizhjerai turned into a cold fury. Talk of vengeance against the Skylanders started to abound. The Skylanders were hurt, teetering. Utopeia was vulnerable and we should rally the Clans and wipe the stain from our territories. I could not blame them, in truth I agreed with them silently. But I knew it was futile. Without a way to strike at the Skylands themselves more Skylanders would come. They would arrive on our shores in an unstoppable wave, and we would not be able to turn them back once more. They knew of our strength now, they would not attack us without gathering enough strength to crush us. The Clans did not understand the full scope of the entity that opposed us. They believed that destroying Utopeia would be the end of the war. Despite myself, I started to believe them. I knew that the Skylanders were nothing if not pragmatic. If we proved to them that fighting us was costly, they would rather turn their attentions to weaker prey. They could build another settlement further down the coast, away from Clan territory or even search for other lands on the other side of the ocean. The Skylands was safe out in the ocean. We had no way to retaliate so if they just left us alone, we would leave them alone. At least that is what I told myself. Red was fully on board with destroying Utopeia, her grief over her fallen father, the last of her blood, had filled her heart with desire for vengeance. If for nothing else I would support the destruction of Utopeia in the hopes that her mind would be free of the dark cloud of fury that suffused her thoughts. Despite the anger that suffused the Clan our attention turned to rebuilding and when the plains dried out in the spring we focused on replenishing the stock of buffalo. Many had been taken by the Skylanders and even more had been slaughtered in preparation for the winter. Vengeance could wait. The dragons returned to their roost, promising to come to our aid should the conflict arise anew. I had started to relax and were once again out on the courtyard, playing with Marissa. Hope that Utopeia had learned their lesson cautiously filled my breast. I was weary of war and violence. I wanted to relax with my family and watch my children grow. It was not fated to be so. Red's scouting bugs reported that Utopeia received large quantities of settlers to replace those that were lost, as well with large shipments of weapons. News that one of the Clan Azwail's settlements closest to the border to Utopeia had been sacked reached us when the summer heat reached us in earnest. The Clans were in uproar. Utopeia was still weakened from their massive defeat, despite the influx of soldiers but they were confident in their ability to defend their settlement. The Chiefs of the Clans came to Dun Traelak and it was decided to show the Skylanders that you could not invade unopposed. It was time to go on the offensive. The Chiefs summoned their Clans and in the coming weeks the horde grew. On midsummer eve, for the first time in living memory the united Clans marched for war.

## Chapter 49

The plains trembled beneath the treads of the horde as we slowly made our way toward the Elweyr forest. Bands of Skylanders were everywhere, harassing our herds and settlements but the Riders combined with the skirmishers formed by Red's late father warded them off and the horde approached Utopeia steadily and unopposed. The Skylanders knew that they could not face us in open combat and they settled in for a siege. With the artificial ley line still powering their defences they felt safe behind their shields and walls. Moving such a large group of people was slow, especially with making and breaking camp each day and it took nearly a month to get there. Fifty thousand Clansmen stood arrayed outside Utopeia and for the first time in more than a year I lay eyes on the city. For that is what it was now, no mere settlement. Spires stretched to the sky behind the crystal wall and people crowded the streets. A hundred thousand Skylanders had crossed over in the last few months and the ley line had swelled to twice its former size. Thankfully less than a third of the inhabitants were trained warriors and from what I could see from dragon back almost none of them were properly armed. Most of the fighters were militia or mercenaries, unarmoured or muskets at the most. None had the bolt action rifles of the special forces, or they were too few and I could not see them. The Clans were still outnumbered but for the first time we outgunned our opponents. It would be a hard fight but the only thing that stood between us and them were the shields. There were simply no way we could break through the shields. The ley line was too strong. The Red Flight joined us, bolstering our numbers with air superiority but the shield kept them out. The magical bombardment from the skies proved ineffective, even after many hours. Malkareth left to discuss with the other Greater Dragons, five in number this time not counting my son and he left me in the tent I shared with Red. She paced angrily. She had changed after the death of her father, but I could still see my wife underneath, ready to return to the surface when her need for vengeance was satisfied. For that alone, I would kill all Skylanders I could get my hands on.

"Calm yourself, Red. We have them surrounded, there is no way for them to go but home."

"Each day we are stuck out here drains our supplies. We can't wait forever. They are supplied from the Skylands while those who should produce our supplies sit on their hands out here, waiting."

I stood and pulled her into my arms. She relaxed into my embrace, becoming more like herself at my touch. I kissed the top of her head.

"How can you be so calm, Kyra?"

I chuckled into her hair. "One of us must be. Better it be me than the 'Red Terror'."

That was the name Red had been given in the half a year that had passed. Rumours of her relentless fury towards the Skylanders had spread and the tales of her part in the battle had earned her the nickname. My wife winced. "I hate that name. If I find who started that trend..." She let her threat remain unspoken, and I knew that she did not mean it. I cupped her chin and tilted her head up to mine.

"To me, you will always the 'Red Love'." I bent my head to kiss her and she responded hungrily. Yes, my wife was still there beneath the grief and fury. I had seen her more often as the months passed. So she would be back completely, after these Skylanders were driven from our lands. It was only a matter of time.

"The dragons will figure out how to break the shield, and then we will kill them all."

There was a time when she would not have smiled so brightly at the thought of wholesale slaughter, but none of us were the same person as we had been back then. I could not believe that it had only been a few short years ago. She had been an aspiring warrior, and I had been a broken woman from a land far away. Now we were married and had two wonderful children together. The woman I had fallen for had been a proud warrior, longing for nothing but the glory of proving herself in raiding the other Clans. The Clans she now commanded with the intent to destroy a City. The Clans may have battled for generations, but they were not genocidal. The Skylanders had forced them into this. Her kiss grew desperate and hot and her fingers struggled at the buckles of my armour.

"Mothers!" The mental cry preceded the sound of our son outside the tent. Red let out a frustrated groan.

"I love our son, Kyra, but must he interrupt now? I need you so much right now." I smiled and kissed her nose.

"Let us speak to our son and then you can put your mouth to proper use."

"I'll hold you to that." She returned my kiss and then we exited the tent to join our son.

"The other dragons think that we can bring the shield down with the same tactic that destroyed the Hand of Glory."

"Really? That ley line is twice as thick."

Malkareth bobbed his giant head in affirmation. "Yes, but it will take all of us working in concert. Otherwise we will not be able to disrupt the flow of magic sufficiently."

Red nodded.

"Very well, when will you be ready? The sooner we get this over with the sooner we can all return home and live in peace."

"We are as ready as we will ever be, Mother."

Red was silent for a few moments.

"The Clans will need some time to muster. By the cover of night, will that work for you?"

"Yes."

"Tonight then, we see this war through to the end."

"Very well, I will inform the Flight."

Without further words he launched into the air and glided to where the Dragonkin had made their temporary home. Red turned to me.

"Now, I will have you. As promised."

I gave her a mock bow and a smile.

"As you command, Chief." For the first time since she had claimed her father's title her eyes did not water when she heard it. They filled with desire and she pushed me into the tent. Our lovemaking was tender, loving, and for the first time in a long while our souls mingled completely, opening up to become one being. It was one of the most intimate moments of my life and I dove beneath the storm of anger and grief that covered her brightly shining core. I submerged within her, revelling in what lay beneath. I longed for it to break through the cloud tarnishing its surface. Her words reached me, slightly muffled.

"Soon. The blood of the Skylanders will wash me clean once more." I fell back into my body, our souls coming apart, leaving only a sliver of overlap. I stared into her green eyes as she straddled me.

"Then I will see a river of it flow forth, so that you may bathe in it."

Her lips curled. "What did I do to deserve such a perfect wife?"

She smothered my response with hungry lips, and we lost ourselves in each others bodies. She had saved me, that is what she did. I was dying when I met her, and she had halted my fall. She had filled my empty heart with love, and for that I would do anything for her. Anything.

The wind screamed in my ears as we flew high above Utopeia. Malkareth led the formation of dragons through the skies. Utopeia slept beneath us, only the sentries on the walls awake. The fools ruined their night vision with magical lights and they saw nothing outside the cones of light that spilled forth. The Clans were mustering absent torches and were completely hidden. Field guns and mortars were already being placed just outside the illumination, well within range of the walls. We left Utopeia far behind as we flew out to the sea. We would need a long stretch to build our spell before we released it. The destruction of the shield would be the signal to commence the assault. The field guns and mortars were aimed to take out the guns on the walls first, and then pummel the wall into dust while the Dragonkin entered the city proper to throw the defenders into confusion. Many Drakonids would die, but the dragons did not truly mind. They were hatched to die after all. The Greater Dragons already knew what do to and dipped into the ley line in perfect synchronisation. I threw up the runes of the spell in front of Malkareth and power surged into it from more than seventy Mages astride the six dragons. Power gathered swiftly but still we poured it in. The ley line fell to a trickle, and then faded completely as the dragons drank of the power. The spell blazed in my magesense. I had never seen a spell this powerful. It could have rocked the whole of the Skylands if we had unleashed it on my former home. Utopeia loomed in the distance, rapidly approaching. One of the Mages on the other dragons Archoned, his body burning to ash and his spirit-form tumbling to the ocean. It consumed itself before it struck the waves. Another suffered the same fate, and then a third. Not wishing to risk any more, I released the spell and the dragons pulled out of the ley line. Power surged forth, but not swifter than the spell. The spell punched through the shield as if it were made out of wet paper and the receiver shattered into countless crystal fragments and the ley line bled raw power down on the city centre. Events of wild magic spewed out of the torrent and ravaged the city below. A giant spellbeast that resembled a massive octopus toppled a large building. It did not live long and lost coherency after only a few moments and broke down into lesser, more elemental aspects. The plains lit up as the artillery of the Clans opened up and explosion studded the length of the wall. Guns blew apart and shook the ground. Skylanders appeared out their dwellings like ants after you kicked their home, swarming down the streets to man the walls. Several were only partly clothed, but all were armed. The Riders fired, explosive shots ripping men and women apart. Mal rolled and allowed us who were on his back to fire unimpeded while those on his belly reloaded. Again and again we strafed the streets unopposed, his power pouring into us and then into our ammo chargers. A swarm of Dragonkin descended on Utopeia. The structures closest to the walls were already reduced to rubble by the mortars and the shattered crystal was littered with the ruptured bodies of Skylanders who had been unlucky enough to get caught in the steady rain of explosives. The wall were virtually undefended, no Skylander brave enough to dare cross the rain of death. Thousands mustered beyond the range of the mortars, and when the wall fell the area would turn into carnage. I longed for it. I had meant my promise of a river of blood. These people had come here to take our resources for their own. Our lands. Fuck them. Fuck them all! Malkareth dipped low and we strafed the gathering of defenders. The other dragons joined us but their lesser kin stayed clear of the massive force and instead perused weaker prey further in the city. Large groups of Skylanders diverted back into the city to deal with them and protect their families. Anything that broke apart their formation would make the battle easier to win. There were still tens of thousands of Skylanders defending. The force we had faced at Dun Traelak a drop compared to this ocean, but now they faced not only Clan Bizhjerai. They faced all of the Clans as a single unit. Three of the Greater Dragons swooped over a weakened part of the wall when the rain of mortar shells paused. Magic flared in a powerful burst and the wall blew apart from inside in response to their power. A mighty roar erupted from the Clansmen outside and they surged forth as a giant tidal wave of flesh, bone, steel and murderous intent ready to wash away anything and anyone that stood in its way. The Skylanders charged to meet them in the breach, to contain them in the bottleneck. The two forces met with a clap of thunder, the initial volley felling many on the opposing side. The breach filled with the purple smoke of gunfire. I could sense the warriors clashing in the smoke, fighting with bayonets, sword, spear and axe. Clansmen on either side of the breach raised ladders against the wall and started climbing, having learned from the Skylanders how a breach was conquered. The Riders harried the defenders from above. A thick column of mercenaries approached from the bowels of the city to reinforce the breach, even as the defenders were flanked by those who had scrambled over the walls. In my magesense I saw Red in the thick of it, having crashed into the fighting on blazing wings of magic. Her axe, revolver and magic reaped lives with each attack and the breach would soon be won. But not yet. These reinforcement threatened to take our flankers in the rear. With a thought I send Mal to loop around. He dipped down between the tall buildings framing the wide street and we blasted the column of reinforcements. Many died, but far too few. Our intent had not been to destroy them but buy time to allow Red to capture the breach and let the Clans into the city proper. Once inside we could bring our full numbers to bear. The mercenaries were well versed in urban warfare though, the only kind of warfare on the Skylands. The Clans held dominion on the plains, but in here the Skylanders had the home field advantage. It would be very costly to root them out of the buildings. After the walls were taken and the Skylanders pushed back into the city then the field guns and mortars could be brought inside and we could systematically reduce Utopeia to rubble. The Clans were not here to conquer for they had no interest in Utopeia as a city. They were here to exterminate this blight from our plains. The survivors would be easy pickings after that. Our distraction proved enough and Red slew the last defender who stood in her way in the breach. The rest fled back into the city. The Clans cheered and surged through the breach, following my wife into the home of the enemy. The reinforcements saw them and charged over the rubble of former homes to contain the ingress. Red led the charge to give as much space as possible for the Clans to enter. Red launched ahead of her warriors on her wings, followed by a handful of Valkyries. Shots smattered against her shield, but thankfully it held. I let out the breath I had sucked in when I sensed her getting shot. She landed in the front ranks and was swiftly surrounded. Her Valkyries shored up her position but several ranks of Skylanders separated her from the Clans. Shots rang out and Clansmen and Skylanders alike fell but the headlong charge could not be stopped. The lines of warriors met, and the dying began. Red was deep inside the lines of the Skylanders, disrupting their lines but she was in danger. In her fury and lust for vengeance she had overextended. Two of her Valkyries died in quick succession, shrinking the small circle. One more Valkyrie fell and Skylanders burst into the circle. Red was struck and she lost her footing. I felt her surprise and shock through the bond we shared when she went down.

"Mal! To Red! Your mother is in danger!" He let out a panicked roar and banked around. Red was still alive, but surrounded by Skylanders. I could feel the stab of fear from her when her shield failed, and the pain when a blade found a home in her stomach. Ice filled my veins at the grievous injury. A shaman could heal her, if I could bring her to one. I leaped off the back of my son, plummeting toward my wife at breakneck speed. My wings flared to life and I struck the mass of bodies with the force of a meteor. My magic pushed them aside and my blade and revolver claimed the lives of those too slow in getting clear. I slammed down a shield over both of us and knelt by my wife. She had lost her helmet in the scuffle and her green eyes were clouded by pain and shock when they found mine. Blows hammered down on the shield and the backlash staggered me. Mal crashed down outside the shield, slamming clusters of Skylanders aside with wide sweeps of his powerful forelimbs. The Riders dismounted, clearing the area. I felt Marie go down, wounded in the hip. She would live. I focused on my wife, clutching her belly. I gathered her into my lap.

"I am here, Red. I am here."

Fear clutched my heart. I was not a healer. Flesh wounds I could deal with but organ damage...

"Kyra! It hurts!"

"I know. Sshh. Let me look." I sent my mind into her body, probing the edges of her body. Her abs were severed, but to my great surprise and relief that was the worst of it. The blade had not pierced any organs below. I could hardly believe it. The wound was painful and would prove fatal if the bleeding was not stopped but that was well within my capabilities. I returned to my own body.

"I can fix this, Red. You will be fine. But you will have another impressive scar."

I let my fingers trail her armour above the round scar where Grasax had impaled her on his staff. It was wondrous that she could suffer two catastrophic belly wounds without great internal damage. I focused my mind on her wound as I pinched it close with my fingers. I ignored the few shots that flattened against my shield and the blood that welled beneath my hands. My son would deal with the shooters soon enough. His power coursed into me and I fed it into the shield that kept us safe as I worked. I adjusted the edges of her wound, aligning the skin and muscles beneath carefully before I stitched it close with telekinetic bonds. Within minutes the bleeding had lessened and I patched the whole thing over with a plate of force. The triage would hold until I got her to a shaman, but she would fight no more this night. Her face still pale with pain, that I could do little about, as I helped her to her feet. I set her gently on her feet but her knee buckled beneath her when her weight settled on her wound. The lines of battle had advanced when I worked and to my left were Skylanders, steadily falling back before the onslaught of Clansmen from my right. I steadied Red and shifted her around. A Bizhjerai warrior rushed forward to take her from me. She would not fight more this night, but I was still able and more than willing. Fury at her injury boiled within, tightly controlled and contained until I saw her to safety. I dropped the shield to transfer her to the warrior's arms. He looped her arm around his shoulders and shored up her weight.

"Take her to the shaman! Do no let her out of your sight until she is healed."

"Yes, Bàs Marbhadair!" He guided her gently around to push through the press of Clansmen behind him. I watched them turn and made myself ready to unleash my fury. The Skylanders would pay for her pain. She would have her river, as promised. I watched her for a second longer before I turned back to the fight. Something whistled past my face. A shot. It would have struck my helmet in the back, possibly punching through into my head if I had not turned just then. I was lucky. From the corner of my eye I saw Red's head slump to her chest and her knees folded. The warrior fell at the suddenness of her full weight on his shoulders. Her presence in my mind winked out. I was frozen in shock. This could not be happening. Red rolled listlessly to the ground and lay still. No! I rushed to her side, rolling her onto her back. Her green eyes stared sightlessly at the night sky, the side of her head a gaping mess of broken bone and blood that blended neatly into her hair. No! No, no, no no no no NO! I sent my mind into her dead body. Her soul was already evaporating into the magic field. I scoured her form, dove into the darkness. I lost all notion of the physical realm as I hunted. She could not be dead! I refused to believe it! There! In the distance I saw the fading light of her soul. It was as beautiful as all the other times I had gazed upon it. It was fraying at the edges, no longer contained by her body it stretched and thinned. I could feel her waning attention focus on me as I approached. I wrapped myself around her, gathering up her fading edges and shored up her energies with my own. Her fading mind returned to coherency.

"Kyra."

"I am here, love. Oh dear spirits no! Baby, don't leave me. Please don't leave! I can fix this. I can fix this, babe, just let me think for a moment." In the distance I heard a roar of pure pain. Malkareth. His power surged into me, strengthening my grip on Red.

"Hurts."

"I know, Red. Just power through it. I can fix this." I had no idea how to fix it, but I could not simply give up. She had been fine, wounded but fine, just moments ago. She could not be dead. Just couldn't. I would not allow it. She started slipping through my grasp and I strengthened my mental grip.

"Tired."

"Anjali! Don't you dare let go. Fight it, damn you. Just let me think!" My thoughts were a jumble. I could see no way fix this. The dagger! Grasax' dagger could hold a soul without a body. But it was still in the cellar of Dun Traelak where I had dropped it so many months ago. Her energy was fading fast. How could that be? I held it within my soul, shielding her from the darkness. Then I saw it. Against my will my soul was drinking her power, consuming it. I could not stop. Instinctively I pushed her away from my devouring grasp. She shot out in all directions, thinning, and then she was gone. Three words lingered in my mind.

"Now and forever…"

I was alone in the darkness. There were no sign of my wife anywhere around me. She was gone. I slammed back in my body and found my eyes inches from her own glazed orbs. A roar filled my ears, my own voice mingled with that of my son, howling our pain to the night. I pressed my forehead to hers and cradled her limp body to my chest. Denial ripped from my throat. Malkareth was there, standing protectively over our bodies, his presence in my mind a torrent of grief to match my own. For the first time in more than a year there was just the two of us in my mind. Red was gone. The enormity of it struck me and my vision blurred. Tears streamed down my cheeks. The Skylanders had taken her from me. They had taken everything from me. She had been a proud warrior, a Chief of the Clans. My wife. A stray shot had stolen her brightness and warmth from this worthless world. If only that shot had found a home in my skull instead of hers. She was so much more deserving of life than I. Fury replaced my grief in a flash. I gently placed Red back on the ground and stood up. A last, lingering gaze on her beautiful face. With her head angled like that and the entry wound covered by her brilliantly red hair, the hair that had inspired the name I had gifted her with all those years ago. The only pet name she had ever suffered, only because it was I who had given it to her. If not for her staring eyes she could have been sleeping. I did not have it in me to close them forever. Let her gaze upon the world a while longer. My magic joined my fury and the world around me brightened with the light that blazed from my eyes. My anger boiled my tears to steam. I howled in rage and a torrent of magic swirled around me. I would kill them all. I turned around and charged through the ranks of the Clansmen. They sensed my coming and threw themselves out of my way. My son charged at my side and we barrelled into the lines of Skylanders with equal force. My weapons forgotten, I unleashed raw power on them. They died in fire. The died torn apart by invisible hands. They died crushed to the stones as if a great weight had fallen upon them. They died in a thousand horrific ways with my cruel laughter and desperate sobs the final sound they heard. They died in the malevolent violent light of my eyes, the twin blazes the last sight they saw when their worlds went dark. My son was a dervish of destruction, no barricade was strong enough to withstand his sharp claws and massive momentum. Men, women and children died before us, savaged by teeth, claw and magic. I gave no thought to defence. Come, I thought, end my pain if you can. They could not. I was cut. I was shot. Blood glowing with magic spilled forth but the wounds cauterised themselves. My veins were filled with burning poison. My power waned and I reached out with all of my fury and pulled. More. I needed more. There were still Skylanders to kill. Souls ripped out of their bodies that burned from the leaking power. Their weapons burned as I claimed the magic that they were made of for my own. Their armour dissolved, melting into caustic rivulets that evaporated into me. Even their clothes rushed into me, and I returned the power violently. A beam of incandescent fury sprang from my hand and I played it through the throng of Skylanders, burning clean through the bodies. I cut them in two, severed their limbs. My own armour burned away from the power that coursed through me and I channelled it without regard for my own safety. My wounds throbbed, ripping with agony as the enchantments were stretched to their limits and beyond. I killed hundreds by myself, floating above the crystal cobbles. Any that survived my wrath were dealt with by my son, darting about with deadly grace as he killed. Clansmen followed our mad rampage, putting any unfortunate survivors to the sword. I ripped buildings apart, not caring that women and children were crushed beneath the rubble. The city burned around me, but the fires were as nothing compared to the bonfire of my inner torment. I ripped a screaming man apart piece by piece, not caring that he was unarmed and had been fleeing or that I had just turned the head of his young daughter into a steaming bloody mist. An eternity of slaughter followed, and the river of blood that I had promised my wife flowed through the streets of Utopeia. No matter how many I killed, no matter how many buildings I shattered it did not lessen my pain. My wife was dead. She was gone! With a mournful howl of fury I curled my fingers, crystal and flesh and bone both, into claws and with a ripping motion I shattered a crystal spire. It ponderously fell from the sky into a cloud of violet dust. My wounds flared and ripped, the enchantments burning and unfurling. I sucked the pain inside and clung to it. It was my salvation and my curse. If I ever stopped hurting then Red would be truly gone. I cast about for a new foe, another Skylander to kill but there were none. In an instant my power was consumed and I fell the few feet I had hovered above the ground. My naked feet struck the crystal cobbles and my knees buckled. I fell to all fours in the burning city. Around me I sensed Clansmen murdering the innocent Skylanders cowering in the rubble. These people had not taken part in any battle. I did not care. There were no innocent Skylanders. Not even me. Utopeia was no more. The battle was won. But I had lost everything.

## Chapter 50

Her weight was as nothing in my arms. I carried her slowly from the keep of Dun Traelak through the corridor in the wall of flesh. Bizhjerai warriors lined the open stretch, each man holding a torch high to illuminate the final journey of their young Chief. I carried her toward the waiting pyre by the shield tower. I limped from my wounds, each step filled with pain but I would not allow any other to carry my wife to her final resting place. That task was mine, and mine alone. The crowd was deathly silent, except for a few sobs. My mother stood at the head of the crowd, grief and tears lining her face. She clutched Marissa by the hand. Our daughter had not stopped crying since Malkareth and I returned with Red's body. My son towered above his Grandmother, head lowered. His eye traced the slow procession. His grief was ever present in the back of my mind, mirroring my own. I lowered my wife gently onto the pyre and adjusted the white shroud that covered her body. I lowered the cloth covering her face. I had to see her face one more time. Her hair was neatly arranged, by my own hand, to cover the horrific wound that had ended her life. Someone had closed her beautiful green eyes for the last time. If I ever found out who it was I would strike him from this world. Her eyes was what had captivated me so that first time I saw her. Just before she knocked me out with her spear. I would not have them closed forever. I bent down and kissed her full lips for the last time. For the first time ever, she did not return the kiss. She lay motionless beneath me. For the first time, my touch failed to rouse her body into action, and it would never do so again. I would never clutch her to my chest again. I would never taste her body. A thousand small moments flashed before my eyes, taken for granted and not savoured as they deserved. Not knowing what was there right before my eyes until lost forever. I saw her poke her tongue out of the corner of her mouth as she focused on a spell. I saw the odd little skipping walk she did when she went to the privies after holding it in for too long. The face she made right before climax. The look in her eye when she saw our children. The way she tapped her bottom lip in thought. All things that had died with her, snuffed out by a small crystal ball. I pulled back from her lips and stroked her hair.

"Farewell, Anjali. My love. I love you. Now and forever."

I reached to cover her face, but I could not do it. She deserved to face eternity uncovered, to feel the warmth of the setting sun one last time. I stepped back and a tear escaped my eye. I had not cried once since the battle. The days had passed in a cold numbness. I raised my arm and set the pyre aflame with my magic. Marissa broke from my mom and rushed forward, clutching my waist as heart wrenching sobs wracked her body. I put my crystal hand on her head and stroked her hair. I stayed close until the heat of the flames scorched my face and I only stepped back for Marissa's sake. I could burn, for all I cared. The flames spread rapidly but my eyes never left my wife's face. I devoured every detail of it, committing it to a memory that already knew it. Her hair caught fire first. The flames were of the same colour as her hair. Her skin blackened and charred and the shroud darkened as the little fat that resided in her body melted and poured through her skin. With a sudden whoosh her body immolated. The disgustingly pleasant smell of burning meat spread from the pyre and it turned my stomach. I would never again eat the glorious meat she had introduced to me, the taste of it forever bound to the smell of my burning wife. I covered Marissa's eyes with my crystal fingers. She should not see her mother so. She struggled and freed her eyes. I had no right to deny her the sight, so I let her be. Red was hardly recognisable by now, her pale skin black and flaking off. Her eyes, her beautiful green eyes that had so often regarded me with love and amusement and sometimes with anger but always beautiful. They cooked and popped with faint plops and dribbled down her temples. The woman I loved was gone, both her body and soul. There was nothing left for me here now. I turned away and relinquished my daughter to my mother. She reached out for me.

"Kyra..."

I ignored her and limped back into the keep. Iolan stepped into my path. With the death of both Red and her father and Clan Bizhjerai greatly diminished by the casualties of war he had claimed leadership of all of the Clans. Clan Ithlak was too powerful for any other Chief to oppose him. I wondered if he would be powerful enough to maintain the hold on the unified Clans or if they once more would break apart into raiding factions. At least until the Skylanders returned. He sneered at me.

"Bàs Marbhadair." His voice was loud and carried through the silence so that anyone could hear. "Now that the Skylanders are dead, along with your whore, there is nothing keeping you here. I expect you to gather what remains your kin and return to the hole whence you came! You have brought nothing but war and destruction upon the Clans. I would see you dead for your treachery but the kind words of the Chiefs have swayed my intentions. Begone, and never return."

I stared at him numbly. I reached out and squeezed his shoulder and he relaxed visibly. Then the claws of my crystal hand extended and I punched them into his belly. My strike was angled upwards, beneath his ribcage and plunged deep. His body stiffened in shock and my crystal fingers closed around his rapidly beating heart. The tremors of it rebounded down the crystal bones into my arm. I squeezed it and ripped. It was lodged firmly in his chest and I tugged again, bracing against his shoulder. An artery snapped and the heart came slightly loose. I thrust it home and used the cleared space to build momentum. I tugged again and something else snapped. Piece by piece veins, sinew and tissue came loose and finally I ripped the heart out of his chest. None moved to stop me, not even the Ithlaki. He should not have called Red a whore. If he hadn't I may not have killed him. Even if I had then perhaps someone may have stopped me. His heart beat in my hand, spraying blood across both our faces. His knees buckled and he fell to the ground. His eyes never left his own still beating heart, even when they glazed over in death. The Clans would have to find a new High Chieftain. I resumed my limping walk, letting my hand fall limply to my side. Iolan’s heart struck the stones with a faint, wet smack. There was only one thing left for me to do. A short detour later and I found myself back in the chambers that I had shared with my wife. I stripped out of my clothes. The same style of clothing I had worn when I first met her. She had said I looked exotic and beautiful in them and I had wanted to look my best when I saw her off for the last time. I stood naked before I climbed into the bed and clutched her pillow and the sheets close to my chest. Her scent still lingered in the cloth. I would never again sleep in her arms. Finally the tears came. In great hulking sobs and cries of pain. I don't know how long I cried, nor do I care. My wife was gone. Nothing mattered any longer. The dagger was in my hand before I even knew it and I guided the tip to rest between my breasts. I shifted it to the side over my heart and angled the blade to slide between my ribs.

"Now and forever, Anjali. I love you." My whispered words faded, and I plunged the dagger home straight into my heart. There was no pain. My heart was already shattered to pieces near the shores of the Elwyer Forest, and now it was literally so. Darkness overcame me.

## Chapter 51

I floated in the darkness. Was this death? I hoped it was, though I had hoped that death would be more... Total. Hearing was the first sense to return and voices intruded upon my peace.

"Why would she do this?" The words was followed by a sob. That was mom.

"You know full well why." Kendall. Touch returned and I felt someone hold my flesh and bone hand. "She loved Anjali. Kyra died with her in that battle. It only took a while for her body to catch up."

"But she yet lived!"

"Did she? I do not think so." My hand was placed on the bed. "Rest now, Kyra. I pray that the next life will treat you better."

A roar shook the bed. Malkareth. He had sensed my death but his presence now bloomed in the back of my mind. I had hoped that our bond would prevail, but I had not been sure.

"MOTHER!"

"I am here Mal. I just took a nap."

"You were gone from my mind!"

"I know. But I am back."

His relief and fear washed through me, but I could not yet move to reassure him.

"For the first time in my life, I was alone. First Mother died and now you. I can not bear it!"

My heart beat and I realised it had been still. Blood flowed through my veins sluggishly but with increasing force. Breath surged as my lungs filled.

"Kendall! She breathes."

Hands returned to mine.

"Kyra?" The hands dropped my hand but quickly found my shoulders and shook me. "Kyra! Can you hear me?"

My eyes opened, illuminating the dimly lit room with their inner glow.

"I am fine, Kendall," I lied. I was far from fine. I was dead, even though my heart beat once more. I was cold, so very cold and I was sure that I would never again warm up. I felt numb, disconnected from the flesh I wore. The dagger lay on the floor, blade still stained with my hearts blood. It had obviously been ripped from my chest and flung against the wall. I touched my breast, trailing the tips of my fingers over the small scar that had been a mortal wound.

"Fine?! You tried to kill yourself. I still don't know how you failed! You were dead when I found you. Mal went crazy, roaring that you had died."

"It is nothing. All according to the plan."

"Plan?!"

I ignored him and threw the covers off. A waft of familiar scent rose to my nostrils but it failed to move me like it had previously. I reached up and activated my armour and it started manifesting around me. I stood up and addressed them both.

"I have work to do. Take care of Marissa for me, will you?"

Mom stepped closer. "Of course, Kyra. We will make sure she is fine until you return." I chose not to tell her that I most likely would not return. "Where are you going?"

"Home."

Mom sobbed and gathered me into her arms. I patted her back awkwardly. Her embrace felt strange, as if her arms were wrapped around someone else. Kendall saw the look in my eyes, and I saw his heart breaking in his chest. When my mom finally let go and collapsed onto the bed he pulled me close for a swift, firm embrace.

"Do what you must, Kyra. And return if you can."

I did not answer and headed for the door. Before I left them behind I paused.

"I love you both."

I pulled the door shut behind me, cutting off my mom's hysteria. I descended the stairs as I had so many times before. This fortress had been my home for years, but with Red gone I felt like a stranger within these familiar walls. This was not my home any more. Red had been my home, and with her nothing but ash so was I. There would be no other home for me. I found my son on the courtyard, curled around Marissa. She lurched to her feet and rushed me as soon as she noticed my approach. I knelt down and caught her, wrapping arms around her.

"Marissa. My daughter. Be nice to grandmother and Uncle Kendall."

I pushed her away and she looked up at me with those serious dark eyes brimming with tears.

"Will you come back?"

Despite my numbness pain sheared into my heart.

"Yes. As soon as I can," I lied. I could tell that she was not fooled by my response and the tears finally burst forth in a silent stream. I reluctantly turned my back to her and placed my palm on my sons flank.

"Mal, I need one more favour of you."

"Anything, Mother. Even if you tried you could not force me from your side." His great head turned to the ash that had been my wife. I refused to look at it. "She was my Mother, and I loved her just as much as you. I know what you intend to do and even as it pains me dearly I will aid you. For Mother."

"For Mother," I agreed and climbed onto his back. With a last look at Marissa silently crying nearby we launched into the air. We shot across the plains that I had come to love. My mind was clear, my body numb. The grief was still as powerful but the fury had settled down into a cold hatred. I felt disconnected from the storm of my emotions. The ruins of Utopeia loomed. The city was rubble, the city centre a storm of wild magic that still sprayed forth from the ruptured ley line. The Skylands were still unaware that their colony had fallen, otherwise they would have cut off the power. We left the land far behind, the land I had gone to full of hope of a brighter future. A future I had found. A future that had been ripped away from me by the very same land that had sent me to it. The looming shadow of the Skylands had reached the land, and had changed it forever. The Clans were no longer the free ranging nomads they had been. The war had forced them to adopt industry, to become more like the invaders from the skies. No more. The Skylands would taint no other noble people, not if I could help it. The Skylands was far out in the ocean, too far for Malkareth to carry me in a single flight. The relay stations of the artificial ley lines were large and we made camp to rest on one of them. I discovered that I no longer had a need for sleep. The enchantment in Grasax' dagger kept my soul separate from my body, divorced from it's needs. Magic was all that sustained me now and we sat on the second greatest source of magic in the world. Only the Great Geyser powering the Skylands was greater. I had once wondered what could drive a man to sacrifice his life for power. To forsake humanity and become a liche. I now knew. Hatred. Hatred and loss of everything that made life worth living. Grasax had craved power and immortality. I cared nothing for the latter, in fact I considered it a curse when bereft of your loved ones. But the former... Power. If it could grant me the vengeance I desired then I wanted it all. Malkareth rested through the night, but my eyes remained fixed on the horizon in the direction of the Skylands. For three more days we flew along the ley lines. On the second day we met the Skyway tram, packed to the brim with soldiers. They watched through the crystal windows with wide eyes as we hurtled past each other, gone from sight in an instant. They would find a rude surprise when they reached the end of their journey, being pitched from the broken end of the ley line into a cauldron of Wild Magic. The thought almost brought a smile to my face. Almost. I doubted I would ever smile again. As the sun was setting on the third day since our first rest a small fleck of shadow appeared on the horizon. The Skylands. For the first time in years I once more beheld the city of my birth. Hatred seethed with me. I had always hated that place, even though I had not always realised it. But the flames of my hatred had never been this strong. The entire city was corrupt, from the lofty spires of the surface that was home of the rich and powerful to the deepest crime-fraught bowels of the Undercity. The Great Geyser loomed below, keeping the massive monolith aloft and powering the lives of two and a half million souls.

"Bring me down below. I will do what I must. Drop me off and then return home. Take care of Marissa."

"NO! We are in this together, Mother. Our fates are intertwined."

"No, son. I must do this alone."

He was silent for several beats of his great wings.

"I loved her too. She was my Mother, just as much as you are."

I know he had, but he was my son. I could not allow him to do this. Red's voice echoed in my ears.

"His life is his own, Kyra. He must make his own decisions. You can't protect him his entire life!"

She was right, and it broke my heart. I could not deny my wife, even in this. I loved her too much.

"Alright. But I ask only one thing of you."

"Anything. Anything but that you ask me to stay the course you have set us upon."

I almost smiled again. Even now his speech was so formal.

"Let me try to do this alone. Only if it is clear that I will fail may you intervene. I want you to live, Malkareth. Your Mother gave you the name of the great patriarch of old because she believed that you would achieve great things in your life. You have eternity ahead of you."

"As do you now, Mother. But for the love we share for Mother, I will do as you ask. I will hold back until it is clear that you can not finish this on your own."

"Thank you. You are the best son a mother could ever ask for. I love you. Anjali did too. More than you can ever believe."

"I shared a bond with her too. I know how much she loved me. And you know how much I love the both of you. It pains me dearly to see you like this, but I know that there is no other recourse for either of us. Even if we both die this day, know that I will be forever grateful to have had such wonderful Mothers. I may be only a few years old, but I would gladly forsake eternity for the privilege of being your son!"

I had no words. Tears streamed down my face as we circled the Great Geyser. I could feel the vast energy swirling from it.

"I love you, son. Now and forever." I leaped from his back and fell free of his slipstream. With a thought my Valkyrie armour brought me toward the Geyser. I threw up as powerful a shield as I could and I plunged deep into the swirling energies. The power pushing against the bottom of my shield propelled me upwards, even as the magic burned my feet. I pulled on the energies around me, drawing them into myself. Power beyond imagining filled me and beyond. Pain wracked my body, but it was distant and I turned my attention from it. The power surged into me, much more than I should have been able to hold. I already dwarfed the vast reserves of my son but there seemed to be no end to my capacity. Grasax had been like a moth to my power. I channelled power into my shield, angling it to stop my hurtling ascent. It would not do to smash into the underside of the Skylands. Despite my absorption the Geyser hardly diminished. My magesense expanded rapidly, taking in the entirety of the Skylands in a flash. There was the fat magic peddler, high in the spires. He was feasting on the flesh of some poor human, killed to feed his taste for flesh. There was a Stardust slinger, selling pounds of evil white powder to a ratlike man with nervous, shifting eyes. There was a woman, singing softly to an infant as it fell asleep, her husband in the room next to her preparing fungus for them both to eat for dinner. I pulled harder on the Geyser and it thinned perceptibly. My wounds shone brighter than the sun and the enchantments containing them smoked and curled. Despite the liche enchantment my body was coming apart from all the power flowing into it. I channelled power into my Bizhjerai rune, remembering the strength that had filled my body. I stabilised, held together by the unknown magic. I pulled harder. There were the mercenary, slitting the throat of a shop owner after he failed to pay for 'protection'. There were a group of teenage boys, nervously approaching a gaggle of beautiful girls on the cusp of womanhood. I pulled harder, straining and screaming with effort. There was a toddler girl, standing up from her crawl and taking her first stumbling step toward her father whose face lit up in wonder. He called out for his wife who where in the room nearby, relieving herself. There was the Mage, lovingly constructing a fence for a client, crafting the crystal into a replica of a flower he had never seen except for on the faded pages of an ancient tome of history for no other reason than that the shape pleased him. He had not been paid to make the fence pretty, only to make it serviceable. There was that woman in the Undercity, plunging her axe into the head of a young boy. Her belly gnawed with hunger, and the boy had fungus in his hands. He had just been about to deliver the food to his sickly grandmother. There were a raid on a Stardust lab, women clad only in thongs being butchered by mercenaries, just like I had done all those years ago. Outside stood Detective Ford, overseeing the action. I pulled harder. My wounds ripped and spread wider. I was unable to contain all of this power. Perhaps if I unleashed it all I could pound the Skylands into dust! I knew that the hope was futile. I would need much more power than this if I wanted to do just that. I played with the thought as a hundred scenes from above played out in my magesense. My body was coming apart. My time was limited. I pulled harder. The Skylands trembled. The geyser that had supported the monolith for centuries was diminished and the delicate balance was upset. The tremor was too faint to be noticed by more than a handful up there, most of them dismissed the trembling as nothing.

"Mother!"

I looked down sharply at the mental cry from below even though my magesense now was a thousand times more acute than my eyes. My son came hurtling straight for the Geyser. No, dear spirits, don't! He plunged into the torrent and hovered there. He drank deeply of the power, just as much as I. The Skylands trembled again, more violently as it shifted to the side. I did not care. I had eyes only for my son. He turned his head upwards and a pained grin spread over his draconian features.

"Together!"

Tears flashed to steam in my eyes.

"Together. Forever and always, my son."

He roared as he drank the magic, his power increasing rapidly. Glowing cracks appeared on his beautiful scales. A hundred thousand scenes of panic and fear played out above, but I did not care. My son was dying below me, what was a few million humans compared to that? The Skylands slid slowly from its centuries long perch atop the Geyser, the flow too diminished to support it. The wounds on his hide spread wider. His wings, his glorious wings, shrivelled and burned and he started to fall.

"Goodbye, my beautiful son."

He was beyond words as he fell, roaring his pain even as he relentlessly consumed the power surging toward him. His body came apart, and the power stored within him burst out in a violent storm. His last word whispered through my mind.

"Mother."

I opened my mouth to answer him, but the shockwave of his death struck me. My body burned and ripped, coming apart in bits and pieces that was tossed skyward even as they atomized. I Archoned fully and the power I drank was all that kept my spirit-form coherent. Now I had truly lost everything. My wife. My son. My body. Only my daughter remained, safe in Dun Traelak. The Skylanders would never threaten her again! The Great Geyser sprang skyward again, caressing the underside of the Skylands. But the damage was done, the colossal city was off balance. It's fall had already begun. It tilted, pushed to the side by the force of the Geyser. A million voices screamed in fear, and it was music to my ears. Skylanders were tumbled around as their homes shifted, the walls becoming floor and the floor becoming walls. Thousands died, heads dashing against the shifting walls or crushed beneath falling furniture. The monolith started falling, rapidly gaining speed. A thousand yards to the surface of the boiling ocean. I watched the monolith fall beside my spirit-form with deceptive slowness. Mile after mile of purple crystal flashed past, obscuring the sunset. The Skylands, no longer deserving of that name, struck the waves with a titanic splash, sending up a gigantic wave that would drench the lands for miles once it hit the shores. Water flooded the Undercity and air rushed out. I hovered above it all like a vengeful spirit, revelling in the death of my homeland. On a whim I gathered part of the power I had consumed. I did not know any spell that would fulfil my desires, but with such power that was not required. My will formed and the power jumped to comply. A gem formed and I poured my memories into it. They flashed before my eyes as I inscribed them. The raid against the Stardust makers. My encounter with Raynard afterwards. How I had stomped that poor girl to death after destroying her body. My murder of Markus. The fight with the invading Dragonkin. Greg's death. Faster and faster they came. My trek with Alissa. The attack of the bear. My first meeting with Red, how I had mistaken her for the girl I had murdered. The attack of the Outcasts on the Bizhjerai camp. Our fight against Clan Kriath. Faster and faster. My first fight against Grasax and how I had nearly died. The first time I had made love to my wife on the night of my adoption. The hatching of my son and watching him grow up. The first hesitant flight we had shared. The plans for the cottage that we would never share. The battle against the Skylanders at Dun Traelak. The death of my wife at the second battle. My suicide that transformed me into a liche. But most of all I implanted my memories of Red. Of Anjali. My wife. My beloved wife ripped from my arms and her life by a stray bullet. She was the most important part of my story. She was the sole reason my life had been worth living. The Skylands sank into the depths below me. I had promised Red that I would kill them all, and now I had delivered. It was time to rest. Upon my death the spell would activate and taking inspiration from Anjali a large magical spellbeast would carry the stone to Marissa. She deserved to know what had happened, but most of all she deserved to know the mother she had not had the chance to spend much time with but who had loved her dearly. I have been called many names throughout my thirty years. Whore. Slut. Mercenary. Traitor. Dragonbane. Bàs Marbhadair. But to the one that I had loved with all of my heart, all of my being, I had been known simply as Kyra. My name is Kyra Zorantis, and this has been the story about the happiest years of my life. This was the story about a love that ended with two and a half million deaths. May they all rot in a watery grave.

## Epilogue

I opened my eyes with a great sob. I sat in my chambers, my mothers chambers. The memories of her last years were burned into my mind and the gem faded and fell from slack fingers. I buried my face in my hands and wept. I had not known what had happened to my mother after that day a year ago when she left with my dragon brother. All I know is that no new wave of Skylanders arrived. Now I knew. The door opened and gentle arms pulled me to a broad chest. Uncle Kendall held me tight.

"Shh it's okay, little one. What is wrong? What has upset you so, Marissa?"

Unable to form words I pointed at the gem. Puzzled, he bent to pick it up. He recognised the rune carved into the top of the dodecahedron and I could feel him channel a trickle of power into it. His eyes glazed over as the memories bombarded his mind. Just like I had moments ago, after the spell bug so similar to those mother had made had dropped the gem on my pillow before it dissolved he relived her memories. It was surprisingly fast. I had lived through years of her life in mere moments. His eyes brimmed over with tears of his own and he clutched me tight, rocking me back and forth.

"She killed them all, dear spirits. She killed them all."

No. Not all. There were still Skylanders on the mainland, thousands had survived and fled into the Elweyr forest. I was sure that many of them still drew breath. I did not mention this to Uncle Kendall.

"Yes, she killed them all."

She hadn't. Some had slipped through her fingers. But I would finish what she started. Not today. Not tomorrow. Not even this year. I would have to train. I was just a little girl, but I would grow. I would learn. I would fight. I would kill them all.
